The two write response codes are logged when they return and graded after the 2-beat read, so the read is checked whatever code the writes answered.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope*: the walk is inbound-filter entries 0 and 7, two address
windows (`SEP_SW_DEBUG` and scratch-cold[0]), `{rw, read-only, write-only}` at
`src_id=0`, plus the source-ID product on entry 0 / window 0, then the
`allow_burst` deny/allow pair on AR and AW of scratch and the burst-to-single
Lite split, then the same-page 4 KB granule, page-bound, and `FILTER_CONFIG.locked`
on entry 15. `CHK-OWNERSHIP` keeps inbound CFG, outbound CFG, the remap banks, and `SEP_GLOBAL_BASE_ADDR` / `SEP_REGION_SIZE` outside every allow window. WRAP, FIXED and
`AxLEN>1` are not walked: the Lite bridges convert those bursts to singles, so the
filter only ever sees `tx_len==0`.

'''''

[[sep_fabric_remap_filter_csr_bank_test]]
===== 2.4 `sep_fabric_remap_filter_csr_bank_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: Fabric and remap

*Run mode*: `no_cpu` (`lsu_stub_all_live`), `+skip_fuse_sense`, 3 seeds

*Source Module*: `sep_fabric_remap_filter_csr_bank_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip

*Objective*: R/W, 64-bit, RO, valid, and write-once-set across the alias/AP/STEE remap and inbound/outbound filter CSR banks, and that every entry of the alias remap bank and of the inbound and outbound filter banks holds its own value. The AP and STEE output-remap banks are checked on one seeded region each per seed. Each filter entry and remap region is an independent rule with its own storage, so a decode that aliased two entries, or a bank that implemented fewer entries than the map declares, would be invisible to a sweep that walks one entry per group.

*Test Coverage*: Remap and filter CSR banks: R/W, 64-bit, RO, valid, write-once-set, and per-entry storage independence across all 16 alias regions, 16 inbound and 32 outbound filter entries.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Write each bank and require the readback to differ from the observed pre-write. Each written word is read first; when the seeded pattern equals that value under the word's R/W field mask, every R/W bit of the pattern is inverted, so a pattern equal to the reset value cannot hide a register that ignores the write.
. Prove RO `data_bus_width` ignores writes on both filters.
. Write a distinct pattern into every entry of each bank, then read all of them back, and require each to hold its own pattern.
. Set and try to clear the alias `valid` bit; it clears.
. Lock one inbound and one outbound filter entry, try to clear `locked`, then write the `FILTER_CONFIG` lo word, `START_ADDR` and `END_ADDR` of the locked entry; require DECERR on each write and no change to each word.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-NONVAC
|A written register's readback differs from its *observed* pre-write value, and the neighbouring field is undisturbed. The pre-write sample is required: asserting only that the written pattern is non-zero is a property of the stimulus constructor, not of storage.
|CHK-ALIAS-RW
|Region start, end and attribute registers are read/write, including the 64-bit upper word: `REGION_START` hi, `REGION_END` lo and `REGION_ATTRS` lo each read back the written value, and that value differs from the word's *observed* pre-write value.
|CHK-AP-STEE-RW
|The output-remap CSRs are read/write across both banks: `REGION_ATTRS` lo and hi of the seeded AP and STEE region each read back the written value, and that value differs from the word's *observed* pre-write value.
|CHK-INFILT-CFG / CHK-OUTFILT-CFG
|Filter-configuration read/write fields (`rd`, `wr`, `ns`, `burst`, `src_id`, `group_id`) read back exactly on both the inbound and the outbound bank, and differ from the word's *observed* pre-write value.
|CHK-BANK-INDEP
|Every R/W word of every bank entry holds its own distinct pattern: 224 words across 16 alias regions (`REGION_START` lo+hi, `REGION_END`, `REGION_ATTRS` lo+hi) and 48 filter entries (`FILTER_CONFIG`, `START_ADDR`, `END_ADDR`) are each written a value carrying their bank number, entry index and word number, then all are read back and required to match through the same mask the write used. The bank term matters because the two filter banks are instances of one RDL array type and share stride and word list: without it, inbound entry *k* and outbound entry *k* would carry the same pattern and a decode that aliased one onto the other would still read back what it wrote. A bank that decodes two entries to one storage, or that implements fewer entries than the address map declares, fails here and the message names the entry and word; the walked word count is asserted against 224 so a short walk cannot pass on whatever it reached, and every entry count comes from the register export rather than a sequence literal. The per-group field sweep above picks one random entry per seed, so this is the only leg that shows the other entries exist and are distinct. Deterministic: the same words are covered on every seed, so the three `reseed` runs repeat this leg rather than sampling different slices. `FILTER_CONFIG`'s hi word is not walked -- its only field above bit 31 is `locked[63]`, which `CHK-WOSET` owns; the read-only `data_bus_width` is masked out here and graded by `CHK-RO`.
|CHK-RO
|The data-bus-width field reads its fixed value and ignores writes of the inverse pattern, on both filters.
|CHK-VALID-RW
|The region valid bit is read/write in both directions.
|CHK-WOSET
|The write-once-set `FILTER_CONFIG.locked` bit holds, and while it is set every write to that entry's `FILTER_CONFIG`, `START_ADDR` and `END_ADDR` completes DECERR, on the inbound and the outbound bank. The clear write to the `FILTER_CONFIG` hi word must complete DECERR with `locked` still 1. A write that flips every R/W field of the `FILTER_CONFIG` lo word (`read_allowed`, `write_allowed`, `entry_enabled`, `allow_ns`, `src_id`, `group_id`, `allow_burst`), and a write that flips 4 KB-aligned bits of `START_ADDR` and `END_ADDR`, must each leave the word unchanged. Each probe logs the written value and the word before and after. Source: `hw/ip/axi_filter/regs/filter_ctrl.rdl` (`locked`) and `hw/ip/axi_filter/doc/index.adoc` ("Locking a Filter Entry"). Every code is logged before it is graded.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope limit*: the field sweep (`CHK-NONVAC`, `CHK-ALIAS-RW`, `CHK-AP-STEE-RW`,
`CHK-INFILT-CFG`, `CHK-OUTFILT-CFG`, `CHK-RO`, `CHK-VALID-RW`, `CHK-WOSET`)
covers one seeded region or entry per bank per seed. `CHK-BANK-INDEP` covers
every alias region and every inbound and outbound filter entry, but not the AP
and STEE output-remap banks.

'''''

[[sep_fabric_slot_csr_strobe_rand_test]]
===== 2.5 `sep_fabric_slot_csr_strobe_rand_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: Fabric and remap

*Run mode*: `no_cpu` (`lsu_stub_all_live`), `+skip_fuse_sense`, 3 seeds

*Source Module*: `sep_fabric_slot_csr_strobe_rand_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip; register model from the generated IP-XACT (`sep_reg_meta.register_fields`)

*Randomization*: `SepSeededRng` from the run seed: slot and register order, write order within each register's plan, access offsets and sizes of the reads, write data, the fill on inactive byte lanes, the BREADY/RREADY hold lengths and the W-ahead-of-AW gap. `reseed = 3` samples different data, fill and orderings; the plan shape (which accesses each register gets) is the same on every seed.

*Objective*: The byte-strobe, access-size, back-pressure and write-once-set rules hold at every slot of the five System-block fabric banks, not at one. Each of the 16 alias-remap regions, 16 AP and 16 STEE output-remap regions, 32 outbound and 16 inbound filter entries is its own register block behind its own AXI-Lite port, so a rule that one slot obeys says nothing about the others.

*Test Coverage*: All 224 registers of the 96 slots: reset, every byte lane written alone and in 16/32/64-bit groups, inactive lanes driven with data, read-only and reserved bits, the filter `START_ADDR`/`END_ADDR` granule write-back, `FILTER_CONFIG.locked` on all 48 filter entries, and a write and a read of every slot outstanding together on `s_axi`.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Read every register as one 64-bit access and as one 32-bit word before any write.
. Per register, in seeded order: one 64-bit write, one write per byte lane, two 16- or 32-bit writes, each with seeded data on the active lanes and seeded fill on the inactive ones, and a seeded-size read after each write; then a 64-bit read.
. Per slot, twice: start a 32-bit write of one register's low word and a 32-bit read of its high word together on `s_axi`, once with BREADY and RREADY held and once with W presented ahead of AW and RREADY held; sample the `s_axi` pins during the pair; then read the register.
. Per filter entry, in seeded order: lock it with a write that strobes `FILTER_CONFIG.locked`; then four seeded writes to its registers, each chosen so that the entry would change if the write were taken, and a write of 0 to the lock bit; read every register of the entry.
. Read every register of every slot.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-SLOT-RESET
|Every register reads the reset value its RDL fields declare (`filter_ctrl.rdl`, `alias_remap.rdl`, `output_remap.rdl`, through the generated IP-XACT), as a 64-bit access and as a 32-bit word. Reserved bits read 0; `data_bus_width` reads its declared value 3.
|CHK-SLOT-STROBE
|Every write answers OKAY and changes exactly the writable field bits in its strobed byte lanes (AMBA AXI write-strobe rule); read-only and reserved bits keep their RDL value. The master drives seeded data on every inactive lane, and always a 1 on `FILTER_CONFIG.locked` and alias `REGION_ATTRS.valid` when their lane is inactive, so a block that ignored WSTRB would take the fill, lock the entry or arm the remap, and read back changed. A filter `START_ADDR`/`END_ADDR` pair that lands in one granule (4 KB with `allow_burst`, 2^`data_bus_width` bytes without) reads back widened to it, as `filter_ctrl.rdl` describes. The write count is asserted against the plan (11 per register). The W beats that carry data on an inactive lane are counted on the TB `s_axi` pins and at the AXI-Lite W port of each slot's register block (`fabric_slot_w_*` probes in `tb/tb_top.sv`, observation-only): the count must be non-zero, the slot-port count of beats and of fill beats must equal the `s_axi` counts, and every one of the 96 slot blocks must see fill, so the deny leg is exercised at the block that applies WSTRB. The log names how many writes moved the register and how many carried fill that differed from it.
|CHK-SLOT-PIPE
|On the `s_axi` pins, each pair has at least one cycle in which both the write (AW accepted) and the read (AR accepted) are unanswered; in the held pair, B and R each wait with VALID high and READY low (the hold lasts 40 to 71 cycles from the request); in the W-first pair, WVALID rises before AWVALID. Both answer OKAY, the read returns the half of the register the write does not strobe (its value does not depend on the order the DUT serves them in), and the write lands. Asserted for 2 pairs per slot. Overlap at the slot's own AXI-Lite port is not claimed: the AXI-Lite demux in front of each slot holds one transaction per direction and forwards W only after its AW, so the slot block does not see the two in flight together or W ahead of AW.
|CHK-SLOT-LOCK
|After a write that strobes `FILTER_CONFIG.locked` with a 1, every write to that entry's `FILTER_CONFIG`, `START_ADDR` and `END_ADDR` leaves the entry unchanged, and a write of 0 does not clear the lock (`filter_ctrl.rdl` `locked`, `onwrite = woset`). Each refused write is checked on the model to be one that would change the entry if it were taken. Every refused write, the write of 0 included, must complete DECERR (`filter_ctrl.rdl` `locked`: the write is steered to the AXI error subordinate); the response-code tally is logged. All 48 filter entries are asserted locked.
|CHK-SLOT-FINAL
|At the end, every register of every slot holds its own model value, so no write to one slot or register moved another.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope limit*: CSR layer only. Whether a filter entry or remap region acts on live traffic with the programmed values is graded by the datapath tests in this bucket. Alias-remap `REGION_ATTRS.valid` is never set through an active lane, because a valid region rewrites the CPU-LSU traffic this test runs on.

'''''

[[sep_fabric_output_remap_datapath_proxy_test]]
===== 2.6 `sep_fabric_output_remap_datapath_proxy_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: Fabric and remap

*Run mode*: `no_cpu` (`lsu_stub_all_live`), `+skip_fuse_sense`

*Source Module*: `sep_fabric_output_remap_datapath_proxy_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (CPU-LSU master); `tb/sep_outbound_mbx.sv` (outbound responder: OKAY and zero read data for any address)

*Randomization*: RANDCFG — the seed selects one bank, one remap region and one filter entry; the checkers and the addresses they compare follow from that choice. Coverage is one region of the bank per run, so the entry runs at a single seed and the entry claims one cell, not a sweep.

*Objective*: Proves that a programmed output-remap window translates a live beat to its remapped target, and that the outbound filter answers DECERR for a beat outside the remapped allow set and for the same beat with its allow entry disabled.

*Test Coverage*: Live outbound / AP remap datapath, not CSR storage alone.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Program one region to `0x8000_0000` and allow-list the remapped beat. CPU-LSU read of the window is OKAY.
. Disable the outbound allow entry and repeat the read of the programmed window. It returns DECERR. Enable the entry again.
. A second region, left invalid so its beat passes through untranslated, returns DECERR.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-REMAP-TRANSLATE
|The programmed window completes OKAY at the remapped target. Identity would miss the allow window. The OKAY comes from `tb/sep_outbound_mbx.sv`, which answers any address, so the check shows that the beat passed the outbound filter, not which address it reached.
|CHK-FILTER-DROP
|A beat outside the remapped allow set is DECERR. One probe is the other region, left invalid, whose beat passes through untranslated. A second probe is the next beat of the allowed region, which translates to a non-zero address outside the one-beat allow entry.
|CHK-FILTER-DISABLE
|With the outbound allow entry disabled, the same remapped read that completed OKAY under CHK-REMAP-TRANSLATE returns DECERR. The target and the translation do not change, so the OKAY comes from the allow entry and not from the target.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

'''''

[[sep_fabric_outbound_remap_filter_walk_test]]
===== 2.7 `sep_fabric_outbound_remap_filter_walk_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: Fabric and remap

*Run mode*: `no_cpu` (`lsu_stub_all_live`), `+skip_fuse_sense`

*Source Module*: `sep_fabric_outbound_remap_filter_walk_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (CPU-LSU master); `tb/sep_outbound_mbx.sv` (outbound responder: OKAY at any address); `seq_lib/sep_fabric_entry_walk_seq.py` (START/END readback model under the same-granule write-back rule of `filter_ctrl.rdl`)

*Randomization*: RANDCFG — the seed selects the in-region beat, the offsets and the windows of every pair. Every region and every entry runs at each seed; one seed per regression, because the bit coverage does not depend on the seed.

*Objective*: Every AP/STEE output-remap region and every outbound-filter entry translate and compare all 56 address bits on live traffic.

*Test Coverage*: All 2 x 16 remap regions (`output_remap.rdl` offset[55:0], valid[63]) and all 32 outbound-filter entries (`filter_ctrl.rdl` start_addr[55:0], end_addr[55:0]). AP region r pairs with entry r and STEE region r with entry 16 + r. Each pair runs offset O (bit 55 clear) and then ~O, and each bound takes a value and its inverse, so every offset, START and END bit takes a 0->1 and a 1->0 step.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Program region r with offset O1, then enable only entry e with a random window that holds the remapped beat X1. A CPU-LSU read of the region answers OKAY.
. Narrow the window to the one granule at X1: OKAY at X1, DECERR at the next granule of the same region.
. Set START to the inverse of the first window's START (above X1): DECERR.
. Program offset O2 = ~O1, so X2 is at or above 2^55. A window holding X2 answers OKAY; a window ending at the inverse of that END (below X2) answers DECERR; the granule at X2 answers OKAY.
. For every address bit k above the granule, program a window where START bit k alone decides the response for a phase-2 beat of the region, then one where END bit k alone decides it.
. Clear valid: the granule at X2 answers DECERR and the granule at the beat's own local address answers OKAY.
. Restore the entry and the region to reset.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-WALK-READBACK
|Every START/END (56 bits), FILTER_CONFIG and remap ATTRS write, bit-leg windows included, reads back as the readback model says (`filter_ctrl.rdl` start_addr: rounded write-back only when START and END share a granule).
|CHK-WALK-ALLOW
|A window that holds the remapped beat answers OKAY. The filter blocks by default and only this entry is enabled, so the OKAY places the 56-bit remapped address inside the window.
|CHK-WALK-EXACT
|The one granule at the predicted address `{offset[55:IDX_START], adjusted[IDX_START-1:0]}` (`output_remap.rdl` offset, region granularity; `hw/sys/sep/doc/fabric.adoc`: the output remap replaces the address with the region offset) answers OKAY and the next granule answers DECERR, so the remap produced exactly the predicted address.
|CHK-WALK-ABOVE
|A window whose START is above the beat answers DECERR.
|CHK-WALK-BELOW
|A window whose END is below the beat answers DECERR.
|CHK-WALK-BIT
|For every address bit k above the granule, and for START and for END, one window whose other bound is 0 or all-ones, so that bound's bit k alone puts a phase-2 beat of the region inside (OKAY) or outside (DECERR). The beat is chosen per bit among beats of the region whose offsets differ in one bit; the selector raises when a (bit, bound) has no such beat. A compare that ignores bit k of either bound flips the answer. Every window is read back.
|CHK-WALK-PASSTHRU
|With valid clear the beat passes through with its address unchanged (`output_remap.rdl` valid: "if clear, they pass through with their address unchanged"): the one granule at the beat's own local address answers OKAY, and the granule at the translated address answers DECERR.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

'''''

[[sep_fabric_inbound_filter_window_walk_test]]
===== 2.8 `sep_fabric_inbound_filter_window_walk_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: Fabric and remap

*Run mode*: `no_cpu` (`lsu_stub_all_live`), real PROD fuse sense (`sep_debug=0`, value-checked against the lifecycle golden)

*Source Module*: `sep_fabric_inbound_filter_window_walk_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (CPU-LSU master and the external SMN master); `seq_lib/sep_fabric_entry_walk_seq.py` (START/END readback model)

*Randomization*: RANDCFG — the seed selects the staged value and every window. Every entry runs at each seed; one seed per regression, because the bit coverage does not depend on the seed.

*Objective*: Every inbound-filter entry compares all 56 address bits on live external traffic.

*Test Coverage*: All 16 inbound-filter entries (`filter_ctrl.rdl` start_addr[55:0], end_addr[55:0]). The target is a pure-RW CSR (`SEP_SW_DEBUG`) whose address has zero upper bits, so the upper bound bits [55:32] decide each response.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Bring up PROD with the inbound filter active. Disable every entry and stage a value in the target CSR from the CPU-LSU master.
. For each entry, enable only that entry and program: a window [S, E] holding the target, then [S, ~E] (both END values at or above the target); START S_B and ~S_B (both above the target); a window ending below the target; the one granule at the target.
. Stage the cold scratch words as extra probes. For every address bit k above the granule, program a window where START bit k alone decides the response for one probe, then one where END bit k alone decides it (for k >= 32 the deciding bound is the one-hot `1 << k`).
. After each, the external master reads the target (and, for the granule, the next granule).
. Restore the entry to reset.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-WALK-READBACK
|Every START/END (56 bits) and FILTER_CONFIG write to the entry under test, bit-leg windows included, reads back as the readback model says. The setup disable of every entry before the walk is not graded.
|CHK-WALK-ALLOW
|A window holding the target answers OKAY with the staged value (the read reached the CSR).
|CHK-WALK-EXACT
|The granule at the target answers OKAY with the staged value; the next granule answers DECERR.
|CHK-WALK-ABOVE
|A window starting above the target answers DECERR and does not return the staged value (`hw/ip/axi_filter/doc/index.adoc`, Blocked Transactions).
|CHK-WALK-BELOW
|A window ending below the target answers DECERR and does not return the staged value.
|CHK-WALK-BIT
|For every address bit k above the granule, and for START and for END, one window whose other bound is 0 or all-ones, so that bound's bit k alone puts a staged probe word inside (OKAY with its value) or outside (DECERR without it). The probe is the target or one of the cold scratch words, chosen per bit; the selector raises when a (bit, bound) has no probe. A compare that ignores bit k of either bound flips the answer. Every window is read back.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

'''''

[[sep_reg_bit_bash_rand_test]]
===== 2.9 `sep_reg_bit_bash_rand_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: Fabric and remap

*Run mode*: `no_cpu`, `+skip_fuse_sense`

*Source Module*: `sep_reg_bit_bash_rand_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip

*Randomization*: RANDCFG — three seeds (`reseed = 3`). The seed varies the block order, the complement-vs-ones order and every touch value, never which registers are swept: the cell set is identical on every seed, so coverage is not seed-dependent. Reseeding is what exposes a register that accepts one mask-legal value and refuses another. The reset walk is the inventory after reasoned skips. Write-lands is the full-mask registers; the inbound START/END pairs use the wrap model.

*Objective*: Proves that every register in the generated SystemRDL export reads its RDL reset value, that a write moves exactly its software-usable bits, that read-only and reserved bits hold, and that every side-effect-free register stores a seeded value. `env/sep_reg_meta.py` exports `addr`, `reset`, `mask` (software-usable field bits) and `mask_all` (storage, reserved included) from the generated SystemRDL.

*Test Coverage*: Seeded CSR bit-bash across the LSU-reachable register map.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Build the seeded configuration from `SepRegBitBashCfg`. Set `clk_wdt` to eight core periods and bring up in `no_cpu`.
. Read every register in the reset walk and compare it to its exported reset, with the bits of fields that have no RDL reset masked out (CHK-RESET).
. For every register in the write walk, write the complement of the current value and all ones, in the seeded order of the two, and read back after each write. Compare inbound START/END readback to the same-beat wrap model. Then write the reset value and read it back (CHK-WRITE-LANDS, CHK-RO, CHK-RESERVED).
. For every register in the storage-touch walk, write a seed-derived value (twice for a shadowed register), read it back under the software-usable mask, and restore the reset value (CHK-BLOCK-TOUCH).
. Require the reset, write and storage-touch walks each to cover every register the configuration named, and log the walk sizes (CHK-RANDCFG).

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-RESET
|Every reset-eligible register reads its exported reset value on every bit except the bits of fields with no RDL reset, which the compare masks out. Each masked row logs its read, reset and mask, and the PASS line gives the masked-row count.
|CHK-WRITE-LANDS
|A complement write moves exactly the software-usable mask bits: the full-mask registers over the full mask, plus the inbound START/END pairs over ``mask[31:3]`` whose ``[2:0]`` are pinned by the same-beat wrap model instead.
|CHK-RO
|Bits outside the mask stay unchanged across the write bash. Counted only where the register has out-of-mask bits. On a register with an all-ones mask the compare cannot fail, so it is not counted. The PASS line gives the count, and the check fails when the count is 0.
|CHK-RESERVED
|Reserved bits (`mask_all` minus `mask`) read back 0. Counted only where the register has a non-zero reserved field. The PASS line gives the count, and the check fails when the count is 0.
|CHK-BLOCK-TOUCH
|Every side-effect-free export RW storage register of the inventory, not one per IP: write a seed-derived ``x``, assert ``(readback & mask) == (x & mask)``, restore reset. Shadowed names take a dual write. The gate is the per-register safety predicate AND the side-effect predicate; the second is required, because the first admits registers whose write drops live beats. `TOUCH_BLOCKS` is the anti-vacuity list, so the sweep fails if any of those nine IPs stops offering a candidate. Excluded registers each carry a tallied reason and the sweep accounts for the whole inventory. Not storage: hardware-owned status and state-machine observability words, the CSRNG reseed counters, an identity register, two read ports, `ENTROPY_SOURCE.FIPS_LOCK` (a sticky lock is never a storage touch), and two selectors that refuse a random mask-legal value — `HT_WATERMARK_NUM`, whose unsupported encodings sanitize, and `NOISE_OBS_CTRL`, whose mask contains a write-only singlepulse field.
|CHK-RANDCFG
|The whole seed-built configuration ran in one invocation: the reset, write and storage-touch walks each covered every register the cfg named. `TOUCH_BLOCKS` is the anti-vacuity list, not the third walk. A completeness control over the sweep itself, not evidence about the DUT -- it fails when a walk silently drops work, not when a register misbehaves. The walk sizes (`export`, `inventory`, `nometa`) are logged with it so a shrunken inventory is visible rather than inferred from a PASS.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope*: This is not a UVM RAL model. `iter_register_walk` counts OFFSET symbols that lack DEFAULT/struct (`nometa`) instead of dropping them silently. `SepRegBitBashCfg` is the single source of truth for both the walk and the skip reasons. ENTROPY_SOURCE registers that hardware advances while the noise source runs are excluded from the reset walk by `sep_reg_meta.reg_hw_updating()`: every register whose fields all declare `sw = r` in the generated JSON model, minus the constants named in `_CONSTANT_RO`. Part of that set is tallied under `hw-owned; read value is not the POR value`; the `STATUS` and `RDATA` name suffixes claim the rest first. `sw = r` alone is not the criterion: COMPONENT_ID is software-read-only but hardwired (`entropy_source.rdl` `hw = na`, no storage in `entropy_source_reg.sv`), so it is opted back in and stays in the walk. The dead-space change compare uses the same accessor, so the two checks cannot drift apart. Write-lands is the anti-vacuity control: a complement write must move exactly the software-usable mask. Two skips are read off the generated IP-XACT. A register the RDL declares `sw = w` returns no storage on a read, and a register that is read-only with no RDL reset value is driven by hardware, so the generated `_REG_DEFAULT` is a field default and not a POR value. Both shapes read back 0 against a DEFAULT of 0 in most cases, so a reset compare on them passes without the DUT having shown anything. `_ipxact_access()` joins the IP-XACT to the inventory by address -- the IP-XACT spells an array as one register with a `dim` where the Python header spells one symbol per element -- and `iter_register_walk` refuses an inventory register with no IP-XACT entry rather than deciding a skip on missing data. The `sep_reg_meta` self-test pins the resulting shapes (the hardware-driven registers by name, the write-only count, and two read-only-with-reset witnesses), so a generator change that alters the `access` or `resets` element name fails there instead of silently restoring the vacuous compare. The same rule applies to each field of a read-write word. A field the RDL gives no reset value has no POR value, and the generated `_REG_DEFAULT` holds a 0 placeholder for it. `sep_reg_meta.word_unreset_mask()` reads those bits off the IP-XACT (no `resets` element on the field). A word whose every storage bit is such a field is skipped, under `no field with an RDL reset; the export DEFAULT is a placeholder`: HMAC `DIGEST_*` and `MSG_LENGTH_*`. A word with only some such bits stays in the walk, and CHK-RESET leaves those bits out of its compare: HMAC `CFG.hmac_en` and `CFG.sha_en`. The `sep_reg_meta` self-test pins the masks of HMAC `CFG` (`0x3`) and `DIGEST_0` (all ones). Read-only WITH a declared reset is a different shape and stays in the reset walk: `ABR.MLDSA_VERIFY_RES_*` is `sw = r` with `resetsignal`, so its reset value is real and only the storage touch refuses it -- software cannot write it, and a touch would compare the readback against a value that never landed. The behaviour behind the access-shaped skips is proven over the frontdoor elsewhere, not dropped: the eight ABR identity words have no RDL reset and no value in any SEP document, so no leaf grades a value for them: `sep_abr_access_size_test`, `sep_abr_pipelined_read_matrix_test` and `sep_abr_concurrent_rw_test` read them against a reference captured from the DUT by `CHK-ABR-ID-REF`, which requires each word to answer OKAY, read the same twice, be nonzero and differ from its granule partner; `ENTROPY_POOL.IRQ_CAUSE` and `.DATA` by `CHK-IRQ-CAUSE-LOW` and `CHK-POP-DATA` on `sep_entropy_pool_aperture_test`. The write-only registers -- keys, data-in windows, command triggers and clear registers -- have no read-side POR to relocate, and their coverage is the functional tests that write them and observe the effect. Inbound-filter START/END stay in the write sweep under the full export mask; readback is checked against the `allow_burst=0` 8-byte granule (`hw/ip/axi_filter/doc/index.adoc`, `filter_ctrl.rdl`) with the peer at reset (`END_ADDR` reset `0x7`): START rounds down and END rounds up when they share a beat. The 4 KB granule is `CHK-PAGE-WIDEN` on `sep_fabric_inbound_filter_rule_matrix_test`. The inventory is seed-stable. The walk line logs the live tally (export, inventory, nometa, reset, write-lands, storage touch), and the checkers assert against configuration-derived totals. Write-lands is the full-mask registers (scratch-cold, scratch-warm, `SEP_CPU_CTRL`) plus the inbound START/END pairs under the wrap model. Storage touch is every admitted side-effect-free register. `TOUCH_BLOCKS` is the anti-vacuity list (AES/HMAC/KMAC/OTBN/DMA/SPI/WDT and both mailboxes); the sweep fails if any of those nine IPs stops offering a candidate. `WDT_TIMER` threshold registers return the write on `clk_i` and stay busy until `prim_reg_cdc` finishes on `clk_wdt_i`. The eight-core-period `clk_wdt` lets that handshake retire inside the AXI timeout. The compare is the written value.

*Evidence*: each register's write leg logs a failure under CHK-WRITE-LANDS, CHK-RO or CHK-RESERVED, or under `CHK-WRITE` when an inbound START/END readback misses the same-beat wrap model (part of CHK-WRITE-LANDS). The test then stops with one `CHK-WRITE FAIL` summary that counts the failing registers. The PASS records are `CHK-WRITE-LANDS`, `CHK-RO` and `CHK-RESERVED`.

'''''

[[sep_fabric_deadspace_decode_test]]
===== 2.10 `sep_fabric_deadspace_decode_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: Fabric and remap

*Run mode*: `no_cpu`, `+skip_fuse_sense`

*Source Module*: `sep_fabric_deadspace_decode_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip

*Randomization*: RANDCFG — the twelve directed wrap offsets, four directed ABR probes and six directed TRNG-window probes on every seed, plus two seed-selected dead offsets per block window.

*Objective*: Negative control on intra-block dead space. Each block owns an address window and populates only part of it; an access past the allocated size owns no register and must be refused. Window ends come from `hw/sys/sep/doc/memory_map.adoc`, which states the rule: the fabric refuses an address past the extent a unit allocates, and such an access never reaches a unit. Landing on a live register instead is a hard failure. Bursts are graded in the crypto region only: `hw/sys/sep/doc/crypto.adoc` ("Single-Beat Access Only") answers every beat of a burst there DECERR, and no beat reaches an accelerator. A burst into any other register region is outside the specification (`hw/sys/sep/doc/memory_map.adoc`, "Single-Beat Register Access") and is not graded. The TRNG window, forwarded whole to an adopter endpoint and terminated in the reference integration, must refuse every access, alias no neighbouring ESRC register, and answer the code `memory_map.adoc` states for a window with no external TRNG: DECERR on a read and on a write.

*Test Coverage*: Dead-space accesses are refused and do not alias live register data or state.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Build the seeded probe set. Require every watched window to supply its two seeded dead-offset probes (CHK-DEADSPACE-RAND). Bring up in `no_cpu`.
. Snapshot each watched window's registers twice. Require every watched register to answer OKAY and at least one register to be armed for the change compare (CHK-WINDOW-LIVE).
. Issue every directed anchor and seeded probe. A refusal that still writes the register is a failure, so every probe reads back the window's live registers as well as the response (CHK-DEADSPACE-REFUSE, CHK-DEADSPACE-NO-ALIAS).
. In the ABR window, probe every seed at the first word past the register map (read and write), at `error_intr_en_r` with offset bit 14 set, and at the last word of the window.
. In the TRNG window, read and write the first, middle and last word every seed, plus two seeded offsets. Use the neighbouring ESRC register set as this window's no-alias snapshot, which an access that drops address bit 12 reaches (CHK-TRNG-UNOWNED).
. In each crypto-region window (OTBN through ABR in the generated memory map: aes, otbn, abr, csrng, edn, entropy_src, km_mailbox, lifecycle and trng), issue a four-beat INCR read burst and, where the window takes writes, a four-beat INCR write burst. Start the burst two words before the extent where a legal burst can cross it, and at the window base otherwise. secure_dma, wdt_timer and spi_controller lie outside the crypto region and get no burst (CHK-DEADSPACE-BURST, CHK-DEADSPACE-BEAT).

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-DEADSPACE-RAND
|Stimulus precondition. Each watched window supplies its full quota of two seed-selected, word-aligned dead-offset probes. No two probes, and no probe and directed anchor, share both address and operation. A window with no dead span counts as zero of two. The probe count is the random-coverage claim, so a short window fails the leaf before bring-up and is not absorbed into a smaller probe set. The checker has no PASS line; the `deadspace config` line records the probe count per seed.
|CHK-WINDOW-LIVE
|Each of the twelve watched windows (secure_dma, wdt_timer, aes, otbn, abr, csrng, edn, entropy_src, km_mailbox, lifecycle, spi_controller, and trng against the neighbouring entropy_src registers) has a non-empty register snapshot and at least one register armed for the change compare, so both no-alias compares can fail. Every watched register answers both snapshot reads OKAY; a register that a snapshot read refuses or times out on is left out of the change compare, so the checker fails and names each one. A register that reads two different values is self-changing and is left out of the snapshot. The line reports watched, refused or timed out, self-changing, readable, compared and armed separately. The per-probe change compare drops hardware-updating addresses. Armed counts the compared registers with at least one software read-write field in the generated IP-XACT (`hw/sys/sep/regs/gen/ipxact/sep.xml`): a `sw = r` field has no bus write path and a write-only field reads back nothing, so only an armed register can show a stored write. Armed is the falsifiable count, and a window with none armed fails.
|CHK-DEADSPACE-REFUSE
|Every probed address past the allocated size is refused (not OKAY), including the directed wrap anchors (KM `0x10920ff8`, DMA `0x108008a8`). A single accepted probe fails the checker; there is no tolerated count.
|CHK-DEADSPACE-NO-ALIAS
|No allocated register in that window changes across a probe, the directed wrap anchors included, and a read of a dead offset never returns a live register's value. The alias compare is not gated on the response: `memory_map.adoc` says an access past a unit's extent never reaches a unit, so a refused read that still hands back live data has reached it. Inside the extent the same passage grounds non-aliasing in exact-match register decode rather than in refusal, so an accepted read that returns a live value is the failure there. A single aliased probe fails the checker.
|CHK-DEADSPACE-BURST
|In every crypto-region window, no beat of the read burst returns the value of a register in the window snapshot, the write burst answers DECERR, and no armed register moves. A burst that times out fails. At least one window must answer a single beat at a burst address OKAY, so the refusal is the burst rule and not a dead address.
|CHK-DEADSPACE-BEAT
|In every crypto-region window, the bus monitor's per-beat `RRESP` vector for the read burst is DECERR on every beat, inside the extent as well as past it. A missing vector, or one whose length does not match the beats issued, fails, since unrelated traffic on the bus would lengthen it. A write burst has one `BRESP`, so it is graded under CHK-DEADSPACE-BURST.
|CHK-TRNG-UNOWNED
|Every TRNG-window probe is refused (never OKAY, no timeout), a refused read returns no neighbouring ESRC register value, and no ESRC register moves; at least one read and one write are refused. The reference integration connects no external TRNG, so no offset owns a register. For that case `hw/sys/sep/doc/memory_map.adoc` states the code: the window ends in a DECERR slave, so every single-beat read and write answers DECERR. Each probe is graded against that code, and the `TRNG-UNOWNED-RESP` lines log each one. The window lies in the crypto region, so its burst leg, issued at the window base, is graded under CHK-DEADSPACE-BEAT and CHK-DEADSPACE-BURST.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope*: The TRNG window (`TRNG_REG_MAP_BASE_ADDR` up to the lifecycle base) allocates no SEP register.

*Evidence*: each probe that is not refused, or that moves a live register, logs `CHK-DEADSPACE FAIL [anchor]` or `[rand]` with the reason. The probe loop then fails once with a `CHK-DEADSPACE-REFUSE FAIL` summary that counts the accepted and the aliasing probes, which covers CHK-DEADSPACE-REFUSE and CHK-DEADSPACE-NO-ALIAS.

'''''

[[sep_fabric_local_alias_datapath_test]]
===== 2.11 `sep_fabric_local_alias_datapath_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: Fabric and remap

*Run mode*: `no_cpu`, `+skip_fuse_sense`

*Source Module*: `sep_fabric_local_alias_datapath_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip

*Randomization*: RANDCFG — region and source page from the run seed; the dest is `CLOCK_GATE_CTRL` so the offset is determined and non-vacuous.

*Objective*: Scope is the sixteen programmable local-master regions ahead of the system-peripherals routing demux (`hw/sys/sep/doc/fabric.adoc`, "Address Remapping").

*Test Coverage*: Local-alias remap datapath, not the CSR bank alone.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Bring up in `no_cpu`. Read the seeded source page through the identity path.
. Write the marker to `CLOCK_GATE_CTRL` and read it back. Require the source page's value to differ from the marker.
. Park `CLOCK_GATE_CTRL` at the inverse of the marker and read it back.
. Program the seeded region and write the marker through the alias; the identity `CLOCK_GATE_CTRL` readback must move to the marker (CHK-OFFSET-WRITE). Log the `ext_debug_bus_o` lane.
. Read through the alias and require the marker. Log the `ext_debug_bus_o` lane. Then change `CLOCK_GATE_CTRL` at its identity address only; the aliased read must follow it (CHK-OFFSET).
. Write the marker to `CLOCK_GATE_CTRL`. Reprogram the same region with bounds and offset live and only the valid bit clear, and read the source address. Require the source page's own value, not the marker (CHK-VALID-GATE).

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-OFFSET-WRITE
|An aliased write of the marker moves the identity `CLOCK_GATE_CTRL` readback from a parked value (the marker with every implemented bit inverted) to the marker. A write that lands on any other address leaves the parked value.
|CHK-OFFSET
|A programmed region's live read equals input plus the programmed offset. The aliased read returns the marker, then returns the parked value after a write to `CLOCK_GATE_CTRL` at its identity address only. The source page's own value differs from the marker, so a read that passes through, or lands on any other register, cannot match both.
|CHK-VALID-GATE
|The region valid bit gates the remap: `hw/sys/sep/doc/fabric.adoc` ("Address Remapping") states that an invalid entry behaves as a transparent pass-through. The same window is reprogrammed with bounds and offset live and only the enable clear, and the beat must then read the value at the address the master issued rather than the remapped destination. Programming the window first is what separates a working gate from an address that was never in range, and the vacuity guard on `CHK-OFFSET` has already shown the two values differ. The cacheable flag that `fabric.adoc` lists per region is not checked: this bench has no observable on the outbound cache bits.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope*: This entry is distinct from the CPU high-alias window (`sep_cpu_ifu_lsu_alias_remap_matrix_test`). CSR programming stays on `sep_fabric_remap_filter_csr_bank_test`. Local-master `REGION_ATTRS` has `valid` and `cacheable`. Cacheable overrides AXI `cache` on a hit; this vehicle does not observe that field. The `ext_debug_bus_o` lane is information only. No RDL, generated header or document defines its layout, so no checker decodes it.

'''''

[[sep_fabric_local_alias_offset_walk_test]]
===== 2.12 `sep_fabric_local_alias_offset_walk_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: Fabric and remap

*Run mode*: `no_cpu` (`lsu_stub_all_live`), `+skip_fuse_sense`

*Source Module*: `sep_fabric_local_alias_offset_walk_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (CPU-LSU master); `tb/sep_outbound_mbx.sv` (outbound responder: OKAY at any address)

*Randomization*: RANDCFG — the seed selects every target, bound and the staged word. Every region runs at each seed; one seed per regression, because the bit coverage does not depend on the seed.

*Objective*: Every local-master alias region matches and translates with all 56 address bits on live traffic.

*Test Coverage*: All 16 alias regions (`alias_remap.rdl` start_addr[55:12], end_addr[55:12], offset[55:12], valid[63]). The source beat is a staged START_ADDR low word of the last inbound-filter entry, which stays disabled. A hit targets an address at or above `0x1_0000_0000`, which the routing demux sends (`hw/sys/sep/doc/fabric.adoc`) to the SMU path and through the block-by-default outbound filter.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Stage the source word from the CPU-LSU master.
. For each region: with offset O, then ~O, the region starts at the source page and ends at E, then ~E (both above the page); one outbound entry admits only the granule at the predicted target. Read the source beat and the next beat.
. Clear valid with the hit bounds: read the source beat.
. Program bounds starting at S, then ~S (both above the source page): read the source beat.
. Program the region to start and end at the source page (END is non-inclusive), with offset ~O and valid set: read the source beat.
. Restore the region and the entry to reset.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-ALIAS-WALK-READBACK
|Every alias START/END/ATTRS and outbound-filter write reads back as programmed (56 bits).
|CHK-ALIAS-WALK-HIT
|The translated beat answers OKAY in the one granule at `{offset[55:12] + addr[55:12], addr[11:0]}` and DECERR one granule up, so the alias adder produced exactly that 56-bit address.
|CHK-ALIAS-WALK-MISS
|A region that starts above the source page does not translate, and a valid region that starts at the source page and ends there does not translate: OKAY with the staged word. The END leg keeps the outbound entry open at the ~O target, so a translated beat would return the outbound responder's data, not the staged word; it fails an END compare that is ignored or stuck true.
|CHK-ALIAS-WALK-VALID
|With valid clear the region does not translate: OKAY with the staged word.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

'''''

[[sep_axi_order_sweep_test]]
===== 2.13 `sep_axi_order_sweep_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: Fabric and remap

*Run mode*: `no_cpu`, `+skip_fuse_sense`

*Source Module*: `sep_axi_order_sweep_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip

*Randomization*: RANDCFG — every (register x ordering) cell runs on every seed, and every (ordering x size) cell with it. The seed varies the staged data, the channel separation and the response backpressure, never which cell runs.

*Objective*: AXI write address and write data are independent channels with no ordering requirement between them (IHI 0022 A3.3), so AW-first, W-first and same-cycle are all legal stimulus and each must leave the written value in the addressed register without displacing its neighbour. The ordering is driven by holding the trailing channel until the leading one asserts VALID, and the ordering each cell actually presented is read off the bus and asserted against what was requested. The orderings are presented at the s_axi fabric ingress, and the contract is end to end: each one must land at every write-safe register of every swept block, not only at one scratch word. The crossbar in front of the block adapters can re-serialize a write (on the CSRNG path it delivers W one cycle after AW whatever the master presents, see <<sep_drbg_axil_adapter_port_arbitration_test>>), so this test does not claim that each adapter sees all three orderings; W-first and same-cycle orderings at an adapter port are covered for the DRBG lane adapter module by `sep_drbg_axil_adapter_port_arbitration_test`. The sweep configures all three orderings at every write-safe register and crosses them with the 1/2/4-byte sizes on the scratch words, where a narrow write has no side effect. The narrow cells compare the whole software-usable word against the AXI lane rule; `sep_axi_strobe_window_test` owns the same rule at default timing.

*Test Coverage*: AW/W channel ordering at every write-safe register, from the LSU splice.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Take the register inventory and the exclusion reasons from `sep_reg_bit_bash_seq`: `write_reason() is None` for the no-side-effect blocks, plus `touch_reason() is None` restricted to `TOUCH_BLOCKS` for plain RW storage inside the other major IPs.
. Drop the blocks where the access itself would decide the result. `WDT_TIMER` is that block: `clk_wdt_i` is 5 µs and the AXI timeout is 50 µs, about ten watchdog edges, so whether a `prim_reg_cdc` round trip fits depends on the phase the access arrives on. A probe there measures CDC latency against the timeout rather than channel delivery. `sep_reg_bit_bash_rand_test` covers that block's storage, and it runs `clk_wdt` at eight core periods so the handshake retires inside the timeout.
. Prime the register with the complement under its write mask at default timing, and read it back, so a write that never lands reads as the prime rather than looking plausible.
. Apply the cell's timing profile through the VIP master (`AxiTimingProfile`, `ocah_axi_master_config`) to hold AW or W back, write the staged value, and read it back at default timing so the compare tests the write and not the read.
. Read a second register in the same block, write it back with one software-usable bit flipped at default timing, read it again, then re-read the swept register. Deriving the value from the current contents keeps a write that never arrived from reading back correct.
. A shadowed register commits on the second identical write. The profile arms a one-shot release, so it shapes the first write only and the committing second write goes out same-cycle. The ordering under test is the one the register sees first; the commit itself is not an ordered access.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-ORDER-LAND
|The written value is in the register after the ordering write. An adapter that latches a pending-write flag on AW accept and reads that flag in the same cycle the W arrives answers OKAY while dropping the data, so the compare is on the readback, never on the response. Every cell must produce a data compare; a cell that could not run is named with its reason, and the count then fails the test rather than reading as a full sweep.
|CHK-ORDER-DISPLACE
|The next write in the block lands on the register it addresses, and the swept register does not change when its neighbour is written. A pending flag left set by the ordering commits the following W handshake to the wrong target, which CHK-ORDER-LAND cannot see: it reads the register that was written, not the neighbour that was corrupted. The follow-on value is derived from what the neighbour currently holds and flips one software-usable bit, so a write that never arrived cannot read back correct. A refused follow-on write or readback fails this checker rather than being recorded as a skip. A cell in a single-register block offers no neighbour to write, so the required witness count is the number of cells that have one.
|CHK-ORDER-XSIZE
|All nine (ordering x size) cells produced a data compare, so the write lands at every transfer size and not only at the bus width.
|CHK-ORDER-STIM
|Each cell presented the ordering it requested, read off the AW/W valid assertions rather than taken from the configured profile. Asserted per cell. The slave's handshake is logged separately and is allowed to coincide: a slave that holds WREADY until AW answers a W-first presentation same-cycle, which is its own contract, not a stimulus failure.
|CHK-COVERAGE
|The cell count is asserted against a floor and against the cells the config presented, then the per-ordering tally, the blocks reached, the (ordering x size) grid and the witness count are logged. Every skipped register is counted under its reason on the configuration line the test logs first. A silent skip would let a shrinking sweep keep reporting PASS.
|CHK-RANDCFG
|The cell count for the seed is logged against the configured total, so a shrunken sweep is visible.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

'''''

[[sep_axi_order_sweep_m_axi_test]]
===== 2.14 `sep_axi_order_sweep_m_axi_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: Fabric and remap

*Run mode*: `no_cpu`, `+skip_fuse_sense`

*Source Module*: `sep_axi_order_sweep_m_axi_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip

*Randomization*: RANDCFG -- every (register x ordering) cell runs on every seed. The seed varies the staged data, the channel separation and the response backpressure, never which cell runs.

*Objective*: The same ordering contract as `sep_axi_order_sweep_test`, driven from the SMN inbound master instead of the CPU-LSU splice. Both masters reach the same IP block adapters, so an adapter that mishandles a channel ordering has to be caught from either. This path also grants a W-first handshake: the CPU-LSU register adapters hold WREADY until AW, so a W-first presentation is accepted same-cycle there, while the inbound path accepts W before AW.

*Test Coverage*: AW/W channel ordering at every write-safe register, from the SMN inbound master.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Assert the cell floor when the walk completes, and require the compare count to equal the cells the config presented, so a walk shrunk by a map or routing change fails rather than reporting a clean pass over fewer cells.
. Program the inbound filter from the CPU-LSU side: the filter denies by default, so five allow windows are opened over the swept extent. The window bounds follow `hw/ip/axi_filter/doc/index.adoc` (Address Range Granule): with `allow_burst = 0` the granule is the data bus width, address bits [2:0] are ignored, `START_ADDR` widens down and `END_ADDR` widens up.
. Walk the cells exactly as the CPU-LSU sweep does.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-ORDER-LAND
|The written value is in the register after the ordering write, compared on the readback rather than on the response, so an adapter that answers OKAY while dropping the data fails. Every cell must produce a data compare; a cell that could not run is named with its reason and the count then fails the test.
|CHK-ORDER-DISPLACE
|The next write in the block lands on the register it addresses and the swept register does not change when its neighbour is written, so a pending flag left set by the ordering cannot commit the following W handshake to the wrong target. The follow-on value is derived from what the neighbour currently holds with one software-usable bit flipped. The required witness count is the number of cells whose block offers a neighbour.
|CHK-ORDER-XSIZE
|All nine (ordering x size) cells produced a data compare, so the write lands at every transfer size and not only at the bus width.
|CHK-ORDER-STIM
|Each cell presented the ordering it requested, read off the AW/W valid assertions rather than taken from the configured profile. On this path a W-first presentation is accepted before AW, which is the inbound adapter's own contract and is logged rather than treated as a stimulus failure — the opposite of the CPU-LSU register adapters, which hold WREADY until AW and answer W-first same-cycle.
|CHK-COVERAGE
|The cell count is asserted against a floor and against the cells the config presented, then the per-ordering tally, the blocks reached, the (ordering x size) grid and the witness count are logged. Every skipped register is counted under its reason on the configuration line the test logs first, including the sixteen `INBOUND_FILTER_CTRL` blocks this path cannot sweep. A silent skip would let a shrinking sweep keep reporting PASS.
|CHK-RANDCFG
|The cell count for the seed is logged against the configured total, so a shrunken sweep is visible.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope*: the sixteen `INBOUND_FILTER_CTRL` blocks are not swept here and are counted in the skip tally. Those CSRs are the filter the access is passing through, so writing one mid-walk would reprogram the path under the test and measure filter behaviour rather than adapter ordering. They are swept in full on `sep_axi_order_sweep_test`, whose bus has no inbound filter. No allow window covers the filter CSR bank, so the ownership hole `sep_fabric_inbound_filter_rule_matrix_test` asserts stays shut.

'''''

[[sep_drbg_axil_adapter_port_arbitration_test]]
===== 2.15 `sep_drbg_axil_adapter_port_arbitration_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: Fabric and remap

*Run mode*: `no_cpu`, `+skip_fuse_sense`

*Source Module*: `sep_drbg_axil_adapter_port_arbitration_test`

*BFM / Model*: TB-instantiated `drbg_axil64_lane_adapter` (`u_tbadp_vehicle` in `tb/tb_top.sv`), driven pin-level from cocotb

*Randomization*: none. The three orderings are fixed and all three run on every seed; the contract is a cycle alignment, not a data pattern.

*Objective*: AW, W and AR are independent AXI channels (IHI 0022 A3.3). In idle the adapter accepts each write half independently until that half is pending, and accepts a read only when neither write half is pending. This leaf presents all three legal orderings at the port and requires both accesses to retire under each.

*Test Coverage*: All three legal AW/W/AR orderings at the TB-owned adapter port.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Read the live CSRNG lane and require OKAY before the vehicle is touched (`CHK-PORT-ANCHOR`).
. On the vehicle, retire a lone write, a lone read, and an AW-then-W gap with no AR, each answering OKAY (`CHK-PORT-CONTROL`).
. Present each of the three legal AW/W/AR orderings at the vehicle port. Confirm the port presented the named ordering and, in the two gapped-write cells, that a cycle had AR valid with one write half handshaken and the other pending (`CHK-PORT-STIM`). Confirm both accesses retire in bound (`CHK-PORT-PROGRESS`). In every cell, require that no AR handshakes while a write half is pending, and in the two gapped-write cells that AR handshakes only after both write halves (`CHK-PORT-ARBITRATION`). Reset the vehicle between cells.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,4",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract

|CHK-PORT-ANCHOR
|A plain read of the live CSRNG lane answers OKAY before the vehicle is touched. The vehicle is a TB-owned instance, so without this the leaf could report a pass against a DUT that never left reset; it also puts a transaction through the AXI agent, which the scoreboard requires as positive evidence before it will allow a pass at all.

|CHK-PORT-CONTROL
|Three legs, all required to retire AND to answer OKAY, before any overlap cell runs. A lone write and a lone read show the vehicle and the AXI-Lite-32 responder behind the adapter are alive at all -- without them a broken driver would report every ordering as stalled and imitate the defect exactly. A third leg drives AW and then W four cycles later with no AR, the same separation the `aw-then-ar` and `w-then-ar` cells use, so the separation itself is excluded as the cause of their stall by observation rather than by reading the design under test. The response code carries the other half: an access the adapter rejects as unsupported is answered SLVERR straight out of `ST_IDLE` with nothing forwarded and retires just as promptly, so OKAY is what shows the forwarding leg is alive, and OKAY at the 64-bit port cannot be produced without the downstream handshake. The access itself is AMBA-legal by construction -- aligned, with the byte-lane strobe its address selects (IHI 0022), computed by `sep_spec_tables.axi_lane_strobe` -- so an adapter whose supported-access rule disagreed with the protocol answers this stimulus for itself rather than selecting it.

|CHK-PORT-STIM
|The ordering the port actually presented, read off `tbadp_chan_o` rather than taken from the offsets requested. In `aw-then-ar` and `w-then-ar` the cell must also reach the half-committed state the arbitration row grades: a cycle with AR valid, one write half handshaken and the other pending. That needs the two write halves to handshake in different cycles and AR to be valid by the second. A cell that misses either is a stimulus failure and is reported as one, never scored as coverage -- a cell that did not overlap says nothing about the arbitration in either direction.

|CHK-PORT-PROGRESS
|Both accesses retire: BVALID and RVALID are both seen within a bounded cycle count, and both responses are OKAY. The bound also records the longest run of held-valids-with-every-ready-low, so a hang that `ASSERT_KNOWN` would miss (a stable `1'b0` is not X) still fails the leaf.
|CHK-PORT-ARBITRATION
|In every ordering, no AR handshake falls after one write-half handshake and at or before the other, so no read is accepted while a write half is pending. In `aw-then-ar` and `w-then-ar`, where AR arrives while the leading half is pending, the AR handshake occurs strictly after both AW and W handshakes. In `all-same-cycle` all three may handshake together from idle. Logging the cycles without comparing them is not evidence.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope*: the MODULE's arbitration, not the SEP integration. The DUT's own lane adapters sit behind the crossbar, which delivers W one cycle after AW and re-serializes every write to that order whatever a master presents -- `CHK-CONCURRENT-CAL` on the two fabric-driven leaves measures the gap at both ends and reports it as fabric-introduced. A same-cycle AW/W/AR presentation and a W-before-AW presentation are therefore not producible at a DUT adapter port from the fabric side, which is why this vehicle exists. It is a second instance of the same RTL module with its own reset and no fabric in front of it: every legal ordering is presentable to the cycle, and a wedged cell is cleared without resetting the DUT, so the three verdicts are independent. It claims nothing about the integration; the two leaves that follow own that half.

*Not claimed*: the SEP integration. That a fabric master can present the one ordering the fabric can produce is proven separately.

'''''

[[sep_drbg_axil_adapter_refusal_test]]
===== 2.16 `sep_drbg_axil_adapter_refusal_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: Fabric and remap

*Run mode*: `no_cpu`, `+skip_fuse_sense`

*Source Module*: `sep_drbg_axil_adapter_refusal_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip on s_axi for the DUT's CSRNG and EDN lane adapters, with each adapter's AXI-Lite-64 input handshakes observed on `drbg_csrng_axil_chan_o` / `drbg_edn_axil_chan_o` and its AXI-Lite-32 request on `drbg_csrng_fwd_o` / `drbg_edn_fwd_o`; TB-instantiated `drbg_axil64_lane_adapter` (`u_tbadp_vehicle` in `tb/tb_top.sv`) driven pin-level from cocotb, with its AXI-Lite-32 request observed on `tbadp_fwd_o`

*Randomization*: RANDCFG -- per DUT lane, `SepSeededRng(seed)` picks the byte offset of the misaligned read (1, 2 or 3), the width of the narrow write (1 or 2 bytes), and the value that write carries (any implemented `INTR_ENABLE` pattern that differs from the register's value). The vehicle cells are fixed and all run on every seed.

*Objective*: The supported-access rule of `drbg_axil64_lane_adapter` as `hw/ip/drbg/doc/architecture.adoc` ("Bus Protocol Adaptation") states it: the adapter forwards only aligned single-lane accesses with WSTRB `0x0F` or `0xF0`, selects the 32-bit data lane by address bit 2, and answers every other access AXI SLVERR with no downstream request. The graded refusals are a write whose strobe is not `0x0F` or `0xF0` and a write whose address is not 4-byte aligned. The refusal must leave the adapter able to serve the next supported access, and a supported read returns the downstream word in the lane address bit 2 selects.
Three rules are in the adapter RTL header only: a read must be 4-byte aligned, a legal strobe must match address bit 2, and a supported read returns zero in the other lane. The cells that depend on them -- the misaligned reads on the DUT lanes and the vehicle, and the two vehicle wrong-lane strobes -- are driven on every seed for coverage, and the other lane of each vehicle control read is recorded. Their response, data and forward probe are logged at info level as not graded, and they do not enter the verdict: no specification states those rules.

*Test Coverage*: Graded: the refused narrow write on both DUT lane adapters (CSRNG, EDN), and on the vehicle a full 64-bit beat, a byte strobe, a halfword strobe, a zero strobe and a misaligned write address in each lane; the supported access after every vehicle cell. Driven only: the misaligned read on both DUT lanes, and on the vehicle a misaligned read at each byte offset of each lane and a wrong-lane strobe for each lane.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Bring up `no_cpu`. Require the CSRNG and EDN bits of `PERIPH_BUS_ERR_STATUS` clear and read each block's `INTR_ENABLE` (`CHK-REFUSE-ANCHOR`).
. Per DUT lane, write the seeded value to `INTR_ENABLE` as a 1- or 2-byte transfer. Confirm the W strobe presented on s_axi (`CHK-REFUSE-STIM`). Require SLVERR, AW and W handshakes at the lane adapter's AXI-Lite-64 input, the forward probe low on every cycle, `INTR_ENABLE` unchanged and the status bit clear (`CHK-REFUSE-DUT-WRITE`).
. Write the same value as a supported 32-bit write and read it back, each seen on the forward probe, then restore the original value and read it back (`CHK-REFUSE-DUT-CONTROL`).
. Read one byte at the seeded misaligned offset into `INTR_ENABLE`, last on the lane so it cannot change a graded check. Confirm the AR presented on s_axi (`CHK-REFUSE-STIM`). Log the response, the AXI-Lite-64 input handshakes, the forward probe and the status bit as not graded; a read that does not complete still fails the run.
. Release the vehicle. Present the driven-only cells first and log each response and forward probe as not graded. For each graded refused cell, require SLVERR with no AXI-Lite-32 request on any cycle (`CHK-REFUSE-VEH`). After every cell, without a vehicle reset, present the supported access of the same kind on the same lane and require OKAY, a forwarded request, and for a read the responder's word in the lane address bit 2 selects (`CHK-REFUSE-VEH-CONTROL`); log the other lane of the read as not graded.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,4",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract

|CHK-REFUSE-ANCHOR
|The CSRNG and EDN bits of `PERIPH_BUS_ERR_STATUS` are clear before any refused access, and `INTR_ENABLE` reads OKAY on both blocks. A bit already set would make the "stays clear" half of every DUT check vacuous.

|CHK-REFUSE-STIM
|s_axi presented the access the cell names: a W beat whose strobe is the one AMBA assigns to the narrow write at that address (`sep_spec_tables.axi_lane_strobe`), and ARADDR at the misaligned byte with ARLEN 0 and ARSIZE 0 for the driven-only read. A mismatch is a stimulus miss, reported as one.

|CHK-REFUSE-DUT-WRITE
|The narrow write answers SLVERR, and `drbg_<lane>_axil_chan_o` shows AW and W handshakes at the adapter's AXI-Lite-64 input with no X/Z cycle, so the adapter accepted the beat it refused. The forward probe is low and not X/Z on every cycle of the access, `INTR_ENABLE` still holds its value under the block's implemented mask, and the lane's status bit is still clear. The written value differs from the register's in an implemented bit, so a forwarded write is visible.

|CHK-REFUSE-DUT-CONTROL
|A supported 32-bit write of the same value answers OKAY and is seen as a write on the forward probe, its read-back is seen as a read and returns the value, and the restore write reads back. This shows the probe sees a forwarded access and the value the refused write carried lands when the adapter forwards it, so "probe low" and "unchanged" in the two checks above can fail, and that the adapter serves a supported access after a refusal.

|CHK-REFUSE-VEH
|Every graded refused vehicle cell (a strobe that is not `0x0F` or `0xF0`, or a misaligned write address) retires with SLVERR, and `tbadp_fwd_o` is low and not X/Z on every cycle from presentation to four cycles after the response. The driven-only cells are not part of this check.

|CHK-REFUSE-VEH-CONTROL
|After each vehicle cell, graded or driven only, with no vehicle reset, the supported access of the same kind on the same lane answers OKAY and is seen on `tbadp_fwd_o`, which shows the probe can see a forwarded request. A read returns the responder's word in the lane address bit 2 selects. The other lane is logged, not graded.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope*: the DUT half grades the adapter as software reaches it. It grades "nothing forwarded" on the adapter's AXI-Lite-32 request into its TL-UL bridge (`drbg_csrng_fwd_o` / `drbg_edn_fwd_o`, an observation-only probe), which must be low and known on every cycle of the refused access, and through what the DUT shows: the register keeps its value, and the lane's `PERIPH_BUS_ERR_STATUS` bit, which is the bridge's sticky TL-UL error (`hw/sys/sep/doc/crypto.adoc`, "Crypto Register-Bridge Faults"), stays clear. No legal access sets the CSRNG or EDN bit in this build: their crypto-demux windows end at the last register, so an unmapped offset answers DECERR before it reaches the bridge. The status bit is therefore a second consequence only; the probe is the observable that `CHK-REFUSE-DUT-CONTROL` shows live. One AXI master transfer has a strobe AMBA derives from its address and size, so a wrong-lane strobe, a full-beat 32-bit write, a zero strobe and a misaligned write address with a lane strobe are not presentable at a DUT port; the vehicle presents them.

*Not claimed*: the `unsupported_access_pulse_o` output. It has no CSR and no SEP consumer outside assertions. The adapter's response to a misaligned read or a wrong-lane strobe, and the other lane of a read: no specification states those rules.

'''''

[[sep_drbg_axil_concurrent_csrng_aw_then_ar_test]]
===== 2.17 `sep_drbg_axil_concurrent_csrng_aw_then_ar_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: Fabric and remap

*Run mode*: `no_cpu`, `+skip_fuse_sense`

*Source Module*: `sep_drbg_axil_concurrent_csrng_aw_then_ar_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip

*Randomization*: RANDCFG -- the seed varies the staged register value only. The channel placement is measured per build, not drawn, so a seed replays the cell without pinning it to a latency the fabric may have changed.

*Objective*: The same arbitration contract as <<sep_drbg_axil_adapter_port_arbitration_test>>, but on the DUT's own CSRNG lane adapter and reached the way software reaches it. The two lane adapters sit on the CSRNG and EDN control buses (`drbg.sv` `u_csrng_axil_adapter` / `u_edn_axil_adapter`, fed from `sep_crypto.sv` `csrng_axil` / `edn_axil`), which is the path every SEP-level CSRNG and EDN register access already takes. The cell writes the block's `INTR_ENABLE` and reads its `INTR_STATE` concurrently, so both accesses are behind the same adapter.

*Test Coverage*: One AW-then-AR overlap at the DUT CSRNG lane adapter.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Measure the CSRNG `INTR_ENABLE` writable width, then a lone write and a lone read, and place the AW-then-AR overlap from the measured crossbar latencies (`CHK-CONCURRENT-CAL`).
. Present that overlap on `INTR_ENABLE` / `INTR_STATE`. Confirm the CSRNG adapter port (`drbg_csrng_axil_chan_o`) saw the named ordering (`CHK-CONCURRENT-STIM`).
. Require AR to handshake at the adapter port only after both AW and W have handshaken (`CHK-CONCURRENT-ARB`).
. Require both accesses to retire and the write to land (`CHK-CONCURRENT-LAND`).

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,4",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract

|CHK-CONCURRENT-CAL
|The register's writable width is measured, not assumed: all-ones is written and read back, and the seed's pattern is narrowed to the bits that stick. The two blocks implement different interrupt counts, so a hardcoded width is wrong for one of them and a non-existent bit reads back 0 -- indistinguishable from a dropped write. A lone write and a lone read then measure when AW, W and AR arrive at the adapter port through the crossbar. The overlap is placed from those measured latencies: a placement the measured latency cannot reach is reported unreachable rather than fired blind. The same measurement records the AW-to-W gap at the master and at the port and states which side introduced it. Plain untimed traffic already puts AW and AR in the same cycle whenever a store and a load are in flight together.

|CHK-CONCURRENT-STIM
|The ordering the ADAPTER PORT presented, read off `drbg_csrng_axil_chan_o`, not the ordering requested and not the presentation at `s_axi`. The crossbar restaggers the channels, so a presentation at the TB master is not evidence of one at the arbitration point. The leaf is covered only when that presentation is the named ordering. A different overlap, or a cell that missed its overlap, is reported unreachable and does not count as this leaf.

|CHK-CONCURRENT-ARB
|The arbitration rule, read off the handshakes at `drbg_csrng_axil_chan_o`: AR handshakes only after both AW and W have handshaken, so the adapter accepted no read while a write half was pending.

|CHK-CONCURRENT-LAND
|Both accesses retire and the write lands. The check is a bounded timeout plus a data compare against a complement prime; the prime makes a dropped write read back as the prime rather than as a plausible value. The check also records the longest run of held-valids-with-every-ready-low, so a hang that `ASSERT_KNOWN` would miss still fails the leaf.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope*: one lane, one ordering, one leaf. A stalled adapter cannot be recovered inside a simulation -- the port stays held and the master stays stuck on it -- so a second cell after a wedge would measure the wedge rather than itself.

*Not claimed*: the other two orderings. A true same-cycle AW+W+AR presentation and a W-before-AW presentation are not reachable at a DUT adapter port from a SEP master, for the reason `CHK-CONCURRENT-CAL` measures. They are graded on <<sep_drbg_axil_adapter_port_arbitration_test>> instead, at the module's port. `CHK-CONCURRENT-CAL` logs the measured arrivals.

'''''

[[sep_drbg_axil_concurrent_edn_aw_then_ar_test]]
===== 2.18 `sep_drbg_axil_concurrent_edn_aw_then_ar_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: Fabric and remap

*Run mode*: `no_cpu`, `+skip_fuse_sense`

*Source Module*: `sep_drbg_axil_concurrent_edn_aw_then_ar_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip

*Randomization*: RANDCFG -- as <<sep_drbg_axil_concurrent_csrng_aw_then_ar_test>>.

*Objective*: The same contract on the second lane adapter, the EDN control path. `drbg.sv` instantiates `drbg_axil64_lane_adapter` twice, so the two lanes are separate hardware and a defect in one instance is not evidence about the other. The checks are those of <<sep_drbg_axil_concurrent_csrng_aw_then_ar_test>>, with the probe on `drbg_edn_axil_chan_o` and the access pair on the EDN block's own registers.

*Test Coverage*: One AW-then-AR overlap at the DUT EDN lane adapter.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Measure the EDN `INTR_ENABLE` writable width, then a lone write and a lone read, and place the AW-then-AR overlap from the measured crossbar latencies (`CHK-CONCURRENT-CAL`).
. Present that overlap on the EDN block's own registers. Confirm the EDN adapter port (`drbg_edn_axil_chan_o`) saw the named ordering (`CHK-CONCURRENT-STIM`).
. Require AR to handshake at the adapter port only after both AW and W have handshaken (`CHK-CONCURRENT-ARB`).
. Require both accesses to retire and the write to land (`CHK-CONCURRENT-LAND`).

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,4",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract

|CHK-CONCURRENT-CAL
|Same contract as <<sep_drbg_axil_concurrent_csrng_aw_then_ar_test>>, on the EDN interrupt registers. The writable width is measured on this block; the lone write and lone read measure arrival at `drbg_edn_axil_chan_o`.

|CHK-CONCURRENT-STIM
|The ordering the EDN adapter port presented, read off `drbg_edn_axil_chan_o`, not the ordering requested and not the presentation at `s_axi`.

|CHK-CONCURRENT-ARB
|Same contract as <<sep_drbg_axil_concurrent_csrng_aw_then_ar_test>>, read off the handshakes at `drbg_edn_axil_chan_o`.

|CHK-CONCURRENT-LAND
|Both accesses retire and the write lands. The stall signature is the same held-valids-with-every-ready-low bound as the CSRNG leaf.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

'''''

[[sep_axi_id_routing_test]]
===== 2.19 `sep_axi_id_routing_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: Fabric and remap

*Run mode*: `no_cpu`, `+skip_fuse_sense`

*Source Module*: `sep_axi_id_routing_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip

*Randomization*: none. The proof is a value compare between an ID and the word
it asked for; a random ID or a random value on either side would remove it.

*Objective*: a response comes back to the request that owns it. The crossbars
prepend the master index to the incoming `AxID` and the demux keeps one
outstanding counter per ID, so the ID field is address-like state on the
response path, and a master matches its responses by it.

*Test Coverage*: the transaction-ID dimension of the SEP slave-port crossbar
path, with several reads outstanding at once on distinct IDs, including the
top ID the port's width allows.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Prime the eight `SCRATCH_COLD` words, each with a value that names its own
word, and read each back sequentially.
. Issue eight reads, one per word, each on its own `AxID`, and hold them all
outstanding together by driving the VIP master sequence directly -- the SEP
AXI sequencer awaits each item to completion, so nothing overlaps through it.
. Require each read to return the value of its own word. A response carrying
another word's value is reported with the word it actually came from.
. Grade separately that the IDs issued covered the whole width of the field,
so a shortened list cannot pass the routing compare silently.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-ID-PRIME
|The eight scratch words are independent storage each holding its own distinct value. Without this a block that aliased every word onto one register would let the routing compare pass for whichever value was written last.
|CHK-ID-ROUTE
|With eight reads outstanding together on eight distinct IDs, each returns the value of its own word. An ID that is mangled, truncated or dropped delivers a read's data to a different outstanding request, and every access still answers OKAY while it happens -- only the value compare sees it.
|CHK-ID-OVERLAP
|All eight reads are outstanding on the bus at once. A bus that retires each read before it accepts the next returns every value correctly whatever it does to the ID, so without this the routing compare passes on a truncated ID field.
|CHK-ID-TOP
|A breadth guard on the stimulus, not a second routing claim: the set of IDs the routing compare was given covered the whole width of the port's ID field. `CHK-ID-ROUTE` only compares the IDs it was handed, so an edit that shortened the list would keep passing over a subset; an ID field carried in too few bits only surfaces as a data mismatch if a read was actually issued on the top ID.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope*: the SEP slave port only, whose `AxID` is three bits wide. The wider
inbound port and write-response (`BID`) routing are not claimed here.

*Anti-vacuity*: the prime leg establishes eight distinct values in eight
independent words before any routing claim is made, so a misrouted response is
distinguishable from a correct one. The concurrency is what gives the fabric
several responses to place: with one access in flight there is one response to
deliver and any routing would look correct. A read that never returns is
reported as such rather than counted as a pass.

'''''

[[sep_axi_strobe_window_test]]
===== 2.20 `sep_axi_strobe_window_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: Fabric and remap

*Run mode*: `no_cpu`, `+skip_fuse_sense`

*Source Module*: `sep_axi_strobe_window_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip
