*Randomization*: RANDCFG — the size and lane axes are walked exhaustively rather than seeded, so every AxSIZE at every legal lane offset runs on every seed and no run can issue zero narrow writes. The seed varies the data.

*Objective*: A write narrower than the bus beat must change only the byte lanes its strobe selects (IHI 0022 A3.4.3), and a memory window must return the data that was written to it. A stage that widens the strobe, or writes the whole beat, changes bytes the master never asked for; only a data compare sees it, because the response is OKAY either way.

*Test Coverage*: Write-strobe windows on the LSU splice.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Prime a scratch word with a known value.
. Issue a write narrower than the bus beat at each legal lane offset for each AxSIZE, and read the whole word back.
. Compare against the AXI lane rule: the addressed lanes take the new data, every other lane keeps the primed value.
. Write and read back the OTBN IMEM and DMEM windows.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-STROBE
|Each narrow write changed only its own byte lanes, at every AxSIZE and every legal offset. The line reports the count, so a run that issued no narrow write cannot read as a pass. The compare is the addressed 32-bit word: the generated SEP C headers contain no 4-byte-adjacent register pair, so a 64-bit beat has no neighbour CSR in bytes 4–7 and a widened strobe has no second register to corrupt.
|CHK-WINDOW-DATA
|Each memory window returned the value written to it. A window behind an SRAM-style TileLink adapter applies the mask on reads, unlike a register behind a register adapter which ignores it, so a bridge driving that read mask from the write strobe returns zeros with a correct response. A window not writable in this configuration is named with its reason. At least one window must have been verified: a walk where none was writable proves nothing and fails.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

'''''

[[sep_axi_partial_lane_read_test]]
===== 2.21 `sep_axi_partial_lane_read_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: Fabric and remap

*Run mode*: `no_cpu`, `+skip_fuse_sense`

*Source Module*: `sep_axi_partial_lane_read_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip

*Randomization*: RANDCFG — `SepAxiPartialLaneReadCfg` is the single source of truth for stimulus and goldens. Required cells walk every seed: all 36 contiguous (offset, length) byte-run slices of a 64-bit word (`8+7+…+1`), all 14 aligned narrow-ARSIZE cells (AxSIZE 0/1/2 at every legal lane offset: `8+4+2`), and the all-zeros / all-ones CSR patterns. The seed varies walk order, SRAM address, the 64-bit word, and extra CSR patterns only.

*Objective*: A read narrower than the 64-bit CPU-LSU beat only obligates the responder to drive the addressed byte lanes: a 32-bit CSR endpoint leaves RDATA[63:32] undriven, and a narrow-ARSIZE beat leaves every non-addressed lane undriven. The VIP master samples the full beat and extracts the addressed bytes, so the value a test receives must be a pure function of the addressed lanes — exact against an independent golden and identical on re-read — regardless of what the undriven lanes carry. `sep_axi_strobe_window_test` owns the write-side lane rule; here the write is trusted and the read extraction is on trial. The contract is pinned through the public VIP read path alone, with no cocotb or cocotbext-axi global state involved.

*Test Coverage*: Partial-lane reads on the LSU splice.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Log the seed, word, addresses and cell counts, and hold the walked counts against the 8-byte-beat floors (36 slices, 14 ARSIZE cells) plus the two required CSR extremes.
. Write a pattern to the 32-bit `SW_DEBUG` CSR, read it back twice as 4-byte reads with a checked read of the non-zero RO `SEP_LOCAL_BASE_ADDR` register between them; repeat for the all-zeros, all-ones and seed-random patterns.
. Prime a seed-random 64-bit SRAM word and its neighbour with the complement value.
. Read every contiguous (offset, length) byte run of the primed word, re-reading each slice after a checked full-width read of the complement neighbour.
. Read the primed word at every aligned narrow-ARSIZE cell (AxSIZE 0/1/2 at each legal lane offset), re-reading each cell after the same complement-neighbour disturb.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-RANDCFG
|Walked slice and ARSIZE counts equal the combinatorial floors (`36`, `14`), and the CSR walk starts with all-zeros then all-ones. Seed, word, addresses and counts are logged, so a shrunken walk fails rather than reporting PASS over fewer cells.
|CHK-CSR-LANE
|Each pattern reads back exactly and identically on the repeat, through a beat whose upper four lanes the CSR endpoint never drives. All-zeros always runs next to all-ones and random patterns on the same register, so a dead write path or a zero-filled read cannot pass the set.
|CHK-SRAM-SLICE
|Every byte-run slice equals the Python slice of the primed word, and re-reads it exactly after the disturbing read. An extraction that starts at the wrong byte, takes the wrong length, or depends on leftover channel payloads fails the compare; the disturbing read is itself compared against the complement word, so the disturbance is proven to have happened.
|CHK-ARSIZE
|Every aligned AxSIZE-0/1/2 cell returns exactly the addressed lanes of the primed word, and re-reads them identically after the complement-neighbour disturb, on beats where the responder legitimately drives nothing else.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Testlist*: `system.toml` (one seed per regression), also in `all.toml` / `cpu_stub`

*Not claimed*: write-side strobe masking (`sep_axi_strobe_window_test`); AxSIZE=3 (that is the slice walk's full-width baseline).

'''''

[[sep_crypto_csr_wide_access_test]]
===== 2.22 `sep_crypto_csr_wide_access_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: Fabric and remap

*Run mode*: `no_cpu`, `+skip_fuse_sense`

*Source Module*: `sep_crypto_csr_wide_access_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip

*Objective*: Proves that a 64-bit read on each crypto host path returns the data that path's spec defines, and that concurrent 64-bit reads each return their own data. `hw/sys/sep/doc/crypto.adoc` (the `sep_crypto_axi_interconnect` paragraph) decodes one 64-bit AXI slave port to the host paths for OTBN, HMAC, AES, KMAC, ESRC, CSRNG and EDN, "with data-width conversion where required by the endpoint". Every path it names is walked. At CSRNG and EDN, `hw/ip/drbg/doc/architecture.adoc` ("Bus Protocol Adaptation") defines a lane adapter that narrows a 64-bit access to the 32-bit lane selected by address bit [2]; the other lane is not defined, so only bits [31:0] are graded there. At the other five paths the 64-bit read must return both words. The shared register driver issues 32-bit beats, so this leaf issues its 64-bit beats directly.

*Test Coverage*: The seven crypto host paths named in `hw/sys/sep/doc/crypto.adoc` (the `sep_crypto_axi_interconnect` paragraph) -- OTBN, HMAC, AES, KMAC, entropy source, CSRNG and EDN -- each presented one 64-bit read and its 32-bit equivalents, then several 64-bit reads held in flight at once.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. For each aperture, read its chosen 8-byte aligned register pair as two 32-bit single beats.
. Read the same two words again, single-beat, and require both passes to agree. A word that changes between them is live state rather than a comparand, and its aperture is reported instead of compared.
. Read the same 8 bytes as ONE 64-bit beat.
. Compare the 64-bit value against the two 32-bit values concatenated.
. At the entropy source, issue `CRYPTO_CONCURRENT_READS` 64-bit reads at that many DISTINCT addresses with distinct `ARID`s, presenting every `AR` before consuming any `R`, and require each to return its own golden with an OKAY response.
. At every aperture, issue the same number of 64-bit reads of the one address already proved readable, distinct `ARID`s, all in flight at once, and require each to return the golden.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-WIDE-SPLIT
|The 64-bit read equals the two 32-bit reads of the same words, at OTBN, HMAC, AES, KMAC and ESRC. The golden is the DUT's own single-beat path, so this is wide-against-single-beat and never a recomputation.
|CHK-WIDE-LANE
|At CSRNG and EDN, the aligned 64-bit read carries the 32-bit register at its address in bits [31:0], as the DRBG lane adapter defines (`hw/ip/drbg/doc/architecture.adoc` ("Bus Protocol Adaptation")). The 32-bit golden must be non-zero. The other lane is not defined by the spec and is not graded.
|CHK-WIDE-NONVAC
|Every aperture in the table was presented, at least three compared a non-zero value, and at least two had distinct non-zero halves. A pair that reads zero compares 0 against 0, and equal or zero halves hide some mutation classes; the two floors make the exact comparisons and the representative zero/duplicate/swap sensitivity explicit. Also requires that the slot spread ran at every aperture.
|CHK-WIDE-OUTSTANDING
|Concurrent 64-bit reads at the entropy source, distinct ids AND distinct addresses, each returning its own data and an OKAY response. The goldens must hold at least two distinct values, else a read answered with another read's data would compare equal and go unseen.
|CHK-WIDE-SLOTS
|Concurrent 64-bit reads at every aperture, distinct ids, each returning the golden. The same integrity claim as CHK-WIDE-OUTSTANDING, carried to every host path in the table rather than only the entropy source, so an aperture answering a concurrent read with zeros or stale data fails. A read answered with another read's data is not visible here because every id reads the same word; CHK-WIDE-OUTSTANDING owns that case with distinct addresses.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Outstanding reads*: a read issued after the previous one retired is answered by an otherwise idle host path, so serial traffic exercises one path however much of it there is. Concurrency is the only shape under which a 64-bit read can be answered with a DIFFERENT read's data, and that is the failure this phase grades. The ids are distinct because a slave may legitimately order same-id reads behind one another, which would serialise the traffic and undo the concurrency. AXI permits the shape: several outstanding reads with different ids, each answered with its own data (IHI 0022 A5.3). The depth is DV-owned (`CRYPTO_CONCURRENT_READS` in `env/sep_spec_tables.py`): the graded claim is data integrity under concurrency, which holds at any depth.

*Evidence*: every pair has a non-zero generated reset value. CSRNG (`INT_STATE_READ_ENABLE`) and EDN (`BOOT_INS_CMD`) have a non-zero low word for the lane check. KMAC (`CFG_REGWEN` / `CFG_SHADOWED`) and the entropy source (`COMPONENT_ID` / `CTRL`) have distinct non-zero halves and carry the full zero/duplicate/swap mutation sensitivity. AES has equal non-zero halves; HMAC and OTBN have one zero half. Those three still require the 64-bit value to equal their two 32-bit reads exactly, but do not claim that every half mutation is observable on that pair. Addresses come from the generated register header by symbol, never a literal.

*Scope note*: the walked set is the host-path list in `hw/sys/sep/doc/crypto.adoc` (the `sep_crypto_axi_interconnect` paragraph); the per-path contract comes from that path's spec. The write direction is out of scope: these are status and configuration registers, and writing them to obtain a comparand would test the register rather than the 64-bit read path.

'''''

[[sep_axi_map_refuse_test]]
===== 2.23 `sep_axi_map_refuse_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: Fabric and remap

*Run mode*: `no_cpu`, `+skip_fuse_sense`

*Source Module*: `sep_axi_map_refuse_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip

*Randomization*: RANDCFG — every directed anchor that is not on the exclude list runs on every seed, plus seed-selected addresses from the reserved rows. Excluded spans are skipped with a counted reason, and a row that could not yield its full quota is reported in the per-row shortfall line.

*Objective*: Rows marked reserved in the DV-owned table in `env/sep_axi_decode_map.py` allocate nothing, so an access there must not answer OKAY. The refusal expectation is taken from that table. Named reserved spans are excluded from the probe set with a counted reason. The walk grades refusal only, so any refusal passes and the code is logged; the code `sep.rdl` states is graded by `sep_unmapped_access_policy_test` at the points that test probes. Scope is the gaps BETWEEN block windows; `sep_fabric_deadspace_decode_test` walks the dead tail INSIDE one, and neither subsumes the other.

*Test Coverage*: Reserved addresses complete with an AXI error response (DECERR or SLVERR). The code `sep.rdl` states for each is not graded here.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Classify from the DV-owned table in `env/sep_axi_decode_map.py`; a reserved row, and any address in no row at all, allocates nothing. Inside the dual scratch bank (`0x1080_2000`-`0x1080_2FFF`), OTP (`0x1093_0000`-`0x1093_FFFF`) and system-bus (`0x10A0_0000`-`0x10A3_FFFF`) windows, each allocated row is one register block's decoded extent in `hw/sys/sep/regs/gen/py/sep_reg.py` (an RDL array spans all its elements at the array stride). Every span between those blocks is owned by no RDL block and is a reserved row. The OTP anchor is the first byte above the `EFUSE_MMR` block.
. Drop the named excluded spans from the probe set: the CPU TCM aperture, the external chiplet and SMU apertures (TB-terminated), the SEP External window (adopter-defined) and the system-bus reserved span (graded by `sep_unmapped_access_policy_test`). The crypto (`0x1091_4000`), Key Manager (`0x1092_1000`) and OTP reserved gaps are walked, each with a directed anchor.
. Read and write the surviving anchors and the seed-selected reserved addresses, and report the per-row shortfall where a row yielded fewer probes than its quota.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-MAP-REFUSE
|Every probed address is refused. This checker grades refusal only, so DECERR and SLVERR both satisfy it and the line reports the split. OKAY, EXOKAY or a timeout fails the probe; the code `sep.rdl` states is graded by `sep_unmapped_access_policy_test` at the points that test probes. The directed anchors include the exact first byte above the generated boot-ROM extent; remaining probes come from map-reserved addresses this test asserts. Excluded spans are skipped before the walk with a counted reason.
|CHK-MAP-REFUSE-DATA
|A refused read returns none of the live words sampled on the same bus over the ordinary path: the live-bus control (`SEP_NMI_VEC`), `SW_RESET_N` (the block below the `0x10803008` anchor) and boot-ROM word 0 (the block below the one-past-ROM anchor). A refused access never reaches a unit (`hw/sys/sep/doc/memory_map.adoc`), so a refusal that hands back one of these values has reached its owner. Zero words are dropped from the set because they cannot discriminate. At least one refused read must be compared. Other live words are not claimed.
|CHK-NONVAC
|The DECERR beats the monitor observed on the bus equal the count the master reported, so the refusals are evidence from the pins and not only from the driver.
|CHK-OKAY
|A known-mapped CSR on the same bus returns OKAY and its generated reset value, read before any refusal probe. Without it a wedged or dead bus would refuse everything and read as a clean pass. The address and the expected value come from the generated SystemRDL export, and the register's reset is non-zero so the compare cannot pass against a tied-off decode.
|CHK-RANDCFG
|The probe and anchor counts for the seed are logged, so a shrunken walk is visible.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

'''''

[[sep_unmapped_access_policy_test]]
===== 2.24 `sep_unmapped_access_policy_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: Fabric and remap

*Run mode*: `no_cpu`, `+skip_fuse_sense`

*Source Module*: `sep_unmapped_access_policy_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE — every address is derived from the generated register export and walked on every run.

*Objective*: The SEP components view of the SystemRDL memory map (`hw/sys/sep/regs/gen/py/sep_memory_map.py`, generated from `hw/sys/sep/regs/sep.rdl` by `tools/regs/rdlmap.py`, the same model that renders `hw/sys/sep/regs/gen/adoc/memory_map.adoc`) gives each unit's Decoded Extent and states how a 32-bit access that no register backs answers, as seen at the SEP inbound port: in a hole inside the extent, past the extent, and in a reserved row between apertures. Each response gives the read response, the RDL read data and the write response. `doc/trm/src/memory_map.adoc` (Decode Response Codes) defines the cells. This leaf holds the DUT to that table at the points that sit next to live registers and that `sep_fabric_deadspace_decode_test` and `sep_axi_map_refuse_test` do not probe. `env/sep_decode_resp.py` imports that view, so no expected code is typed into the test. `rdata` is a 64-bit field in `sep.rdl`: its low word answers a read with address bit 2 clear and its upper word a read with address bit 2 set. A 32-bit RDL rdata (no upper word) is the word a 32-bit read returns on either half of the bus (`ocah_resp.rdata` in `hw/common/regs/regblock_udps.rdl`; Decode Response Codes in `doc/trm/src/memory_map.adoc`). The expected codes and read data are the `ocah_resp` values `sep.rdl` states. `sep.rdl` is the specification of record for these codes, so `CHK-UNMAPPED-CODE` holds the DUT to the specification. Where the map and the RDL allocation of an array disagree, `CHK-ARRAY-TAIL` grades against the RDL allocation.

*Test Coverage*: System-CSR holes, the reserved row above SEP CPU control, the mailbox page's upper half, the space past each eFuse sibling block and past the SPI host, the end of the eFuse token MMR extent, and every remap and filter array slot tail answer the response code and read data the map states, and none of them aliases a live register.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Program a distinct non-zero value into one live word of every array slot, the first and last AP / STEE output-remap entries, `SEP_NMI_VEC`, three mailbox thresholds, both eFuse timeouts, two eFuse token inputs and the SPI host `CSID`, and read each back. `CSID` takes effect only when a command is issued, and this leaf issues none. Each programmed word is read before its write, for the restore, except a word with a field that has no RDL reset. The two eFuse token inputs are such words: `hw/ip/efuse/regs/efuse_mmr.rdl` gives the `token` field of `RMA_TOKEN_I` and `SEC_DISABLE_TOKEN_I` no reset value, so the register has no value before its first write. The test reads this from the generated IP-XACT (`hw/sys/sep/regs/gen/ipxact/sep.xml`, no `resets` element on the field), not from the generated `_REG_DEFAULT`, which reads 0 for a field without a reset. These words are written before any read of them. Snapshot every other word of those slots, every mailbox `STATUS`, `TOKEN_MATCH_FAULT` and the SPI host `CONFIGOPTS`.
. Read `TOKEN_MATCH_FAULT` through its generated symbol.
. Read and write each probe with 32-bit singles. After each write, re-read every programmed word and the non-array snapshot words. For system-CSR and reserved-row probes, record whether the access reached the system-CSR AXI-Lite port and whether it arrived at the local crossbar's `ext` initiator. Before the probes, write and read the first address of the External row of the SEP CPU logical map (`0x0000_0000`) as the control for the `ext` initiator watcher.
. Read and write each array slot tail and the first word past each filter array, and after each write re-read the words of that slot and of the next slot. After each write to a tail inside the array extent, read that tail again.
. Re-read every live word, then restore the programmed words that were read before their write. The eFuse token inputs are not restored.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-UNMAPPED-LIVE
|Every programmed word reads back its value with OKAY, and every snapshot word reads OKAY. A word with a field that has no RDL reset is written before its first read; the config does not build if a snapshot-only word has such a field. This is the positive control: it shows the bus reaches every block that owns a probed hole, and the distinct values are what make an alias visible.
|CHK-SYSCSR-HOLE-REFUSE
|Every read and write in the system-CSR holes is refused: not OKAY, and not a timeout. For this checker and the five below it, the config does not build unless the map states a refusal at every probe in the group.
|CHK-SYS-RESERVED-REFUSE
|Every read and write in the reserved row above SEP CPU control is refused, the `0x10A5_0000` page included.
|CHK-MBOX-UPPER-REFUSE
|Every read and write in the upper half of the mailbox page is refused.
|CHK-EFUSE-CTRL-PAST-REFUSE
|Every read and write past the `efuse_interface_ctrl` extent is refused.
|CHK-EFUSE-MMR-PAST-REFUSE
|Every read and write past the `efuse_mmr` extent is refused.
|CHK-SPI-PAST-REFUSE
|Every read and write past the `spi_controller` extent, to the end of its aperture, is refused.
|CHK-SYSCSR-HOLE-DECODE
|No system-CSR hole or reserved-row probe reaches the system-CSR AXI-Lite port: the system-peripherals crossbar refuses each one before the AXI-to-AXI-Lite converter, which answers every write error behind it with SLVERR. At least one probe must be watched. A watched write and read of the programmed `SEP_NMI_VEC` word must each show their handshake at that port, so a watcher that sees nothing fails.
|CHK-SYS-RESERVED-NO-LOOPBACK
|No system-CSR hole or reserved-row probe arrives at the local crossbar's `ext` initiator, the input on which `sep_system_peripherals` forwards an address that its peripheral crossbar does not decode (`hw/sys/sep/doc/fabric.adoc`). Each probe is refused at its first decode, by the local crossbar or the system-peripherals crossbar, and is not sent back into the local crossbar. At least one probe must be watched. A watched write and read of `0x0000_0000`, the first address of the External row, which the local crossbar sends to `sep_system_peripherals` and the peripheral crossbar returns on that initiator, must each show their handshake there, so a watcher that sees nothing fails. Their response is not graded.
|CHK-TOKEN-FAULT-EXTENT
|`TOKEN_MATCH_FAULT`, the last register `hw/ip/efuse/regs/efuse_mmr.rdl` places in the token MMR (`@0x70`), reads OKAY with its RDL reset value, and the first word after it (`EFUSE_MMR` base + `REG_MAP_SIZE`) is refused. The extent therefore ends at `0x1093_0573`, where the RDL ends it. That the register holds live fault state is graded by `sep_efuse_rma_token_rand_test`, which reads a raised fault bit through the same address.
|CHK-ARRAY-TAIL
|The array extent is the array base + `SEP_TOP_<ARRAY>_TOTAL_SIZE`, the RDL allocation. Every tail inside it, the last slot's tail included, answers OKAY, and a read of it returns zero. A re-read of such a tail after its write answers OKAY with zero, so the write was discarded. The first word past the extent is refused where no other RDL block owns it. The config does not build unless the array's map row spans exactly that extent and the map states a refusal for every word past it. A tail inside the extent where the map states anything other than OKAY with zero is a map disagreement: it is graded here only and logged as `UNMAPPED-MAP-DISAGREE`. A tail write never changes a word of its own slot or of the next slot. The walk must grade at least one word of each kind. A failure names the tail address, the response and the extent.
|CHK-UNMAPPED-CODE
|Every probe and tail access that completes, except the map-disagree tail words, answers the response code the map states for its address and channel, and every read returns the stated read data: the low word of the RDL rdata, or its upper word when address bit 2 is set. The codes and read data are the `ocah_resp` values `sep.rdl` states. A 32-bit RDL rdata is graded as that word on both bus halves. Past `efuse_interface_ctrl` and `spi_controller`, reads cover both 32-bit bus lanes. Every refusal read is issued inside the monitor's error-read-data window, so an X or Z in an error payload fails the run instead of reading as zero; every error-response read must be lane-checked. A failure names the address, the response and read data seen, and the map row, column and cell. The walk must grade at least one access.
|CHK-UNMAPPED-NO-ALIAS
|No refused read returns the value of a programmed word. No probe write changes a watched live word. A closing re-read of every live word matches the snapshot.
|CHK-UNMAPPED-PINS
|The DECERR beats the bus monitor saw equal the DECERR responses the master reported, and the run reported at least one.
|===

The `UNMAPPED-CODE` lines tally the codes `CHK-UNMAPPED-CODE` graded, per group and channel, and count the system-CSR and reserved-row probes that reached the system-CSR AXI-Lite port, which `CHK-SYSCSR-HOLE-DECODE` requires to be none.

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. `UVM_ERROR` is 0.

*Scope*:

* System-CSR holes: the gaps between the AP and STEE output-remap arrays, after the STEE array, between the outbound and inbound filter arrays, before SEP CPU control, past the SEP CPU control extent, one SEP CPU control image up, past the cold scratch bank, before and past the warm scratch bank, and the last word below one scratch-pair image up. The first and last `SCRATCH` word of each bank are programmed live words.
* Reserved row: the generated map row from the end of the SEP CPU control aperture to the external IO bridge, first and last word of each 64 KiB page. The row has two refusal points. The system-peripherals crossbar refuses the `0x10A4_0000` page itself, because its system-CSR rules cover only the register blocks' extents, so the access never reaches the system-CSR AXI-Lite port. The local crossbar refuses `0x10A5_0000` and above at its own decode: its system-peripherals CSR window ends where the system-peripherals crossbar's system-CSR window ends. An address that the local crossbar sent into that window and that the peripheral crossbar does not decode would return to the local crossbar on its `ext` initiator (`hw/sys/sep/doc/fabric.adoc`), so no reserved-row probe may arrive there.
* Mailbox upper half: from `AXIL_MAILBOX` base plus its size rounded up to a power of two (`0x10A0_8000`) to the end of the 64 KiB mailbox aperture. All of it is past the mailbox's Decoded Extent. The probes include the images of outbound mailbox 0 `WRITE_DATA`, `WIRQT`, `RIRQT` and `STATUS` and of the last inbound mailbox `WIRQT`.
* eFuse: past `efuse_interface_ctrl` (28 B extent) and past `efuse_mmr` (116 B extent), each to the end of its 256 B window, including the image of a live register one extent up and half a window up. Past `efuse_interface_ctrl`, reads cover both 32-bit lanes of the 64-bit bus (address bit 2 set and clear).
* SPI host: past `spi_controller` (56 B extent) to the end of its 1 MiB aperture: the first two words past the extent (both bus lanes), the `CSID` image one extent up, the `CONFIGOPTS` image half an aperture up, and the last word of the aperture.
* Array tails: every word between the end of a slot's registers and the next slot, for the 16 alias-remap, 32 outbound-filter and 16 inbound-filter slots. The array extent is the array base plus `SEP_TOP_<ARRAY>_TOTAL_SIZE` from the generated `hw/sys/sep/regs/gen/c/sep_addr.h` (`0x200`, `0x400` and `0x200`): the RDL allocates the full slot stride to every slot, the last one included. That size must equal the aperture of the array's map row. Every tail inside the extent, the last slot's tail included, must read zero and discard a write with OKAY. `sep.rdl` sets `ocah_full_stride_extent` on these arrays, so the map row's Decoded Extent is the full allocation and the map states OKAY with zero for every tail, the last one included. The first word past the outbound and inbound filter apertures (`0x10A2_0400`, `0x10A2_1200`) is in a reserved row and must be refused. The first word past the alias-remap array is `AP_OUTPUT_REMAP_CTRL[0]`, a live word, so it is not a refusal point.
* The Key Manager's own view of the token MMR (`0x0001_1570`) needs KM firmware and is not probed here.

'''''

[[sep-vplan-phase3-fabric-remap]]
==== 2. Fabric and remap, Phase 3

This bucket grades the fabric and remap contracts that the specification states. Each test is written from the specification and the RDL. A test extends an open test only with the cells that the open test does not grade, and the Test Coverage field of the entry names the open test. Legs that share a stimulus and a run mode are legs of one test.

Initiators:

* LSU is the CPU load/store splice on `s_axi`. It does not pass the inbound filter.
* SI is the SMN-inbound master on `m_axi`. It passes the inbound filter.
* DMA and IFU exist only in the `cpu` run mode.

Probes and hook. A probe only reads. Every probe or hook has one status:

* approved: the probe exists in `tb/tb_top.sv` and `docs/SEP_TB_ARCH.adoc` lists it.
* observation tap: the probe is not in the closed set of probes that `docs/SEP_TB_ARCH.adoc` holds, and the test adds it to the SEP_TB_ARCH observation-probe list. A check on an observation tap is graded.
* added hook: a top-port drive or an error inject that `docs/SEP_TB_ARCH.adoc` does not list (<<sep-vplan-credit-rules>>). The test adds a top-port drive to the port table of the HDL Top section of `docs/SEP_TB_ARCH.adoc`. An added hook blocks no check, and a check that needs it is graded.

The frontdoor anchors are approved: the LSU and SI responses and read data, the read-back of a register or an SRAM word, and the DMA status registers.

[cols="1,4,3",options="header"]
|===
|Probe |Watches |Status
|PR-CSR |The AW and AR handshakes and the low 32 address bits at the system-CSR AXI-Lite port. |approved: `sys_csr_axil_*_o`; AXI-Lite split handshakes
|PR-XEXT |The AW and AR handshakes and the low 32 address bits at the `ext` initiator of the local crossbar. It carries no data, ID or AxUSER. |approved: `xbar_ext_in_*_o`
|PR-OUT |Every AW and AR handshake on `smn_outbound_axi_req_o` (address, ID, AxUSER, AxCACHE, AxPROT, AxLEN, AxBURST) and every W beat. |observation tap: the net `smn_outbound_req_w` exists in `tb_top` and no port exports it
|PR-EXT |`axi_extension_axi_req_o`: address, AxSIZE, AxLEN, strobe and data. |observation tap
|PR-SRAM |`sep_sram_req_o`. |observation tap
|PR-ROM |`sep_boot_rom_req_o`. |observation tap
|PR-SMC |`sep_ext_to_smc_axi_req_o`. |observation tap
|PR-DMACSR |The request at the DMA CSR target port. |observation tap
|PR-ALIAS |The request at the input and at the output of the local-master alias remap: address and AxCACHE. |observation tap
|BH-SMC |The drive of `smc_global_base_addr_i` and `smc_region_size_i`, from plusargs or from the leaf before reset release, and an SMC responder on `sep_ext_to_smc_axi`, in the `lsu_stub_all_live` target of `sep_fabric_smc_route_test` and in the `cpu` run mode of `sep_fabric_dma_endpoint_matrix_test`. The default bench ties both inputs to 0 and the SMC responder exists in the `rom_boot` target only. |added hook: top-port drive of `smc_global_base_addr_i`, `smc_region_size_i` and `sep_ext_to_smc_axi_resp_i`
|===

No test of this bucket injects a fault. The CPU-LSU splice is the one stimulus exception that the tests use. It is approved.

Bring-up modes:

* Real PROD fuse sense: the inbound filter is active.
* Real PROD fuse sense, then one DEMOTE_1 write: the inbound filter is bypassed.
* `+skip_fuse_sense`: used only for outbound and decode legs.

Every leaf reads FEAT_CTRL and logs it, so the log names the leg.

Shared rules:

* AxSIZE is the AXI size encoding: 0 is 1 byte, 1 is 2 bytes, 2 is 4 bytes and 3 is 8 bytes on the 64-bit bus. An access is aligned to its size and never crosses the end of its window.
* A read of a 32-bit register at AxSIZE 3 compares bits [31:0] only. Bits [63:32] of a `SCRATCH` word and of `SEP_SW_DEBUG` are reserved, and the specification states no read value for reserved bits, so the leaf logs them and does not grade them.
* Every graded register compare follows the shared reserved-bit rule (<<sep-vplan-reserved-bits>>): it uses the RDL field bits of the register only, and the bits that the RDL marks Reserved with no reset value are masked out of the compare and logged in the same line.
* A never check pairs with a control in the same leaf. In the control a healthy design drives the same probe or answers the same response. A leaf whose control stays silent fails.
* A deny cell pairs with an allow cell that differs in one attribute. A dead bus cannot pass the pair.
* The filter reference model is written from the `axi_filter` document (`hw/ip/axi_filter/doc/index.adoc`, "Instances", "Match, Then Permit" and "Address Range Granule") and from `hw/sys/smc/doc/assets/smc-traffic-filters.svg`. It never reads the RTL.
* The source ID that the filter compares with `src_id` is AxUSER[3:0] (`smc-traffic-filters.svg`, description of `axi_filter_wrap`: `src_id` is 0 or equals the source ID in AxUSER[3:0]). The filter document states that the decode is the same in every instance. OTHERS is source ID 0. Outside the source-ID legs every entry has `src_id` 0 and every probe carries AxUSER 0, so the source ID does not decide a verdict.
* Verdict anchor. The filter error subordinate answers DECERR to a refused request. An admitted outbound request reaches the bench responder, which answers OKAY, and the OKAY answer of the paired allow cell is the control. The response code is therefore the outbound verdict and needs no PR-OUT.
* Randomized stimulus is a pure function of the seed. `--stage sim --seed N` replays a leaf. A per-seed value is not evidence.
* A read-back of each programmed filter register sits between its write and the first dependent transaction, because the specification states no ordering between a CSR write and the next transaction.
* Every check logs `CHK-<NAME> PASS: ...` or `CHK-<NAME> FAIL: ...` with the values it compared. A leaf fails when a named check line is missing from `results.xml`.
* A `no_cpu` leaf uses target `lsu_stub_all_live`, group `cpu_stub` and `testlists/system.toml`. A `cpu` leaf uses a firmware image, group `cpu` and `testlists/cpu.toml`.
* Tool "Both" means Verilator and VCS. Covergroup collection is VCS only.

[[sep_fabric_inbound_rebase_test]]
===== 2.25 `sep_fabric_inbound_rebase_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: Fabric and remap

*Run mode*: `no_cpu` (`lsu_stub_all_live`, group `cpu_stub`, `testlists/system.toml`), real PROD fuse sense (no `+skip_fuse_sense`) with a pinned image: PROD, SEC_DIS 0, and fixed `SIP_DIS` and `SYS_DIS` values whose DBG_1 bit 0 is clear in both, 3 seeds. Tool: Verilator and VCS.

*Source Module*: `sep_fabric_inbound_rebase_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (LSU master on `s_axi`, SI master on `m_axi`); `tb/sep_outbound_mbx.sv` (outbound responder: OKAY and zero read data for any address), used by the unit leg only. Probes: PR-XEXT (approved: rebased request of an SRAM access), PR-CSR (approved: rebased request of a scratch access), the SI and LSU responses and read data, the LSU read-back (approved). PR-SRAM (an observation tap the test adds to the SEP_TB_ARCH observation-probe list) only supplements the LSU read-back, and no check needs it. The rebase model is written from `hw/sys/sep/doc/fabric.adoc` and never reads the RTL. No inject.

*Randomization*: `SepSeededRng` from the run seed, RAND-REP over a directed configuration. Three fixed (base, size) pairs: base `0x40_0000_0000` with sizes `0x2000_0000` (A), `0x1000_0000` (B) and `0x8000_0000` (C), each a power of two and a 4 KiB multiple. The seed samples the SRAM read offset `o` and the SRAM write offset `o2` (8-byte aligned, inside `0x0` to `0x3_FFF8`, `o2` different from `o`) and the cold scratch word offset `s` (8-byte aligned, inside the 64-byte bank). `reseed = 3` samples different offsets. The pairs, the cells and their order are the same on every seed. The test makes no claim about other base or size values, because the specification states no legal values.

*Objective*: An inbound request meets the inbound filter first on the chiplet-global address. The global-to-local remap then rebases the `SEP_REGION_SIZE`-byte window at `SEP_GLOBAL_BASE_ADDR` to address 0 and passes every other address unchanged. The peripheral crossbar forwards a local address below `0x4000_0000` to the local crossbar and answers DECERR at or above `0x4000_0000`. The inbound port has no connection to the Boot ROM, Reset Control, ICCM, DCCM, PIC and the AP and STEE regions, and answers DECERR for them at any aperture. Cites `hw/sys/sep/doc/fabric.adoc` ("Fabric Topology", input fabric; "Address Remapping"), `hw/sys/sep/doc/assets/sep-input-fabric.svg`, `hw/sys/sep/regs/gen/adoc/blocks/sep_cpu_ctrl.adoc` (`SEP_GLOBAL_BASE_ADDR`, `SEP_REGION_SIZE`), `hw/ip/axi_filter/doc/index.adoc` ("Blocked Transactions") `hw/sys/sep/doc/memory_map.adoc` ("Units Unreachable from the Inbound Port"), `hw/sys/sep/doc/assets/sep_axi_connectivity.svg` and `hw/sys/sep/doc/lifecycle_controller.adoc` ("Per-LC-state Feature Control Profile": the PROD state with no demotion keeps the inbound filter active).

*Test Coverage*: In-window SRAM read, SRAM write and scratch read behind entries over the global ranges; the filter-first corner; the bottom word, the top word and the last byte of the window, with the first address above and the first address below the window; the crossbar limit at `0x4000_0000` with the word below it; a local address at `0x4000_0100` and the CPU Resources addresses (ICCM, DCCM, PIC and the two Reserved rows) that the filter admits; and the first word of the Boot ROM, Reset Control, AP region and STEE region at the two rebased apertures A and C. Extends `sep_fabric_inbound_filter_rule_matrix_test`, which grades the per-entry inbound allow and block cells, `sep_address_map_test` and `sep_reg_bit_bash_rand_test`, which grade the storage of the two aperture registers, and `sep_lcc_uvm_inbound_filter_gating_test` (CHK-DBG-UNREACHABLE), which grades the first and last word of the six unreachable units at the reset aperture with the inbound filter bypassed. Only the new cells are graded here: the rebase, the filter-first order, the window edges on both sides, the crossbar limit, the four in-window units at the rebased apertures and the CPU Resources addresses behind an active filter. The open tests keep the rest. This test programs the aperture away from its reset values; `sep_fabric_filter_match_priority_rand_test` and `sep_fabric_row_response_matrix_test` run at the reset aperture. Functional coverage: `sep_fabric_inbound_aperture_cg` (`cp_in_ap_class`, `cp_out_ap_class`, `cp_translation`, `cp_rebased_limit`, `cp_dest_class_verdict` for the loopback admitted cells and the unreachable-unit cells), `sep_fabric_port_silence_cp.sil_inbound_refused` (cause `rebase_ge_0x4000_0000`), existing `sep_inbound_filter_allow_cg`.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Bring up with real PROD fuse sense of the pinned image, so the inbound filter is active. The LSU reads `FEAT_CTRL` (64 bits) and compares it with the golden decode that the model computes from the profile table of `lifecycle_controller.adoc` for that image. The golden holds the SEP_DBG state that keeps the filter active. A mismatch prints `CTL-REBASE-FILTER-ACTIVE FAIL` and stops the leaf.
. Read `SEP_GLOBAL_BASE_ADDR` and `SEP_REGION_SIZE` and log the reset values.
. Draw `o`, `o2` and `s`. The LSU stages a non-zero marker `M1` at SRAM word `0x1000_0000` + `o`, a non-zero marker `M3` at SRAM word `0x1000_0000` + `o2` and a non-zero marker `M2` at cold scratch word `0x1080_2000` + `s`. The scratch register holds 32 data bits (bits [63:32] are reserved, and the specification states no read value for them), so `M2` fits in bits [31:0] and every compare of a scratch read uses bits [31:0]. The three markers and the write data `W` of step 8 are pairwise different. The LSU reads each staged word back.
. Configuration A. The LSU writes `SEP_GLOBAL_BASE_ADDR` = `0x40_0000_0000` and `SEP_REGION_SIZE` = `0x2000_0000`, then reads both back. `G` is the base.
. The LSU programs inbound entry 0 over the global range `G` + `0x1000_0000` to `G` + `0x1003_FFFF` and inbound entry 1 over `G` + `0x1080_2000` to `G` + `0x1080_203F`. Both entries are enabled and allow read and write, with `allow_burst` 0, `src_id` 0 and `allow_ns` equal to `prot[1]` of the SI probe. The LSU reads back every programmed filter register.
. SI reads 8 bytes at `G` + `0x1000_0000` + `o`. The response is OKAY and the data is `M1`. PR-XEXT shows the AR address `0x1000_0000` + `o`.
. SI reads 8 bytes at `G` + `0x1080_2000` + `s`. The response is OKAY and bits [31:0] of the data are `M2`. Bits [63:32] are logged and not graded. PR-CSR shows the AR address `0x1080_2000` + `s`.
. SI writes `W` as 8 bytes at `G` + `0x1000_0000` + `o2`. The response is OKAY. PR-XEXT shows the AW address `0x1000_0000` + `o2`.
. The LSU reads the word `0x1000_0000` + `o2` at its direct address and compares it with `W`.
. Unreachable units, configuration A. The LSU programs inbound entry 3 over `G` + `0x1000_0000` to `G` + `0x11FF_FFFF` (enabled, read and write allowed, `allow_burst` 0, `src_id` 0, `allow_ns` equal to the SI `prot[1]`) and one outbound entry pair over `0x1100_0000` to `0x11FF_FFFF` (one entry with `allow_ns` 0 and one with `allow_ns` 1, enabled, read and write allowed, `src_id` 0), so a request that reached the output fabric would be admitted and answered OKAY by the bench responder. The LSU reads every programmed register back. The LSU reads `SW_RESET_N` (`0x1080_3000`) and the first Boot ROM word (`0x1004_0000`) at their direct addresses.
. SI reads 8 bytes at `G` + `0x1000_0000` + `o`. The response is OKAY and the data is `M1`. This read is the control of the unit cells: the same entry admits a live unit.
. For each unit U of the Boot ROM (`0x1004_0000`), Reset Control (`0x1080_3000`), AP region (`0x1100_0000`) and STEE region (`0x1180_0000`): error injection at `smn_inbound_axi_req_i`: SI reads 4 bytes (AxSIZE 2) at `G` + U and SI writes 4 bytes at `G` + U. The write data is the value that the LSU read at U for the Boot ROM and Reset Control, so a unit that a faulty fabric connected keeps its value, and a seeded non-zero word for the AP and STEE regions. The expected response is DECERR on RRESP and on BRESP. The PR-XEXT handshake is logged and not graded, because the crossbar forwards these addresses to the local crossbar, which refuses them.
. The LSU disables inbound entry 3 and the two outbound entries and reads them back.
. Filter-first corner. The LSU disables entries 0 and 1, programs inbound entry 2 over the local range `0x1000_0000` to `0x1003_FFFF` (enabled, read and write allowed, `allow_burst` 0, `src_id` 0, `allow_ns` equal to the SI `prot[1]`) and reads entry 2 back.
. Error injection at `smn_inbound_axi_req_i`: SI reads `G` + `0x1000_0000` + `o`. No enabled entry covers the global address. The expected response is DECERR on RRESP, and PR-XEXT shows no handshake.
. SI reads the plain address `0x1000_0000` + `o`. It lies below `G`, so it passes the remap unchanged and the entry 2 range covers it. The response is OKAY and the data is `M1`.
. The LSU disables entry 2.
. Configuration B. The LSU writes `SEP_REGION_SIZE` = `0x1000_0000` and reads it back. The LSU programs entry 0 over `G` - `0x10` to `G` + `0xF` and entry 1 over `G` + `0x0FFF_FFF0` to `G` + `0x1000_000F`. Both are enabled with read and write allowed, `allow_burst` 0, `src_id` 0 and `allow_ns` equal to the SI `prot[1]`. The LSU reads the entries back.
. SI reads 8 bytes at `G` (bottom word). PR-XEXT shows the AR address 0. The response is logged and is not graded, because the specification states no response for this local address. The leaf waits for the response in a bounded wait; a timeout fails CHK-REBASE-EDGE.
. SI reads 8 bytes at `G` + `0x0FFF_FFF8` (top word). PR-XEXT shows the AR address `0x0FFF_FFF8`. The response is logged and is not graded. Same bounded wait.
. SI reads 1 byte (AxSIZE 0) at `G` + `0x0FFF_FFFF` (last byte). PR-XEXT shows the AR address `0x0FFF_FFFF`. The response is logged and is not graded. Same bounded wait.
. Error injection at `smn_inbound_axi_req_i`: SI reads 1 byte at `G` + `0x1000_0000` (first address above the window). Both entries admit it, the remap passes it unchanged, and the address is at or above `0x4000_0000`. The expected response is DECERR on RRESP, and PR-XEXT shows no handshake.
. Error injection at `smn_inbound_axi_req_i`: SI reads 1 byte at `G` - 1 (first address below the window). The expected response is DECERR on RRESP, and PR-XEXT shows no handshake.
. Configuration C. The LSU disables entries 0 and 1, writes `SEP_REGION_SIZE` = `0x8000_0000`, reads it back, programs entry 0 over `G` + `0x3FFF_FFF0` to `G` + `0x4000_00FF` (enabled, read and write allowed, `allow_burst` 0, `src_id` 0, `allow_ns` equal to the SI `prot[1]`) and reads entry 0 back.
. Unreachable units, configuration C. Repeat steps 10 to 13. The window ends at `G` + `0x7FFF_FFFF`, so the four units and the SRAM control word rebase to their local addresses.
. SI reads 8 bytes at `G` + `0x3FFF_FFF8`. It rebases to `0x3FFF_FFF8`. PR-XEXT shows the AR address `0x3FFF_FFF8`. The response is logged and is not graded. The leaf waits for the response in a bounded wait; a timeout fails CHK-REBASE-XBAR-LIMIT. The next step starts after the response.
. Error injection at `smn_inbound_axi_req_i`: SI reads 8 bytes at `G` + `0x4000_0000`. It rebases to `0x4000_0000`. The expected response is DECERR on RRESP, and PR-XEXT and PR-CSR show no handshake.
. Above-limit corner. The LSU disables entry 0, programs entry 0 over `0x4000_0100` to `0x4000_01FF` and entry 1 over `0xC000_0000` to `0xCFFF_FFFF` (same attributes) and reads both back. The window of configuration C includes none of these addresses, so the remap passes them unchanged.
. Error injection at `smn_inbound_axi_req_i`: SI reads 8 bytes at `0x4000_0100`. The filter admits it, and the local address is at or above `0x4000_0000`. The expected response is DECERR on RRESP, and PR-XEXT shows no handshake.
. Error injection at `smn_inbound_axi_req_i`: SI reads 4 bytes and writes 4 bytes at each CPU Resources address: the ICCM base `0xC000_0000`, the DCCM base `0xC004_0000`, the Reserved row `0xC006_0000`, the PIC base `0xC008_0000` and the Reserved row `0xC008_8000`. The filter admits them, and each local address is at or above `0x4000_0000`. The expected response is DECERR on RRESP and on BRESP, and PR-XEXT and PR-CSR show no handshake.
. The LSU disables entries 0 and 1, writes `SEP_GLOBAL_BASE_ADDR` = `0x0` and `SEP_REGION_SIZE` = `0x0100_0000`, reads both back and logs them.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CTL-REBASE-FILTER-ACTIVE
|(Precondition of every check of this leaf. It is not a counted check.) The bring-up image is PROD with SEC_DIS 0 and no demotion, so `FEAT_CTRL` equals the golden decode of the profile table and the SEP_DBG state keeps the inbound filter active (`lifecycle_controller.adoc`, "Per-LC-state Feature Control Profile"). `sep_fabric_inbound_filter_rule_matrix_test` and `sep_lcc_uvm_inbound_filter_gating_test` (CHK-PROD-FEAT) grade this value, so this leaf uses the compare only to stop on a wrong bring-up. A mismatch prints `CTL-REBASE-FILTER-ACTIVE FAIL: feat_ctrl=0x<v> golden=0x<g>` and stops the leaf, so the named checks of the leaf are missing and the leaf fails. Anchor: the LSU read of `FEAT_CTRL` on the control bus. Evidence: `CTL-REBASE-FILTER-ACTIVE LOG: feat_ctrl=0x<v> golden=0x<g> sep_dbg=<n>`.
|CHK-REBASE
|A request at `G` + n inside the window reaches the local fabric at address n (`fabric.adoc`, "Fabric Topology"; `sep-input-fabric.svg`). In configuration A the model computes n from the programmed base and size only. The SRAM read returns the marker `M1` that the LSU staged, so the data is a real readback of the staged word, and PR-XEXT shows the AR address `0x1000_0000` + `o`. The scratch read returns `M2` in bits [31:0] (bits [63:32] are logged and not graded), and PR-CSR shows `0x1080_2000` + `s`. The SRAM write shows the AW address `0x1000_0000` + `o2` on PR-XEXT, and the LSU direct read of that word returns `W`, which differs from the staged `M3`. Every response is OKAY. A DUT with no rebase or a wrong base answers DECERR (the global address is at or above `0x4000_0000`) or reaches another word and shows another address. Anchor: the SI read data, the LSU read-back, PR-XEXT and PR-CSR, all approved. PR-SRAM, an observation tap, may supplement them, and no verdict depends on it. Control: the three legs each drive their own probe in the same leaf. Evidence: one line per leg, `CHK-REBASE PASS: leg=sram_rd\|sram_wr\|scratch_rd base=0x4000000000 size=0x20000000 global=0x<g> local_seen=0x<l> resp=OKAY rdata_lo=0x<r> staged=0x<m> wdata=0x<w>\|na lsu_direct=0x<d>\|na`.
|CHK-REBASE-FILTER-FIRST
|The inbound filter compares the global address before the remap (`fabric.adoc`, "Fabric Topology"). With only the local-range entry 2 enabled, the read of the global address answers DECERR and PR-XEXT shows no handshake, and the read of the plain address, which lies outside the window, answers OKAY with the staged marker `M1`. A filter that compares the rebased address admits the first read and fails the check. Anchor: the SI responses and read data, PR-XEXT (approved). Control (differential cell): the plain-address read answers OKAY with data and drives PR-XEXT. Evidence: `CHK-REBASE-FILTER-FIRST PASS: global_resp=DECERR plain_resp=OKAY plain_rdata=0x<m1> staged=0x<m1> xext_global=0 xext_plain=<n>`.
|CHK-REBASE-EDGE
|For the bottom word, the top word and the last byte, the model computes the rebased address n from the programmed base and size. When n is below `0x4000_0000`, PR-XEXT shows n. Otherwise the response is DECERR and PR-XEXT shows no handshake. The global addresses `G` + size (first address above) and `G` - 1 (first address below) lie outside the window, pass the remap unchanged and are at or above `0x4000_0000`, so both answer DECERR with PR-XEXT silent. The in-window responses are logged and not graded. A DUT with a window that is one byte too large or too small, or one that rebases the first address above the window, shows the wrong PR-XEXT address or a non-DECERR answer. Anchor: PR-XEXT and the SI responses (approved). Control: the in-window cells drive PR-XEXT in the same leaf, so a dead tap fails the check. Evidence: `CHK-REBASE-EDGE PASS: size=0x<s> bottom_seen=0x<n>\|none top_seen=0x<n>\|none last_byte_seen=0x<n>\|none above_resp=DECERR above_xext=0 below_resp=DECERR below_xext=0 control_seen=<n>`.
|CHK-REBASE-XBAR-LIMIT
|The peripheral crossbar answers DECERR at or above `0x4000_0000` (`fabric.adoc`, "Fabric Topology"). In configuration C the read that rebases to `0x4000_0000` answers DECERR, and PR-XEXT and PR-CSR show no handshake. A DUT that forwards `0x4000_0000` to the local crossbar shows a PR-XEXT handshake. Anchor: the SI response, PR-XEXT and PR-CSR (approved). Control: the read that rebases to `0x3FFF_FFF8` shows on PR-XEXT. Evidence: `CHK-REBASE-XBAR-LIMIT PASS: below_seen=0x3FFFFFF8 local=0x40000000 resp=DECERR xbar_ext_in=0 csr_seen=0`.
|CHK-REBASE-ABOVE
|A local request at `0x4000_0100`, outside the window and admitted by the filter, answers DECERR and PR-XEXT shows no handshake. The same holds for a read and a write at each CPU Resources address of the step (`fabric.adoc`, "Fabric Topology": the crossbar answers DECERR at or above `0x4000_0000`; `memory_map.adoc`, "Units Unreachable from the Inbound Port"). A DUT that truncates the address to 32 bits and forwards it fails the check. Anchor: the SI response, PR-XEXT and PR-CSR (approved). Control: the `0x3FFF_FFF8` read of configuration C drives PR-XEXT in the same test. Evidence: `CHK-REBASE-ABOVE PASS: addr=0x<a> dir=R\|W resp=DECERR xbar_ext_in=0 csr_seen=0 control_seen=<n>`.
|CHK-REBASE-UNREACH
|A read and a write of the first word of the Boot ROM, Reset Control, AP region and STEE region at `G` + U, in configurations A and C, answer DECERR through an entry that admits them (`memory_map.adoc`, "Units Unreachable from the Inbound Port"; `sep_axi_connectivity.svg`: the System Interface has no path to these units). A DUT that connects the inbound port to one of these units answers OKAY, and for the AP and STEE regions the enabled outbound pair would admit a request that reached the output fabric. Anchor: the SI responses (approved). Control: the read of the staged SRAM word through the same entry answers OKAY with `M1` in each configuration, so the entry and the path are alive. Evidence: `CHK-REBASE-UNREACH PASS: cfg=A\|C unit=boot_rom\|reset_ctrl\|ap_region\|stee_region dir=R\|W global=0x<g> resp=DECERR control_resp=OKAY control_rdata=0x<m1>`.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope limit*: The test does not grade the per-entry inbound allow and block cells, the storage of the two aperture registers, other base or size values, or the legal values of the two registers (the specification states none). Those cells stay with `sep_fabric_inbound_filter_rule_matrix_test`, `sep_address_map_test` and `sep_reg_bit_bash_rand_test`. The DECERR of the six unreachable units at the reset aperture and the last word of each unit stay with `sep_lcc_uvm_inbound_filter_gating_test`. The responses of the in-window edge reads and of the read at `0x3FFF_FFF8` are logged only, because the specification states no response for those local addresses. The inbound filter bypass is not used: the filter is active on every request.

'''''

[[sep_fabric_filter_match_priority_rand_test]]
===== 2.26 `sep_fabric_filter_match_priority_rand_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: Fabric and remap

*Run mode*: `no_cpu` (`lsu_stub_all_live`, group `cpu_stub`, `testlists/system.toml`), real PROD fuse sense (no `+skip_fuse_sense`) with a pinned image: PROD, SEC_DIS 0, and fixed `SIP_DIS` and `SYS_DIS` values whose DBG_1 bit 0 is clear in both, 4 seeds. Tool: Verilator and VCS.

*Source Module*: `sep_fabric_filter_match_priority_rand_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (LSU master on `s_axi`, SI master on `m_axi`); `tb/sep_outbound_mbx.sv` (outbound responder: OKAY and zero read data for any address); the filter reference model of this bucket, written from `hw/ip/axi_filter/doc/index.adoc` and `hw/sys/smc/doc/assets/smc-traffic-filters.svg`, which reads only the programmed entry fields and the probe attributes and never the RTL. Probes. Approved: PR-XEXT and PR-CSR (an inbound refusal shows no handshake), the SI and LSU responses and read data, the LSU read-back of the SRAM and scratch words. PR-OUT, PR-EXT and PR-SRAM are observation taps the test adds to the SEP_TB_ARCH observation-probe list: PR-OUT supplements the outbound DECERR verdict, PR-EXT serves the extension-window probe of leg 3, and PR-SRAM supplements the LSU read-back. No inject.

*Randomization*: `SepSeededRng` from the run seed, two classes. Legs 1, 2 and 4 are RANDCFG. Dimensions: entry count (3 to 6 per instance), entry indices (inbound 0 to 15, outbound 0 to 31), overlapping range placement, `entry_enabled`, `allow_ns`, `allow_burst`, `src_id` (0 to 15), AxUSER[3:0] of the probe (0 to 15), `read_allowed`, `write_allowed`, `group_id` (0 to 15), probe attributes, granule index, in-granule offsets of START and END, and the shape. Leg 3 is RAND-REP. Dimensions: probe address, direction, AxSIZE, probe `prot[1]` (0 or 1) and the control entry index; every destination class is probed in the directions that leg 3 lists for it, on every seed. The armed range of leg 3 is the directed value START_ADDR 0, END_ADDR 2^48-1, which covers every probed address and ends below 2^56-1. Legal range per `hw/ip/axi_filter/regs/gen/adoc/filter_ctrl.adoc` (`FILTER_CONFIG`, `START_ADDR`, `END_ADDR`). Rejection list: an inverted range; a range that touches 2^56-1; a range where START is in a higher granule than END; any outbound burst; any inbound entry that covers the filter-bank page or `SEP_CPU_CTRL` in legs 1, 2 and 4; the `locked` bit; any draw of the `SEP_DBG` bit; probe addresses of units that the inbound port does not reach (their DECERR comes from decode); in a leg 1 (entry state, attribute) cell, any other stack entry that matches the probe in the deny cell or in the allow cell (each other entry does not cover the probe address or fails a match term, so the covering entry alone decides both verdicts). In the granule leg a range is whole granules inside SRAM (inbound) or inside the SMU window above `0x8000_1000` (outbound, `src_id` 0). `reseed = 4` samples different stacks, values and probe attributes. The cell classes of each leg are the same on every seed. Leg 1 draws the destination class of each (entry state, attribute) cell from the classes of its instance, and every class gets at least one cell per instance on every seed. The cross of attribute and destination class is seed-dependent and has no bin. Leg 2 runs the source-ID values 1, 2, 4, 8 and 15 (each bit alone and all four bits) and the wildcard probes with AxUSER[3:0] 0 and 15 on every seed. It draws one more non-zero source ID from the other ten values and two more wildcard AxUSER[3:0] values from 1 to 14. No bin records a value (`cp_src_id_class` bins the classes), and no regression claims the full value sets. The other values come only over a merge of regressions.

*Objective*: A filter entry matches only when it is enabled, the address is in the widened range, `prot[1]` equals `allow_ns`, the source ID equals `src_id` or `src_id` is 0, and `allow_burst` is 1 or AxLEN is 0. The source ID is AxUSER[3:0]. The lowest-numbered match wins and only its permission bit counts. A failed match falls through. A clear permission bit on the lowest match blocks. A transaction that no entry matches is blocked with DECERR. AW and AR decode independently. `group_id` is programmed with a random value and is not graded. After reset every entry is disabled, so unmatched traffic is blocked. Default deny rests on `entry_enabled`: an entry that holds a range, permission bits and an `allow_ns` equal to the probe `prot[1]` does not match while it is disabled. The granule is 4 KB with `allow_burst` 1 and 8 bytes with `allow_burst` 0. START_ADDR widens down and END_ADDR widens up, and a range that straddles a boundary admits both granules. The specification states no write-back timing, so the test grades the admitted set through the verdicts and logs the START_ADDR and END_ADDR read-back without grading it. Cites `hw/ip/axi_filter/doc/index.adoc` ("Instances"; "Match, Then Permit"; "Address Range Granule"; "Blocked Transactions"), `hw/ip/axi_filter/regs/gen/adoc/filter_ctrl.adoc` (`FILTER_CONFIG`, `START_ADDR`, `END_ADDR`), `hw/sys/smc/doc/assets/smc-traffic-filters.svg` (the five match conditions of `axi_filter_wrap`, including `src_id` against AxUSER[3:0]) `hw/sys/sep/doc/fabric.adoc` ("Top Level AXI4"; "Filtering and Protection"; "Transaction Routing") and `hw/sys/sep/doc/lifecycle_controller.adoc` ("Per-LC-state Feature Control Profile": the PROD state with no demotion keeps the inbound filter active).

*Test Coverage*: Four legs that share one stimulus family (programmed entries and one probe per cell), one run mode and one tool.

* Leg 1, match and priority: entry state (enabled, disabled) by attribute (range, `prot[1]`, burst, read permission, write permission) on each instance; the corner cells fall-through (a), permission block (b), burst fall-through (c, inbound only), disabled lowest entry (d), read and write that choose different entries (e) and no match (g); the destination classes SRAM and scratch inbound and the SMU window and the AP region outbound, each as a read and as a write.
* Leg 2, source ID: the non-zero values 1, 2, 4, 8 and 15 and one drawn non-zero value, the wildcard against AxUSER[3:0] 0 and 15 and two drawn values, the fall-through on a source-ID mismatch, an upper AxUSER bit, and the outbound exact and mismatch cells.
* Leg 3, default deny: the reset state, the armed-but-disabled state of all 48 entries and the enabled control entry per instance.
* Leg 4, granule: seven cells. Outbound 4 KB granule by the one, equal and straddle shapes. Inbound 4 KB granule by the equal and straddle shapes. 8-byte granule by the straddle shape on both instances.

Extends `sep_fabric_inbound_filter_rule_matrix_test`, which grades the per-entry inbound cells (enabled, range, burst, read and write permission), one `src_id` match value and one mismatch on entry 0, the 4 KB widening of one entry and the reset-state block. It also extends `sep_fabric_inbound_filter_window_walk_test` and `sep_fabric_outbound_remap_filter_walk_test`, which grade the one 8-byte granule that holds the probe address on both instances, `sep_lcc_uvm_inbound_filter_gating_test`, which grades the inbound block with the debug bit clear, `sep_fabric_output_remap_datapath_proxy_test`, which grades one outbound entry whose enable is cleared after it admitted an access, and `sep_fabric_slot_csr_strobe_rand_test`, which reads the reset values of all 48 entries. Only the new cells are graded here:

* leg 1: the outbound instance, the fall-through, permission-block and no-match corner cells, the read and write divergence, the permission block that hides an allow, and the inbound `prot[1]` mismatch cell (`allow_ns` different from the probe `prot[1]`) with its paired allow cell;
* leg 2: every source-ID cell beyond the single inbound match value, namely the non-zero values 1, 2, 4, 8 and 15 and one drawn non-zero value, the wildcard against AxUSER[3:0] 0 and 15 and two drawn values, the fall-through on a source-ID mismatch and the outbound exact and mismatch cells;
* leg 3: the armed-but-disabled sweep over all 48 entries, the outbound reset state and the enabled control entry per instance;
* leg 4: the outbound 4 KB granule, the equal shape on the 4 KB granule and the straddle shape on both granules and both instances.

The open tests keep the rest. Functional coverage: `sep_filter_match_cg` (`cp_fail_cond_fallthrough`, `cp_src_id_class`, `cp_ar_aw_independent`, `cp_winner_class`), `sep_filter_range_granule_cg` (`cp_granule_shape_inst`, `cp_probe_point_verdict`, `cp_subgranule_off`), `sep_filter_default_policy_cg` (`cp_deny_basis`, `cp_filter_active_block`), `sep_fabric_inbound_aperture_cg.cp_dest_class_verdict`, `sep_fabric_port_silence_cp.sil_inbound_refused` (cause `filter_deny`), existing `sep_inbound_filter_allow_cg`.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Bring up with real PROD fuse sense of the pinned image, so the inbound filter is active. The LSU reads `FEAT_CTRL` (64 bits) and compares it with the golden decode that the model computes from the profile table of `lifecycle_controller.adoc` for that image. The golden holds the SEP_DBG state that keeps the filter active. A mismatch prints `CTL-FILTER-ACTIVE FAIL` and stops the leaf.
. The LSU stages a non-zero marker at two consecutive SRAM words (16-byte aligned, so a 2-beat probe at the first word stays inside one 4 KB page and reads both) and at one cold scratch word, and reads all three back. The scratch register holds 32 data bits, so every compare of a scratch read uses bits [31:0], and bits [63:32] are reserved and logged only. These markers differ from every value that a probe writes. Each inbound write probe to a staged word drives a seeded value that differs from the value that the model holds for that word (the staged marker or the last write that landed), so a landed write changes the LSU read-back and a refused write leaves it unchanged.
. The LSU programs AP output remap region 0 with `valid` 1 and offset `0x20_0000_0000`, and STEE output remap region 0 with `valid` 1 and offset `0x28_0000_0000`. The model predicts the outbound address of an AP or STEE probe as the offset bits [55:19] joined with the region address bits [18:0] (`hw/ip/output_remap/regs/gen/adoc/output_remap.adoc`, `region_attrs`). The LSU reads the registers back. No filter entry is programmed at this step.
. Leg 3, reset state. SI reads and writes SRAM, scratch, a mailbox word and a crypto-region word, and SI reads the filter bank page and `SEP_CPU_CTRL`, each with `prot[1]` 0 and with `prot[1]` 1 (AxLEN 0, AxUSER 0). Error injection at `smn_inbound_axi_req_i`: every entry is disabled. The expected response is DECERR on RRESP or BRESP.
. The LSU reads back the staged SRAM and scratch words. Both hold their staged value.
. Error injection at the LSU outbound path: the LSU reads one SMU-window word (above `0x8000_1000`) and one AP region word (offset below `0x8_0000` in region 0), each with `prot[1]` 0 and with `prot[1]` 1. Every outbound entry is disabled. The expected response is DECERR.
. SI reads one word of the extension window (`0x2000_0000` to `0x3FFF_FFFF`, outside the eFuse shim window) and the word `0x4000_0100`, each with `prot[1]` 0 and with `prot[1]` 1. The responses are logged and are not graded. PR-EXT shows no handshake for the extension-window read.
. Leg 3, armed but disabled. The LSU programs all 16 inbound and all 32 outbound entries with the range START_ADDR 0, END_ADDR 2^48-1, which covers every probed address (SRAM, scratch, mailbox, crypto word, filter bank page, `SEP_CPU_CTRL`, the SMU window and the translated AP and STEE words), and with read and write permission, `src_id` 0, `allow_burst` 1 and `entry_enabled` 0. `allow_ns` is 0 on half of the entries of each instance and 1 on the other half, so for each probe `prot[1]` at least one entry would match if it were enabled. The LSU reads every entry back.
. Repeat steps 4 to 7 with the armed entries.
. Leg 3, wide-range control. For each probe `prot[1]` value and each instance, the LSU enables one armed entry whose `allow_ns` equals that `prot[1]` value, keeps its range START_ADDR 0, END_ADDR 2^48-1, and reads it back. SI reads the staged SRAM word and the staged scratch word, and the LSU reads one SMU-window word and one translated AP word. Every read answers OKAY, the inbound reads return the staged data and show their handshake on PR-XEXT or PR-CSR. With the inbound entry enabled, SI also reads the extension-window word of step 7 with the same `prot[1]`. The filter admits it, so PR-EXT shows one request at that address (the PR-EXT control of CHK-RESET-DENY). Its response is logged and is not graded. The LSU disables the entry again. This shows that the armed range matches a probe when the entry is enabled.
. Leg 3, control. The LSU selects the seeded control entry index `k` on each instance, programs it over the control probe range only (SRAM or scratch inbound, the SMU window or the AP region word outbound) with `allow_ns` equal to the probe `prot[1]`, and enables it. The other entries stay armed and disabled. The LSU reads the entry back.
. Leg 3, control probes. SI reads the control-eligible inbound probe and the LSU reads the control-eligible outbound probe. Both answer OKAY. The inbound probe shows its handshake on PR-XEXT or PR-CSR.
. The LSU disables every entry of both instances. Legs 1, 2 and 4 follow. Before each cell of those legs the LSU programs every entry that the cell uses, disables all others and reads each programmed register back.
. Leg 1, cell list. Per instance, the test builds one cell for each (entry state, attribute) pair (the burst attribute applies to inbound SRAM only), the corner cells a, b, d, e and g on both instances and the corner cell c inbound only. Each cell is a read probe and a write probe, each with its own `prot[1]`. Each (entry state, attribute) cell runs on one destination class of its instance that the seed draws: SRAM or scratch inbound, the SMU window or the AP region outbound. The draw gives each destination class at least one cell per instance, so every class runs as a read and as a write on every seed. The burst attribute applies to the inbound SRAM class only.
. For each cell the LSU programs a seeded stack of 3 to 6 entries at seeded indices. The entries overlap on a seeded window set. For the AP class the entries cover the translated AP address. Every entry gets a random `group_id`, and `src_id` is 0 on every entry of leg 1.
. For each (state, attribute) cell, one attribute of the covering entry is changed so that the probe fails exactly one match term or permission bit (range, `prot[1]`, burst, read permission, write permission, or `entry_enabled`). Run the probe. Error injection: the expected response is DECERR. Then run the paired allow cell, which is the same cell with that one attribute restored. The expected response is OKAY. The burst-attribute cell is inbound SRAM only: its probe is a 2-beat INCR (AxLEN 1) whose 16 bytes lie inside the covering range, the covering entry has `allow_burst` 0 in the deny cell and 1 in the allow cell, and the probe of every other cell has AxLEN 0, because a single beat always satisfies the burst term. The scratch class and the outbound instance do not draw the burst attribute.
. Corner cell a. The lowest entry rejects the probe on `prot[1]`, and a higher entry allows it. The probe is admitted by the higher entry.
. Corner cell b. The lowest entry matches with the permission bit clear, and a higher entry allows it. Error injection: the expected response is DECERR, the higher entry never counts.
. Corner cell c, inbound only. The lowest entry has `allow_burst` 0, the probe is a 2-beat INCR burst (AxLEN 1) to SRAM, and a higher entry has `allow_burst` 1. The probe is admitted by the higher entry. Its paired allow cell is an AxLEN 0 probe to the same address.
. Corner cell d. The lowest entry is disabled and covers the probe, and a higher entry allows it. The probe is admitted.
. Corner cell e. The read and the write of one address carry different `prot[1]` and select different entries, so one is admitted and the other is refused.
. Corner cell g. No enabled entry covers the probe. Error injection: the expected response is DECERR.
. Each corner cell runs once as a read and once as a write on each instance it applies to. Inbound probes come from SI with AxLEN 0, and AxLEN 1 INCR to SRAM runs only for the burst-attribute cell, corner cell c and their allow cells. Outbound probes come from the LSU with AxLEN 0.
. The model computes the expected verdict of every cell from the programmed fields and the probe attributes. Each probe response is compared with it.
. Leg 2 entries have read and write permission, `allow_ns` equal to the probe `prot[1]` and `allow_burst` 0, unless a cell names another value.
. Leg 2, inbound exact and mismatch. For each `src_id` value s of the set 1, 2, 4, 8, 15 and one non-zero value drawn from the other ten (seeded order), the LSU programs an entry over SRAM with `src_id` s. SI probes with AxUSER[3:0] = s (match) and with AxUSER[3:0] different from s, AxUSER[3:0] 0 included (mismatch), as read and as write.
. Leg 2, inbound wildcard. The LSU programs an entry over SRAM with `src_id` 0. SI probes with AxUSER[3:0] 0, 15 and two values drawn from 1 to 14, in a seeded order, as read and as write. Every probe is admitted.
. Leg 2, inbound fall-through. The lowest entry mismatches on the source ID, and a higher entry (wildcard or exact) admits. SI probes the covered address as a read and as a write, on every seed.
. Leg 2, inbound upper bits. When the inbound port carries more than 4 AxUSER bits, SI probes with an upper AxUSER bit set and AxUSER[3:0] equal to s against the entry of s. The probe matches.
. Leg 2, outbound mismatch. The LSU programs an outbound entry over the translated AP range with a non-zero `src_id` and enables it alone. The LSU reads and writes an AP word (source ID OTHERS). Error injection at the outbound filter input: the expected response is DECERR, because OTHERS does not equal the non-zero `src_id`. The LSU disables that entry, programs an entry over the same range with `src_id` 0 and enables it alone. The same probes are admitted: OKAY. The LSU repeats both runs for the STEE range.
. Leg 2, outbound exact. The LSU programs an outbound entry over an SMU-window word with `src_id` u (1 to 15) and enables it alone. The LSU probes the word with AxUSER[3:0] u (match, OKAY), then reprograms `src_id` to a non-zero value other than u and probes again (mismatch). Error injection at the outbound filter input: the expected response of the mismatch run is DECERR. The LSU bench master stands in for a CPU master. The source ID value of a real CPU master is not used. Reads and writes both run.
. Every deny cell of leg 2 runs next to a paired allow cell that differs in AxUSER[3:0] or in `src_id` only.
. Leg 4, granule. For each of the seven cells, draw a granule index `g` so that the granules `g` - 1 to `g` + 2 lie inside SRAM (inbound) or inside the SMU window above `0x8000_1000` (outbound). The first page of the SMU window is not used, because the bench responder decodes stores to `0x8000_0000` as console output.
. Program one entry over the cell range: `allow_burst` 1 for the 4 KB granule and 0 for the 8-byte granule, `src_id` 0, `allow_ns` equal to the probe `prot[1]`, read and write allowed. The shape sets START and END. One: both inside granule `g`, not aligned, START different from END (outbound 4 KB only). Equal: START equal to END, unaligned (4 KB granule, both instances). Straddle: START inside granule `g` and END inside granule `g` + 1 (both granules, both instances). Read START_ADDR and END_ADDR back and log them. The read-back is not graded.
. Probe each shape at the widened base minus 4, the widened base, the widened base plus 4, the last 4 bytes of the last admitted granule and the first 4 bytes after it. AxSIZE 2, AxLEN 0, read and write. Before each inbound cell the LSU stages a non-zero marker at every SRAM word that the cell probes and reads it back. Each write probe drives a seeded value that differs from that marker, and the LSU reads each probed word back after the probes. The model computes the admitted set from the widening rule. The probes outside the admitted set expect DECERR, and the probes inside expect OKAY.
. The LSU disables every entry and restores AP and STEE output remap region 0 to the reset value.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CTL-FILTER-ACTIVE
|(Precondition of every check of this leaf. It is not a counted check.) The bring-up image is PROD with SEC_DIS 0 and no demotion, so `FEAT_CTRL` equals the golden decode of the profile table and the SEP_DBG state keeps the inbound filter active (`lifecycle_controller.adoc`, "Per-LC-state Feature Control Profile"). `sep_fabric_inbound_filter_rule_matrix_test` and `sep_lcc_uvm_inbound_filter_gating_test` (CHK-PROD-FEAT) grade this value, so this leaf uses the compare only to stop on a wrong bring-up. A mismatch prints `CTL-FILTER-ACTIVE FAIL: feat_ctrl=0x<v> golden=0x<g>` and stops the leaf, so the named checks of the leaf are missing and the leaf fails. Anchor: the LSU read of `FEAT_CTRL` on the control bus. Evidence: `CTL-FILTER-ACTIVE LOG: feat_ctrl=0x<v> golden=0x<g> sep_dbg=<n>`.
|CHK-FILTER-CELL
|The response of every graded leg 1 cell equals the output of the filter reference model (`index.adoc`, "Match, Then Permit"). The graded cells are the new cells of the Test Coverage: every outbound cell, the corner cells on both instances, and the inbound `prot[1]` mismatch cell with its paired allow cell. The other inbound (entry state, attribute) cells (range, burst, read permission, write permission and `entry_enabled`) are graded by `sep_fabric_inbound_filter_rule_matrix_test`; here they run as controls, log `CTL-FILTER-CELL LOG` with the same fields and are not counted. An inbound allow cell also returns the staged data (read; both beats for a 2-beat probe; bits [31:0] only for a scratch word) or lands the written word on the LSU read-back (write; the written value differs from the value that the model holds for the word before the probe). A deny cell answers DECERR and never reaches the target: inbound, PR-XEXT or PR-CSR shows no handshake, and a refused write leaves the word at the value that the model holds on the LSU read-back; outbound, the DECERR is the verdict, and PR-OUT shows no handshake for the refused request. A wrong match term, a wrong winner, a permission bit read from the wrong entry, a fall-through that does not happen and a deny that leaks to the target each give a response or a handshake that differs from the model. Anchor: the SI and LSU responses, read data, the LSU read-back, PR-XEXT and PR-CSR (approved). Control: the paired allow cell drives the same probe. Evidence: `CHK-FILTER-CELL PASS: inst=in\|out dir=R\|W prot1=<0\|1> len=<n> winner=<idx\|none> perm=<0\|1> expect=<OKAY\|DECERR> got=<resp> data=0x<value> target_seen=<n> control_seen=<n>`.
|CHK-FILTER-SRC
|The verdict of every leg 2 cell equals the model output: a non-zero `src_id` matches only the equal AxUSER[3:0], `src_id` 0 matches every value, and a source-ID mismatch falls through to a higher entry (`smc-traffic-filters.svg`, `src_id` against AxUSER[3:0]). An upper AxUSER bit does not change the verdict. A filter that ignores the source ID, compares other bits, reads 0 as an exact value or lets an upper bit decide gives a verdict that differs from the model. Anchor: the SI and LSU responses (approved). Control: the paired cell that differs in AxUSER[3:0] or in `src_id` only. Evidence: `CHK-FILTER-SRC PASS: inst=in\|out dir=R\|W class=exact\|mismatch\|wildcard\|fallthrough\|upper_bits src_cfg=<n> user=<n> expect=<OKAY\|DECERR> got=<resp> control_resp=<resp>`.
|CHK-FILTER-RAND
|Stimulus-completeness control. Per seed and instance, the test runs at least one cell of each class: allow, block, fall-through, permission block, no match, a read and write pair that diverge, and a source-ID exact, mismatch and wildcard cell. Every count in the line is above zero. The DUT cannot fail this checker, and it makes no DUT claim. Evidence: `CHK-FILTER-RAND PASS: seed=<n> inst=in\|out cells=<n> allow=<n> block=<n> fallthrough=<n> perm_block=<n> no_match=<n> ar_aw_diverge=<n> src_exact=<n> src_mismatch=<n> src_wildcard=<n>`.
|CHK-RESET-DENY
|After reset, with no filter programmed, every outbound probe answers DECERR (`index.adoc`, "Instances"; "Blocked Transactions"). The inbound reset-state block is graded by `sep_fabric_inbound_filter_rule_matrix_test` and `sep_lcc_uvm_inbound_filter_gating_test`; here the inbound reset-state probes run as a control and log `CTL-RESET-DENY LOG inst=in` with the same fields: PR-XEXT and PR-CSR show no handshake (the mailbox has no approved tap, so its probes show the response alone), and the staged SRAM and scratch words read back unchanged after the write probes. The responses of the extension-window and `0x4000_0100` probes are logged only, because a healthy and a faulty filter both end in DECERR there (the extension tie-off and the crossbar limit answer DECERR even when the filter admits). The check grades the PR-EXT silence of the extension-window probe: PR-EXT shows no handshake for it. An entry that resets enabled, or an unmatched policy that admits, gives an OKAY answer or a handshake. Anchor: the SI and LSU responses, the LSU read-back, PR-XEXT, PR-CSR (approved) and PR-EXT. Controls: CHK-RESET-DENY-CONTROL, and the extension-window read of the wide-range control step, which the enabled entry admits and which shows one request on PR-EXT, so PR-EXT is live in the same leaf. A leaf whose PR-EXT control shows no request fails the check.
