Evidence: `CHK-RESET-DENY PASS: inst=out probes=<n> prot1_0=<n> prot1_1=<n> decerr=<n> target_seen=0 readback_same=<n> ext_seen=0 ext_ctrl_seen=1`.
|CHK-RESET-DENY-ARMED
|With all 48 entries armed and disabled, every graded probe of each `prot[1]` value answers DECERR, with the same inbound silence and the same read-back as CHK-RESET-DENY. A filter that matches on range and permission without `entry_enabled` answers OKAY or shows a handshake. Every entry holds the range START_ADDR 0, END_ADDR 2^48-1, which covers every graded probe address and lies below 2^56-1, so the check rests on no unspecified top-of-space behaviour. For each probe `prot[1]` at least one entry holds that covering range, permission bits, `src_id` 0 and an equal `allow_ns`, so the entry would match if it were enabled. The wide-range control step proves it: with one armed entry per instance enabled and the range unchanged, the control-eligible probes answer OKAY and the inbound probes show their handshake. A DUT that ignores `entry_enabled` therefore answers OKAY or shows a handshake in the disabled run, and the check fails. Anchor: the SI and LSU responses, the LSU read-back, PR-XEXT and PR-CSR (approved). Control: the wide-range control step and CHK-RESET-DENY-CONTROL. Evidence: `CHK-RESET-DENY-ARMED PASS: entries=48 enabled=0 range_end=2^48-1 armed_ns0=<n> armed_ns1=<n> probes=<n> prot1_0=<n> prot1_1=<n> decerr=<n> target_seen=0 wide_ctrl_resp=OKAY wide_ctrl_seen=<n>`.
|CHK-RESET-DENY-CONTROL
|With one entry per instance enabled over the probed unit only, the same control-eligible probe answers OKAY, and an inbound probe shows its handshake on PR-XEXT or PR-CSR. This proves that the probe path is alive, so the DECERR of the two deny checks comes from the filter. Anchor: the SI and LSU responses, PR-XEXT and PR-CSR (approved). Evidence: `CHK-RESET-DENY-CONTROL PASS: enabled_entry=<k> inst=in\|out probe=sram\|scratch\|smu\|ap prot1=<0\|1> resp=OKAY seen=1`.
|CHK-GRANULE
|The verdict at each leg 4 probe equals the admitted set that the model computes from the widening rule (`index.adoc`, "Address Range Granule"): START_ADDR widens down and END_ADDR widens up to the granule, a range shorter than the granule admits the whole granule, and a straddling range admits both granules. A refused inbound probe shows no PR-XEXT handshake, and a refused write leaves the probed SRAM word at the marker that the leg 4 cell staged there, on the LSU read-back. A DUT with no widening, a widening on the wrong side or a straddle that admits one granule answers a probe differently from the model. The START_ADDR and END_ADDR read-back is logged and not graded. Anchor: the SI and LSU responses, the LSU read-back and PR-XEXT (approved). Control: the admitted probes of the same shape answer OKAY and show their handshake. Evidence: `CHK-GRANULE PASS: inst=in\|out gran=8\|4096 shape=one\|equal\|straddle start=0x<hex> end=0x<hex> rb_start=0x<hex> rb_end=0x<hex> admitted=[0x<lo>,0x<hi>] probes=<n> allow=<n> block=<n> refused_seen=0 control_seen=<n>`.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope limit*: The test does not grade the `group_id` field, which has no effect in SEP (`index.adoc`, "Instances"; a grade needs a probe that carries a group, see <<sep-vplan-phase3-blocked,Blocked features>>), the `locked` bit, the filter register storage, or the SEP debug bypass. The per-entry inbound cells, the single-granule probes and the reset values of the entries stay with the open tests named under Test Coverage. The extension-window and `0x4000_0100` reset-state responses are logged only. The test sends no outbound burst and no inbound burst to a register region, because the specification states no response for a burst to a register region. The test grades the lowest-match rule on the programmed fields only and does not claim a verdict for an inverted range or a range that touches 2^56-1.

'''''

[[sep_fabric_outbound_route_attr_test]]
===== 2.27 `sep_fabric_outbound_route_attr_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: Fabric and remap

*Run mode*: `no_cpu` (`lsu_stub_all_live`, group `cpu_stub`, `testlists/system.toml`), real PROD fuse sense (no `+skip_fuse_sense`) with a pinned image: PROD, SEC_DIS 0, and fixed `SIP_DIS` and `SYS_DIS` values whose DBG_1 bit 0 is clear in both, then one DEMOTE_1 write for the no-bypass leg, 4 seeds. Tool: Verilator and VCS. VCS is required for the X check on the PR-OUT capture.

*Source Module*: `sep_fabric_outbound_route_attr_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (LSU master on `s_axi`, SI master on `m_axi`); `tb/sep_outbound_mbx.sv` (outbound responder: OKAY and zero read data for any address); the filter reference model of this bucket (written from `hw/ip/axi_filter/doc/index.adoc`, never from the RTL). Probes. Approved: the LSU and SI responses and read data, the LSU read-back of local words, the LSU and SI reads of `FEAT_CTRL`. PR-OUT (an observation tap the test adds to the SEP_TB_ARCH observation-probe list), for CHK-OUT-CAPTURE, CHK-OUT-NOEXTRA and the disabled-pair silence of CHK-OUT-ROUTE. No inject.

*Randomization*: `SepSeededRng` from the run seed, RANDCFG. Dimensions: region index (0 to 15 per remap), offset bits 55:19 (non-identity), direction order, AxPROT value, LSU AxUSER[3:0] u (1 to 15, upper AxUSER bits 0). The SMU aperture stays at the reset pair (`0x8000_0000`, size `0x4000_0000`). Legal range per `hw/ip/output_remap/regs/gen/adoc/output_remap.adoc` (`region_attrs`). Rejection list: an offset equal to the region identity; an offset sum at or above 2^56; a translated AP or STEE address, or the untranslated word of the step 9 pair, that lies inside the SMU aperture, inside the local pair range, or inside the range of any other pair or stack entry that is enabled in the same step. `reseed = 4` samples different region indices, offsets, AxPROT values and u. Every route class runs in both directions on every seed.

*Objective*: The route demux sends the SMU aperture (reset `SMU_GLOBAL_BASE_ADDR` and `SMU_REGION_SIZE`) and the AP and STEE regions through their output remaps to `smn_outbound_axi_req_o`. A scratch or system-CSR request does not leave on that port. The AP and STEE remaps set the source ID in AxUSER to OTHERS (zero). Other traffic keeps the AxUSER of its initiator. AxPROT passes unchanged. The outbound filter checks address, NS and source ID after remapping and has no bypass. The test grades the forcing of OTHERS through the outbound filter: while the LSU drives a non-zero AxUSER[3:0] `u`, an AP or STEE request carries OTHERS, so it does not match an entry whose `src_id` is `u` and it matches an entry whose `src_id` is 0. The route of an address at or above `0x1_0000_0000` is graded by the hit cells of `sep_fabric_alias_remap_attr_rand_test`, and the NS mismatch response and the exact source-ID match of an SMU word by `sep_fabric_filter_match_priority_rand_test`. The specification states two conflicting rules for an address below `0x1_0000_0000` outside every window, so the test does not write the SMU aperture registers and does not grade a route outside every window. Cites `hw/sys/sep/doc/fabric.adoc` ("Fabric Topology", output fabric; "Transaction Routing"), `hw/sys/sep/doc/assets/sep-output-fabric.svg`, `hw/sys/sep/regs/gen/adoc/blocks/sep_cpu_ctrl.adoc` (`SMU_GLOBAL_BASE_ADDR`, `SMU_REGION_SIZE`), `hw/ip/output_remap/regs/gen/adoc/output_remap.adoc` (`region_attrs`), `hw/ip/axi_filter/doc/index.adoc` ("Match, Then Permit"; "Blocked Transactions") `hw/sys/smc/doc/assets/smc-traffic-filters.svg` (`src_id` against AxUSER[3:0]) and `hw/sys/sep/doc/lifecycle_controller.adoc` ("Per-LC-state Feature Control Profile": PROD with SEC_DIS 0 and the demotion of DBG_1).

*Test Coverage*: The SMU reset aperture (first, middle and last word) and the AP and STEE regions with a non-identity offset, each on read and write and each with `prot[1]` 0 and 1; the source-ID stack over the AP and STEE words with the LSU AxUSER[3:0] non-zero; the outbound pair after DEMOTE_1; and local scratch and `SEP_SW_DEBUG` accesses behind an outbound pair that would admit them. Extends `sep_fabric_outbound_remap_filter_walk_test` and `sep_fabric_output_remap_datapath_proxy_test`, which grade the offset translation and the low-bit pass-through of the AP and STEE regions through read requests and the valid-clear pass-through, `sep_lcc_uvm_inbound_filter_gating_test` and `sep_lcc_demote_feat_ctrl_matrix_test`, which grade the `FEAT_CTRL` value and the inbound filter bypass after DEMOTE_1, and `sep_address_map_test`, which grades the local scratch and `SEP_SW_DEBUG` accesses with no outbound entry. Only the new cells are graded here: the SMU aperture on read and write, the AP and STEE writes, the forcing of OTHERS on AP and STEE traffic and the outbound pair with the inbound filter bypassed. The absence of scratch and `SEP_SW_DEBUG` requests on the port and the PR-OUT capture of AxPROT, AxUSER and write data are new cells, and this test grades them. The AP and STEE read cells run as controls, and the open tests grade them. The open tests keep the rest. Functional coverage: `sep_fabric_outbound_route_cg` (`cp_route_class_dir` for the SMU, AP and STEE cells, `cp_smu_aperture_cfg`, `cp_out_attr`), `sep_remap_output_offset_cg.cp_instance_dir`, `sep_filter_match_cg.cp_fail_cond_fallthrough` (the outbound source-ID mismatch cells), `sep_filter_default_policy_cg.cp_dbg_bypass`, `sep_fabric_port_silence_cp` (`sil_out_local_target`, `sil_out_filter_deny`).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Bring up with real PROD fuse sense, so the inbound filter is active. Read `FEAT_CTRL` and log it (the no-bypass leg uses it as a logged precondition). Read `SMU_GLOBAL_BASE_ADDR` and `SMU_REGION_SIZE` and log them. The test never writes them.
. Draw the AP region index `i`, the STEE region index `j`, their offsets `O_ap` and `O_stee` (bits 55:19 differ from the region identity), the AxPROT values, the direction order and `u`. The in-region word address is `a` = `0x100` (below `0x8_0000`). The model predicts the AP address as `{O_ap[55:19], a[18:0]}` and the STEE address as `{O_stee[55:19], a[18:0]}`.
. The LSU programs AP output remap region `i` with `valid` 1 and offset `O_ap`, and STEE output remap region `j` with `valid` 1 and offset `O_stee`. The LSU reads the registers back.
. Every outbound entry of this test comes as a pair over one range: one entry with `allow_ns` 0 and one with `allow_ns` 1, read and write allowed, `src_id` 0, so a probe with either `prot[1]` value matches one entry of the pair. The pairs cover the SMU aperture `0x8000_0000` to `0xBFFF_FFFF` (the SMU pair), the translated AP word (the AP pair), the translated STEE word (the STEE pair) and the local range `0x1080_2000` to `0x10A3_1FFF` (the local pair). The pairs use entry indices 2 and above. Entries 0 and 1 are for the source-ID stack. The LSU enables the SMU pair and reads it back.
. SMU reset aperture. The LSU reads and writes the first word `0x8000_0000`, the middle word `0xA000_0000` and the last word `0xBFFF_FFF8` with `prot[1]` 0 and with `prot[1]` 1 (the other AxPROT bits are seeded) and AxUSER[3:0] `u`. Each answers OKAY. The expected PR-OUT capture is one AW or AR at the issued address with the issued AxPROT and AxUSER `u`, and the W data and strobe as issued.
. The LSU disables the SMU pair. Error injection at the outbound filter input: the LSU reads and writes the first word again. The expected response is DECERR, and no PR-OUT capture shows. The LSU enables the SMU pair again.
. AP region. The LSU enables the AP pair. The LSU reads and writes `0x1100_0000` + `i` * `0x8_0000` + `a` with `prot[1]` 0 and with `prot[1]` 1. Each answers OKAY. The read cells are controls that the open tests grade; the write cells are graded here. The expected PR-OUT capture shows the translated address, AxUSER 0 although the LSU drove `u`, AxPROT as issued, and the W data and strobe as issued.
. The LSU disables the AP pair. Error injection at the outbound filter input: the LSU repeats the AP accesses. The expected response is DECERR.
. The LSU enables an outbound pair over the untranslated AP word only (the AP pair stays disabled). Error injection at the outbound filter input: the LSU repeats the AP accesses. The filter sees the translated address, so the expected response is DECERR. The LSU disables this pair.
. STEE region. Repeat steps 7 to 9 for `0x1180_0000` + `j` * `0x8_0000` + `a` and the STEE pair.
. Source-ID stack. For each class (AP word, STEE word), the LSU programs outbound entry 0 over the translated range with `src_id` `u`, read and write permission clear, and entry 1 over the same range with `src_id` 0 and both permissions set. Both entries are enabled and use the `allow_ns` of the probe `prot[1]`. The SMU pair stays enabled. The LSU reads the entries back.
. The LSU reads and writes each class word with AxUSER[3:0] `u`. AP and STEE requests carry OTHERS, skip entry 0 and are admitted by entry 1: OKAY.
. Control for the forcing. The LSU sets the `src_id` of entry 0 to 0 and keeps its permissions clear. Error injection at the outbound filter input: the LSU repeats the AP and STEE requests with AxUSER[3:0] `u`. Entry 0 matches the requests and refuses them. The expected response is DECERR. The LSU disables entries 0 and 1.
. Local addresses. The LSU enables the local pair. The LSU stages a non-zero marker in cold scratch word `0x1080_2000` and in `SEP_SW_DEBUG`. The LSU reads both words (8 bytes) and logs the response and bits [31:0] of the data. The log is a control and is not graded, because the open address map test grades the data of these registers. The LSU reads the SMU word `0xA000_0000` as the capture control (the SMU pair is enabled). The expected PR-OUT result is no capture for the scratch and `SEP_SW_DEBUG` reads and a capture for the SMU read. The LSU restores `SEP_SW_DEBUG` to its reset value and disables the local pair.
. No-bypass leg. The LSU reads `FEAT_CTRL` (64 bits) on the control bus and logs it. With every inbound entry disabled, SI reads `FEAT_CTRL` and logs the response. Both reads are logged and not graded, because `sep_lcc_uvm_inbound_filter_gating_test` and `sep_lcc_demote_feat_ctrl_matrix_test` grade the golden value and the inbound block.
. The LSU writes `DEMOTE_1` with the `demote` bit (bit 0) set and reads `DEMOTE_1` back. The LSU reads `FEAT_CTRL` and logs it. The SI read of the next step starts only after this read.
. SI reads `FEAT_CTRL` with no inbound entry. The read answers OKAY, which shows that the inbound filter is bypassed. This is the precondition of the check. When it does not answer OKAY, the leaf prints `CHK-OUT-NOBYPASS FAIL: bypass_not_established` and skips the next two steps.
. The LSU disables the SMU pair and reads the SMU word `0xA000_0000`. Error injection at the outbound filter input: the expected response is DECERR, with no capture on PR-OUT.
. The LSU enables the SMU pair and reads the SMU word `0xA000_0000` again. The read answers OKAY.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-OUT-ROUTE
|The graded cells are the SMU aperture on read and on write, and the AP and STEE writes. Each answers OKAY with an enabled outbound entry over the class, and DECERR with no enabled entry (`fabric.adoc`, "Transaction Routing"; `index.adoc`, "Blocked Transactions"). For AP and STEE the entry covers the translated range, and an enabled entry over the untranslated range alone gives DECERR on the write, because the filter checks the address after remapping. A class that does not reach the outbound filter, or a remap that does not move the address, gives an answer that differs from the model. The AP and STEE read cells, with their disabled and untranslated-only variants, run as controls and are not graded here: the open tests grade them (`sep_fabric_output_remap_datapath_proxy_test`, `sep_fabric_outbound_remap_filter_walk_test`), and the PASS line does not count them as graded classes. For the SMU first-word read and write with the SMU pair disabled, PR-OUT shows no capture from the request to the DECERR response. The same request with the pair enabled captures on PR-OUT, and a leaf whose enabled-pair request shows no PR-OUT capture fails the check. Anchor: the LSU responses, with the responder OKAY as the admitted verdict (approved), and PR-OUT (an observation tap the test adds to the SEP_TB_ARCH observation-probe list) for the disabled-pair silence. Control: the same request answers OKAY with the entry enabled and DECERR with it disabled, and the read cells drive the same classes. Evidence: `CHK-OUT-ROUTE PASS: class=smu\|ap\|stee dir=<R and W for smu, W for ap and stee> entry_on_resp=OKAY entry_off_resp=DECERR untranslated_only_resp=DECERR\|na control_reads=<n> entry_off_out_seen=0\|na entry_on_out_seen=1\|na`.
|CHK-OUT-USER
|Behind the source-ID stack, AP and STEE requests with AxUSER[3:0] `u` from the LSU are admitted, on read and on write: OKAY (`fabric.adoc`, "Transaction Routing": the AP and STEE remappers replace the source ID with `OTHERS`; `smc-traffic-filters.svg`). A remapper that keeps the initiator AxUSER matches entry 0 (`src_id` `u`, permissions clear) and answers DECERR. Anchor: the LSU responses (approved). Control: with the `src_id` of entry 0 set to 0, the same requests answer DECERR, so entry 0 is the entry that decides and the stack is alive. The AxUSER retention of an SMU request is graded by leg 2 of `sep_fabric_filter_match_priority_rand_test` and by CHK-OUT-CAPTURE. Evidence: `CHK-OUT-USER PASS: class=ap\|stee dir=R\|W user_issued=<u> resp=OKAY control_resp=DECERR`.
|CHK-OUT-NOBYPASS
|With the inbound filter bypassed (the precondition step: the SI read of `FEAT_CTRL` answers OKAY with no inbound entry after DEMOTE_1), the LSU read of the SMU word answers DECERR with the SMU pair disabled and OKAY with it enabled (`fabric.adoc`, "Filtering and Protection": the outbound filter has no bypass). A debug bypass that reaches the outbound filter admits the request with the pair disabled. The `FEAT_CTRL` value and the inbound bypass are graded by `sep_lcc_uvm_inbound_filter_gating_test` and `sep_lcc_demote_feat_ctrl_matrix_test`, and this check grades only the outbound pair. Anchor: the LSU responses (approved). Control: the enabled pair, and the OKAY of the SI read that shows the bypass. Evidence: `CHK-OUT-NOBYPASS PASS: bypass_pre=OKAY feat_after=0x<v1> disabled_resp=DECERR enabled_resp=OKAY`.
|CHK-OUT-NOEXTRA
|PR-OUT shows no capture for the LSU reads of the cold scratch word and `SEP_SW_DEBUG` behind an enabled local pair that covers them (`fabric.adoc`, "Fabric Topology": a local address stays local). The response and the data of these reads are logged and not graded, because the open address map test grades them. Anchor: PR-OUT (an observation tap the test adds to the SEP_TB_ARCH observation-probe list). Control: the SMU read of the same leaf captures on PR-OUT. Evidence: `CHK-OUT-NOEXTRA PASS: local_reads=<n> out_seen=0 control_out=<n>`.
|CHK-OUT-CAPTURE
|Each PR-OUT capture matches its issued request: AxPROT as issued, the W data and strobe as issued, the predicted address, AxUSER 0 for an AP or STEE request, and the issued AxUSER for an SMU request (`fabric.adoc`, "Transaction Routing"). X or Z in a captured field fails on VCS. Anchor: PR-OUT (an observation tap the test adds to the SEP_TB_ARCH observation-probe list). Control: the capture cells themselves drive PR-OUT. Evidence: `CHK-OUT-CAPTURE PASS: class=smu\|ap\|stee dir=R\|W issued=0x<addr> seen=0x<addr> prot=<n> user_issued=<u> user_seen=<n> wdata=0x<d>\|na wstrb=0x<s>\|na`.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope limit*: The test does not write the SMU aperture registers, does not grade the route of an address below `0x1_0000_0000` outside every window (the specification states two conflicting rules: the routing prose sends it out to the SMN and the output fabric text returns it to the peripheral crossbar), and does not grade the offset translation of the AP and STEE read cells or the valid-clear pass-through. Those stay with `sep_fabric_outbound_remap_filter_walk_test` and `sep_fabric_output_remap_datapath_proxy_test`, which also keep the grading of the AP and STEE read cells that run here as controls. The route of an address at or above `0x1_0000_0000` is graded with the alias hit cells of `sep_fabric_alias_remap_attr_rand_test`. The NS mismatch response of the outbound filter and the exact source-ID match of an SMU word stay with `sep_fabric_filter_match_priority_rand_test`. The `FEAT_CTRL` value and the inbound bypass stay with the open lifecycle tests. The test does not claim the AxUSER of a real CPU master, only that the AP and STEE remappers force OTHERS while the LSU bench master drives another value.

'''''

[[sep_fabric_alias_remap_attr_rand_test]]
===== 2.28 `sep_fabric_alias_remap_attr_rand_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: Fabric and remap

*Run mode*: `no_cpu` (`lsu_stub_all_live`, group `cpu_stub`, `testlists/system.toml`), `+skip_fuse_sense`, 4 seeds. Tool: Verilator and VCS. VCS is required for the X check on AxCACHE at the alias remap output.

*Source Module*: `sep_fabric_alias_remap_attr_rand_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (LSU master on `s_axi`); `tb/sep_outbound_mbx.sv` (outbound responder: OKAY and zero read data for any address); the filter reference model of this bucket. Probes. Approved: the LSU response and the outbound-filter verdict (an outbound entry over the predicted address). PR-ALIAS (address and AxCACHE at the input and at the output of the local-master alias remap; an observation tap the test adds to the SEP_TB_ARCH observation-probe list), for the AxCACHE checks: CHK-ALIAS-CACHE and the AxCACHE part of the valid-clear control. PR-OUT is not used. No inject.

*Randomization*: `SepSeededRng` from the run seed, RANDCFG. Dimensions: region index, start page `S`, page count (2 to 5, inside the SMU window above `0x8000_1000`), offset `O` (bits 55:12, bit 32 set, sum below 2^56), `cacheable` `c`, incoming AxCACHE `a` (from the AXI4-defined encodings `0x0`, `0x2`, `0x3` and `0xF`), and the direction order. Legal range per `hw/ip/axi_alias_remap/regs/gen/adoc/alias_remap.adoc` (`region_start`, `region_end`, `region_attrs`). Rejection list: `S` equal to or above `E`; overlapping valid regions (the specification states no priority); an offset carry out of bit 55 (the specification states no result); `c` equal to `a`. `reseed = 4` samples different regions, pages, offsets, `c` and `a`. The six boundary classes and the two AxCACHE corners run on every seed.

*Objective*: A transaction hits a remap region when `start_addr <= address < end_addr`, with `end_addr` non-inclusive. A hit adds the offset to address bits [55:12] and replaces all four AxCACHE bits with the `cacheable` field. A miss keeps the address and AxCACHE. The specification states AxCACHE pass-through after the alias remap only for AxPROT, so AxCACHE is graded at the alias remap output (PR-ALIAS) and not at PR-OUT. The specification states no AxCACHE pass-through from the LSU port to the alias remap input, so a miss cell compares the output AxCACHE with the input AxCACHE of the same request, both on PR-ALIAS, and a hit cell compares the output AxCACHE with `c`. The address is graded through outbound-filter verdicts. Cites `hw/ip/axi_alias_remap/regs/gen/adoc/alias_remap.adoc` (`region_start`, `region_end`, `region_attrs`), `hw/sys/sep/doc/fabric.adoc` ("Address Remapping") and `hw/ip/axi_filter/doc/index.adoc` ("Address Range Granule"; "Blocked Transactions").

*Test Coverage*: Six boundary classes on read and write (byte `S` - 1, byte `S`, a middle page, byte `E` - 1, byte `E`, a page above `E`), the AxCACHE override on all four bits (`c` = `0xF` over `a` = `0x0`, and `c` = `0x0` over `a` = `0xF`) on read and write, and a valid-clear run of the same region. Extends `sep_fabric_local_alias_offset_walk_test` and `sep_fabric_local_alias_datapath_test`, which grade the hit and miss address rule, the start-hit and end-miss cells and the valid gate. Only the new cells are graded here: the byte classes at `S` - 1 and `E` - 1, a middle page and a page above `E`, the AxCACHE override on all four bits, and the six classes with `valid` 0 for an offset that carries into bit 32. The `S` and `E` classes stay as controls. The open tests keep the rest. Every hit translates to an address at or above `0x1_0000_0000`, because the offset has bit 32 set, so the hit cells are also the read and write cells of the route class at or above 4 GiB. Functional coverage: `sep_remap_alias_cg` (`cp_boundary_dir`, `cp_cacheable_override_dir`, `cp_valid_gate`, `cp_offset_expansion`) and `sep_fabric_outbound_route_cg.cp_route_class_dir` (the `ge_4g` cells).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Bring up with `+skip_fuse_sense`. Read `FEAT_CTRL` and log it.
. Draw the region `k`, the start page `S`, the page count and so `E`, the offset `O`, `c` and `a` with `a` different from `c`. The other 15 alias regions stay invalid.
. The LSU programs alias region `k`: `region_start` = `S`, `region_end` = `E`, `region_attrs` with `valid` 1, `cacheable` `c` and `offset` `O`. The LSU reads the three registers back.
. The model computes, for each class source address `src`, the hit flag from `S` <= `src` < `E` and the translated address `((src>>12)+(O>>12))<<12 \| src[11:0]`. The classes are byte `S` - 1, byte `S`, the first byte of page `S` + 1 (the middle page), byte `E` - 1, byte `E` and the first byte of the page above `E`.
. For each class and each direction, the LSU programs one outbound entry over the 8-byte granule of the translated address (`allow_burst` 0, `src_id` 0, `allow_ns` equal to the probe `prot[1]`, read and write allowed) and disables all other outbound entries. The LSU reads the entry back.
. The LSU issues a 1-byte probe (AxSIZE 0, AxLEN 0) at `src` with AxCACHE `a`. For a hit the expected response is OKAY. For a miss the expected response is DECERR. The LSU logs the response.
. The LSU programs the entry over the 8-byte granule of `src` instead and disables the entry of step 5. The LSU reads it back and repeats the probe. For a hit the expected response is DECERR. For a miss the expected response is OKAY.
. Run steps 5 to 7 for the six classes, read and write.
. AxCACHE corners. For the middle-page hit probe, run `c` = `0xF` over `a` = `0x0` and then `c` = `0x0` over `a` = `0xF`, each as a read and as a write. The LSU reprograms `cacheable`, programs the outbound entry over the translated 8-byte granule as in step 5 and reads both back before each run. The expected PR-ALIAS value is AxCACHE equal to `c` for the hit.
. For the byte `E` miss probe, with the outbound entry over the source granule, run AxCACHE `a` as a read and as a write. The expected AxCACHE at the PR-ALIAS output equals the AxCACHE at the PR-ALIAS input of the same request.
. Valid-clear run. The LSU reprograms region `k` with the same bounds and offset, `cacheable` `c` and `valid` 0. It reads the registers back. It repeats steps 5 to 7 for the six classes, read and write. Every class is a miss.
. Valid-clear run with `cacheable` `0xF`. The LSU reprograms `cacheable` = `0xF` with `valid` 0 and repeats the middle-page probe with AxCACHE `0x0` and an outbound entry over the source granule, read and write. The model expects a miss. The expected AxCACHE at the PR-ALIAS output equals the AxCACHE at the PR-ALIAS input of the same request.
. The LSU restores alias region `k` to the reset values and disables every outbound entry.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-ALIAS-CLASS
|For every class the model computes hit or miss from `start_addr <= address < end_addr` (`alias_remap.adoc`, `region_start` and `region_end`). A hit is admitted at the address `((src>>12)+(O>>12))<<12 \| src[11:0]` and refused at the source address. A miss is admitted at the source address and refused at the translated address. An inclusive end, an exclusive start or a wrong offset each flips one verdict of the pair. Anchor: the LSU responses with the outbound-filter verdict as the address anchor (approved). The valid-clear run is graded: with `valid` 0 every class is admitted at the source address and refused at the translated address, so a region with `valid` 0 does not apply the offset that carries into bit 32. Control: the `S` and `E` classes. Evidence: `CHK-ALIAS-CLASS PASS: region=<k> valid=<0\|1> class=below\|start\|mid\|end_m1\|end\|above dir=R\|W src=0x<addr> predicted=0x<addr> hit=<0\|1> hit_addr_resp=<code> src_addr_resp=<code>`.
|CHK-ALIAS-CACHE
|The AxCACHE at the alias remap output equals `c` for a hit, on all four bits (`alias_remap.adoc`, `region_attrs`: the field overrides all existing AxCACHE bits). For a miss and for the valid-clear run, the output AxCACHE equals the input AxCACHE of the same request (`fabric.adoc`, "Address Remapping": an invalid entry is a transparent pass-through). A partial AxCACHE override shows a different value on at least one bit when the input differs from `c` on all four bits. A corner cell or a valid-clear `cacheable` `0xF` cell fills its bin only when the input AxCACHE differs from `c` on all four bits; otherwise the cell is graded, logged with the input value, and fills no bin. X or Z in AxCACHE fails on VCS. Anchor: the input and output requests on PR-ALIAS (an observation tap the test adds to the SEP_TB_ARCH observation-probe list). Control: the miss cells for the hit cells. Evidence: `CHK-ALIAS-CACHE PASS: region=<k> dir=R\|W cache_issued=0x<a> cache_remap_in=0x<i> cache_remap_out=0x<o> expect=0x<c\|i> hit=<0\|1>`.
|CHK-ALIAS-RAND
|Stimulus-completeness control. Per seed, the test runs at least one hit, one miss and one AxCACHE override. The DUT cannot fail this checker, and it makes no DUT claim. Evidence: `CHK-ALIAS-RAND PASS: seed=<n> hits=<n> misses=<n> cache_override=<n>`.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope limit*: The test does not draw empty, inverted or overlapping regions, an offset carry out of bit 55, or an offset with bit 32 clear, because the specification states no result for them. The test does not grade AxCACHE at the outbound port, because the specification states AxCACHE pass-through after the alias remap only for AxPROT. The hit and miss address rule at `S` and `E`, the start-hit and end-miss cells and the valid gate stay with `sep_fabric_local_alias_offset_walk_test` and `sep_fabric_local_alias_datapath_test`.

'''''

[[sep_fabric_smc_route_test]]
===== 2.29 `sep_fabric_smc_route_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: Fabric and remap

*Run mode*: `no_cpu` (`lsu_stub_all_live`, group `cpu_stub`, `testlists/system.toml`), `+skip_fuse_sense`, 3 seeds, one testlist entry. The seed draws configuration A (base `0x4000_0000`, size `0x0100_0000`) or configuration B (base `0x9000_0000`, size `0x0100_0000`), and the leaf drives the aperture inputs through BH-SMC before it releases reset. Tool: Verilator and VCS. VCS is required for the X check on the SMC read data of CHK-SMC-ROUTE.

*Source Module*: `sep_fabric_smc_route_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (LSU master on `s_axi`); `tb/sep_outbound_mbx.sv` (outbound responder: OKAY and zero read data for any address). Probes and hook. Approved: the LSU response and read data, the read of `SMC_FUSE_SENSE_STATUS`. Added hook: BH-SMC, a top-port drive that the test adds to the port table of the HDL Top section of `docs/SEP_TB_ARCH.adoc` (the drive of `smc_global_base_addr_i` and `smc_region_size_i`, from plusargs or from the leaf before reset release, and an SMC responder that stores and returns written data on `sep_ext_to_smc_axi` in the `lsu_stub_all_live` target; the default bench ties both inputs to 0 and has no SMC responder in this target). PR-SMC (`sep_ext_to_smc_axi_req_o`) and PR-OUT are observation taps the test adds to the SEP_TB_ARCH observation-probe list. No inject.

*Randomization*: `SepSeededRng` from the run seed, RANDCFG. Dimension: the configuration, A or B, with equal weight. The two apertures, the markers and the probe words are fixed, because the specification states no legal aperture values. The SMU aperture stays at its reset values. A seed runs the cells of the drawn configuration only, because the specification states no behaviour for an aperture change after reset and a second configuration would need a second reset. The configuration bins are seed-dependent and close on a merge of regressions (`SEP_FCOV.adoc`, fabric and remap groups); one regression of 3 seeds misses one configuration with a probability of 25 %, so no single regression claims both configurations.

*Objective*: The route demux matches the SMC aperture that the SMC supplies on `smc_global_base_addr_i` and `smc_region_size_i` first in the order. It sends that traffic to `sep_ext_to_smc_axi_req_o` without the outbound filter. The route demux order decides the route: only the aperture that the SMC supplies goes to the SMC port, so the static SMC row of the memory map (`0x4000_0000` to `0x7FFF_FFFF`) names the SMC address space and is not the selector. Requests to the SMC are issued only after `smc_fuse_sense_done` reads 1, because the register description states that they hang until then. Cites `hw/sys/sep/doc/fabric.adoc` ("Fabric Topology", output fabric; "Transaction Routing"), `hw/sys/sep/doc/port_table.adoc` (`smc_global_base_addr_i`, `smc_region_size_i`, `sep_ext_to_smc_axi_req_o`), `hw/sys/sep/doc/peripheral_subsystem.adoc`, `hw/sys/sep/regs/gen/adoc/memory_map.adoc` (SMC row), `hw/sys/sep/regs/gen/adoc/blocks/sep_cpu_ctrl.adoc` (`SMU_GLOBAL_BASE_ADDR` and `SMU_REGION_SIZE` reset values, `SMC_FUSE_SENSE_STATUS`), `hw/sys/sep/doc/assets/sep-output-fabric.svg` and `hw/ip/axi_filter/doc/index.adoc` ("Blocked Transactions").

*Test Coverage*: The first and last aperture word of configuration A on read and write; the word above the aperture top, inside the memory-map row of the SMC, on read and write; and the first-match order against the overlapping reset SMU window (configuration B). A seed runs the cells of the configuration that it draws. The `rom_fw` boot tests (for example `sep_rom_non_secure_boot_test`) grade the basic configuration A route and the unfiltered path: the Boot ROM writes and reads back four patterns at an SMC scratch word through the aperture while every outbound entry is disabled, and a mismatch fails the boot. This entry extends them. Only the new cells are graded here: the aperture edge words, the word above the aperture top and the configuration B first-match order. The unfiltered accesses of this entry and the DECERR answer to an SMU-window read with every outbound entry disabled are graded in CHK-SMC-ROUTE: they show that the aperture bypasses the outbound filter while the filter refuses other traffic. `sep_address_map_test` reads the SMU registers only. Functional coverage: `sep_fabric_outbound_route_cg` (`cp_route_class_dir` bin `smc_aperture`, `cp_smc_cfg_class_dir`, `cp_smc_readiness`), `sep_fabric_port_silence_cp` (`sil_smc_outside_aperture`, `sil_out_on_smc_route`).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Draw the configuration from the seed, log `CFG-SMC cfg=A|B base=0x<b> size=0x<s>`, and drive its aperture inputs through BH-SMC before reset release. Bring up. Read `FEAT_CTRL` and log it. Read `SMU_GLOBAL_BASE_ADDR` and `SMU_REGION_SIZE` and log them. The test never writes them.
. Read `SMC_FUSE_SENSE_STATUS` until `smc_fuse_sense_done` is 1, in a bounded wait. A timeout fails the test. Log the number of reads. No SMC request is issued before this step ends.
. Configuration A (steps 3 to 8 run when the seed draws A). The LSU programs outbound pair 0 over `0x4000_0000` to `0xBFFF_FFFF` (one entry with `allow_ns` 0 and one with `allow_ns` 1, read and write allowed, `src_id` 0) and enables it. The LSU reads the pair back. A request that took the outbound path would pass the filter and show on PR-OUT.
. The LSU writes and reads the first aperture word `0x4000_0000` and the last aperture word `0x40FF_FFFC` with two distinct fixed markers. Each read answers OKAY with its marker. PR-SMC counts one AW and one AR for each word. PR-OUT shows no handshake.
. PR-OUT control. The LSU reads `0x8000_0100` (SMU window, outside the aperture). The read answers OKAY and PR-OUT captures it.
. Unfiltered leg. The LSU disables pair 0, so all 32 outbound entries are disabled, and reads the pair back. The LSU repeats the accesses of step 4. Each answers OKAY, and PR-SMC counts it.
. Error injection at the route demux input: the LSU reads `0x8000_0100` (SMU window) with all outbound entries disabled. The expected response is DECERR on RRESP (`index.adoc`, "Blocked Transactions"). PR-OUT shows no handshake.
. Static-row leg. Error injection at the route demux input: the LSU reads and writes `0x4100_0000`, one word above the aperture top and inside the memory-map row of the SMC. The route demux sends only the supplied aperture to the SMC port (`fabric.adoc`, "Fabric Topology"), so PR-SMC shows no handshake. The specification gives two conflicting rules for where the word goes instead (the SMN or the peripheral crossbar), so the responses and the PR-OUT count are logged and not graded. The leaf waits for each response in a bounded wait; a timeout fails CHK-SMC-STATIC-ROW.
. Configuration B (steps 9 to 12 run when the seed draws B). The SMC aperture `0x9000_0000` to `0x90FF_FFFF` lies inside the reset SMU window `0x8000_0000` to `0xBFFF_FFFF`. After step 2, the LSU programs outbound pair 0 over `0x8000_0000` to `0xBFFF_FFFF` (same attributes as in step 3), enables it and reads it back.
. The LSU writes and reads the first aperture word `0x9000_0000` and the last aperture word `0x90FF_FFFC` with distinct fixed markers. Each read answers OKAY with its marker. PR-SMC counts one AW and one AR for each word. PR-OUT shows no handshake.
. PR-OUT control. The LSU reads `0x8000_0100`, which lies inside the SMU window and outside the aperture. The read answers OKAY and PR-OUT captures it.
. The LSU disables pair 0.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-SMC-ROUTE
|The SMC aperture that the SMC supplies is matched first and sent to `sep_ext_to_smc_axi_req_o` without the outbound filter (`fabric.adoc`, "Fabric Topology"). In configuration A, over the accesses of step 4, the PR-SMC count equals the number of those accesses (one AW and one AR for each of the two edge words), and the PR-OUT count of these accesses is zero. Each edge-word read through the SMC responder returns the written value (a real readback), and X or Z in the read data fails on VCS. A route that misses the aperture edges, or sends aperture traffic outbound, gives a lower PR-SMC count or a non-zero PR-OUT count. Unfiltered leg: with all 32 outbound entries disabled, each access of step 6 answers OKAY, each read returns its marker and PR-SMC counts each access, and the SMU-window read of step 7 answers DECERR with no PR-OUT handshake (`index.adoc`, "Blocked Transactions"). A filter on the SMC path refuses the step 6 accesses, and a bypassed outbound filter answers OKAY to the step 7 read, so either fails the check. The `smc_fuse_sense_done` read is 1 before the first request. Anchor: PR-SMC, PR-OUT and the LSU response and read data (BH-SMC drives the aperture). Control: the SMU-window read of step 5, outside the aperture, answers OKAY, is captured on PR-OUT and shows no PR-SMC handshake; the aperture accesses of step 4 drive PR-SMC. Evidence: `CHK-SMC-ROUTE PASS: addr=0x40000000\|0x40FFFFFC smc_aw=<n> smc_ar=<n> out_seen=0 control_out=<n> control_smc=0 rdata=0x<M> wr=0x<M> unfilt_smc=<n> deny_resp=DECERR deny_out=0 fuse_done=1`.
|CHK-SMC-STATIC-ROW
|PR-SMC shows no handshake for the word above the top, on read and on write (`fabric.adoc`, "Fabric Topology": the route demux sends only the supplied aperture to the SMC port). A route that decodes the static SMC row to the SMC port shows a handshake. The PR-OUT count and the responses for this word are logged and not graded, because the specification gives two conflicting rules for where an address outside every window goes. Anchor: PR-SMC. Control: the aperture accesses of the same leaf drive PR-SMC. Evidence: `CHK-SMC-STATIC-ROW PASS: above=0x41000000 dir=R\|W smc_seen=0 out_seen=<logged> resp=<logged> control_smc=<n>`.
|CHK-SMC-FIRST-MATCH
|In configuration B the first and last aperture word reach PR-SMC and PR-OUT shows no handshake for them, and the SMU-window read outside the aperture is captured on PR-OUT and shows no PR-SMC handshake (`fabric.adoc`, "Fabric Topology": the SMC aperture is first in the order). A DUT with the SMU match ahead of the SMC match sends the aperture words outbound, so PR-SMC stays silent. The `smc_fuse_sense_done` read is 1 before the first request. Anchor: PR-SMC and PR-OUT. Control: the `0x8000_0100` read, which drives PR-OUT; the aperture words, which drive PR-SMC. Evidence: `CHK-SMC-FIRST-MATCH PASS: smc_base=0x90000000 smu_base=0x80000000 smc_seen=<n> out_seen=0 control_out=<n> control_smc=0 fuse_done=1`.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker of the drawn configuration PASSes: CHK-SMC-ROUTE and CHK-SMC-STATIC-ROW for configuration A, CHK-SMC-FIRST-MATCH for configuration B. A missing check line of the drawn configuration fails the leaf. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope limit*: The test does not grade where the word above the supplied aperture goes (the specification gives two conflicting rules for an address outside every window: the SMN or the peripheral crossbar), only that the word does not reach the SMC port. It does not grade the hang of a request to the SMC before `smc_fuse_sense_done` (the testbench SMC responder is the only SMC, and a hang that the responder models cannot fail the SEP RTL), or other aperture values. The SMU aperture registers are not written. Nothing here claims that the SMC fabric itself decodes the aperture.

'''''
[[sep_fabric_extension_port_window_test]]
===== 2.30 `sep_fabric_extension_port_window_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: Fabric and remap

*Run mode*: `no_cpu` (`lsu_stub_all_live`), real PROD fuse sense, 3 seeds

*Source Module*: `sep_fabric_extension_port_window_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (LSU splice master on `s_axi`; SI master on `m_axi`). The bench drives `axi_extension_axi_resp_i` with DECERR for every request. This is the value that the port table ties to an unused port. Approved probes: PR-XEXT (the SI request that reaches the local crossbar), the LSU and SI responses, and the register read-back. PR-EXT (`axi_extension_axi_req_o`: address, AxSIZE, AxLEN, strobe and data) is an observation tap the test adds to the SEP_TB_ARCH observation-probe list. No inject.

*Randomization*: `SepSeededRng` from the run seed: the middle word offset, the AxSIZE of each single-beat probe, the write data and the page offset of the SI burst. Legal range: every single-beat address is aligned to its AxSIZE (the drawn offset is rounded down) and starts at or above `0x2000_0000` + `EFUSE_SHIM_SIZE`. The middle word offset is drawn at byte grain from `0x2000_0008` to `0x3FFF_FFF7`, so after the round-down it stays above the shim window and the first word and below the last word. The first word above the shim takes AxSIZE 0 to 2. The middle word and the last word `0x3FFF_FFF8` take AxSIZE 0 to 3. The burst starts 8-byte aligned inside the 4 KB page at `0x2000_1000`, and the whole burst stays in that page. `EFUSE_SHIM_SIZE` stays at its default, because the specification states no range for it. The initiators, the directions and the address classes are fixed loops, not draws. `reseed = 3` samples different middle offsets, sizes, data and page offsets.

*Objective*: The extension port serves `0x2000_0000` to `0x3FFF_FFFF` except the first `EFUSE_SHIM_SIZE` bytes, for the LSU and the System Interface. The eFuse shim window does not leave on the port. The System Interface may issue bursts. A request that leaves on the port gets the response that the port returns. The port table ties an unused port to DECERR, and the bench drives that value. A burst that the inbound filter refuses answers DECERR and never reaches the local crossbar. Cites `hw/sys/sep/doc/fabric.adoc` ("Top Level AXI4"; "Fabric Topology", local fabric), `hw/sys/sep/doc/port_table.adoc` (`axi_extension_axi_req_o`, `axi_extension_axi_resp_i`), `hw/sys/sep/doc/memory_map.adoc` ("External Window Reference Model"), `hw/sys/sep/regs/gen/adoc/memory_map.adoc` (SEP External row), `hw/ip/axi_filter/doc/index.adoc` ("Blocked Transactions") and `hw/sys/sep/doc/assets/sep_axi_connectivity.svg`.

*Test Coverage*: LSU and SI, read and write, at the first word above the shim, a middle word and the last word of the window. The first and last byte of the shim window. An SI INCR write burst with AxLEN 3 and an SI INCR read burst with AxLEN 7 through an entry with `allow_burst` 1. The same two bursts with the covering entry disabled. This entry extends `sep_address_map_test`, which grades the LSU decode bounds of the extension demux. Only the new cells are graded here: the System Interface initiator with reads, writes and bursts, the PR-EXT capture of the issued attributes and data, the shim window silence on PR-EXT, and the response at each initiator. `sep_address_map_test` keeps the LSU decode bounds. The reserved word `0x1FFF_FFFC` below the window is a cell of `sep_fabric_row_response_matrix_test`. The word `0x4000_0000` above the window is a crossbar-limit cell of `sep_fabric_inbound_rebase_test`. Functional coverage: `sep_fabric_dedicated_port_cg` (`cp_ext_init_dir`, `cp_ext_addr_class`, `cp_ext_burst`) and `sep_fabric_port_silence_cp` (`sil_ext_shim_window`, `sil_ext_filter_deny`).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Bring up with real PROD fuse sense. Read `FEAT_CTRL` and log it. The bench drives DECERR on `axi_extension_axi_resp_i` for every request.
. From the LSU, program inbound entry 0: `START_ADDR` `0x2000_0000`, `END_ADDR` `0x3FFF_FFFF`, and `FILTER_CONFIG` with `entry_enabled` 1, `read_allowed` 1, `write_allowed` 1, `allow_burst` 1, `src_id` 0 and `allow_ns` equal to AxPROT[1] of the SI requests. Read back the three registers before the first SI request.
. Draw the middle word offset, the AxSIZE of each single-beat probe and the page offset of the burst from the seed.
. From SI, issue one single-beat read and one single-beat write to each address class: the first word above the shim, the middle word and the last word `0x3FFF_FFF8`. Keep one request outstanding. A write drives seeded data with the strobes of its AxSIZE. For each request, record the PR-XEXT handshake and address, the PR-EXT capture and the SI response.
. From the LSU, issue the same reads and writes to the same address classes. For each request, record the PR-EXT capture and the LSU response.
. Shim window. From the LSU and from SI, read and write the first byte `0x2000_0000` and the last byte `0x2000_0000` + `EFUSE_SHIM_SIZE` - 1 with AxSIZE 0. A write drives the reset value of the byte (`EFUSE_BANK_INIT_TIME` `0x20` at byte 0, `0x00` at byte 3), so the shim register keeps its value. Record PR-EXT for each request. Log each response and do not grade it. A response that does not arrive within a bounded wait fails the leaf.
. From SI, issue an INCR write burst with AxLEN 3 and AxSIZE 3 at the drawn start address, with all strobes set and seeded data on the four beats. Record the PR-XEXT handshake and address, the PR-EXT AxLEN, AxSIZE and write beats, and the SI response.
. From SI, issue an INCR read burst with AxLEN 7 and AxSIZE 3 at a drawn start address in the same page. Record the PR-XEXT handshake and address, the PR-EXT AxLEN and AxSIZE, and the SI response.
. From the LSU, disable inbound entry 0 (write `FILTER_CONFIG` with `entry_enabled` 0 and the other fields unchanged). Read `FILTER_CONFIG` back.
. Error injection at `smn_inbound_axi_req_i`: repeat the write burst of step 7 with the covering entry disabled. Expected response: DECERR on B (`hw/ip/axi_filter/doc/index.adoc`, "Blocked Transactions"). PR-XEXT stays silent from the request to the response.
. Error injection at `smn_inbound_axi_req_i`: repeat the read burst of step 8 with the covering entry disabled. Expected response: DECERR on every R beat until RLAST. PR-XEXT stays silent from the request to the last beat. The beat count is not graded.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-EXT-REACH
|Each SI single-beat request of step 4 shows one AW or AR handshake on PR-XEXT with the issued low 32 address bits, and the SI receives DECERR, the response that the bench drives on the port (`hw/sys/sep/doc/port_table.adoc`). Catches a filter or crossbar that does not forward the request, a wrong address, and a response that does not return or carries another code. The PR-XEXT capture is the anchor. The DECERR alone cannot show that the request reached the crossbar, because the fabric also answers DECERR for its own errors. A response that does not arrive within a bounded wait fails the check. Control: PR-XEXT shows handshakes in the admitted legs, and CHK-EXT-BURST shows it silent for the refused burst. Evidence: one line per request, `CHK-EXT-REACH PASS: dir=R\|W class=first\|mid\|last issued=0x<addr> xbar_seen=0x<addr> init_resp=DECERR`.
|CHK-EXT-PORT
|PR-EXT shows for each LSU and SI request of steps 4 and 5 one request with the issued address, the issued AxSIZE, AxLEN 0, the issued strobe and, for a write, the issued data on the strobed lanes. The LSU receives DECERR. Catches a wrong window decode and a request that leaves with other attributes or data. The PR-EXT capture is the anchor, because the DECERR at the initiator does not show which unit produced it. Evidence: `CHK-EXT-PORT PASS: init=LSU\|SI dir=R\|W issued=0x<addr> seen=0x<addr> size=<n> len=0 strb=0x<s> data_ok=<0\|1\|na> init_resp=DECERR`.
|CHK-EXT-SHIM
|The first and last byte of the shim window give no PR-EXT capture, for either initiator and either direction. Catches a shim window that leaks onto the port. Control: the first word above the shim of steps 4 and 5 gives a capture on PR-EXT in the same leaf. A leaf whose control gives no capture fails. Evidence: `CHK-EXT-SHIM PASS: first=0x20000000 last=0x<addr> seen=0 next_word_seen=1`.
|CHK-EXT-BURST
|The admitted write burst and the admitted read burst each show a PR-XEXT handshake at the start address, and the SI receives DECERR, the response of the port. The two bursts with the entry disabled answer DECERR at SI, and PR-XEXT stays silent for each. Catches a filter that passes a burst with no enabled entry. Control: the admitted burst of the same shape in the same leaf, which shows PR-XEXT alive. Evidence: `CHK-EXT-BURST PASS: dir=R\|W len=<n> xbar_seen=<n> init_resp=DECERR denied_resp=DECERR denied_xbar_seen=0`. The check also grades the PR-EXT part: PR-EXT shows the issued AxLEN and AxSIZE and, for the write, every beat with the issued data. The PR-EXT part of the PASS line is `beats_seen=<n> data_ok=<0\|1>`.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope limit*: The leaf does not grade the response of an adopter extension device, because the bench port answers DECERR. It does not grade the response of the eFuse shim window, which it logs. It does not grade the LSU decode bounds of the extension demux (`sep_address_map_test`), the reserved word `0x1FFF_FFFC` (`sep_fabric_row_response_matrix_test`) or the word `0x4000_0000` (`sep_fabric_inbound_rebase_test`). DMA access to the port is graded by `sep_fabric_dma_endpoint_matrix_test`. The CPU debug master has no stimulus path in this run mode.

'''''

[[sep_fabric_row_response_matrix_test]]
===== 2.31 `sep_fabric_row_response_matrix_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: Fabric and remap

*Run mode*: `no_cpu` (`lsu_stub_all_live`), real PROD fuse sense, 4 seeds. The Key Manager leg holds KM in reset with no KM image. VCS is required for the X check.

*Source Module*: `sep_fabric_row_response_matrix_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (LSU splice master on `s_axi`; SI master on `m_axi`). The expected cells come from the generated memory-map table, the `ocah_*` annotations of `sep.rdl` and the register allocation of the generated IP-XACT (`sep_reg_meta`). Approved probes: the SI and LSU responses and read data, and the LSU read-back of live and neighbour registers. The test adds no observation tap. The attribution of a DECERR to the decode and not to the filter rests on the control that the decoded registers answer OKAY through the same entry. No inject.

*Randomization*: `SepSeededRng` from the run seed. Every seed walks every cell of the inventory, so row, cell kind, direction, initiator and the four OTBN AxCACHE values are fixed loops. The dimensions are the offset inside each cell, the initiator order and AxID (non-zero). Every graded single-beat cell uses AxSIZE 2 with address bit 2 clear and with address bit 2 set, except a live-word cell, which uses the address of its word. AxSIZE 3 is logged and not graded. AxSIZE 0 and 1 serve only the no-alias compare in the reset-control gaps. The burst leg walks every crypto window, start kind and direction, and draws the start address and AxLEN (INCR, AxSIZE 3, AxLEN 1 to 255, the whole burst inside one 4 KB page). Legal range per `hw/sys/sep/regs/gen/adoc/memory_map.adoc`. Rejection list: Forwarded rows (AP, STEE); adopter-defined cells (TRNG, SEP External); the two reserved CPU rows (no stated response); bursts outside the burst leg and bursts to any register region other than the crypto region (no stated response); burst starts on a past-extent word or a Reserved row (their single-beat answer is DECERR as well, so a burst there cannot show the burst rule); any SEP_DBG-bit draw; the cells that open tests grade (listed under Test Coverage). The beat count of a refused burst is not graded, because the specification states none. `reseed = 4` samples different offsets, orders and IDs over the same cell set. Every seed walks the whole inventory, so more seeds only repeat the cells.

*Objective*: Each memory-map row answers as its cells state. The table states the cells as seen at the inbound AXI port, so every Reserved, Past Extent and Hole in Extent cell of a row that the inbound port reaches is graded through SI behind an enabled entry over the row. The reset-control rows state what the SEP CPU sees, so the reset-control gaps, tails and past-extent cells are graded from the LSU only. The inbound port answers reset control with DECERR and states no read data. The table states the cells for a 32-bit access, so the code and data of a cell are graded for AxSIZE 2 in either half of the 64-bit data bus. An AxSIZE 3 access is logged and not graded. A Reserved row answers DECERR with read data `0xBADCAB1E` and DECERR on a write. Past the decoded extent a row answers its Past Extent cell. An unbacked offset inside the extent answers its Hole in Extent cell: SLVERR with `0xFFFFFFFF` for OTBN, HMAC and KMAC; OKAY with 0 for the entropy source and ABR (read 0, write discarded). A live word of the extent answers OKAY with the register value. An OTBN register access is served with AxCACHE[1] = 0 (non-modifiable) and with AxCACHE[1] = 1 (modifiable), because the crypto interconnect applies a modifiable-bit fix before the data-width converter (`hw/sys/sep/doc/otbn.adoc`, "OCAH Modifications"). The values `0x0`, `0x2`, `0x3` and `0xF` are chosen test values. The reset controller gaps and tails answer DECERR with `0xBADCAB1E` and do not alias onto a live register. In the Key Manager mailbox host window only the seven registers at offsets `0x00` to `0x18` decode; every other offset and the reserved span answer DECERR with `0xBADCAB1E`. A non-zero AxLEN to the crypto region `0x1090_0000` to `0x1094_FFFF`, whatever the address, is answered with DECERR on every beat, and no beat reaches an accelerator. An inbound entry that covers a register region with `allow_burst` 1 admits bursts that the target rejects, so the DECERR comes from the crypto demux and not from the filter. Cites `hw/sys/sep/regs/gen/adoc/memory_map.adoc` (Hole in Extent and Past Extent columns), `hw/sys/sep/regs/sep.rdl` (`ocah_*` annotations), `doc/trm/src/memory_map.adoc` ("Decode Response Codes"), `hw/sys/sep/doc/memory_map.adoc` ("Memory Map"; "Single-Beat Register Access"), `hw/sys/sep/doc/fabric.adoc` ("Fabric Topology"; "Filtering and Protection"), `hw/sys/sep/doc/crypto.adoc` ("Single-Beat Access Only"), `hw/sys/sep/doc/otbn.adoc` ("OCAH Modifications"), `hw/ip/key_manager/regs/gen/adoc/km_mailbox_sep.adoc`, `hw/sys/sep/regs/gen/adoc/blocks/sep_reset_ctrl.adoc` (`SW_RESET_N`) and `hw/sys/sep/doc/assets/sep_axi_connectivity.svg`.

*Test Coverage*: The 8 Reserved rows with bases `0x1005_0000`, `0x1080_4000`, `0x1091_4000`, `0x1092_1000`, `0x1093_0600`, `0x1096_0000`, `0x10C0_0000` and `0x1200_0000` (DECERR, `0xBADCAB1E`), each with its first word, last word and a drawn word. The last word of the row at `0x1200_0000`, `0x1FFF_FFFC`, is the word below the extension window. The hole-in-extent cells of OTBN, HMAC and KMAC from SI (SLVERR, `0xFFFFFFFF`, both halves, reads and writes; `sep_irq_ip_to_aggregator_test` keeps the LSU single read), of the entropy source (OKAY, 0) and of a drawn ABR hole word with a 32-bit access from SI (OKAY, 0, write discarded). The past-extent cells of the DMA, watchdog, OTBN, AES, CSRNG, EDN, entropy source and lifecycle controller (DECERR) from SI. The live-word cell of each of these rows (DMA, watchdog, reset control, OTBN, AES, HMAC, KMAC, CSRNG, EDN, entropy source, lifecycle controller, KM mailbox and ABR): the highest-offset register of the extent that is stable, has no read side effect and has an RDL reset value on every field; for the entropy source and ABR, whose holes answer OKAY with 0, it is the highest-offset such register with a non-zero reset value. RMOD, FIFO, window and hardware-updated words are excluded. The leaf logs the chosen word per row. The reset-control gaps, tails, past-extent cells and the adjacent Reserved row from the LSU, with AxSIZE 0 and 1 for the no-alias compare. The no-alias references HMAC `CFG`, one KMAC `PREFIX` word and `SW_RESET_N`. The OTBN host access with AxCACHE `0x0`, `0x2`, `0x3` and `0xF` on both channels. The Key Manager mailbox window from SI with KM held in reset. The SI write and read bursts to the crypto windows through an entry with `allow_burst` 1, starting on an in-extent register and on a hole, each with a single-beat control. The burst leg shares the rows, the initiator, the entry and the run mode of the single-beat legs, so it is a leg of this test. Other tests grade the cells below, and this entry does not repeat them. `sep_unmapped_access_policy_test` grades the exact code and data of the Reserved rows at `0x10A1_0280`, `0x10A1_0380`, `0x10A2_0400`, `0x10A2_1200` and `0x10A3_2000`, the two scratch gap Reserved rows, the alias remap bank, filter bank and SEP CPU control hole and past-extent cells, the eFuse control and token past-extent cells and the SPI gaps and tails. `sep_address_map_test` reads one word in every LSU-reachable block. `sep_fabric_deadspace_decode_test` grades the past-extent refusal and the no-alias compare of the DMA, watchdog, AES, OTBN, ABR, CSRNG, EDN and entropy source windows, and the crypto-region burst refusal from the LSU with a single-beat control. `sep_abr_access_size_test` grades the ABR past-extent cells and, with a 64-bit access from the LSU, the hole word above the ABR error counter. `sep_axi_map_refuse_test` grades refusal only for every reserved row. `sep_irq_ip_to_aggregator_test` grades the DMA hole cells and the LSU single read that completes SLVERR at the HMAC CSR and FIFO gap, the KMAC gap and the OTBN CSR and IMEM gap. `sep_entropy_pool_aperture_test` grades the entropy pool cells. `sep_lcc_uvm_inbound_filter_gating_test` grades SI access to the boot ROM, the reset controller and the ICCM. The Phase 3 tests `sep_pic_reg_rand_test` and `sep_mailbox_access_error_inject_test` own the PIC rows and the mailbox-wrapper cells. This entry adds only: the exact code and data of the other 8 Reserved rows, the exact code and data of the past-extent cells from SI (from the LSU for reset control), the live-word cell of each row, the hole-in-extent cells of OTBN, HMAC and KMAC from SI (the System Interface initiator, the `0xFFFF_FFFF` data in both halves of the word, and the writes), the hole-in-extent cell of the entropy source, a drawn ABR hole word with a 32-bit access from SI, the Key Manager mailbox window, the no-alias compare of the reset controller, HMAC and KMAC, and the System Interface burst to the crypto region through an entry that admits bursts. The open owner keeps every other cell. Functional coverage: `sep_aperture_reserved_access_cg` (`cp_row_cell`, `cp_row_init_dir`, `cp_aperture_offset_dir`, `cp_non_aliasing`), `sep_crypto_bus_access_cg` (`cp_otbn_cache_reg`) and `sep_fabric_inbound_aperture_cg` (`cp_burst_region`). The existing `sep_axi_decode_cg` (`cp_resp_wr`, `cp_resp_rd`) and `sep_inbound_filter_allow_cg` fill from the OKAY cells.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Bring up with real PROD fuse sense. Read `FEAT_CTRL` and log it. Leave `SW_RESET_N` bit 0 at 0, so KM stays in reset, and load no KM image.
. Build the cell inventory from the generated memory-map table, the `ocah_*` annotations of `sep.rdl` and the register allocation of the generated IP-XACT. Every cell is one (row, cell kind, direction, initiator) tuple. The burst cells are (crypto window, start kind, direction) tuples. The inventory excludes the Forwarded and adopter-defined cells and every cell that the Test Coverage section assigns to another test.
. From the LSU, program inbound entry 0: `START_ADDR` `0x1000_0000`, `END_ADDR` `0x1FFF_FFFF`, and `FILTER_CONFIG` with `entry_enabled` 1, `read_allowed` 1, `write_allowed` 1, `allow_burst` 1, `src_id` 0 and `allow_ns` equal to AxPROT[1] of the SI requests. Read the three registers back before the first SI request. Every SI access of this test goes through this entry.
. Reset-control leg, from the LSU. Read `SW_RESET_N` (`0x1080_3000`) at AxSIZE 2. Its field bits [6:0] read the RDL reset value `0x7E`, and this value is the reference. Bits [31:7] are Reserved with no stated read value, and the leaf logs them. Then, per direction, access the pairs `0x1080_3008` and `0x1080_300C`, a drawn 8-byte-aligned pair in `0x1080_300C` to `0x1080_3FFC`, `0x1080_3FF8` and `0x1080_3FFC`, and `0x1080_4000` and `0x1080_4004` at AxSIZE 2. Error injection at the decode of the row: each of these is a past-extent or reserved address. Expected response: DECERR, with read data `0xBADCAB1E` on a read. Log the AxSIZE 3 access of each cell and do not grade it.
. No-alias draws on the reset controller, from the LSU. Write the gap `0x1080_3008` to `0x1080_3FFF` at drawn addresses with AxSIZE 0, 1, 2 and 3. Error injection at the decode of the row. Expected response: DECERR on every write. Each write drives data whose bits [6:0] are the bitwise complement of the reference (`0x01`) and seeded data above bit 6. After each write, read `SW_RESET_N`. Grade the DECERR response of the AxSIZE 2 draws under CHK-ROW. Log the response of the AxSIZE 0, 1 and 3 draws and do not grade it; those draws serve only the no-alias compare.
. Reset-control control, from the LSU. Write `SW_RESET_N` = `0x76` (bit 3, `hmac_sw_rst_n`, cleared) and read it back. Write `SW_RESET_N` = `0x7E` and read it back. This pair restores the reset value, so KM stays in reset and HMAC runs again.
. Read HMAC `CFG` from the LSU until it answers OKAY, in a bounded wait. A timeout fails the leaf. The wait ends the isolation and reset of the HMAC domain before the next write.
. From the LSU, program the no-alias references: HMAC `CFG` and one KMAC `PREFIX` word, each at a seeded value that differs from its reset value. Read both back.
. OTBN host access, from the LSU. For each AxCACHE value in the fixed loop `0x0`, `0x2`, `0x3`, `0xF`, drive that value on AR and on AW. Read `INTR_ENABLE`, write it with the inverse of bit 0 of the value read, read it back and read `STATUS`. AxCACHE[1] is 0 for `0x0` and 1 for the other three, so each channel carries both values of AxCACHE[1].
. Reserved rows, from SI. For each of the 8 rows and each direction, access three 8-byte words: the first, the last and a drawn word. Access each word at AxSIZE 2 at its low half (address bit 2 clear) and at its high half (bit 2 set). A write drives seeded data. Error injection at the decode of the row. Expected response: DECERR on every access, with read data `0xBADCAB1E` on a read. Log the AxSIZE 3 access of each word and do not grade it.
. Hole-in-extent cells, from SI. For each of OTBN, HMAC, KMAC, the entropy source and ABR, draw an 8-byte word whose two halves are both holes. Per unit, pick a neighbour register (a stable register of the same unit with no read side effect; HMAC `CFG` and the KMAC `PREFIX` word are the references). Read the neighbour from the LSU. Read both halves of the hole at AxSIZE 2. Write both halves at AxSIZE 2 with the bitwise complement of the neighbour value. Read the neighbour from the LSU again. Error injection at the decode of the row. Expected response: SLVERR with `0xFFFFFFFF` on a read and SLVERR on a write for OTBN, HMAC and KMAC. OKAY with read data 0 on a read and OKAY on a write for the entropy source and ABR. Log the AxSIZE 3 access of each word and do not grade it.
. Hole-write control. For each unit of step 11, write the same complement to its neighbour register as an in-extent write, read it back and restore the value read in step 11.
. Past-extent cells, from SI. For each of the DMA, watchdog, OTBN, AES, CSRNG, EDN, entropy source and lifecycle controller, and each direction, access the pair E and E + 4, where E is the first byte past the decoded extent, and a drawn 8-byte-aligned pair above E + 4 inside the aperture, at AxSIZE 2. Error injection at the decode of the row. Expected response: DECERR on every access, with read data `0xBADCAB1E` on a read. Log the AxSIZE 3 access of each cell and do not grade it.
. Live-word cells. For each row of the Test Coverage list except reset control, read the chosen live word from the LSU, read it from SI at AxSIZE 2, then read it from the LSU again. The model gives the expected value of the RDL field bits of the word: their RDL reset value, or the value that an earlier step of the leaf left in them. The Reserved bits of the word are logged. For reset control, the live word is the `SW_RESET_N` read of step 4.
. Key Manager mailbox, from SI, with KM held in reset. Read `SEP_STATUS`, `SEP_IRQ_STATUS`, `SEP_CTRL` and `SEP_IRQ_ENABLE` as the baseline. Read `SEP_WRITE_SEPARATOR`. Do not access `SEP_WRITE_DATA` or `SEP_READ_DATA`. Then, per direction, access the pairs at offsets `0x1C` and `0x20`, `0xFF8` and `0xFFC`, drawn pairs in `0x1C` to `0xFFC`, and drawn pairs in `0x1092_1000` to `0x1092_FFFC`. Read the baseline again after each access. Error injection at the decode of the row. Expected response: DECERR on every access, with read data `0xBADCAB1E` on a read. Baseline control: after the last access, SI writes `SEP_IRQ_ENABLE` = `0x1C` (the three sticky-event enables; reset value 0), reads it back, writes 0 and reads it back.
. Burst leg, from SI, for each cell: each of the OTBN, HMAC, KMAC, entropy source and ABR windows, each start kind (a stable RW register at an 8-byte-aligned address, and a hole) and each direction. Draw the start address and AxLEN. From the LSU, read the snapshot of every stable register of the touched window that has no read side effect.
. Error injection at `smn_inbound_axi_req_i`, for the same cell: issue the INCR burst with AxSIZE 3 and the drawn AxLEN. Each write beat drives the bitwise complement of the snapshot words at its address, and seeded data where no snapshot word exists. Expected response: DECERR on the single B or on every R beat.
. For a write burst, read every snapshot register from the LSU again.
. Control, for the same cell: issue a single-beat SI access with AxSIZE 2 at the start address. For a register, write the complement of its snapshot value, read it back, and restore the snapshot value. For a hole, read it and write it.
. At the end of each seed, compare the number of cells walked with the inventory count for each row, cell kind, direction and initiator, the burst cells included.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-ROW
|The response code and the addressed data lane equal the cell of the generated table, for every SI cell and for the LSU reset-control cells, at AxSIZE 2. Each non-live cell is accessed with address bit 2 clear and set. A live-word cell is accessed at its own address. X or Z in an error payload fails on VCS. After a hole write, the neighbour register of step 11 reads unchanged, and the write data is the bitwise complement of the neighbour value. The live-word cell answers OKAY, and its RDL field bits equal the expected value of the model (the RDL reset value of the fields, or the value that an earlier step left in them). The Reserved bits of the word have no stated read value, so they are masked out of the compare and logged. The two LSU reads of the word are preconditions: the field bits of each equal the expected value, or the check fails. For the entropy source and ABR the expected field value is non-zero, so an SI read that decodes to a hole (OKAY, 0) fails. The reset-control live word answers OKAY with `0x7E` on bits [6:0], its RDL reset value. Every register compare of this check and of CHK-ROW-NOALIAS, CHK-ROW-CACHE, CHK-ROW-KM, CHK-ROW-BURST and CHK-ROW-BURST-CONTROL (neighbour, reference, `INTR_ENABLE` bit 0, baseline, snapshot and read-back) uses the RDL field bits only. Catches a wrong code, a wrong payload, a hole write that lands and a live word that does not return its value. Anchor: the SI and LSU responses and read data, and the LSU read of the neighbour. Control: the in-extent write of step 12 to the same neighbour changes its read, and the live-word cell of the same row answers OKAY. Evidence: `CHK-ROW PASS: row=<unit> kind=<cell> init=LSU\|SI dir=R\|W size=2 addr=0x<addr> wdata=0x<w>\|na resp=<code> rdata=0x<value> expect=<code>/0x<value>`; a live-word line adds `field_mask=0x<m> lsu_before=0x<v> lsu_after=0x<v> rsvd=0x<r>`. Each AxSIZE 3 access logs `row=<unit> kind=<cell> size=3 resp=<code> rdata=0x<value> graded=0` at info level.
|CHK-ROW-RAND
|Stimulus-completeness control. Per seed, the number of cells walked equals the inventory count for each row, cell kind, direction and initiator, the burst cells included. A missing cell fails. The DUT cannot fail this checker, and it makes no DUT claim. Evidence: `CHK-ROW-RAND PASS: seed=<n> walked=<n> inventory=<n> rows=<n> reserved=<n> past=<n> hole=<n> live=<n> si=<n> burst=<n>`.
|CHK-ROW-NOALIAS
|Each live reference register (HMAC `CFG`, the KMAC `PREFIX` word and `SW_RESET_N`) keeps its value after every write draw. Every draw writes data that differs from the reference value on every watched bit: bits [6:0] for `SW_RESET_N`, and the writable bits of the RDL for HMAC `CFG` and the KMAC `PREFIX` word. The draws are the gap and tail writes of step 5 and the hole writes of step 11. Catches a gap or hole write that aliases onto a live register. Anchor: the LSU read of the reference after each draw. Control: an in-extent write to the same register changes its read (steps 6 and 12). A leaf whose control does not change the read fails. Evidence: `CHK-ROW-NOALIAS PASS: unit=<name> off=0x<o> live=0x<a> before=0x<b> after=0x<b> wdata=0x<w>`.
|CHK-ROW-CACHE
|An OTBN register access from the LSU answers OKAY on both channels with AxCACHE[1] = 0 and with AxCACHE[1] = 1 (`hw/sys/sep/doc/otbn.adoc`, "OCAH Modifications"). The chosen values `0x0`, `0x2`, `0x3` and `0xF` carry both values of AxCACHE[1] on each channel, and the `INTR_ENABLE` read-back equals the written value. The written value is the inverse of the value read before it, so a write that does not land fails. Catches a host port that refuses a modifiable or non-modifiable access. Anchor: the LSU responses and the read-back. Evidence: `CHK-ROW-CACHE PASS: init=LSU arcache=0x<c> awcache=0x<c> rresp=OKAY bresp=OKAY readback=0x<v>`.
|CHK-ROW-KM
|Every Key Manager past-extent and reserved access answers DECERR with `0xBADCAB1E` on a read and DECERR on a write, and the baseline registers read the same after each access. Catches a mailbox window that decodes offsets past its seven registers and an access that disturbs a baseline register. Anchor: the SI responses and the baseline reads. Control: the five registers without a FIFO side effect answer OKAY through the same entry, and the baseline control write of `SEP_IRQ_ENABLE` reads back `0x1C`, so a baseline register can change while KM is held in reset (`reset_controller.adoc`, section Resetting the Key Manager: the SEP-facing side of the mailbox is in the Key Manager cold domain, so the SEP host can still reach the mailbox during the reset). A leaf whose baseline control does not read back `0x1C` fails. Evidence: `CHK-ROW-KM PASS: off=0x<o> dir=R\|W resp=DECERR rdata=0xbadcab1e baseline_same=1 baseline_ctl=0x1c`.
|CHK-ROW-BURST
|Every SI burst of step 17 answers DECERR on B or on every R beat. After a write burst, every snapshot register equals its snapshot from before the burst. The burst write data is the bitwise complement of the snapshot, so a landed beat shows as a changed register. Catches a demux that forwards a burst or its first beat. Anchor: the SI response of each beat and the LSU read of the touched window. Control: CHK-ROW-BURST-CONTROL. The count of DECERR beats is logged and not graded. Evidence: `CHK-ROW-BURST PASS: init=SI addr=0x<addr> kind=reg\|hole len=<n> dir=W\|R resp=DECERR beats_decerr=<n> wdata=0x<w>\|na regs_compared=<n> changed=0`.
|CHK-ROW-BURST-CONTROL
|The single-beat SI access of step 19 with AxSIZE 2 at the same start address, through the same entry, answers its 32-bit cell: OKAY for a register (the write lands and reads back, then the snapshot value is restored), and SLVERR with `0xFFFFFFFF` or OKAY with 0 for a hole. The single-beat answer differs from DECERR, so the DECERR of CHK-ROW-BURST comes from the crypto demux and not from the filter, and a dead path cannot pass. Evidence: `CHK-ROW-BURST-CONTROL PASS: init=SI addr=0x<addr> size=2 kind=reg\|hole single_resp=<OKAY\|SLVERR> single_rdata=0x<value>`.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope limit*: The leaf grades the cells that Test Coverage lists, and the open tests named there keep every other cell. It does not grade the Forwarded rows (AP, STEE) or the adopter-defined cells (TRNG, SEP External). It does not grade the response of a burst to a register region other than the crypto region, or the beat count of a refused burst, because the specification states neither. It does not grade an AxSIZE 3 access. The LSU response of a cell that the SEP CPU does not see as an error is not graded. The live-word cell is a read. An in-extent write is made only at the reference registers, the hole neighbours, the burst control registers and the Key Manager mailbox `SEP_IRQ_ENABLE` of the baseline control. The LSU single read that completes SLVERR at the HMAC CSR and FIFO gap, the KMAC gap and the OTBN CSR and IMEM gap stays with `sep_irq_ip_to_aggregator_test`; this leaf grades only the new hole cells.

'''''

[[sep_cpu_lsu_alias_window_twin_test]]
===== 2.32 `sep_cpu_lsu_alias_window_twin_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: Fabric and remap

*Run mode*: `cpu`, firmware image `alias_twin_test`, `+skip_fuse_sense`, 3 seeds. The splice stub cannot run this test, because the alias remap sits in the core path. VCS is required for the X check on the reads.

*Source Module*: `sep_cpu_lsu_alias_window_twin_test`

*BFM / Model*: CPU FW (CPU LSU reads and writes; the firmware prints each value). Approved probe: the CPU read-back of each static word through the alias and the direct address. PR-SRAM (`sep_sram_req_o`), for the address compare of the SRAM words only, is an observation tap the test adds to the SEP_TB_ARCH observation-probe list. No inject.

*Randomization*: `SepSeededRng` from the run seed: the seeded value of each writable static word (the cold scratch word and the SPI host `CSID`) and of each SRAM word, and the marker value. The host patches the values into the firmware parameter block. Every seed covers all five unit classes and both SRAM words. `SEP_LOCAL_BASE_ADDR` stays at reset, because the specification states no legal range for it. Rejection list: twins that have a read side effect (entropy pool drain, DMA start). `reseed = 3` samples different static values and markers over the same word set.

*Objective*: The 768 MiB window at `SEP_LOCAL_BASE_ADDR` (reset `0xD000_0000`) rewrites to `0x1000_0000`, so an alias address answers as its direct twin on every target the leaf reads. The leaf drives no LSU access to the extension window: its tie-off answers DECERR, and the specification states no CPU consequence of an error response on a load. Cites `hw/sys/sep/doc/fabric.adoc` ("Address Remapping"; "Fabric Topology", local fabric), `hw/sys/sep/doc/memory_map.adoc` ("Memory Map"), `hw/sys/sep/doc/cpu.adoc` (introduction, system-bus masters) and `hw/sys/sep/regs/gen/adoc/blocks/sep_cpu_ctrl.adoc` (`SEP_LOCAL_BASE_ADDR`).

*Test Coverage*: Direct and alias reads of one static word per unit class: scratch (a cold scratch word), AES (`CTRL_SHADOWED`, read only), system CSR (`SEP_VERSION_ID`), SPI host (`CSID`) and entropy source (`COMPONENT_ID`). A marker write through the alias address to the RW scratch word, read at the direct address. Direct and alias reads of the SRAM start word `0x1000_0000` and last word `0x1003_FFFC` (alias `0xD000_0000` and `0xD003_FFFC`). This entry extends `sep_cpu_ifu_lsu_alias_remap_matrix_test`, which grades the LSU alias read and write of the SRAM window. Only the new cells are graded here: the five unit classes and the window start and last SRAM word. `sep_cpu_ifu_lsu_alias_remap_matrix_test` keeps the LSU alias read and write of the SRAM window. The DMA alias forms are legs of `sep_fabric_dma_endpoint_matrix_test`. Functional coverage: `sep_remap_alias_cg` (`cp_local_alias_twin`).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. The host patches the seeded values into the firmware parameter block, stages the image and releases the CPU.
. Firmware writes the seeded value of each writable static word at its direct address: the cold scratch word and the SPI host `CSID`. It writes the seeded values of the SRAM words at `0x1000_0000` and `0x1003_FFFC`.
. For each unit class, firmware reads the static word at its direct address, then at its alias address (the direct address + `0xC000_0000`), then at its direct address again. It prints the three values. The words of `SEP_VERSION_ID` and `COMPONENT_ID` are read-only, and firmware does not write them. Firmware does not write AES `CTRL_SHADOWED` either: an AES register write that the unit ignores while it is not idle (`aes.hjson`) has no stated result, and a read has no idle gate.
. For each of the two SRAM words, firmware reads the direct address and then the alias address. It prints both values. PR-SRAM records the address of each request.
. Firmware writes the marker through the alias address of the cold scratch word, reads the direct address and prints the value.
. The host compares the printed values with the seeded values and the marker, and logs the checkers.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-TWIN
|For each unit class and for the two SRAM words, the alias read equals the direct read. The two direct reads of a unit class are equal, so the word is stable. For a writable word, both reads equal the seeded value that the host patched.
