A graded compare of a register read covers only the bits of the RDL fields of that register (`axil_mailbox.adoc`, `sep_cpu_ctrl.adoc`, `el2_pic.adoc` and the other register descriptions that an entry cites). A bit whose RDL row is `Reserved` with no access and no reset value has no stated value: the compare masks it, and the PASS line logs it as `rsvd=0x<v>`. A register value in a check or a step of this section (`ERROR_FLAGS` reads `0x1`, `DMA_BUS_ERR_STATUS` equals 0b10, a timeout count reads 0x1, a clear register reads 0) is the value of the field bits. The read data of an offset that holds no register keeps its full-word compare where the memory map states it (a mailbox or PIC hole reads 0x0).
* Log lines. A check prints `CHK-<NAME> PASS <key>=<value> ...` on pass and `CHK-<NAME> FAIL ...` on fail. A leaf prints `SEED seed=<S>` first and `DRAW <name>=<value>` for every drawn value. The host counts the expected `CHK` lines of each check. A leaf passes only when every named check prints PASS and no error is reported. A missing line fails the leaf. A clean simulator exit is not evidence. A firmware test prints the same line shapes on the console, and the host also gates on the pass or fail magic word of the firmware. A blocked check prints `OBS-<NAME> LOG ...` and never `CHK-<NAME> PASS`.
* Random stimulus is a pure function of the seed. Every draw uses `SepSeededRng`. A firmware test receives the drawn values in its parameter block. The stream is not a CSPRNG. Mailbox payloads are test data, and no key, token or nonce is drawn. No per-seed value is quoted as evidence.
* Seed-dependent cells. A cell that a leaf draws from its seed fills on a merge of regressions and never in one regression (`SEP_FCOV.adoc`, "Seed-dependent groups"). A leaf has no run index, so no seed pins a cell, and no testlist variant pins a cell. Each entry names its seed-dependent cells. Cheap boundary cells, one representative of each leg and the error-injection cases run on every seed.
* No leaf draws `SYS_DIS` or any disable-vector bit. Bit 0 is `SEP_DBG`, and it admits all inbound traffic (`hw/sys/sep/doc/fabric.adoc`, "Filtering and Protection").
* Every negative ("never") check has a control in the same leaf where a healthy design drives the same signal. The entry names the control.
* Run modes. `no_cpu` means target `lsu_stub_all_live` with the CPU-LSU master as a testbench master. `cpu` means the full CPU model on the default target with firmware. The PIC is inside the CPU, so a PIC register is reachable only from firmware in a `cpu` leaf (`hw/sys/sep/doc/memory_map.adoc`, "Units Unreachable from the Inbound Port").
* Every entry also carries the shared `CHK-FW-IDENTITY` and `CHK-FW-CONSOLE` records when it runs firmware, as stated in Test Procedures.

'''''
[[sep_mailbox_fifo_model_rand_test]]
===== 3.13 `sep_mailbox_fifo_model_rand_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: Mailbox, IRQ, PIC

*Run mode*: `no_cpu` (`lsu_stub_all_live`), `+skip_fuse_sense`, 3 seeds

*Source Module*: `sep_mailbox_fifo_model_rand_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (CPU-LSU master on the outbound apertures; external SMN master on the inbound apertures through one open inbound filter window per port); a golden queue per FIFO and a golden `STATUS`, `IRQS`, `IRQP` and line model, written from the spec text. Observation points: `sep_internal_interrupts_probe_o` bits [7:0] and bit 14 (`hw/sys/sep/dv/tb/tb_top.sv`) and `smc_mailbox_interrupt_o` (DUT port). No PROPOSED item. Every check is a reached check.

*Randomization*: RAND-REP. `SepSeededRng` from the run seed. The draws are: the mailbox order; for each threshold run `IRQEN` in [0, 7] per port (the gate and acknowledge legs drive every `IRQS` and `IRQEN` cell of each cause on each port); the payload (non-zero, no repeated word inside one fill); the access width (64-bit, or 32-bit at either half); two threshold values for each FIFO of each mailbox (0 to 255, weighted toward the corners 1, 6 and 9, the other values from 2 to 5 and 10 to 254); the fill count of a threshold run below 7 (in {threshold-1, threshold, threshold+1}, threshold-1 only for a threshold above 0; a threshold of 7 or more always fills to 8); the flush kind of each mailbox (each of the four kinds on two mailboxes); the fill counts of the flush leg (1 to 8 per FIFO); the two alias thresholds; the subsets of mailboxes with a high line. Every push runs below occupancy 8 and every pop above occupancy 0. `reseed = 3` samples different mailbox orders, payloads, widths, threshold values, flush-kind assignments, fill counts and subsets. The boundary threshold values 0, 7, 8 and 255 on both FIFOs of the first mailbox of the order, the four flush kinds and the all-eight outbound step run on every seed. The threshold values 1, 6, 9 and the other 8-bit values are seed-dependent cells and close on a merge of regressions (`SEP_FCOV.adoc`, "Seed-dependent groups").

*Objective*: Each mailbox pair holds two 8-entry FIFOs of 64 bits. A write at either half of `WRITE_DATA` pushes one entry. A read at either half of `READ_DATA` pops one entry. A threshold above 7 acts as 7, and a threshold of 0 detects any queued word. A flush bit discards the selected FIFO, and `CTRL` reads back 0. The level interrupt of each port is the OR of `IRQS` AND `IRQEN` of that port. The inbound line of mailbox `m` is vector bit `m` (PIC source `m + 1`). The outbound lines are eight bits of `smc_mailbox_interrupt_o`, graded as a set. The two ports of one mailbox share a FIFO, so a push on one port can raise the line of the peer port. A line carries no state of another mailbox. Sources: `hw/sys/sep/doc/mailbox.adoc` ("Mailboxes"); `hw/ip/axi_lite_mailbox_unit/doc/architecture.adoc` ("Paired FIFOs", "Interrupts"); `hw/ip/axi_lite_mailbox_unit/doc/interface.adoc` ("Access Results", "Sending and Receiving"); `hw/ip/axi_lite_mailbox_unit/regs/gen/adoc/axil_mailbox.adoc` (`STATUS`, `WIRQT`, `RIRQT`, `IRQS`, `IRQEN`, `IRQP`, `CTRL`); `hw/sys/sep/doc/interrupts.adoc` ("SEP PIC source assignments"); `hw/sys/sep/doc/port_table.adoc` (`smc_mailbox_interrupt_o`).

*Test Coverage*: Threshold values 0, 7, 8 and 255 on both roles of FIFO A and of FIFO B on every seed, and drawn values (1, 6, 9 and other 8-bit values) on every mailbox, with occupancy moved across 0, 1, 7 and 8. Flush of each kind (`wflush`, `rflush`) on both ports while the other FIFO of the pair holds data, each kind on two drawn mailboxes. The two-threshold alias on FIFO A. The `IRQEN` gate on the line. The acknowledge with occupancy below and above the threshold. The lines of all 16 ports together; probe bit 14 is logged. The outbound lines as a set, up to all eight high. The width of the port. The test extends the open tests named below, and only the new cells are graded. On outbound mailbox 0 the open tests grade the write threshold and the `wtirq` gate of FIFO A, the `IRQS` write-one-to-clear while the occupancy is above the threshold, the outbound `wflush`, and the outbound read threshold of FIFO B at, over and drain. The leaf runs these cells on mailbox 0 as controls of the other mailboxes and prints them as `CTL-<NAME> LOG`, not as `CHK` lines. On outbound mailbox 0 only the thresholds 0, 7, 8, 9 and 255, the alias leg and the flush kinds other than the outbound `wflush` print `CHK` lines. `sep_mailbox_peer_rx_rirqt_test` keeps the round trip, one pop per read, the lost high half and `RIRQT` at, over and drain. `sep_mailbox_datapath_walk_test` keeps the empty and full bits of `STATUS` at every depth, the push-order walk, the strobe lanes and the partial push that makes one entry and does not merge. `sep_axil_mailbox_iface_rand_test` keeps one `wflush`, the `IRQP` gate and the `IRQS` write-one-to-clear at register level on outbound mailbox 0. `sep_mailbox_plic_test` keeps the delivery of the inbound line to PIC source `m + 1` for a push. `sep_mailbox_peer_rx_rirqt_test`, `sep_mailbox_datapath_walk_test` and `sep_axil_mailbox_iface_rand_test` share the run mode and the tool of this entry. `sep_mailbox_plic_test` runs firmware. Functional coverage: `sep_mbox_fifo_model_cg` (`x_occ_op`, `cp_boundary_move`, `cp_thresh_val`, `x_clamp`, `x_flush`, `x_alias_thresh`), `sep_mbox_irq_line_cg` (`x_gate`, `cp_w1c_ack`, `cp_line_iso`, `cp_quiet_glitch`) and `sep_mbox_transfer_cg` (`x_in_attr`, `x_out_count`).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Bring up in `no_cpu` mode with fuse sense skipped and ungate the mailbox clock. Reset SEP. Print `SEED seed=<S>` and a `DRAW` line for every drawn value. Read `$bits` of the `smc_mailbox_interrupt_o` port as declared on the DUT instance.
. With the CPU-LSU master, program one inbound filter window per mailbox over its inbound aperture (start `0x10A0_0800` + _m_ × `0x1000`, end `0x10A0_0FFF` + _m_ × `0x1000`): `entry_enabled` 1, `src_id` 0, read and write allowed. `SEP_DBG` stays off. The external master drives `AxPROT[1]` equal to `allow_ns`.
. Define the check cycle. After an operation, wait until `sep_internal_interrupts_probe_o` [7:0] and `smc_mailbox_interrupt_o` equal the golden model values (a bounded wait; a timeout fails the check cycle). Then run one quiet window: a fixed number of clocks, set by the test, with no access to the mailbox unit. Sample `sep_internal_interrupts_probe_o` [7:0], `smc_mailbox_interrupt_o` and bit 14 of the probe on every clock of the quiet window. Bit 14 is logged as `OBS-KM-LINE LOG bit14=b` and is not graded. Then read `STATUS`, `IRQS`, `IRQEN` and `IRQP` of both ports of the mailbox under test. Compare `STATUS` bits [3:2] with the golden model (CHK-STATUS) and print bits [1:0] against the model (`CTL-STATUS LOG`), and `IRQS` and `IRQP` with the golden model (CHK-LINE-IN, CHK-GATE, CHK-W1C). The model sets a cause bit of `IRQS` when the golden occupancy of the watched FIFO is above the golden threshold, keeps it until the test writes a one to it, and sets it again after that write while the occupancy condition still holds. `IRQP` is `IRQS` AND the `IRQEN` that the test wrote, and `IRQEN` reads back the written value. No expected value comes from a read-back of the DUT. When exactly one outbound model line rose in the step, log `OBS-SMC-MAP LOG mbox=m bit=o`.
. Draw the mailbox order, a permutation of 0 to 7. Run steps 5 to 10 on each mailbox in that order. Steps 11 to 14 run once, after the last mailbox. Each mailbox starts at its reset state: both FIFOs empty, `IRQS`, `IRQEN`, `WIRQT` and `RIRQT` 0. On mailbox 0 the cells named in Test Coverage as open cells (the outbound write threshold and `wtirq` gate of FIFO A, the acknowledge while above the threshold, the outbound `wflush` and the outbound read threshold of FIFO B) run in the same steps as controls and print `CTL-<NAME> LOG`.
. Threshold leg. On the first mailbox of the order take the boundary values 7, 0, 8 and 255 (7 first, as the reference of CHK-CLAMP) and then its drawn values. On every other mailbox take its drawn values. For each value run one fill on FIFO A and one on FIFO B. For each run: draw `IRQEN` in [0, 7] for both ports; write the value to the `WIRQT` of the write port and to the `RIRQT` of the read port of that FIFO; push to the fill count (the count is 8 for a value of 7 or more, and a drawn count in {value-1, value, value+1} with value-1 only above 0 for a smaller value); run a check cycle after each push; pop to 0 with a check cycle after each pop; then write `IRQS` as `0x7` on both ports. Pushes use a 64-bit full-strobe store or a 32-bit store at a drawn half. Pops use a 64-bit read or a 32-bit read at a drawn half.
. Alias leg. Draw two different thresholds `a` and `b` in [0, 7]. Write `WIRQT` of the outbound port as `a` and `RIRQT` of the inbound port as `b`. Push 8 distinct non-zero 64-bit full-strobe words into FIFO A through the outbound `WRITE_DATA`, with a check cycle after each push. Pop all 8 words through the inbound `READ_DATA`, compare each with the head of the golden queue (`CTL-ENTRY LOG`), and run a check cycle after each pop. Write `IRQS` as `0x7` on both ports.
. Flush leg. Run the flush kind drawn for the mailbox, one of the four kinds: `wflush` on the outbound port (discards FIFO A), `rflush` on the inbound port (discards FIFO A), `wflush` on the inbound port (discards FIFO B) and `rflush` on the outbound port (discards FIFO B). Over the eight mailboxes each kind runs twice. The outbound `wflush` control of mailbox 0 runs only when mailbox 0 draws that kind. For the drawn kind: push a drawn count of 1 to 8 distinct full-strobe words into FIFO A and another into FIFO B; run a check cycle; the `STATUS` of the port that reads the FIFO to be flushed is the pre-flush control and reads non-empty; write the flush bit of `CTRL` on the port of that kind; read `CTRL`; run a check cycle; pop the entries left in the FIFO that is not flushed, compare each with the head of the golden queue, and run a check cycle after each pop; write `IRQS` as `0x7` on both ports.
. Gate leg. Run it for each cause (`wtirq`, `rtirq`) on each port. Write `IRQEN` 0 and `WIRQT` and `RIRQT` 0 on the port, and write `IRQS` as `0x7`. Push one word into the FIFO that the cause watches (the write FIFO for `wtirq`, the read FIFO for `rtirq`) and run a check cycle: the cause bit of `IRQS` reads 1, `IRQP` reads 0 and the line of the port equals the model (low, because no other cause bit is set on that port). Write `IRQEN` with only that cause bit and run a check cycle: `IRQP` reads 1 and the line is high. Pop the word and write `IRQS` as `0x7`.
. Acknowledge leg. Run it for each cause on the outbound port and on the inbound port, with `IRQEN` set to only that cause bit. Draw a threshold `w` in [1, 6] and write it to the `WIRQT` (cause `wtirq`) or the `RIRQT` (cause `rtirq`) of the port. Push `w + 2` words into the watched FIFO and run a check cycle (cause set, line high). Pop 2 words so the occupancy is `w`, which is not above the threshold, and run a check cycle (the latched cause stays set and the line stays high). Write `IRQS` with that cause bit and run a check cycle (`IRQS` reads 0 and the line is low). Push 2 words so the occupancy is `w + 2` again and run a check cycle. Write `IRQS` with that cause bit while the occupancy is above the threshold, and run a check cycle (`IRQS` reads 1, the line stays high). Pop all words, write `IRQS` as `0x7` and write `IRQEN` 0.
. Drain the mailbox. Pop every remaining entry, write `IRQS` as `0x7` on both ports, write `IRQEN` 0, and run a check cycle. All lines of the mailbox are low.
. Outbound-set leg. It runs once, after the last mailbox. Write `IRQEN` as `0x1` and `WIRQT` 0 on the outbound port of every mailbox. Draw an order of all eight mailboxes and a subset size _k_ in [1, 6]. The first _k_ mailboxes of the order are the subset. Raise the outbound line of each member in order: one push into FIFO A through the outbound `WRITE_DATA`, then a check cycle. Raise mailboxes _k_ + 1 and _k_ + 2 back to back, with one check cycle after both pushes, so that two outbound model lines rise in one check cycle. Raise the remaining mailboxes one at a time with a check cycle after each, until all eight outbound lines are high (the port reads `0xFF`).
. With the outbound lines still high, write `IRQEN` as `0x1` and `WIRQT` 0 on the inbound port of each mailbox of the subset. Push one word through each of those inbound `WRITE_DATA` (external master), with a check cycle after each push. The inbound lines of the subset and all outbound lines are high.
. Release one at a time in drawn order. For an outbound line: pop the word through the inbound `READ_DATA`, write `IRQS` as `0x1` on the outbound port, run a check cycle. For an inbound line: pop the word through the outbound `READ_DATA`, write `IRQS` as `0x1` on the inbound port, run a check cycle. When all lines are released the port reads `0x00`.
. End state. Check that every FIFO is empty and write `IRQS` as `0x7` on all 16 ports. Run a check cycle: the 8 inbound lines and the whole outbound port read 0.

*Checkers*:

A check on an outbound mailbox 0 cell that an open test grades (Test Coverage) prints `CTL-<NAME> LOG` and is not a `CHK` line.

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-ENTRY
|A popped entry equals the head of the golden queue, with the half selected by address bit 2 for a 32-bit read (`hw/sys/sep/doc/mailbox.adoc`, "Mailboxes"). A DUT that returns the wrong entry or the wrong half after a flush fails. The check grades the pops of the entries left after a flush. The in-order, bit-exact pops of the alias leg are graded in `sep_mailbox_datapath_walk_test`; here they print `CTL-ENTRY LOG`. It grades only the entries whose push is a 64-bit full-strobe store. The strobed-byte lanes of a partial push are not compared. Anchor: the popped read data. Evidence: `CHK-ENTRY PASS seed=S mbox=m fifo=A half=1 got=0xH exp=0xH occ_before=n`.
|CHK-STATUS
|The two above bits of `STATUS` (bit 2, write level above; bit 3, read level above) of both ports equal the model after every operation of the threshold, flush and alias legs (`axil_mailbox.adoc`, `STATUS`; `architecture.adoc`, "Interrupts"). A bit that does not follow occupancy and threshold fails. Bits [1:0] (empty, full) at every depth are graded in `sep_mailbox_datapath_walk_test` (CHK-MBX-DEPTH); here they print `CTL-STATUS LOG`, except the reads after a flush that CHK-FLUSH grades. Anchor: `STATUS` read-back of both ports. Evidence: `CHK-STATUS PASS mbox=m port=out occ=n wirqt=a rirqt=b wabove=1 rabove=0 exp_wabove=1 exp_rabove=0`; `CTL-STATUS LOG mbox=m port=out occ=n empty=0 full=0 exp_empty=0 exp_full=0`.
|CHK-CLAMP
|A threshold of 8 to 255 acts as 7: the above bits at occupancy 7 and at occupancy 8 equal those read for threshold 7 in the same leaf, and equal the model (`architecture.adoc`, "Interrupts": the write is clamped to `MAILBOX_DEPTH - 1`). A DUT that wraps the value, or that ignores the upper bits, shows a different above bit at occupancy 7 or 8 and fails. Anchor: `STATUS` read-back at occupancy 7 and at occupancy 8. Control: the threshold 7 run supplies the reference. Evidence: `CHK-CLAMP PASS written=255 fires_at_occ=8 not_at_occ=7 ref_thr7_fires_at_occ=8`.
|CHK-FLUSH
|A flush bit discards exactly the selected FIFO (`architecture.adoc`, "Paired FIFOs": flushing a write FIFO discards data the peer would read; flushing a read FIFO discards data the peer has sent). After the flush, `STATUS` of both ports equals the model: the port that reads the flushed FIFO reads empty, and the other FIFO keeps its occupancy. A DUT that leaves the FIFO non-empty, or flushes the other FIFO, fails. Anchor: `STATUS` of both ports and the pops of the other FIFO. Control: the `STATUS` read of the same port before the flush reads non-empty. Evidence: `CHK-FLUSH PASS seed=S mbox=m kind=wflush port=out flushed=A reader_status_empty=1 pre_flush_reader_empty=0 other_occ=n exp_other_occ=n`.
|CHK-CTRL0
|`CTRL` reads 0 with an OKAY response after a flush write, because the flush bits are pulses (`interface.adoc`, "Access Results"; `memmap.adoc`, "Per-Mailbox Register Map"). A DUT that stores the flush bit fails. Anchor: `CTRL` read-back after each flush write. Evidence: `CHK-CTRL0 PASS mbox=m kind=rflush ctrl_read=0x0 resp=OKAY`.
|CHK-ALIAS
|The two above bits of FIFO A follow their own threshold when the thresholds differ: the write-level bit of the outbound port follows `WIRQT` and the read-level bit of the inbound port follows `RIRQT` (`architecture.adoc`, "Paired FIFOs"). A DUT that uses one threshold for both bits fails at an occupancy between `a` and `b`. Anchor: both `STATUS` bits against the model at every occupancy from 0 to 8. Evidence: `CHK-ALIAS PASS mbox=m wirqt_out=a rirqt_in=b occ_A=n wabove=x rabove=y exp_wabove=x exp_rabove=y`.
|CHK-LINE-IN
|The inbound line of mailbox `m` equals the OR of `IRQS` AND `IRQEN` of the inbound port, which is bit `m` of the vector (`architecture.adoc`, "Interrupts"; `interrupts.adoc`, "SEP PIC source assignments"). `IRQS` latches independently of `IRQEN` and stays set until acknowledged. A DUT that drops the line or the `IRQS` bit when the occupancy falls below the threshold before the acknowledge, that raises the line with the cause disabled, or whose `IRQS` or `IRQP` differs from the model, fails. Anchor: probe bit `m` after every check cycle, and the `IRQS` and `IRQP` read-back of both ports, against the model built from the golden queue, the golden thresholds and the written `IRQEN`. No expected value comes from a read-back of the DUT. Evidence: `CHK-LINE-IN PASS seed=S mbox=m port=in occ_B=n wirqt=a irqen=e irqs=0xH exp_irqs=0xH irqp=0xH exp_irqp=0xH probe=1 model=1`.
|CHK-LINE-OUT
|The number of high bits of `smc_mailbox_interrupt_o` equals the number of outbound ports whose model line is 1. The port reads `0x00` when every model line is 0 and `0xFF` when every model line is 1 (`mailbox.adoc`, "Mailboxes"; `port_table.adoc`). A DUT in which two outbound lines share one port bit shows a short count. The test does not compare a port bit with a mailbox index, because no text states the map. Anchor: the whole-port value of `smc_mailbox_interrupt_o` after every quiet window. Control: at least one window has two or more model lines high and one window has all eight high. Evidence: `CHK-LINE-OUT PASS seed=S high_model=k smc=0xH popcount=k all_zero_ok=1 all_one_ok=1`; `OBS-SMC-MAP LOG mbox=m bit=o` (logged, not graded).
|CHK-LINE-ISO
|A line moves only with the state of its own mailbox. While one line rises or falls, the seven other inbound lines equal their model values, and the Hamming distance between the settled samples of the outbound port of two consecutive check cycles equals the number of outbound ports whose model line changed. A DUT that couples two mailboxes fails. Anchor: probe bits [7:0] and the outbound port, in the same quiet window. Probe bit 14 (Key Manager mailbox line) is logged as `OBS-KM-LINE LOG bit14=b` and is not graded, because `interrupts.adoc` states no idle level for it. Control: the driven line moves in the same step. Evidence: `CHK-LINE-ISO PASS seed=S driven=m others=0xH model=0xH smc_hamming=1 model_changed=1`.
|CHK-GATE
|A cause raises the line only when its `IRQEN` bit is set, and `IRQP` equals `IRQS` AND `IRQEN` (`architecture.adoc`, "Interrupts"; `axil_mailbox.adoc`, `IRQP`). A DUT that raises the line with the cause disabled, or whose `IRQP` ignores `IRQEN`, fails. Anchor: `IRQS` and `IRQP` read-back and the line of the port. No other cause bit of that port is set in the step, so the model OR is the expected value. Control: the enabled case of the same cause raises the line. Evidence: `CHK-GATE PASS mbox=m cause=wtirq irqs=0x1 irqen=0x0 irqp=0x0 line=0 then irqen=0x1 irqp=0x1 line=1`.
|CHK-W1C
|An acknowledge clears a cause whose occupancy is not above the threshold, and a cause whose occupancy is still above the threshold reads 1 again (`architecture.adoc`, "Interrupts": acknowledge by writing ones; threshold status can reassert while the occupancy condition remains true; the status latches, so a cause whose occupancy fell to the threshold or below and that is not acknowledged still reads 1 and keeps the line high). A DUT that drops a latched cause before the acknowledge, drops a cause that is still above the threshold, or keeps one that is not, fails. Anchor: `IRQS` read-back and the line, with one enabled cause. Evidence: `CHK-W1C PASS mbox=m cause=wtirq wirqt=a occ_below=n1 occ_above=n2 below_before_ack=line1_irqs0x1 w1c_below=line0_irqs0x0 w1c_above=line1_irqs0x1`.
|CHK-WIDTH
|`smc_mailbox_interrupt_o` is 8 bits wide (`mailbox.adoc`, "Mailboxes"; `port_table.adoc`). A port of another width fails. Anchor: `$bits` of the `smc_mailbox_interrupt_o` port as declared on the DUT instance, not of a testbench signal. Evidence: `CHK-WIDTH PASS width=8`.
|CHK-GLITCH
|A line does not toggle inside a quiet window, because no access to the mailbox unit happens in it. The window starts after the settle wait of the check cycle, so no transition clock is graded: the spec states no completion latency (`interface.adoc`, "External Interface"). A DUT with a glitching line fails. Anchor: the line samples of every clock of each quiet window, counted after the sampled lines equal the model. Control: at least one quiet window holds a line high, and CHK-NONVAC shows that the sampler sees a rise. Evidence: `CHK-GLITCH PASS windows=N toggles=0 windows_line_high=N`.
|CHK-NONVAC
|At least one inbound line and at least one outbound line rise because of a driven push. Without this the line checks prove nothing. Anchor: the line samples before and after the driven push. Evidence: `CHK-NONVAC PASS in_rises=N out_rises=N`.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope limit*: No error injection is made: every push has space and every pop has data. The full write, the empty read and the error cause on the line belong to `sep_mailbox_access_error_inject_test`. The test does not claim the zero fill of unstrobed lanes that carry non-zero data, and it does not claim which port bit belongs to which mailbox (see <<sep-vplan-phase3-blocked,Blocked features>>). The open tests named in Test Coverage keep the cells that they grade. The outbound mailbox 0 cells that they grade are controls here and print `CTL-<NAME> LOG`.

'''''

[[sep_mailbox_access_error_inject_test]]
===== 3.14 `sep_mailbox_access_error_inject_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: Mailbox, IRQ, PIC

*Run mode*: `no_cpu` (`lsu_stub_all_live`), `+skip_fuse_sense`, 3 seeds

*Source Module*: `sep_mailbox_access_error_inject_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (CPU-LSU master on the outbound apertures; external SMN master through an open filter window for K1 to K6 on the inbound apertures, for K4, K5 and the `WRITE_DATA` read on both apertures); a golden mailbox model written from the spec text. Observation points: `sep_internal_interrupts_probe_o` bit `m` (inbound line; `hw/sys/sep/dv/tb/tb_top.sv`) and `smc_mailbox_interrupt_o` (outbound lines, graded as a count change; DUT port). No PROPOSED item. Every check is a reached check.

*Randomization*: RAND-REP. `SepSeededRng` from the run seed. Every seed runs a base injection set: K1, K2 and K3 on the outbound port and on the inbound port; K4 on both ports at the first hole word `0x50`, at a drawn interior hole word and at the last hole word `0x7F8`; K5 once as a read and once as a write; K6 once. The draws are: the order of the injection list; extra injections of any kind (K1 to K6); the mailbox of each injection (0 to 7, with K5 fixed to mailbox 7); the port of each extra injection (K5 and K6 on the inbound port only); the read or write operation of each extra K4 access; the hole offset (8-byte aligned, `0x50` to `0x7F8`); the half; a non-zero K4 write word whose bits [7:0] differ from the live `WIRQT` and `RIRQT` values and whose bits [2:0] differ from the live `IRQEN` values, on both ports; the two non-zero words of the K4 and K5 pre-state; distinct non-zero live values for K4 and K5 (`WIRQT` and `RIRQT` in [1, 6] and different from each other, `IRQEN` in [1, 7]); the past-extent address (`0x10A0_7850` to `0x10A0_7FF8`, 8-byte aligned). K1 and K2 are not drawn on outbound mailbox 0, and K3 is not drawn there because its pre-state uses K1. A same-cycle double error is not drawn. `reseed = 3` samples different list orders, extra injections, mailboxes, offsets, halves, words and live values. The base set, which holds every kind and port cell, every hole position and both K5 operations, runs on every seed.

*Objective*: A `READ_DATA` read of an empty FIFO answers `SLVERR` with data `0xFEEDDEAD`. A `WRITE_DATA` write to a full FIFO answers `SLVERR` and discards the data. Both set their error flag and `IRQS` bit 2. A write to a read-only register answers `SLVERR` and changes nothing. A 32-bit access at the inbound AXI port to an offset inside the aperture from `0x50` up, or past the wrapper extent, answers `SLVERR` with data 0x0 and changes no live register. A read of `WRITE_DATA` answers `OKAY` with `0xFEEDC0DE`. The error cause (`IRQS` bit 2) drives the line of its port only when `IRQEN.eirq` is set, and an `ERROR_FLAGS` read does not drop the line. Sources: `hw/ip/axi_lite_mailbox_unit/doc/architecture.adoc` ("Interrupts"); `hw/ip/axi_lite_mailbox_unit/doc/interface.adoc` ("Access Results", "Sending and Receiving"); `hw/sys/sep/regs/gen/adoc/memory_map.adoc` (SEP AXI-Lite Mailbox Wrapper row); `hw/ip/axi_lite_mailbox_unit/doc/memmap.adoc` ("Per-Mailbox Register Map"); `hw/ip/axi_lite_mailbox_unit/regs/gen/adoc/axil_mailbox.adoc` (`ERROR_FLAGS`, `IRQS`, `IRQEN`); `hw/sys/sep/doc/mailbox.adoc` (aperture offsets); `hw/ip/axi_filter/doc/index.adoc` ("Match, Then Permit", "Blocked Transactions").

*Test Coverage*: Five error kinds on both ports of the eight mailboxes: the empty read (K1), the full write (K2), the write to a read-only register (K3), the access to a hole inside an aperture (K4) and the access past the wrapper extent (K5). The access that the filter blocks (K6) runs as a control: the default-block verdict is graded in `sep_fabric_inbound_filter_rule_matrix_test` (CHK-BLOCK-DEFAULT) and in `sep_mailbox_peer_rx_rirqt_test`, so both K6 responses print `CTL-RESP LOG`. The two-flag read. The read of `WRITE_DATA` on 15 apertures. The error cause on the line of both ports. The test extends the open tests named below, and only the new cells are graded. `sep_axil_mailbox_iface_rand_test` keeps K1, K2, the flag read-clear, the `IRQS` write-one-to-clear and the read of `WRITE_DATA` on outbound mailbox 0. `sep_mailbox_peer_rx_rirqt_test` keeps the peer write to the inbound `WRITE_DATA` of mailbox 0 with the entry disabled (`DECERR`, `STATUS` unchanged). `sep_unmapped_access_policy_test` keeps the past-extent accesses from `0x10A0_8000` up. `sep_axil_mailbox_iface_rand_test` and `sep_mailbox_peer_rx_rirqt_test` share the run mode and the tool of this entry. This entry adds the other seven mailboxes, the inbound port, K3, K4, the wrapper tail `0x10A0_7850` to `0x10A0_7FFF`, the two-flag read, the read of `WRITE_DATA` on the other 15 apertures and the error cause on the line of both ports. Functional coverage: `sep_mbox_transfer_cg` (`cp_aperture_pos`, `cp_out_of_extent`, `x_err_kind_port`, `cp_err_resp`, `cp_err_flags`, `cp_wo_read`) and `sep_mbox_irq_line_cg` (`cp_err_line`).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Bring up in `no_cpu` mode with fuse sense skipped and ungate the mailbox clock. Reset SEP. Print `SEED seed=<S>` and a `DRAW` line for every drawn value. With the CPU-LSU master, program two inbound filter entries over each whole 4 KiB pair (start `0x10A0_0000` + _m_ × `0x1000`, end `0x10A0_0FFF` + _m_ × `0x1000`), one with `allow_ns` 0 and one with `allow_ns` 1, `src_id` 0, `entry_enabled` 1, read and write allowed. `SEP_DBG` stays off. The external master reaches both apertures of every pair.
. Build the injection list: the base set of the Randomization paragraph and the drawn extra injections, in drawn order. For each injection of kind K4 or K5, run step 3 on the accessed mailbox first. Then run the step of its kind (steps 4 to 8), then its positive twin (step 9). After the list, run steps 10 to 12.
. Live values (K4 and K5 only). On both ports of the accessed mailbox, write the drawn distinct non-zero values to `WIRQT`, `RIRQT` and `IRQEN`, and read each back. A value that reads 0 fails the leaf (`CTRL-MISSING`). Push one drawn non-zero full-strobe word into each FIFO of the mailbox (FIFO A through the outbound `WRITE_DATA`, FIFO B through the inbound `WRITE_DATA`); the thresholds are at least 1, so occupancy 1 is not above them. Read `STATUS` and `IRQS` bits 1:0 of both ports. Keep the six live read-back values and these `STATUS` and `IRQS` values as the pre-injection snapshot. For K5 the mailbox is 7.
. K1. On the drawn port, read `ERROR_FLAGS` (reads `0x0`) and `IRQS` (bit 2 reads 0). With its read FIFO empty, read `READ_DATA` with a 64-bit read. Expected response: `SLVERR`, low 32 bits `0xFEEDDEAD`, `ERROR_FLAGS.read_error` set, `IRQS` bit 2 set. Read `ERROR_FLAGS` (reads `0x1`). Read it again (reads `0x0`). Read `IRQS` (bit 2 still reads 1). Write `IRQS` bit 2 as 1. Read `IRQS` (bit 2 reads 0). The outbound port is driven by the CPU-LSU master and the inbound port by the external master.
. K2. On the drawn port, read `ERROR_FLAGS` (reads `0x0`) and `IRQS` (bit 2 reads 0). Push 8 distinct full-strobe words into its write FIFO. Write a ninth, different word to `WRITE_DATA`. Expected response: `SLVERR`, FIFO unchanged, `ERROR_FLAGS.write_error` set, `IRQS` bit 2 set. Read `ERROR_FLAGS` (reads `0x2`), read it again (reads `0x0`), read `IRQS` (bit 2 reads 1), write `IRQS` bit 2 as 1 and read `IRQS` (bit 2 reads 0). Pop the 8 entries through the peer port and compare them with the 8 pushed words in order. Read `STATUS` of the peer port: empty.
. K3. Arm the port: read `ERROR_FLAGS` (reads `0x0`) and `IRQS` (bit 2 reads 0), run the K1 access on the drawn port without reading `ERROR_FLAGS` afterwards, then push one word into its read FIFO through the peer port. Read `IRQS` (the armed value) and `STATUS`. Write a drawn non-zero value to `READ_DATA`, `STATUS`, `ERROR_FLAGS` or `IRQP` of that port. Expected response: `SLVERR`, no register change. Read `ERROR_FLAGS` (reads `0x1`, the armed flag), `IRQS` (equals the armed value) and `STATUS` (non-empty). Pop the entry and compare it with the pushed word. Read `STATUS`: empty. Write `IRQS` bit 2 as 1 and read `IRQS` (bit 2 reads 0).
. K4 and K5. From the external master, send a 32-bit read or write at the drawn half of the drawn 8-byte slot: for K4, offset `0x50` to `0x7F8` inside the drawn aperture; for K5, address `0x10A0_7850` to `0x10A0_7FF8`. A write carries the drawn K4 word. Expected response: `SLVERR`, data `0x0` on a read. Read `WIRQT`, `RIRQT` and `IRQEN` of both ports, and `STATUS` and `IRQS` bits 1:0 of both ports, and compare them with the snapshot of step 3. Pop each FIFO once through its reader port, compare the popped word with the word pushed in step 3, and read `STATUS` of both ports: empty.
. K6. Draw the K4 access on an inbound aperture. Send it from the external master with the window open. Expected response: `SLVERR` (`CTL-RESP`). Write `entry_enabled` 0 to both entries over the mailbox. Read `FILTER_CONFIG` of both entries and log `entry_enabled`. Send the same access again. Expected response: `DECERR` (`CTL-RESP`). A response that differs from the expected one prints `CTL-RESP FAIL` and fails the leaf. Write `entry_enabled` 1 to both entries.
. Twin. After each injection, run an access on the same port that a healthy design answers `OKAY`: for K1, a read of `READ_DATA` with one entry present; for K2, a write of `WRITE_DATA` with space; for K3, a write of `WIRQT`; for K4 and K5, a read of `STATUS`; for K6, a read of `STATUS` after the entries are enabled again. Check the response and drain what the twin changed.
. Two-flag corner. On a drawn port other than outbound mailbox 0, read `READ_DATA` with an empty read FIFO (K1). Push 8 words into the write FIFO of the same port. Write a ninth word (K2). Do not read `ERROR_FLAGS` between the two. Read `ERROR_FLAGS` once (reads `0x3`) and again (reads `0x0`). Pop the 8 words through the peer port and write `IRQS` bit 2 as 1.
. Error-line leg. On a drawn mailbox, run it first on the inbound port and then on the outbound port. Write `IRQEN` as 0 and `IRQS` as `0x7` on both ports of the mailbox, with both FIFOs empty. Note the number of high outbound model lines. Read `READ_DATA` with an empty read FIFO (K1). Wait one quiet window (a fixed number of clocks, set by the test, with no access to the mailbox unit). Read `IRQS` (bit 2 reads 1). The line is low. Write `IRQEN` as `0x4`. Wait a quiet window. The line is high. Read `ERROR_FLAGS` (reads `0x1`). Wait a quiet window. The line is still high. Write `IRQS` bit 2 as 1. Wait a quiet window. The line is low. For the outbound port the line is the count of high bits of `smc_mailbox_interrupt_o`.
. Write-only read leg. Read `ERROR_FLAGS` of all 16 apertures and write `IRQS` bit 2 as 1 on all of them, so no flag is armed. For each of the 15 apertures other than outbound mailbox 0: push one word into the read FIFO of the aperture through the peer port; read `STATUS` of both ports; from the external master, send a 32-bit read of `WRITE_DATA` at a drawn half; read `STATUS` of both ports again; read `ERROR_FLAGS`; pop the preloaded word and compare it with the pushed word; read `STATUS`: empty. Expected response of the `WRITE_DATA` read: `OKAY`, low 32 bits `0xFEEDC0DE`. Log the high 32 bits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-ERR-RD
|The empty read answers `SLVERR`, returns `0xFEEDDEAD` on the low 32 bits, and sets `ERROR_FLAGS.read_error` (`interface.adoc`, "Access Results"). A DUT that answers `OKAY`, returns other data or sets no flag fails. The specification states the data `0xFEEDDEAD` only, so the high 32 bits are logged and not graded. Anchor: the AXI response, the read data and the `ERROR_FLAGS` read-back. Evidence: `CHK-ERR-RD PASS seed=S mbox=m port=in resp=SLVERR data=0xFEEDDEAD read_err=1 irqs=0x4`.
|CHK-ERR-WR
|The full write answers `SLVERR`, discards the word, and sets `ERROR_FLAGS.write_error` (`interface.adoc`, "Access Results"). A DUT that answers `OKAY`, keeps the discarded word or sets no flag fails. Anchor: the AXI response, the 8 popped words in order followed by an empty `STATUS` (a kept ninth word shows as a non-empty FIFO), and the `ERROR_FLAGS` read-back. One injection runs at a time. Evidence: `CHK-ERR-WR PASS mbox=m resp=SLVERR occ=8 next_pops_match=1 empty_after=1 write_err=1`.
|CHK-RO
|A write to `READ_DATA`, `STATUS`, `ERROR_FLAGS` or `IRQP` answers `SLVERR` and changes no state (`interface.adoc`, "Access Results"). The armed read-error flag, the latched `IRQS` value and the occupancy read back unchanged after the write. A DUT that answers `OKAY`, clears the flag, pops the read FIFO or acts as a write-one-to-clear on `IRQS` fails. Anchor: the response and the read-back of `ERROR_FLAGS`, `IRQS` and `STATUS`, and the popped word. Control: CHK-TWIN. Evidence: `CHK-RO PASS mbox=m port=out reg=STATUS resp=SLVERR armed_flags=0x1 flags_after=0x1 armed_irqs=0xH irqs_after=0xH occ_before=n occ_after=n`.
|CHK-HOLE
|An access to an offset inside the aperture from `0x50` up answers `SLVERR` and reads data 0x0, and it leaves the live registers unchanged (`interface.adoc, "Access Results"; `memory_map.adoc`, SEP AXI-Lite Mailbox Wrapper row; `memmap.adoc`, "Per-Mailbox Register Map"). `WIRQT`, `RIRQT` and `IRQEN` hold distinct non-zero values before the injection, and the K4 write word differs from all of them in the field bits (bits [7:0] for `WIRQT` and `RIRQT`, bits [2:0] for `IRQEN`). An access to the low half of a slot that aliases a live register reads a non-zero value or, as a write, changes it. An access to either half that aliases a FIFO register pushes a word, pops a word or flushes a FIFO. Each fails. The fields of the live registers are in bits [7:0] (`axil_mailbox.adoc`), so an access to the high half of a slot reaches only reserved bits of an aliased register: for the high half, the response, the read data 0x0 and the FIFO state are graded, and the compare of `WIRQT`, `RIRQT` and `IRQEN` is a control that cannot show an alias. The test does not grade `ERROR_FLAGS` or `IRQS` bit 2 after a hole access, because the spec states no flag effect for it. A live value that reads 0 before the injection fails the leaf (`CTRL-MISSING`). Anchor: the response, the read data, the read-back of the three registers, `STATUS` and `IRQS` bits 1:0 of both ports, and the popped words with the final empty `STATUS`. Control: CHK-TWIN, and one word in each FIFO before the access, so a flush or a pop shows. Evidence: `CHK-HOLE PASS addr=0xH op=rd resp=SLVERR data=0x0 wirqt=0x3 rirqt=0x5 irqen=0x6 live_regs_same=1 status_irqs_same=1 pops_match=2 empty_after=1 twin=STATUS twin_resp=OKAY`.
|CHK-EXTENT
|The same contract as CHK-HOLE for an address from the wrapper extent end `0x10A0_7850` up to `0x10A0_7FFF`, in the inbound aperture of mailbox 7 (`memory_map.adoc`, SEP AXI-Lite Mailbox Wrapper row, `SLVERR, 0x0`). Anchor: the same, on mailbox 7. Control: CHK-TWIN. Evidence: `CHK-EXTENT PASS mbox=7 addr=0x10A07850 op=wr resp=SLVERR data=0x0 wirqt=0x3 rirqt=0x5 irqen=0x6 live_regs_same=1 status_irqs_same=1 pops_match=2 empty_after=1 twin=STATUS twin_resp=OKAY`.
|CHK-FLAGS-CLEAR
|The first `ERROR_FLAGS` read after K1 or K2 reports the flag, the second read returns 0, and `IRQS` bit 2 stays 1 until its write-one-to-clear (`interface.adoc`, "Access Results"; `architecture.adoc`, "Interrupts"). A DUT that misses the flag, does not clear it on read, or drops `IRQS` bit 2 on the read fails. Anchor: two `ERROR_FLAGS` reads and the `IRQS` read-back before and after the write. Evidence: `CHK-FLAGS-CLEAR PASS kind=K1 first=0x1 second=0x0 irqs_bit2=1 after_w1c=0`.
|CHK-FLAGS-BOTH
|When both errors occur before one `ERROR_FLAGS` read, the read reports both flags and the next read returns 0 (`interface.adoc`, "Access Results"). A DUT that reports one flag, or keeps a flag after the read, fails. Anchor: two `ERROR_FLAGS` reads. Evidence: `CHK-FLAGS-BOTH PASS mbox=m port=in first=0x3 second=0x0`.
|CHK-ERR-LINE
|The error cause drives the line of its port only when `IRQEN.eirq` is set: the empty read answers `SLVERR`, `IRQS` bit 2 latches, the line stays low while `IRQEN.eirq` is clear, rises when it is set, stays high after an `ERROR_FLAGS` read, and drops after the write-one-to-clear (`architecture.adoc`, "Interrupts": the `ERROR_FLAGS` read does not acknowledge the shared `IRQS` error bit). A DUT that ignores `IRQEN.eirq`, drops the line on the `ERROR_FLAGS` read or keeps it after the write-one-to-clear fails. Anchor: the response, the `IRQS` and `ERROR_FLAGS` read-back, probe bit `m` for the inbound port, and the count of high bits of `smc_mailbox_interrupt_o` for the outbound port (one more when the line rises and one fewer when it drops). Control: CHK-TWIN, and the line rises after `IRQEN.eirq` is set. Evidence: `CHK-ERR-LINE PASS mbox=m port=in resp=SLVERR irqs_bit2=1 line_before_enable=0 line_rise=1 error_flags=0x1 line_after_read=1 line_after_w1c=0`; `CHK-ERR-LINE PASS mbox=m port=out resp=SLVERR irqs_bit2=1 smc_count_before_enable=k smc_count_after_enable=k+1 smc_count_after_w1c=k`.
|CHK-WO-READ
|A read of `WRITE_DATA` answers `OKAY` with `0xFEEDC0DE` on the low 32 bits, moves no FIFO and sets no flag (`interface.adoc`, "Access Results"). A DUT that answers an error, returns other data, pops the preloaded read FIFO, pushes the write FIFO or sets a flag fails. Anchor: the response, the low 32 data bits, `STATUS` of both ports before and after, the popped preloaded word, and `ERROR_FLAGS`, on 15 apertures. The high 32 bits are logged. Evidence: `CHK-WO-READ PASS apertures=15 resp=OKAY data_lo=0xFEEDC0DE data_hi=0xH status_same=15 flags=0x0`.
|CHK-TWIN
|A "no change" check holds only when the port is live. The positive twin of each injection answers `OKAY` on the same port, so the unchanged state is not the result of a dead port. Anchor: the twin response. Evidence: `CHK-TWIN PASS kind=K3 twin=WIRQT twin_resp=OKAY`.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope limit*: The test drives no same-cycle double error. It does not grade the past-extent accesses from `0x10A0_8000` up, which `sep_unmapped_access_policy_test` owns. It does not re-grade the cells that `sep_axil_mailbox_iface_rand_test` and `sep_mailbox_peer_rx_rirqt_test` keep on outbound mailbox 0 and on the inbound `WRITE_DATA` of mailbox 0. The high 32 bits of the empty-read data and of the `WRITE_DATA` read are logged and not graded.

'''''

[[sep_mailbox_filter_type_matrix_test]]
===== 3.15 `sep_mailbox_filter_type_matrix_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: Mailbox, IRQ, PIC

*Run mode*: `no_cpu` (`lsu_stub_all_live`), `+skip_fuse_sense`, 3 seeds

*Source Module*: `sep_mailbox_filter_type_matrix_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (external SMN master through the enabled entries, with the source ID driver of `sep_fabric_inbound_filter_rule_matrix_test`; CPU-LSU master for the outbound reads and the filter programming); a golden filter match model written from `hw/ip/axi_filter/doc/index.adoc` ("Match, Then Permit"). Observation points: `sep_internal_interrupts_probe_o` bits [7:0] (`hw/sys/sep/dv/tb/tb_top.sv`) and the AXI responses. No PROPOSED item. Every check is a reached check.

*Randomization*: `SepSeededRng` from the run seed (RANDCFG). The draws are: the type of each mailbox (ISS, STEE, Regular; each of the three types on at least one mailbox); the ISS `src_id` (1 to 15); `allow_ns`; the transaction source ID (0 to 15); `AxPROT[1]`; the entry index (low or high); the mailbox order. The `src_id` of STEE and Regular entries is 0. DTEE is not drawn. The lock is the last write of the leaf. `reseed = 3` samples different type maps, source IDs, NS values and entry indexes. Every seed runs all three types, the admit draw of every mailbox, the reject draws of every ISS and STEE mailbox, and the no-entry leg on every mailbox, so every channel 0 to 7 has an admitted and a blocked write.

*Objective*: The mailbox type is the inbound filter entry over its aperture. Every entry tests `AxPROT[1]` against `allow_ns`. ISS adds a non-zero `src_id`. STEE has `src_id` 0 and one entry. Regular has `src_id` 0 and two enabled entries, one per `allow_ns` value, so it admits both `AxPROT[1]` values. A rejected access is blocked and answers `DECERR`. A blocked write moves no FIFO and raises no mailbox interrupt. `src_id` 0 is a wildcard. The lock bit freezes the entry registers. Sources: `hw/sys/sep/doc/mailbox.adoc` ("Mailboxes", mailbox types); `hw/ip/axi_filter/doc/index.adoc` ("Match, Then Permit", "Blocked Transactions", "Locking a Filter Entry"); `hw/ip/axi_filter/regs/gen/adoc/filter_ctrl.adoc` (`FILTER_CONFIG`).

*Test Coverage*: ISS and STEE cells, Regular cells with both `AxPROT[1]` values, the mailbox with no enabled entry, isolation between mailboxes 0 to 7, and the entry lock seen at the mailbox aperture. The verdict of the filter (source ID match, mismatch and wildcard, `allow_ns`, the default block with no enabled entry, and the response code of a blocked access) is graded in `sep_fabric_inbound_filter_rule_matrix_test` (open) and in `sep_fabric_filter_match_priority_rand_test` (Phase 3, 2.26: `CHK-FILTER-CELL`, `CHK-FILTER-SRC`, `CHK-RESET-DENY`). In this entry the response of each write is a precondition and is not graded (`CTL-RESP`). The test extends the open tests named below, and only the new cells are graded. `sep_fabric_inbound_filter_rule_matrix_test` (same run mode and tool) keeps the verdict of a source ID match and mismatch and the entry lock at the filter. `sep_fabric_remap_filter_csr_bank_test` keeps the lock of every entry and the `DECERR` of a write to a locked entry. `sep_mailbox_peer_rx_rirqt_test` keeps the write with the entry disabled on mailbox 0 (`DECERR`, `STATUS` unchanged). This entry adds the mailbox consequence of the verdict (FIFO, `STATUS`, `IRQS`, line) on mailboxes 0 to 7, and at the lock the old ID admitted and the new ID rejected at the mailbox aperture. Functional coverage: `sep_mbox_qualification_cg` (`cp_type`, `x_type_landing`, `x_admit_ch_line`, `cp_lock`, `cp_isolation`).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Bring up in `no_cpu` mode with fuse sense skipped and ungate the mailbox clock. Reset SEP. `SEP_DBG` stays off. Print `SEED seed=<S>` and a `DRAW` line for every drawn value. Every external write below carries a stated expected response. A response that differs from it prints `CTL-RESP FAIL` and fails the leaf, because the consequence checks need the stated verdict as their precondition.
. Draw the type of each mailbox and the mailbox order. With the CPU-LSU master, program the entries for each mailbox in that order. Every entry covers the inbound half (start `0x10A0_0800` + _m_ × `0x1000`, end `0x10A0_0FFF` + _m_ × `0x1000`), has `entry_enabled` 1, read and write allowed, and `allow_burst` 0. ISS: one entry with the drawn `src_id` and `allow_ns`. STEE: one entry with `src_id` 0 and the drawn `allow_ns`. Regular: two entries with `src_id` 0, one with `allow_ns` 0 and one with `allow_ns` 1.
. For each mailbox, with an access that its entry admits, write `IRQEN` as `0x1` and `WIRQT` as 0 on the inbound port. The admitted access carries the entry `src_id` (ISS) or any drawn source ID (STEE, Regular), and `AxPROT[1]` equal to `allow_ns`.
. Define the quiesce. Pop the outbound `READ_DATA` of the mailbox with the CPU-LSU master until `STATUS` reads empty, and count the pops. Then, with an admitted access, write `IRQS` as `0x7` on the inbound port. Run the quiesce before every access of steps 5 to 8.
. Per mailbox in drawn order, run the admit draw. Quiesce. Send an external write of a drawn non-zero word with `AxLEN` 0 to the inbound `WRITE_DATA`, with the source ID and `AxPROT[1]` that the entry admits. Expected response: `OKAY` (`CTL-RESP`). Wait one quiet window (a fixed number of clocks, set by the test, with no access to the mailbox unit). Probe bit `m` is high. Read `STATUS` of the outbound port: non-empty. Read `STATUS` of the outbound port of the other seven mailboxes: empty, and their inbound lines are low. Pop the word through the outbound `READ_DATA` and compare it with the pushed word. Run the quiesce. For a Regular mailbox run this step once for each `AxPROT[1]` value.
. Per mailbox in drawn order, after its admit draw, run the reject draws that its type allows. ISS: one write with a source ID different from `src_id` and the admitted `AxPROT[1]`, and one write with the admitted source ID and the other `AxPROT[1]`. STEE: one write with the other `AxPROT[1]`. Regular has no reject draw. For each reject draw: quiesce; send the write. Expected response: `DECERR` (`CTL-RESP`; error injection: wrong source ID, or wrong NS value). Wait a quiet window. Probe bit `m` is low. Count the entries by a drain of the outbound `READ_DATA` (0 pops). Read `IRQS` of the inbound port with an admitted access (reads 0).
. No-entry leg. Run it on every mailbox, in the drawn mailbox order. After the admit draw and the reject draws of the mailbox, run the quiesce, then write `entry_enabled` 0 to every entry over it with the CPU-LSU master. Send the external write with the attributes that its entry admitted before. Expected response: `DECERR` (`CTL-RESP`; error injection: no matching entry). Wait a quiet window. Probe bit `m` is low. Count the entries by a drain of the outbound `READ_DATA` (0 pops). Write `entry_enabled` 1 to every entry again. Read `IRQS` of the inbound port with an admitted access (reads 0).
. Lock leg. It is the last part of the leaf. Draw one ISS mailbox. Quiesce. Write `FILTER_CONFIG` of its entry with the same fields and `locked` 1. Write `FILTER_CONFIG` of the entry with a drawn different non-zero `src_id`. Expected response: `DECERR` (`CTL-RESP`; the open `sep_fabric_remap_filter_csr_bank_test` grades the response of a write to a locked entry). Read `FILTER_CONFIG` of the entry: `src_id` reads the old value. Send the external write with the old source ID. Expected response: `OKAY`. Wait a quiet window. Probe bit `m` is high. Quiesce. Send the external write with the drawn new source ID and the admitted `AxPROT[1]`. Expected response: `DECERR`. Wait a quiet window. Probe bit `m` is low. Count the entries by a drain of the outbound `READ_DATA` (0 pops).

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-ADMIT
|A write that the entry admits (precondition `CTL-RESP`: `OKAY`) adds one entry to the FIFO and raises the inbound line (`index.adoc`, "Match, Then Permit": the first matching entry decides; `mailbox.adoc`, "Mailboxes"). A DUT that loses the word, adds a wrong entry or raises no line fails. The verdict classes are graded by the fabric entries and are not graded here. Anchor: the `STATUS` of the outbound port, the popped word and probe bit `m`. Evidence: `CHK-ADMIT PASS seed=S mbox=m type=ISS src=5 prot1=0 occ=1 pop=0xH exp=0xH line=1 ctl_resp=OKAY`.
|CHK-REJECT
|A write that no entry admits (precondition `CTL-RESP`: `DECERR`) adds no entry and sets no `IRQS` bit and no line (`index.adoc`, "Blocked Transactions"). A DUT in which the blocked word lands in the FIFO, or that raises `IRQS` or the line, fails. Anchor: the drained occupancy, the `STATUS` of the outbound port, the inbound `IRQS` read-back and probe bit `m`. Control: the CHK-ADMIT draw on the same mailbox with the same `IRQEN` shows the line high. Evidence: `CHK-REJECT PASS mbox=m type=ISS src=9 entry_src=5 ctl_resp=DECERR occ=0 irqs=0x0 line=0 twin_line=1`.
|CHK-NOENTRY
|A write to a mailbox with no enabled entry (precondition `CTL-RESP`: `DECERR`) lands no word and raises no line (`mailbox.adoc`, "Mailboxes": the filter blocks by default; `index.adoc`, "Blocked Transactions"). A DUT in which the word lands fails. Anchor: the drained occupancy, the inbound `IRQS` read-back after the entries are enabled again, and probe bit `m`. Control: CHK-ADMIT on the same mailbox with its entry. Evidence: `CHK-NOENTRY PASS mbox=m enabled_entries=0 ctl_resp=DECERR occ=0 irqs=0x0 line=0`.
|CHK-ISO-MBX
|An admit to one mailbox changes the `STATUS` and the inbound line of no other mailbox. A DUT that routes the word or the line to another mailbox fails. Anchor: the `STATUS` of the outbound port and the inbound line of the other seven mailboxes, read in the same step as the admit. Control: the line of the admitted mailbox rises in that step. Evidence: `CHK-ISO-MBX PASS admitted=m admitted_line=1 others_status_same=7 others_lines=0x00`.
|CHK-LOCK
|After the `src_id` write to the locked entry (precondition `CTL-RESP`: `DECERR`), the entry keeps its old `src_id`: `FILTER_CONFIG` reads the old `src_id`, a mailbox write with the old source ID is admitted and a mailbox write with the attempted new source ID is rejected with `DECERR` (`index.adoc`, "Locking a Filter Entry"). A DUT that takes the new `src_id`, rejects the old ID or admits the new one, fails. Anchor: the `FILTER_CONFIG` read-back, the responses of the two mailbox writes at the inbound aperture, the drained occupancy and probe bit `m`. Control: the old-ID write is admitted, so the aperture is live. Evidence: `CHK-LOCK PASS mbox=m old_id=5 new_id=9 cfg_write_resp=DECERR cfg_src_after=5 old_resp=OKAY old_line=1 new_resp=DECERR new_occ=0`.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope limit*: The specification does not name the signal that carries the transaction source ID on the inbound port (see <<sep-vplan-phase3-blocked,Blocked features>>). The expected verdict comes from the match rule in `hw/ip/axi_filter/doc/index.adoc`, and the source ID driver of `sep_fabric_inbound_filter_rule_matrix_test` drives it. DTEE has no hardware and is not drawn. The response of every write is a precondition (`CTL-RESP`) and is not graded here: the verdict classes stay with the open and the Phase 3 filter tests named in Test Coverage, and the `DECERR` of a write to a locked entry stays with `sep_fabric_remap_filter_csr_bank_test`. The lock of every entry and the write with the entry disabled on mailbox 0 stay with the open tests named in Test Coverage.

'''''

[[sep_mailbox_debug_bypass_test]]
===== 3.16 `sep_mailbox_debug_bypass_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: Mailbox, IRQ, PIC

*Run mode*: `no_cpu` (`lsu_stub_all_live`), real fuse sense (no `+skip_fuse_sense`), 1 seed

*Source Module*: `sep_mailbox_debug_bypass_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (external SMN master for the inbound writes; CPU-LSU master for the filter programming, the `DEMOTE_1` write and the outbound pops); an OTP image with life-cycle state PROD; the stimulus helper `hw/sys/sep/dv/cocotb/seq_lib/sep_lcc_inbound_filter_gating_seq.py`. Observation points: `sep_internal_interrupts_probe_o` bits [7:0] (`hw/sys/sep/dv/tb/tb_top.sv`) and the AXI responses. No PROPOSED item. Every check is a reached check.

*Randomization*: None (directed). The life-cycle path has one legal sequence. The source IDs and the NS values of the six other mailboxes are directed constants: source IDs 1 to 6 and `AxPROT[1]` 0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1, in the order of mailboxes 0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 7.

*Objective*: The mailbox has no qualification of its own. While `SEP_DBG` bypasses the inbound filter, every mailbox accepts any inbound write and raises its interrupt. `DEMOTE_1` in PROD sets `SEP_DBG` only when bit 0 of `SIP_DIS` and of `SYS_DIS` is clear. Sources: `hw/sys/sep/doc/lifecycle_controller.adoc` ("In-Field Debug Demotion", "Debug and Functional Feature Control"); `hw/sys/sep/doc/mailbox.adoc` ("Mailboxes", mailbox types); `hw/sys/sep/doc/fabric.adoc` ("Filtering and Protection").

*Test Coverage*: The PROD block of a wrong source ID and of a mailbox with no entry, then acceptance on all eight mailboxes after the demote, with the FIFO entry, the occupancy, the line and the data match at the mailbox endpoint. The test extends `sep_lcc_uvm_inbound_filter_gating_test` (same run mode, `no_cpu` with real fuse sense, and the same filter regimes), and only the new cells are graded. That open test keeps the PROD block with `DECERR`, `DEMOTE_1` and the external admit after `SEP_DBG` at one filter entry, and `sep_fabric_outbound_route_attr_test` (Phase 3, 2.27, `CHK-OUT-NOBYPASS`) grades the `DECERR` before and the `OKAY` after `DEMOTE_1` with no inbound entry. The responses of the PROD block of the wrong source ID and of the mailbox with no entry, and the before and after response pair of mailbox 3, run here as controls (`CTL-PROD-BLOCK`, `CTL-NONVAC`) and are not graded. CHK-DBG-ACCEPT grades the mailbox 3 occupancy before and after the demote. This entry adds the mailbox endpoint on all eight mailboxes. Functional coverage: `sep_mbox_qualification_cg` (`cp_bypass_accept`, `cp_bypass_pair`).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Boot with real fuse sense. The OTP image holds life-cycle state PROD and distinct non-zero `SIP_DIS` and `SYS_DIS` values whose bit 0 is clear in both. Wait for the fuse sense to finish (a bounded wait; a timeout fails the leaf). Ungate the mailbox clock.
. With the CPU-LSU master, program one inbound filter entry over the inbound aperture of mailbox 3: `src_id` 5, `allow_ns` 0, `entry_enabled` 1, read and write allowed. Program no entry over mailbox 6 or over any other mailbox. Use the CPU-LSU master to write `IRQEN` as `0x1` and `WIRQT` as 0 on the inbound port of all eight mailboxes, and read `IRQEN` back (reads `0x1`), because mailbox 6 has no entry in PROD.
. PROD block. Send an external write of a drawn non-zero word to the inbound `WRITE_DATA` of mailbox 3 with source ID 9 and `AxPROT[1]` 0. Expected response: `DECERR` (error injection: wrong source ID). Send an external write of a drawn non-zero word to the inbound `WRITE_DATA` of mailbox 6 with source ID 9 and `AxPROT[1]` 1. Expected response: `DECERR` (error injection: no matching entry). After each write wait one quiet window (a fixed number of clocks, set by the test, with no access to the mailbox unit). The inbound line of that mailbox is low. Read `STATUS` of its outbound port: empty.
. Write `DEMOTE_1` with its demote bit set, through the CPU-LSU master.
. Repeat the mailbox 3 write of step 3 until it answers `OKAY`, with a bounded number of tries. No `OKAY` within the bound fails the leaf. Each try that answers `DECERR` leaves the mailbox empty. After the `OKAY` wait one quiet window. Probe bits [7:0] equal the mask of the mailboxes written so far.
. Send the mailbox 6 write of step 3 (source ID 9, `AxPROT[1]` 1). Expected response: `OKAY`. Wait one quiet window. Probe bits [7:0] equal the mask of the mailboxes written so far.
. For the six other mailboxes in the order 0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, send one external write each with a distinct non-zero word, the directed source ID and the directed `AxPROT[1]`. Expected response: `OKAY`. After each write wait one quiet window. Probe bits [7:0] equal the mask of the mailboxes written so far.
. For each of the eight mailboxes: read `STATUS` of the outbound port (non-empty). Pop one entry through the outbound `READ_DATA` with the CPU-LSU master and compare it with the pushed word. Read `STATUS` of the outbound port: empty.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CTL-PROD-BLOCK
|(Control of CHK-DBG-ACCEPT.) In PROD, with `SEP_DBG` not set, an inbound write with a wrong source ID to the ISS mailbox, and an inbound write to a mailbox with no entry, answer `DECERR`, leave the FIFO empty and leave the inbound line low (`fabric.adoc`, "Filtering and Protection": the filter blocks traffic that matches no entry; `index.adoc`, "Blocked Transactions"). The verdict is graded in `sep_lcc_uvm_inbound_filter_gating_test` and in the fabric entries. A DUT that admits either write fails the leaf. Anchor: the AXI response, `STATUS` of the outbound port and probe bit `m`, with `IRQEN.wtirq` set on the port so that a landed word shows as a high line. Control: CTL-NONVAC shows the same write on the same mailbox admitted after the demote. Evidence: `CTL-PROD-BLOCK PASS mbox=3 resp=DECERR occ=0 line=0`.
|CHK-DBG-ACCEPT
|While `SEP_DBG` bypasses the inbound filter, every mailbox accepts the write: the response is `OKAY`, the FIFO holds one entry, the inbound line is high and the popped data equal the pushed data (`fabric.adoc`, "Filtering and Protection"; `lifecycle_controller.adoc`, "In-Field Debug Demotion"; `mailbox.adoc`, "Mailboxes"). This holds for a mailbox with an entry whose source ID does not match, for a mailbox with no entry, and for the six directed writes. A DUT that still rejects, drops the data or raises no line fails. Anchor: the AXI response, `STATUS` and the pop of the outbound port, and probe bit `m`, on all eight mailboxes. On mailbox 3 the check also grades the occupancy pair: the outbound `STATUS` read of step 3 reads empty before the demote, and the FIFO holds one entry after the first `OKAY` write. A DUT whose mailbox 3 occupancy does not go from 0 to 1 across the demote fails. Control: CTL-PROD-BLOCK and CTL-NONVAC. Evidence: `CHK-DBG-ACCEPT PASS mbox=3 occ_before_demote=0 occ_after_demote=1`; `CHK-DBG-ACCEPT PASS mbox=6 entry=none src=9 prot1=1 resp=OKAY occ=1 line=1 data=0xH exp=0xH`.
|CTL-NONVAC
|(Control of CHK-DBG-ACCEPT.) The outcome changes with the demote: the same write on the same mailbox answers `DECERR` before the demote and `OKAY` after it. Without this, a DUT that never blocked in PROD, or never bypassed after the demote, would pass CHK-DBG-ACCEPT on one side only. The two responses are graded in `sep_lcc_uvm_inbound_filter_gating_test`. Anchor: the two AXI responses of the mailbox 3 write. Evidence: `CTL-NONVAC PASS mbox=3 resp_before_demote=DECERR resp_after_demote=OKAY`.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes and every control prints `CTL-<NAME> PASS`. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope limit*: The test does not draw `SYS_DIS` or `SIP_DIS` bits. It grades the mailbox endpoint after the bypass and does not grade the formula of `SEP_DBG` in other life-cycle states or with other disable-vector values. `sep_lcc_uvm_inbound_filter_gating_test` and the life-cycle tests keep those cells.

'''''

[[sep_mailbox_reset_clear_test]]
===== 3.17 `sep_mailbox_reset_clear_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: Mailbox, IRQ, PIC

*Run mode*: `no_cpu` (`lsu_stub_all_live`), `+skip_fuse_sense`, 3 seeds. One leaf runs on VCS for the X-free part and on Verilator for the value checks. Each leaf runs one reset round.

*Source Module*: `sep_mailbox_reset_clear_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (CPU-LSU master for the mailbox apertures and the filter programming; external SMN master for the inbound `WRITE_DATA` that the filter entry admits; the CPU-LSU master does all filter programming); a golden mailbox model for the reset values, written from the spec text. Observation points: the reset input `rst_ni`; `sep_internal_interrupts_probe_o` bits [7:0] and `smc_mailbox_interrupt_o` (the whole port is compared with `0x00`, so no port-bit map is used; `hw/sys/sep/dv/tb/tb_top.sv`, DUT port). No PROPOSED item. Every check is a reached check.

*Randomization*: RAND-REP. `SepSeededRng` from the run seed. The draws are: the pre-reset FIFO counts (1 to 8 per FIFO, with FIFO A above the `WIRQT` of the outbound port); `IRQEN` in [1, 7]; the thresholds in [1, 6]; the mailbox of the locked filter entry and the two mailboxes of the error injections (all different); the reset cell, one per leaf, out of nine equally likely cells: the operation that the reset hits {push, pop, `IRQS` write} x the offset class {0 to 7, 8 to 31, 32 to 64 clocks after the request handshake of that operation}; the mailbox and port of the operation and the offset inside the class. A push is drawn only below occupancy 8 and a pop only above occupancy 0. FIFO A of the second error mailbox is outside the count draw and is filled to 8 for error injection 2. FIFO A of the first error mailbox is empty at error injection 1 and takes its drawn count after it. Only a full SEP reset is drawn. `reseed = 3` samples different counts, enables, thresholds, reset cells and offsets. The reset cell is a seed-dependent cell: one regression does not fill the nine cells, and they close on a merge of regressions (`SEP_FCOV.adoc`, "Seed-dependent groups").

*Objective*: SEP reset empties all FIFOs, clears thresholds, error flags, interrupt status and enables, drops every mailbox line, and restores the ISS source ID of an inbound filter entry to its reset value. The reset source of the `locked` bit and of `entry_enabled` is not stated, so they are logged. Sources: `hw/ip/axi_lite_mailbox_unit/doc/architecture.adoc` ("Clock and Reset"); `hw/sys/sep/doc/mailbox.adoc` ("Mailboxes", the ISS source ID is reset by SEP reset); `hw/ip/axi_filter/regs/gen/adoc/filter_ctrl.adoc` (`FILTER_CONFIG` reset values).

*Test Coverage*: Reset in the middle of a push, a pop or an `IRQS` write at an offset class of 0 to 7, 8 to 31 or 32 to 64 clocks after the request handshake (one drawn cell in each leaf; the nine cells close on a merge of regressions), with a non-reset pre-state on all eight mailboxes. All 16 apertures after the reset. The 16 lines. The ISS source ID of the filter entry (the lock and `entry_enabled` after the reset are logged). The mailbox after the reset. The test extends `sep_reg_bit_bash_rand_test`, which keeps the reset values at idle. This entry is a separate leaf because it resets a mailbox unit that holds live traffic, a different reset state from the idle reset of `sep_reg_bit_bash_rand_test`, and only the new cells are graded. It adds the reset in the middle of a push, a pop or an `IRQS` write, the lines after the reset and the ISS source ID restore. Functional coverage: `sep_mbox_reset_cg` (`x_op_offset`, `cp_pre_nonzero`, `cp_post_state`, `cp_lines_low`, `cp_filter_restore`, `cp_reuse`).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Bring up in `no_cpu` mode with fuse sense skipped and ungate the mailbox clock. Reset SEP. Print `SEED seed=<S>` and a `DRAW` line for every drawn value.
. With the CPU-LSU master, write the drawn thresholds to `WIRQT` and `RIRQT` and the drawn `IRQEN` to every one of the 16 ports. The `IRQEN` of the inbound port of the first error mailbox and of the outbound port of the second error mailbox includes bit 2 (`eirq`).
. Filter entry. With the CPU-LSU master, program one inbound entry over the inbound aperture of the drawn filter mailbox: `src_id` 5, `allow_ns` 0, `entry_enabled` 1, read and write allowed. From the external master, send a write with source ID 5 and `AxPROT[1]` 0 to the inbound `WRITE_DATA` of that mailbox. Expected response: `OKAY`. Write `FILTER_CONFIG` with the same fields and `locked` 1. Read `FILTER_CONFIG` (`locked` reads 1, `src_id` reads 5).
. Error injection 1. On the inbound port of the first error mailbox, with FIFO A empty, read `READ_DATA`. Expected response: `SLVERR`, read-error flag set, `IRQS` bit 2 set. Do not read `ERROR_FLAGS`.
. Fill the FIFOs. For each mailbox, including the first error mailbox after error injection 1, push the drawn count into FIFO A through the outbound `WRITE_DATA` and into FIFO B through the inbound `WRITE_DATA`. Every drawn count is above 0. The count of FIFO B of the filter mailbox includes the word of step 3. The count of FIFO A is above the `WIRQT` of the outbound port. The count of FIFO A of the second error mailbox is 8.
. Error injection 2. On the outbound port of the second error mailbox, with FIFO A at 8 entries, write `WRITE_DATA`. Expected response: `SLVERR`, write-error flag set, `IRQS` bit 2 set. Do not read `ERROR_FLAGS`.
. Pre-state read-back. Wait one quiet window (a fixed number of clocks, set by the test, with no access to the mailbox unit). Sample probe bits [7:0] and the whole `smc_mailbox_interrupt_o` and log them. At least one inbound line and one outbound line are high. For every port read `STATUS` (empty 0), `WIRQT`, `RIRQT` and `IRQEN` (all non-zero). For the outbound port of every mailbox read `IRQS` (bit 0 reads 1). For the two error ports read `IRQS` (bit 2 reads 1). Do not read `ERROR_FLAGS`.
. Take the drawn reset cell: the operation that the reset hits (a push, a pop or an `IRQS` write) and the offset class, with the drawn mailbox, port and offset inside the class. Start the operation with the CPU-LSU master. The master holds the ready of the response channel low (`BREADY` for a push or an `IRQS` write, `RREADY` for a pop) from the start of the operation. Wait for the request handshake in a bounded wait: the later of the AW and W handshakes for a push or an `IRQS` write, the AR handshake for a pop, each with VALID and READY high in the same clock on the channel monitor of the master. A timeout logs `CTRL-MISSING` and fails the leaf. At the drawn offset, in clocks after the request handshake, assert `rst_ni` low for the same duration as the reset of step 1 (CTL-OP-INFLIGHT), and release it. The master abandons the outstanding transaction while `rst_ni` is low, so no beat or retry of it reaches the unit after the release. The response of the interrupted operation is not graded. No access to the mailbox unit is issued before the sample of step 10.
. Repeat the bring-up of step 1 (fuse sense skipped, mailbox clock ungated) without reprogramming any mailbox register.
. Wait one quiet window. Sample probe bits [7:0] and the whole `smc_mailbox_interrupt_o`.
. Read all 16 apertures with the CPU-LSU master: `STATUS`, `IRQS`, `IRQEN`, `WIRQT`, `RIRQT`, `IRQP` and `ERROR_FLAGS`. On VCS keep every bit as sampled, without mapping X to 0.
. Read `FILTER_CONFIG` of the entry of step 3. Grade `src_id` (CHK-RESET-FILTER). Log `locked`, `entry_enabled` and `allow_ns` as `OBS-FILTER-RESET LOG`. From the external master, send the write of step 3 (source ID 5, `AxPROT[1]` 0) and log its response. The response and the later state of the entry are not graded, because the specification does not state which reset restores the lock and `entry_enabled` (see <<sep-vplan-phase3-blocked,Blocked features>>).
. On a drawn mailbox, push one word through the outbound `WRITE_DATA` with the CPU-LSU master. Expected response: `OKAY`. Pop it through the inbound `READ_DATA` with the CPU-LSU master and compare it with the pushed word.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CTL-OP-INFLIGHT
|(Control of the drawn reset cell.) The reset hits an operation in flight: at the falling edge of `rst_ni` the channel monitor of the CPU-LSU master shows the request handshake of the operation (AW and W for a push or an `IRQS` write, AR for a pop) and no B or R handshake after it. A missing request handshake, or a response handshake before the falling edge, logs `CTRL-MISSING` and fails the leaf. A response VALID before the falling edge is logged and not graded, because the unit states no fixed completion cycle (`interface.adoc`: software must not assume a fixed completion cycle). Anchor: the AW, W, AR, B and R handshakes on the channel monitor of the CPU-LSU master, and `rst_ni`. Evidence: `CTL-OP-INFLIGHT PASS op=<push|pop|irqs> mbox=m port=<out|in> req_hs=1 resp_hs=0 offset=<clocks> offset_class=<c>`; `OBS-OP-INFLIGHT LOG op=<o> resp_valid=<0|1>`.
|CHK-PRE-NONZERO
|(Vacuity guard.) The pre-reset state differs from the reset state, so the reset checks can fail. Before the reset: on every port `STATUS.empty` reads 0 (reset value 1) and `WIRQT`, `RIRQT` and `IRQEN` are non-zero; on the outbound port of every mailbox `IRQS` bit 0 reads 1; the two error injections answered `SLVERR`; `IRQS` bit 2 reads 1 on the two error ports; at least one inbound line and one outbound line are high. The error flags are witnessed by the two responses and by `IRQS` bit 2, because an `ERROR_FLAGS` read clears them. A pre-state that already equals the reset state fails the leaf. Anchor: the read-back of the registers and the line samples. Evidence: `CHK-PRE-NONZERO PASS mbox=m status_out=0xH status_in=0xH wirqt=a rirqt=b irqen=0x5 irqs_out=0x5 inj_rd=SLVERR inj_wr=SLVERR lines_pre_probe=0xH lines_pre_smc=0xH`.
|CHK-RESET-STATE
|After the reset, on each of 16 apertures, `STATUS` reads empty 1, full 0 and both above bits 0, and `IRQS`, `IRQEN`, `WIRQT`, `RIRQT`, `IRQP` and `ERROR_FLAGS` read 0 (`architecture.adoc`, "Clock and Reset": reset empties the FIFOs and clears thresholds, error flags, interrupt status and enables). On VCS no bit reads X. A DUT that keeps a pre-reset value, or leaves a register unreset, fails. Anchor: the read-back of the 16 apertures. Evidence: `CHK-RESET-STATE PASS seed=S op=<push|pop|irqs> offset=<clocks> offset_class=<c> apertures=16 status_empty=16 regs_zero=16 x_free=1`.
|CHK-RESET-LINES
|The 8 inbound lines and the whole outbound port read 0 after the release (`architecture.adoc`, "Clock and Reset"). A DUT that holds a line high through the reset fails. Anchor: probe bits [7:0] and the whole port of `smc_mailbox_interrupt_o`, compared with `0x00`. Control: CHK-PRE-NONZERO shows an inbound line and an outbound line high before the reset. Evidence: `CHK-RESET-LINES PASS probe=0x00 smc=0x00 pre_probe=0xH pre_smc=0xH`.
|CHK-RESET-FILTER
|The reset restores the ISS source ID of the inbound filter entry: after the reset `FILTER_CONFIG.src_id` reads 0, its reset value (`mailbox.adoc`, "Mailboxes": the ISS source ID is reset by SEP reset; `filter_ctrl.adoc`, `FILTER_CONFIG`). A DUT that keeps the programmed source ID fails. The `locked` bit, `entry_enabled` and the response of the external write after the reset are logged and not graded, because the specification does not state which reset restores them. Anchor: the `FILTER_CONFIG` read-back. Control: before the reset `FILTER_CONFIG` reads `locked` 1 and `src_id` 5, and the same external write is admitted. Evidence: `CHK-RESET-FILTER PASS pre_cfg=0xH pre_src_id=5 src_id=0x0`; `OBS-FILTER-RESET LOG cfg=0xH locked=l entry_enabled=e ext_write=R`.
|CHK-REUSE
|The mailbox works after the reset: one push answers `OKAY` and the pop returns the pushed word (`interface.adoc`, "Sending and Receiving"). A mailbox that stays dead after the reset fails. Anchor: the push response and the popped data. Evidence: `CHK-REUSE PASS mbox=m push_resp=OKAY pop_data=0xH exp=0xH`.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes and the control prints `CTL-OP-INFLIGHT PASS`. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope limit*: The test drives a full SEP reset only. The effect of a CPU-only reset on the mailbox is not stated, and the test does not drive it. The state of the operation that the reset interrupts is not graded. The X-free half of CHK-RESET-STATE is graded on VCS only; Verilator grades the values. `sep_reg_bit_bash_rand_test` keeps the reset values at idle.

'''''
[[sep_pic_reg_rand_test]]
===== 3.18 `sep_pic_reg_rand_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: Mailbox, IRQ, PIC

*Run mode*: `cpu`, `+skip_fuse_sense`, 3 seeds. VCS (4-state) for the reset X check, Verilator for the value checks. Testlist groups `all`, `cpu`.

*Source Module*: `sep_pic_reg_rand_test`

*BFM / Model*: CPU firmware with the PIC driver `hw/sys/sep/dv/fw/drivers/sep_pic.h` and the mailbox driver `hw/sys/sep/dv/fw/drivers/sep_axil_mailbox.h` (control source only); host console scorer. Probes and injects: firmware CSR reads and writes of the PIC registers, and the firmware trap count; `pic_rd_data_probe_o`, a read-only copy of the PIC register read data (`picm_rd_data`) at each PIC register read (an observation tap the test adds to the SEP_TB_ARCH observation-probe list; it is the anchor of CHK-RESET-X).

*Randomization*: RAND-REP. `SepSeededRng` from the run seed. Dimensions: the source index N (1 to 255, with the anchors 1, 43, 44, 128 and 255 always walked, and at least one drawn entry in each of the ranges 2 to 42, 45 to 127 and 129 to 254); the register group; the value (inside the implemented bits: `meipl` 0 to 15, `meie` 0 or 1, `meigwctrl` 0 to 3, so that every `meigwctrl` value is written at least once per seed, and so that over the drawn sources the pair (`meie`, `meipl`) takes each of the four arming cells (0, 0), (1, 0), (0, non-zero) and (1, non-zero) at least once per seed); the `meigwclr` write value (any non-zero 32-bit value); the hole address (4-byte aligned, inside each hole range, with an entry index K from 1 to 254 in address bits [9:2]); the order of the groups. Entry 0 is outside the read-back draw. The host patches the drawn lists, including the hole addresses, into the firmware parameter block. `reseed = 3` samples different entries, values, hole addresses and orders. The five hole ranges and the past-extent range are walked on every seed.

*Objective*: The PIC register groups sit at base 0xC008_0000 plus 0x0, 0x1000, 0x2000, 0x3000, 0x4000 and 0x5000 with stride 4 (`mpiccfg` is one register), and every field resets to 0. Entry 0 of `meipl`, `meie`, `meigwctrl` and `meigwclr` reads 0 and discards writes. `meigwclr` reads 0. A CPU access to a hole inside the 32 KiB aperture or past the 21 KiB extent answers OKAY and reads 0 (EL2_PIC row, columns Hole in Extent and Past Extent: `OKAY, 0x0 / OKAY`). A hole write answers OKAY and changes no decoded register, because a hole is an undecoded offset. Source 0 never sets. Sources: `hw/sys/sep/doc/interrupts.adoc` ("Sources and Routing", "Software Handling"); `hw/sys/sep/regs/gen/adoc/memory_map.adoc` (EL2_PIC row); `hw/sys/sep/regs/gen/adoc/blocks/el2_pic.adoc` (`mpiccfg`, `meipl`, `meip`, `meie`, `meigwctrl`, `meigwclr`).

*Test Coverage*: Reset reads of the six register groups; read-back of `meipl`, `meie`, `meigwctrl` and `mpiccfg.priord` at every entry class (1, 2 to 42, 43, 44, 45 to 127, 128, 129 to 254, 255); the five hole ranges (0x0400 to 0x0FFC, 0x1020 to 0x1FFC, 0x2400 to 0x2FFC, 0x3004 to 0x3FFC, 0x4400 to 0x4FFC) and the past-extent range 0x5400 to 0x7FFC, read, and written with the decoded registers that a hole write could alias to armed and read back (the last entry of each writable array, the entry at the same low offset in each array, and `mpiccfg`); entry 0 of the four arrays with all-ones writes; the `meigwclr` read after a write; source 0 with an all-ones entry 0 and with a level, active-low entry 0, and the source 1 handler control. This entry extends `sep_pic_irq_source_map_delivery_test` (same run mode and tool), which grades the delivery of the catalog sources through the PIC, and it leaves the `meip` pending map of the driven sources to `sep_pic_pending_map_walk_rand_test` of this plan, so it reads `meip` at reset only. Only the new cells above are graded here. The open test keeps the delivery cells. Functional coverage: `sep_pic_reg_map_cg`, `sep_pic_no_delivery_cg`.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
