Dimensions: the order of the blocks hmac, kmac and otbn (every seed faults all three, so the latched set grows through the sizes 1, 2 and 3); the order of the three blocks in the same-cycle sweep; the in-extent hole offset inside the block (a stated hole); read or write for each re-fault after step 3 (the first fault of each block in step 3 is a write); the clear order (a permutation of the bits 0 to 6); the clear masks over bits [6:0] (1 to 3 steps; each mask holds at least two set bits, at least one of them the bit of an unlatched block); the re-trigger choice; the DMA source address (inside the fixed outbound filter window of step 11) and transfer size. An offset outside the block extent is a decode error and is not drawn. `reseed = 3` samples different block orders, holes, clear orders, masks and DMA sizes.

*Objective*: A CPU access that gets a TL-UL error from a bridge at an unmapped offset latches its block bit, and the faulting access answers `SLVERR`. Source 43 is the OR of the seven bits `aes`, `hmac`, `kmac`, `otbn`, `csrng`, `edn`, `wdt`. Each `PERIPH_BUS_ERR_CLEAR` bit clears only its own block, and both clear registers read 0. `DMA_BUS_ERR_CLEAR.clr` clears both DMA latches only for a written 1. A non-OKAY AXI response to a DMA transfer sets `ERROR_CODE.BUS_ERROR` and `STATUS.ERROR`, latches `host_path_err` (not `reg_path_err`) and raises source 42. A fault that arrives in the same cycle as the clear of its own latch still latches, so a clear cannot drop a concurrent fault. Sources: `hw/sys/sep/doc/interrupts.adoc` (sources 41 to 43); `hw/sys/sep/regs/gen/adoc/blocks/sep_cpu_ctrl.adoc` (`PERIPH_BUS_ERR_STATUS`, `PERIPH_BUS_ERR_CLEAR`, `DMA_BUS_ERR_STATUS`, `DMA_BUS_ERR_CLEAR`); `hw/sys/sep/doc/crypto.adoc` ("Single-Beat Access Only"); `vendor/lowRISC/opentitan/overlay/regs/secure_dma/regs/gen/adoc/secure_dma.adoc` (`ERROR_CODE`, `STATUS`).

*Test Coverage*: One to three latched block bits from in-extent holes of hmac, kmac and otbn; the clear matrix of the seven clear bits against the latched bits; the drain to zero; mask clears that include unlatched bits; the re-trigger of a cleared block and of a block that is still set; the clear register reads; the DMA register-path latch with a write of 0 and a write of 1; the DMA host-path latch from a non-OKAY response to a DMA source read; the host-path clear cells; the same-cycle fault and clear for a peripheral block; the same-cycle fault and clear for the DMA host path. This entry extends `sep_irq_ip_to_aggregator_test` and `sep_periph_bus_err_misaligned_test` (same run mode and tool), which grade a single-block latch and the DMA register-path latch and clear, and `sep_dma_basic_test`, which grades a destination-side fabric non-OKAY with an exclusive `host_path_err`, its clear and a recovery copy. Only the new cells are graded here: the `SLVERR` of a hole write and the latch that it sets, the multi-block set, the clear matrix, the mask clear, the re-trigger, the clear register reads, the `DMA_BUS_ERR_CLEAR` write of 0, the source-read side of the DMA host-path fault and the same-cycle fault and clear. The open owners keep the rest. The `SLVERR` of a hole read, the `SLVERR` of a CPU read or write to an unmapped Secure DMA register offset, the `reg_path_err` latch and its clear by a write of 1 are graded in `sep_irq_ip_to_aggregator_test`; here they are controls and print `CTL-RESP LOG`, `CTL-LATCH LOG` and `CTL-DMA-CLR LOG`. Functional coverage: `sep_fault_source_report_cg`, `sep_fault_source_ack_cg`, `sep_dma_host_fault_cg`.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. The host draws the dimensions with `SepSeededRng` and prints `SEED seed=<S>` and `DRAW` lines. After reset, the CPU-LSU master reads `PERIPH_BUS_ERR_STATUS` and `DMA_BUS_ERR_STATUS`: both read 0, and on VCS no bit is X. The host reads vector bits 40 to 42: all read 0 (CHK-CTRL).
. Control. For each drawn block, the CPU-LSU master reads one legal aligned register (an HMAC, KMAC or OTBN CSR). Each read answers OKAY and `PERIPH_BUS_ERR_STATUS` still reads 0 (CHK-CTRL).
. Error injection. For each drawn block in the drawn order, the CPU-LSU master writes to the drawn in-extent hole offset of the block. Expected response: `SLVERR` to the write (CHK-RESP). After each access, the master reads `PERIPH_BUS_ERR_STATUS`: it equals the set of blocks faulted so far (CHK-LATCH), and vector bit 42 equals 1 (CHK-OR).
. Error injection. The CPU-LSU master accesses an unmapped Secure DMA register offset. Expected response: `SLVERR` (`CTL-RESP LOG`). `reg_path_err` latches, and the master reads `DMA_BUS_ERR_STATUS`: it equals 0b01, and vector bit 40 reads 1 (`CTL-LATCH LOG`, the set-up of the DMA clear cells).
. With both status registers non-zero, the master reads `PERIPH_BUS_ERR_CLEAR` and `DMA_BUS_ERR_CLEAR`: both read 0 (CHK-CLR-READ0).
. DMA register-path cells. The master writes 0 to `DMA_BUS_ERR_CLEAR.clr`: `DMA_BUS_ERR_STATUS` still equals 0b01 and vector bit 40 reads 1 (CHK-DMA-CLR). The master writes 1: `reg_path_err` reads 0 and vector bit 40 reads 0 (`CTL-DMA-CLR LOG`, the control of the write of 0). `host_path_err` reads 0 and vector bit 41 reads 0 (CHK-DMA-CLR, the host-path 0 cell; its control is CHK-HOST of the same leaf, where a healthy DUT sets `host_path_err`).
. Clear matrix. For each clear bit i in the drawn order over the bits 0 to 6: the master first faults every drawn block whose bit reads 0, so that the full set of the three block bits is latched (CHK-NONVAC). It writes 1 to bit i only. It reads `PERIPH_BUS_ERR_STATUS`: the status equals the set minus bit i. A clear of an unlatched bit leaves the set unchanged. Vector bit 42 equals (status != 0) (CHK-CLR-MATRIX).
. Drain. The master restores the full drawn set. It clears the latched bits one at a time in the drawn order. After each clear, the status equals the set minus the cleared bits, and vector bit 42 stays 1 while any bit is set and drops with the last bit (CHK-CLR-MATRIX).
. Mask clears. For each of the 1 to 3 drawn steps: the master restores the full drawn set (CHK-NONVAC), writes the drawn mask over bits [6:0] (the mask includes bits of unlatched blocks), and reads the status. The status equals the previous status AND NOT the mask, and vector bit 42 equals (status != 0) (CHK-MASK).
. Re-trigger. The master restores the full drawn set. It clears one drawn block and faults that block again: its bit sets again and the other bits keep their values. It then faults a block whose bit is still set: the bit stays set and the other bits keep their values (CHK-AGAIN).
. Host-path fault (error inject). The master writes 1 to `DMA_BUS_ERR_CLEAR.clr` and reads `DMA_BUS_ERR_STATUS` as 0. Before the first copy of the leaf, it programs an outbound filter entry pair (one entry with `allow_ns` 0 and one with `allow_ns` 1, read allowed, `src_id` 0, because the Secure DMA leaves the source ID at `OTHERS`) over a fixed source window of the SMU aperture at its reset values (`0x8000_0000` to `0xBFFF_FFFF`), above `0x8000_1000` and away from the console and verdict words of the responder, and large enough for the largest drawn copy. The outbound filter has no bypass and blocks traffic that matches no entry (`fabric.adoc`), so without the entry pair no source read reaches `smn_outbound_axi_req_o`. It programs a DMA copy of the drawn size from the drawn source address inside the window, which the outbound responder serves, into SRAM. The DMA enabled memory range is set wide enough that no address check masks the bus error. The inject makes the responder answer every source read of the copy with `SLVERR`. The master reads `STATUS`: `BUSY` and `ERROR` read 0 (the idle check). It starts the copy and waits for `STATUS.ERROR` in a bounded wait; a timeout fails CHK-HOST. It reads `ERROR_CODE`, `STATUS` and `DMA_BUS_ERR_STATUS`. Expected response: `ERROR_CODE.BUS_ERROR` 1, `STATUS.ERROR` 1, `DMA_BUS_ERR_STATUS` 0b10 (`host_path_err` only), vector bit 41 at 1 and vector bit 40 at 0. The outbound port monitor shows one or more source reads that got `SLVERR`, and a count of 0 fails the check (CHK-HOST).
. Host-path clear cells (error inject). With `host_path_err` set alone, the master writes 0 to `DMA_BUS_ERR_CLEAR.clr`: both latches keep their state. It writes 1: both latches clear and vector bits 40 and 41 read 0. To latch both bits, the master writes 1 to `STATUS.ERROR` (RW1C) and reads `STATUS`: `BUSY` and `ERROR` read 0 (the idle check). It starts a second failing DMA copy as in step 11 and waits for `STATUS.ERROR` in a bounded wait: `host_path_err` latches. It then accesses an unmapped Secure DMA register offset: `reg_path_err` latches and `DMA_BUS_ERR_STATUS` equals 0b11. The master repeats the write of 0 and the write of 1 (CHK-DMA-CLR, host-path cells). It writes 1 to `STATUS.ERROR` so that the next transfer starts from the idle state.
. Peripheral same-cycle fault and clear. For each of the three blocks in the drawn sweep order, the master latches the bit of the block. It then issues the clear write for that bit on the write channel and a faulting hole read to the same block on the read channel, and sweeps the offset between the two over a range of clocks (a test parameter) until `sep_cpu_ctrl_err_pulse_probe_o` shows the fault pulse and the clear pulse of that block in one cycle and no later fault pulse of that block before the status read. A sweep that never shows the coincidence fails CHK-RACE. After the coincidence, the master reads `PERIPH_BUS_ERR_STATUS` and the vector (CHK-RACE).
. DMA same-cycle fault and clear (error inject). The sweep covers a bounded range of clock offsets (a test parameter) between the failing source read of a copy and the `DMA_BUS_ERR_CLEAR` write. For each offset: the master writes 1 to `STATUS.ERROR` and reads `STATUS`, where `BUSY` and `ERROR` read 0 (the idle check). It latches `host_path_err` with a failing copy as in step 11, writes 1 to `STATUS.ERROR`, and repeats the idle check. It then starts a second copy of one word, whose single source read gets `SLVERR`, and issues the `DMA_BUS_ERR_CLEAR` write at the offset. The sweep stops at the first offset where `sep_cpu_ctrl_err_pulse_probe_o` shows the clear pulse and the fault pulse of `host_path_err` in one cycle and no later fault pulse of `host_path_err` before the status read. A sweep that never shows the coincidence fails CHK-RACE. After the coincidence, the master reads `DMA_BUS_ERR_STATUS` and the vector (CHK-RACE). It writes 1 to `STATUS.ERROR`.
. The host requires the expected number of `CHK` lines of each named checker, and no `CHK-<NAME> FAIL` line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-CTRL
|(Control) A legal access latches no bit, so a latch elsewhere is a real fault. The status registers read 0 after reset (`sep_cpu_ctrl.adoc`, reset column) and after the legal reads, vector bits 40 to 42 read 0, and the legal reads answer OKAY. On VCS the status bits hold no X after reset. A wrong DUT latches a bit from a legal access, resets a bit to 1, or leaves X. Anchor: the CPU-LSU read data and response codes, the vector probe. Evidence: `CHK-CTRL PASS legal_reads=3 status=0x0 x_free=1`; `x_free=na` on Verilator.
|CHK-RESP
|The faulting CPU write to an in-extent hole of a bridge answers `SLVERR` (`sep_cpu_ctrl.adoc`: the faulting access also received `SLVERR`; `interrupts.adoc`, source 43). A wrong DUT answers OKAY or DECERR. The `SLVERR` of a hole read and of a CPU access to an unmapped Secure DMA register offset are graded in `sep_irq_ip_to_aggregator_test`; here they print `CTL-RESP LOG`. Anchor: the CPU-LSU response code. Evidence: `CHK-RESP PASS block=hmac op=wr resp=SLVERR`; `CTL-RESP LOG block=dma_reg op=rd resp=SLVERR`.
|CHK-LATCH
|A fault latches its own block bit and no other: `PERIPH_BUS_ERR_STATUS` equals the drawn set (aes bit 0, hmac bit 1, kmac bit 2, otbn bit 3). A wrong DUT latches another block or no bit. Anchor: the status read-back after each access. The reset baseline of CHK-CTRL shows the bit moved from 0 to 1. Evidence: `CHK-LATCH PASS seed=S set=hmac,otbn status=0x0A vec42=1 resp=SLVERR,SLVERR`.
|CHK-OR
|Source 43 equals the OR of the status bits (`interrupts.adoc`, source 43). A wrong DUT holds it low with a bit set, or high with none. Anchor: vector bit 42 against the status read-back. Evidence: `CHK-OR PASS vec42=1 status=0x0A`.
|CHK-CLR-MATRIX
|A clear bit clears only its own block (`sep_cpu_ctrl.adoc`, `PERIPH_BUS_ERR_CLEAR`), a clear of an unlatched bit changes nothing, and source 43 drops with the last bit. A wrong DUT clears another block, misses its own, or drops source 43 while a bit remains. Anchor: the status read-back after each single clear and vector bit 42, for the seven clear bits and for the drain. The clear of an unlatched bit is compared to the latched twin. Evidence: `CHK-CLR-MATRIX PASS cleared=hmac before=0x0A after=0x08 vec42=1`.
|CHK-NONVAC
|(Vacuity guard) Each matrix step and each mask step starts with at least two latched bits, so the off-diagonal cells prove something. Anchor: the status read before the clear. Evidence: `CHK-NONVAC PASS step=1 latched_before=0x0A bits=2`.
|CHK-MASK
|A mask clear gives the previous status AND NOT the mask, and vector bit 42 equals (status != 0). A wrong DUT clears bits outside the mask, ignores a mask bit, or is disturbed by a mask bit of an unlatched block. Anchor: the status read-back and vector bit 42 after each mask step. Evidence: `CHK-MASK PASS step=1 mask=0x7F before=0x0A after=0x0 vec42=0`.
|CHK-AGAIN
|A cleared block latches again on a new fault, and a fault on a block that is still set leaves the other bits unchanged (`sep_cpu_ctrl.adoc`: the status bit holds until its clear). A wrong DUT does not re-latch, or a re-fault disturbs other bits. Anchor: the status read-back after each re-trigger. Evidence: `CHK-AGAIN PASS block=hmac relatched=1 others_kept=0x08`.
|CHK-CLR-READ0
|The clear registers read 0 while status bits are set (`sep_cpu_ctrl.adoc`: "Always reads 0"). A wrong DUT returns the status or a non-zero value. Anchor: the `PERIPH_BUS_ERR_CLEAR` and `DMA_BUS_ERR_CLEAR` read-back with both status registers non-zero. Evidence: `CHK-CLR-READ0 PASS periph_status=0xH periph_clear=0x0 dma_status=0xH dma_clear=0x0`.
|CHK-DMA-CLR
|A write of 0 to `DMA_BUS_ERR_CLEAR.clr` clears no latch, a write of 1 clears both, and clearing one latch does not set the other (`sep_cpu_ctrl.adoc`, `DMA_BUS_ERR_CLEAR`). A wrong DUT clears on a write of 0, misses a latch on a write of 1, or sets the other latch. Anchor: the `DMA_BUS_ERR_STATUS` read-back and vector bits 40 and 41. The register-path write of 0 (the latch stays set) is a reached check. The register-path write of 1 (the latch clears) is graded in `sep_irq_ip_to_aggregator_test`; here it is the control that shows the latch can clear and prints `CTL-DMA-CLR LOG`. The host path stays 0 after the register-path clear; its control is CHK-HOST of the same leaf, where a healthy DUT sets `host_path_err`. The host-path cells use the error inject. With `host_path_err` set alone, a write of 0 keeps it, and a write of 1 clears it while `reg_path_err` and vector bit 40 stay 0. With both latches set, a write of 0 keeps both, and a write of 1 clears both and drops vector bits 40 and 41. Each write of 0 has its control in the write of 1 that follows on the same latch state, which shows that the latch can clear. The 0 of `reg_path_err` in the host-only cell has its control in the unmapped register access of the same leaf, which sets it. A `DMA_BUS_ERR_STATUS` that does not read the stated start state (0b10 or 0b11) before a host-path cell fails the check. Evidence: `CHK-DMA-CLR PASS write0=still_set reg_path_err=1 vec40=1`; `CHK-DMA-CLR PASS cell=reg_clear host_path_err=0 vec41=0`; `CHK-DMA-CLR PASS cell=host_only before=0x2 after_write0=0x2 after_write1=0x0 vec40=0 vec41=0`; `CHK-DMA-CLR PASS cell=both before=0x3 after_write0=0x3 after_write1=0x0 vec40=0 vec41=0`; `CTL-DMA-CLR LOG write1=reg_path_clear reg_path_err=0 vec40=0`.
|CHK-HOST
|A non-OKAY response to a DMA source read sets `ERROR_CODE.BUS_ERROR` and `STATUS.ERROR`, latches `host_path_err` alone and raises source 42 (`interrupts.adoc`, source 42; `sep_cpu_ctrl.adoc`, `DMA_BUS_ERR_STATUS`; `secure_dma.adoc`, `ERROR_CODE`). A wrong DUT does not set `BUS_ERROR` or `ERROR`, sets `reg_path_err`, or does not raise source 42. Anchor: the `ERROR_CODE`, `STATUS` and `DMA_BUS_ERR_STATUS` read-back and vector bits 40 and 41, after the idle check shows `STATUS.ERROR` 0 and `DMA_BUS_ERR_STATUS` 0. The outbound port monitor shows one or more source reads of the copy on `smn_outbound_axi_req_o` that got `SLVERR`; a count of 0 fails the check, so a copy that never reaches the responder cannot pass. Control of `reg_path_err` 0 and vector bit 40 at 0: the unmapped Secure DMA register access of the same leaf sets `reg_path_err` and vector bit 40. Evidence: `CHK-HOST PASS seed=S side=src slverr_reads=N error=1 bus_error=1 bus_err_status=0x02 vec41=1 vec40=0 ctrl_reg_path_err=1`.
|CHK-RACE
|A fault that arrives in the same cycle as the clear of its own latch still latches (`sep_cpu_ctrl.adoc`, `PERIPH_BUS_ERR_CLEAR` and `DMA_BUS_ERR_CLEAR`). A wrong DUT drops the fault: the block bit or `host_path_err` reads 0 after the coincident clear and fault. Anchor: the `PERIPH_BUS_ERR_STATUS` or `DMA_BUS_ERR_STATUS` read-back after the coincidence, and vector bit 42 or bit 41. `sep_cpu_ctrl_err_pulse_probe_o` shows the fault pulse and the clear pulse in one cycle, and a sweep that never shows the coincidence fails the check. Each trial starts with the latch set, and one faulting access (a hole read, or a one-word copy with one source read) gives one fault pulse. The probe shows no later fault pulse of that latch before the status read, so a later fault cannot set a dropped latch again. Controls: a clear with no fault drops the latch, for a peripheral bit in CHK-CLR-MATRIX and for `host_path_err` in the host-path cells of CHK-DMA-CLR. The DMA part uses the error inject on `smn_outbound_axi_resp_i`. Evidence: `CHK-RACE PASS seed=S kind=periph block=hmac coincident=1 later_faults=0 status_after=0x02 vec42=1` and `CHK-RACE PASS kind=dma coincident=1 later_faults=0 status_after=0x02 vec41=1`.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope limit*: Not graded: whether an external access to the same holes also latches a bit (see <<sep-vplan-phase3-blocked,Blocked features>>), the command-integrity cause, a halt of the DMA after the error, and whether one clear (`DMA_BUS_ERR_CLEAR` or the DMA error clear) affects the other report. The misaligned cause, the aes, csrng, edn and wdt bits, and the DMA response at a reserved window or past the mailbox wrapper extent are in <<sep-vplan-phase3-blocked,Blocked features>>. The single-block latch and the DMA register-path latch are owned by `sep_irq_ip_to_aggregator_test` and `sep_periph_bus_err_misaligned_test`, and the destination-side DMA fault by `sep_dma_basic_test`.

'''''
[[sep_cpu_ctrl_timeout_inert_rand_test]]
===== 3.23 `sep_cpu_ctrl_timeout_inert_rand_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: Mailbox, IRQ, PIC

*Run mode*: `no_cpu` (`lsu_stub_all_live`), `+skip_fuse_sense`, `reseed = 3`

*Source Module*: `sep_cpu_ctrl_timeout_inert_rand_test`

*BFM / Model*: CPU-LSU master on `s_axi` (`SepAxiAgent` over `ocah_axi_vip`) and external SMN master on `m_axi` (second `SepAxiAgent`), each with `RREADY` and `BREADY` under test control; the response monitor of each stalled port (`VALID`, `READY` and response handshake count); `sep_internal_interrupts_probe_o`; register model from the generated IP-XACT (`sep_reg_meta`). Error inject: the response hold of the outbound responder on the `sep` input `smn_outbound_axi_resp_i` (without the inject `tb/sep_outbound_mbx.sv` answers OKAY at once), which the test adds to the inject exceptions of `SEP_TB_ARCH.adoc`; the outbound filter, alias remap and DMA legs use it. The outbound port monitor counts the requests on `smn_outbound_axi_req_o` and the response handshakes on `smn_outbound_axi_resp_i`. Secure DMA with an SRAM endpoint for the DMA leg. The entropy write and entropy read legs stall the CPU-LSU master at the entropy pool (`sep_entropy_fifo`), so the response monitor of the CPU-LSU port is their anchor. No added tap.

*Randomization*: RAND-REP. `SepSeededRng` from the run seed: the order of the nine arming writes (`TIMEOUT_ENABLE` and the eight `TIMEOUT_COUNT_*` registers) and the order of the stalled blocks. `reseed = 3` samples three pairs of orders. The hold length, the stalled addresses and the write data are fixed. The `SEP_CPU_CTRL` writes go to `TIMEOUT_ENABLE` and the eight count registers only.

*Objective*: The timeout block is reserved and not implemented. `TIMEOUT_INTERRUPT` (R, reset 0) reads 0. `TIMEOUT_ENABLE` and each of the eight `TIMEOUT_COUNT_*` registers have one RW bit 0 with reset 0 and hold a written 1. A stall of a block path beyond its armed count sets no `TIMEOUT_INTERRUPT` bit, raises no PIC source and aborts no access. Sources: `hw/sys/sep/regs/gen/adoc/blocks/sep_cpu_ctrl.adoc` (`TIMEOUT_INTERRUPT`, `TIMEOUT_ENABLE`, `TIMEOUT_COUNT_*`, `TIMEOUT_CLEAR`, `TIMEOUT_MODE`); `hw/sys/sep/doc/fabric.adoc` (System Interface initiator, Fabric Topology); `hw/sys/sep/doc/cpu.adoc` (Dual Scratch Register Banks) and `hw/sys/sep/regs/gen/adoc/blocks/sep_scratch.adoc` (`SCRATCH`); `hw/ip/axi_lite_mailbox_unit/regs/gen/adoc/axil_mailbox.adoc` (`WIRQT`).

*Test Coverage*: Extends `sep_address_map_test` (open, same run mode and tool), which reads `TIMEOUT_INTERRUPT` and six of the counts at reset and writes and reads back `TIMEOUT_COUNT_DMA`, `TIMEOUT_COUNT_SYS_IN` and `TIMEOUT_ENABLE`, and `sep_reg_bit_bash_rand_test` (open), which grades the reset value of the timeout registers and proves nothing on a count whose register has no software-usable field. `sep_cpu_ctrl_reg_shape_test` (Phase 3, 5.21 of this plan, not an open test) grades the write of `TIMEOUT_CLEAR` and `TIMEOUT_MODE`. This test grades only the new cells: the write of 1 and the read-back of the six counts that `sep_address_map_test` does not write and read back (`TIMEOUT_COUNT_MAILBOX_INBOUND`, `TIMEOUT_COUNT_MAILBOX_OUTBOUND`, `TIMEOUT_COUNT_ENTROPY_WRITE`, `TIMEOUT_COUNT_ENTROPY_READ`, `TIMEOUT_COUNT_FILTER_OUT` and `TIMEOUT_COUNT_ALIAS_REMAP`) and the inertness under a real stall of each block path. The reset reads, and the write and read-back of `TIMEOUT_COUNT_DMA`, `TIMEOUT_COUNT_SYS_IN` and `TIMEOUT_ENABLE`, run as controls (`CTL-ARMED`). Cells: the 12 register and direction cells of the six counts (read and write); a read stall and a write stall for the system input, the inbound mailbox and the outbound mailbox; a read stall and a write stall for the outbound filter and the alias remap, and a source-read stall for the DMA, each held in the outbound responder; the entropy write and entropy read stalls. Functional coverage: `sep_cpu_ctrl_timeout_inert_cg` (`x_reg_dir`, `cp_stall_block`, `cp_stall_inert`).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Reset the DUT with `+skip_fuse_sense`. Print `SEED seed=<S>` and a `DRAW` line for the arming order and the block order. Write no `SYS_DIS` bit, so the inbound filter stays in its default-block state.
. Through the CPU-LSU master, program one inbound filter entry (`FILTER_CONFIG`, `START_ADDR`, `END_ADDR`) that admits the inbound aperture of mailbox 0, one that admits `SCRATCH[0]` of the cold scratch bank (`sep_scratch_cold`), and one that admits the `SEP_CPU_CTRL` register `TIMEOUT_INTERRUPT`. Read the entries back.
. Through the CPU-LSU master, read `TIMEOUT_INTERRUPT`, the eight counts, `TIMEOUT_ENABLE` and `SCRATCH[0]` of the cold scratch bank. Each reads 0x0 (control, `CTL-ARMED`). Do not access `TIMEOUT_CLEAR` or `TIMEOUT_MODE`.
. After a bounded quiet wait, sample `sep_internal_interrupts_probe_o` with the six excluded idle bits masked. This sample is the vector baseline. Log the six masked bits (`OBS-IDLE-UNSTATED`).
. In the drawn order, write 1 to `TIMEOUT_ENABLE` and to each of the eight count registers. Read the nine registers back in the same order. Each reads 0x1 (CHK-ARMED for the six counts, `CTL-ARMED` for the other three).
. Stall leg, in the drawn block order. For the system input, the inbound mailbox and the outbound mailbox, start a read with its `RREADY` low. The system input read targets `SCRATCH[0]` of the cold scratch bank through the SMN master. This register is in a different register block than `TIMEOUT_INTERRUPT`, so the crossbar decodes the two to different targets (`fabric.adoc`, Fabric Topology). The inbound mailbox read targets `WIRQT` of the inbound port of mailbox 0 through the SMN master. The outbound mailbox read targets `WIRQT` of the outbound port of mailbox 0 through the CPU-LSU master. Each target has no read side effect.
. Wait for the response of the stalled read to show `VALID` high with `READY` low (a bounded wait; a timeout fails CHK-STALL-REAL). Hold `READY` low for the hold length. The response handshake count of the stalled access stays 0 during the hold.
. During the hold, read `TIMEOUT_INTERRUPT` with the master that does not hold the stall (the CPU-LSU master when the SMN master holds, otherwise the SMN master) and wait for its response (a bounded wait). When the read completes, it is the during-hold sample. When it does not complete in the bounded wait, print `OBS-TO-INERT LOG block=<block> dir=<dir> sample=during_hold status=not_sampled`. The spec does not state that a read completes while another response is held, so this outcome does not fail CHK-TO-INERT. Sample the masked vector at the end of the hold.
. Raise `READY`. The response handshake count of the stalled access becomes 1 (CHK-STALL-REAL). After a bounded quiet wait, read `TIMEOUT_INTERRUPT` and sample the masked vector. Compare both and the response of the stalled access (CHK-TO-INERT).
. Repeat steps 6 to 9 with a write that holds `BREADY` low. The write targets the same register as the read of the block, and its data is the value that the register already holds (0x0 for `SCRATCH[0]` and `WIRQT`).
. Outbound filter, alias remap and DMA legs. Through the CPU-LSU master, program an outbound filter entry pair (one entry with `allow_ns` 0 and one with `allow_ns` 1, read and write allowed, `src_id` 0) over a fixed word of the SMU aperture at its reset values (`0x8000_0000` to `0xBFFF_FFFF`), above `0x8000_1000` and away from the console and verdict words of the responder. Program one valid alias remap region over a fixed local page, with an offset (bit 32 set) that translates the page to a fixed outbound word, and a second outbound entry pair over that translated word (`fabric.adoc`, Fabric Topology and Address Remapping). Each leg issues one access that reaches `smn_outbound_axi_req_o`, and the error inject holds the response of the outbound responder for the hold length. The outbound filter leg is a CPU-LSU read and a CPU-LSU write to the SMU aperture word, which no alias region hits. The alias remap leg is a CPU-LSU read and a CPU-LSU write to the remapped local page. The write data is 0x0. The DMA leg is a Secure DMA copy of one word from the SMU aperture word into SRAM, with the DMA enabled memory range set wide enough that no address check stops the copy, and with `INTR_ENABLE` of the Secure DMA at its reset value 0, so sources 9 to 11 stay low. Each leg runs steps 7 to 9 with the hold in the responder in place of the master `READY` hold, and the SMN master is the master that does not hold the stall. In the DMA leg the CPU-LSU master also reads the Secure DMA `STATUS` during the hold and, after release, in a bounded wait for `STATUS.DONE`.
. Entropy read leg and entropy write leg. The CPU-LSU master issues a single-beat 64-bit (AxSIZE 3) access to the entropy pool `STATUS` register (offset 0x0 of `sep_entropy_fifo`, `entropy_pool.adoc`; `sep_entropy_pool.adoc`), a read with `RREADY` low and a write with `BREADY` low. A `STATUS` read is non-destructive, and a write to the read-only pool changes no state and terminates with `BRESP=SLVERR` (`entropy_pool.adoc`, "Access Policy"). The write data is 0x0. Each leg runs steps 7 to 9 with the SMN master as the master that does not hold the stall. The anchor of CHK-STALL-REAL is the CPU-LSU R and B channel. The read data is logged (`OBS-ENTROPY-STATUS LOG fifo_level=<n>`) and is not graded, because the pool fills autonomously.
. Vector control. Through the SMN master, write `IRQEN` as `0x1` on the inbound port of mailbox 0 (`WIRQT` stays 0) and push one word through the inbound `WRITE_DATA`. Vector bit 0 (PIC source 1), which reads 0 in the baseline of step 4, reads 1 within a bounded wait. Pop the word through the outbound `READ_DATA` with the CPU-LSU master and write `IRQS` as `0x1` and `IRQEN` as 0 on the inbound port. Vector bit 0 reads 0 again (`CTL-VEC-LIVE`). A missing rise or fall prints `CTL-VEC-LIVE FAIL` and fails the leaf.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-ARMED
|After the writes, each of the six counts `TIMEOUT_COUNT_MAILBOX_INBOUND`, `TIMEOUT_COUNT_MAILBOX_OUTBOUND`, `TIMEOUT_COUNT_ENTROPY_WRITE`, `TIMEOUT_COUNT_ENTROPY_READ`, `TIMEOUT_COUNT_FILTER_OUT` and `TIMEOUT_COUNT_ALIAS_REMAP` reads 0x1 (`sep_cpu_ctrl.adoc`: RW, bit 0). A register that drops the write reads 0x0 and fails. Before the writes the ten readable registers read 0x0 (RDL reset), and `TIMEOUT_ENABLE`, `TIMEOUT_COUNT_DMA` and `TIMEOUT_COUNT_SYS_IN` read 0x1 after the writes. These cells are graded by `sep_address_map_test` and `sep_reg_bit_bash_rand_test` and print `CTL-ARMED LOG`. Anchor: the real read-back through the CPU-LSU master. This check is the control of CHK-TO-INERT: an unarmed register cannot show inertness. Evidence: `CHK-ARMED PASS regs=6 base=0x0 read=0x1`; `CTL-ARMED LOG reset_regs=10 base=0x0 armed_regs=3 armed=0x1`.
|CHK-STALL-REAL
|(Control of CHK-TO-INERT.) For each stall leg, the stalled access gets no response during the whole hold and one response after release. For a leg that holds the master `READY`, the response of the stalled access shows `VALID` high with `READY` low for the whole hold, and the response handshake count is 0 during the hold and 1 after release. For the outbound filter, alias remap and DMA legs, which the responder holds, the access shows one request handshake on `smn_outbound_axi_req_o` before the hold, so it reached the port; the stalled master gets no response handshake during the hold and one after release (`LSU` R or B channel; for the DMA leg `STATUS.BUSY` reads 1 during the hold and `STATUS.DONE` reads 1 after release). A stall that does not stall, a request that does not reach the outbound port, or an access that never completes after release, fails. Anchor: the response monitor on the stalled port: `XM` R and B channel for the system input and the inbound mailbox, `LSU` R and B channel for the outbound mailbox, for the outbound filter and alias remap legs and for the entropy read and entropy write legs at the entropy pool `STATUS` register; the outbound port monitor and the Secure DMA `STATUS` read-back for the DMA leg. Evidence: `CHK-STALL-REAL PASS block=mailbox_inbound dir=read port=xm valid_during_hold=1 responses_during_hold=0 responses_after_release=1`; `CHK-STALL-REAL PASS block=alias_remap dir=read port=lsu req_at_port=1 responses_during_hold=0 responses_after_release=1`; `CHK-STALL-REAL PASS block=dma dir=read req_at_port=1 busy_during_hold=1 done_after_release=1`. One line per reached block and direction.
|CHK-TO-INERT
|After each reached stall, during the hold and after release, `TIMEOUT_INTERRUPT` reads 0x0 (`sep_cpu_ctrl.adoc`: R, reset 0), where the during-hold read completes; a during-hold read that does not complete is logged as an OBS line (step 8) and is not a sample. The masked vector equals the baseline of step 4, so no PIC source rises. The stalled access completes with its stated response: OKAY with read data 0x0 for the system input and mailbox legs, OKAY for the entropy read leg, SLVERR for the entropy write leg (`entropy_pool.adoc`: a write terminates with `BRESP=SLVERR`), the OKAY and the read data 0x0 that the responder returns for the outbound filter and alias remap legs, and `STATUS.DONE` 1 with `STATUS.ERROR` 0 for the DMA copy (`secure_dma.adoc`, `STATUS`). A DUT that implements a timeout would show a set `TIMEOUT_INTERRUPT` bit, a raised vector bit or an aborted access. This is a "never" check. Its controls are CHK-ARMED and CHK-STALL-REAL of the same block in the same leaf, and `CTL-VEC-LIVE` (step 13), where a mailbox push raises vector bit 0 and its release drops it, so a dead vector probe fails the leaf. Anchor: the `TIMEOUT_INTERRUPT` read-back and `sep_internal_interrupts_probe_o`. Evidence: `CHK-TO-INERT PASS block=<block> dir=<read\|write> timeout_int=0x0 vec=baseline resp=<OKAY\|SLVERR\|done>`. One line per reached block and direction; `CTL-VEC-LIVE PASS bit0_base=0 bit0_after_push=1 bit0_after_release=0` once per leaf.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0. The control `CTL-VEC-LIVE` must show the rise and the fall of vector bit 0, else the leaf fails.

*Scope limit*: This test claims no timeout behavior, because the registers are reserved. A write to `TIMEOUT_INTERRUPT` is not driven, because the response is not stated for this register. `TIMEOUT_CLEAR` and `TIMEOUT_MODE` are not accessed (`sep_cpu_ctrl_reg_shape_test`, Phase 3, owns them). The reset value and the plain read-write of `TIMEOUT_INTERRUPT`, `TIMEOUT_ENABLE`, `TIMEOUT_COUNT_DMA` and `TIMEOUT_COUNT_SYS_IN` stay with `sep_address_map_test` and `sep_reg_bit_bash_rand_test`. The `TIMEOUT_INTERRUPT` level is sampled during the hold and after release, and not on every clock. The DMA leg holds the source read only.

'''''

[[sep_nmi_vector_bark_rand_test]]
===== 3.24 `sep_nmi_vector_bark_rand_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: Mailbox, IRQ, PIC

*Run mode*: `cpu`, `+skip_fuse_sense`, `reseed = 3`. One leaf runs two boots of the same image with a cold reset (`rst_ni`) between them, because the lock holds until a cold reset: the locked-copy boot and the free-address boot.

*Source Module*: `sep_nmi_vector_bark_rand_test`

*BFM / Model*: CPU firmware (an image with a stub at 0xC000_0100, four trampoline copies in ICCM and one common NMI handler); ICCM backdoor load for the free handler `Hk`; firmware console and firmware CSR reads; CPU trace `cpu_trace_addr_i` as the retired PC; `wdt_timer_rst_req_o` (DUT port, logged only); register model from the generated IP-XACT (`sep_reg_meta`). No PROPOSED item. Every check is a reached check.

*Randomization*: RANDCFG. `SepSeededRng` from the run seed, passed to the firmware in its parameter block: the trampoline copy (one of four 256-byte-aligned copies in ICCM); the free handler address `A` (halfword-aligned, 0xC000_1000 up to 0xC004_0000 minus the size `H` of `Hk`, outside the image and the four copies, so that `A` plus `H` is at or below the ICCM end 0xC004_0000; `H` is a test parameter and `Hk` stays inside ICCM; `cpu.adoc`, closely coupled memories); the bark threshold of each bark (1 to `N_BARK`; `N_BARK` is a test parameter that the leaf logs, far below the bite threshold 0xFFFF_FFFF, and every bounded wait for a bark is longer than `N_BARK` `clk_wdt_i` periods); the second concurrent-state case ((b) to (d); case (a) always runs first); the pending source (one of the OpenTitan event sources 18, 20, 21, 23, 24, 28 and 30); the raw priority; `priord`. `reseed = 3` samples three draws of each. Every seed runs the reset vector, one trampoline copy, the address `A`, case (a) and one of the cases (b) to (d). The trampoline copy and the case (b) to (d) are seed-dependent cells: one regression does not fill the four copies or the three cases, and they close on a merge of regressions (`SEP_FCOV.adoc`, "Seed-dependent groups"). The lock is set once per boot. A second NMI, an NMI during an external handler and a takeable PIC source at the bark are not drawn.

*Objective*: `SEP_NMI_VEC` holds address bits [31:1]. The NMI is not suppressed by `mstatus.MIE` or any PIC register, and the bark moves no pending bit. A bark with the vector at its reset value jumps to 0xC000_0100. With the vector programmed, then locked, then the bark enabled, a bark jumps to the programmed address and the code at the reset vector does not run. Sources: `hw/sys/sep/regs/gen/adoc/blocks/sep_cpu_ctrl.adoc` (`SEP_NMI_VEC`, `SEP_NMI_VEC_LOCK`); `hw/sys/sep/doc/interrupts.adoc` ("NMI — Watchdog Timer Bark", "Sources and Routing"); `hw/sys/sep/doc/watchdog.adoc` ("Bark Interrupt and Bite Reset"); `hw/sys/sep/regs/gen/adoc/blocks/el2_pic.adoc` (`mpiccfg`, `meipl`, `meie`, `meip`).

*Test Coverage*: Extends `sep_nmi_sanity_test` (same run mode and tool), which grades the reset vector default, the vector write-back, the sticky lock, the order vector then lock then bark enable, and the handler entered at the programmed trampoline. The reserved bit 0 of `SEP_NMI_VEC` after a write is graded by `sep_reg_bit_bash_rand_test` (open). The upper word and the write of 0 or all-ones to the RW1S lock are graded by `sep_cpu_ctrl_reg_shape_test` (Phase 3, 5.21 of this plan, not an open test). This test grades only the new cells: the bark with the vector at its reset value, the jump to a free address `A` with its retired PC, the concurrent PIC states and the PIC state unchanged by the bark. The open owners keep the rest. Cells: a bark with the vector at reset (graded by CHK-BARK-VEC; it is also the control that shows that the detection sees the reset-vector path); one locked-copy boot with a drawn trampoline copy and two barks with the vector locked: case (a) `mstatus.MIE` 0 with a pending enabled source, then one drawn case of (b) `mstatus.MIE` 1 with a pending source and `meie` 0, (c) `mstatus.MIE` 1 with a pending source at the never priority, (d) `mstatus.MIE` 1 with nothing pending; the pending source delivers after the gate opens; and, after a cold reset, a bark with `A` programmed and locked. Functional coverage: `sep_nmi_vector_cfg_cg` (`cp_vec_class`, `cp_order_at_enable`, `cp_nmi_target`), `sep_nmi_concurrency_cg` (`x_case_taken`, `cp_vec_unchanged`, `cp_pic_live_after`) and `sep_pic_no_delivery_cg` (`cp_bark_vec_same`).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Before the first boot, the host loads the free handler `Hk` (size `H`) at `A` in ICCM by backdoor. `A` plus `H` is at or below 0xC004_0000. `Hk` writes the marker `Mk` to the firmware console, writes the end-of-firmware word that the host gates on, and loops. The image holds the stub at 0xC000_0100 in a fixed linker section, the four trampoline copies and the common NMI handler. Each copy records its own address and jumps to the common handler.
. Boot with `+skip_fuse_sense`. The firmware prints `SEED seed=<S>` and a `DRAW` line for each drawn value. It reads `SEP_NMI_VEC` and `SEP_NMI_VEC_LOCK` and prints them. They hold the RDL reset values 0xC000_0100 as an address and 0.
. Reset-vector corner (error injection: bark with the vector unprogrammed). Write `WDOG_BITE_THOLD` 0xFFFF_FFFF, `WDOG_COUNT` 0 and `WDOG_BARK_THOLD` a drawn value in 1 to `N_BARK`. Write `WDOG_CTRL.enable` 1. Wait in the loop at known addresses (a bounded wait longer than `N_BARK` `clk_wdt_i` periods; a timeout fails CHK-BARK-VEC). Expected response: the CPU jumps to 0xC000_0100 and runs the stub there (`sep_cpu_ctrl.adoc`, `SEP_NMI_VEC`).
. The CPU jumps to the stub. The stub prints the marker `M0`, writes 1 to `INTR_STATE.wdog_timer_bark`, writes 0 to `WDOG_CTRL.enable` and `WDOG_COUNT`, and returns with `mret`. The host records the first retired PC after the loop (CHK-BARK-VEC control).
. Choose the drawn trampoline copy. Write its address to `SEP_NMI_VEC`. Write 1 to `SEP_NMI_VEC_LOCK`. Read both back.
. Write the drawn `priord` to `mpiccfg` while no source is enabled or pending. The never priority is 0 when `priord` is 0 and 15 when it is 1.
. Case (a). Clear `mstatus.MIE` and set `mie.MEIE`. For the drawn source `s`, write a usable priority to `meipl[s]` and 1 to its `meie` bit, set its `INTR_ENABLE` bit and its `INTR_TEST` bit. Install an external handler for `s` that counts its run, writes 0 to `INTR_TEST` and writes 1 to its `INTR_STATE` bit. Read `meip[0]` (non-zero) and keep the value as `meip0_before`. No handler runs.
. Bark 1. Write `WDOG_BITE_THOLD` 0xFFFF_FFFF, `WDOG_COUNT` 0, a drawn `WDOG_BARK_THOLD` in 1 to `N_BARK`, then `WDOG_CTRL.enable` 1. Wait in the loop (a bounded wait longer than `N_BARK` `clk_wdt_i` periods; a timeout fails CHK-NMI-TAKEN).
. The NMI handler runs. It prints its entry address and its run count, reads `meip[0]` and compares it to `meip0_before` with the six excluded idle bits masked (CHK-NMI-NOPIC, bits 13 and 15 logged). It writes 1 to `INTR_STATE.wdog_timer_bark`, writes 0 to `WDOG_CTRL.enable` and `WDOG_COUNT`, and returns with `mret`. The host records the first retired PC after the loop (CHK-NMI-TAKEN).
. Open the gate: set `mstatus.MIE`. The external handler of `s` runs once (a bounded wait). A timeout or a second run fails CHK-NMI-NOPIC (`case=a`). Read `meip[0]` until the bit of `s` is clear (a bounded wait).
. Second bark, drawn case, with `mstatus.MIE` 1. Case (b): write 0 to the `meie` bit of `s` and read it back (0), then write 1 to the `INTR_TEST` bit of `s`, with the usable priority of step 7 in place, so that the source is pending and not enabled when it is set. Case (c): in this order, write 1 to its `meie` bit, write the never priority to `meipl[s]`, read it back, then write 1 to its `INTR_TEST` bit. Case (d): leave every source idle. Read `meip[0]` and keep it as `meip0_before`. No handler runs.
. Bark 2. Repeat step 8 with a new drawn bark threshold, then step 9 for the handler. The handler compares `meip[0]` to the value of step 11.
. Open the gate of the drawn case: case (b) writes 1 to the `meie` bit of `s`; case (c) writes a usable priority to `meipl[s]`. The external handler of `s` runs once (a bounded wait). Case (d) has nothing to run; the firmware prints `delivery=none`.
. The firmware prints an end-of-boot marker. The host sets the leg word in the parameter block by backdoor and applies a cold reset. The same image boots again and runs the free-address corner.
. Free-address corner. The firmware reads `SEP_NMI_VEC` and `SEP_NMI_VEC_LOCK` and prints them. They hold the RDL reset values. Write `A` to `SEP_NMI_VEC`. The field `nmi_vec` holds `A >> 1`. Write 1 to `SEP_NMI_VEC_LOCK` and read it (it reads 1).
. Write `WDOG_BITE_THOLD` 0xFFFF_FFFF, `WDOG_COUNT` 0, a drawn `WDOG_BARK_THOLD` in 1 to `N_BARK` and `WDOG_CTRL.enable` 1, as in step 8. Wait in the loop (a bounded wait longer than `N_BARK` `clk_wdt_i` periods; a timeout fails CHK-BARK-VEC).
. The CPU jumps to `Hk`. `Hk` prints `Mk`, writes the end-of-firmware word and loops. The host records the first retired PC after the loop and the console markers (CHK-BARK-VEC). The host then evaluates every checker.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-NMI-TAKEN
|Each of the two barks of steps 8 and 12 enters the common handler through the drawn trampoline copy, once. The handler entry address equals the programmed vector, and the handler run count is 1 per bark (`interrupts.adoc`, "NMI — Watchdog Timer Bark"). Bark 1 runs with `mstatus.MIE` 0 and bark 2 with `mstatus.MIE` 1, so a mask by `mstatus.MIE` fails bark 1 by timeout. A DUT that masks the NMI, enters another address or enters twice fails. `wdt_timer_rst_req_o` is sampled at each handler entry and logged as `OBS-BITE-REQ LOG bark=<n> wdt_timer_rst_req_o=<v>`; it is not part of the PASS condition, because the bite threshold stays above the count and the request cannot rise in this leaf. The open owner `sep_reset_wdt_sanity_test` grades the rise of the bite request. Anchor: the entry address and count that the firmware prints (`nmi_int` is not a port) and the first retired PC after the loop on `cpu_trace_addr_i`. Evidence: `CHK-NMI-TAKEN PASS seed=S copy=<k> bark=1 mie=0 vec=0xH handler_runs=1` and `CHK-NMI-TAKEN PASS seed=S copy=<k> bark=2 mie=1 vec=0xH handler_runs=1`.
|CHK-NMI-NOPIC
|The bark moves no pending bit: `meip[0]` read in the handler equals `meip[0]` read before the bark, with the six excluded idle bits (`meip` bits 13, 15, 16, 37, 38 and 39) masked, and bits 13 and 15 are logged (`interrupts.adoc`, "Sources and Routing", the bark goes to the NMI pin and not to the PIC). A bark that clears or sets a pending bit changes the word and fails. Controls: in case (a) `meip[0]` is non-zero before the bark, so a clear shows, and the pending source runs once after the gate opens in step 10; in cases (b) and (c) the pending source runs once after the gate opens in step 13, so a pending state that did not survive the bark shows as no delivery. Case (d) is a compare of two idle words. Anchor: firmware reads of `meip` and the firmware count of the external handler runs. Evidence: `CHK-NMI-NOPIC PASS case=a meip0_before=0xH meip0_after=0xH bit13=V bit15=V delivery=1` and the same line for the drawn second case (`case=b`, `case=c` or `case=d`) with its delivery count.
|CHK-BARK-VEC
|The bark jumps to the vector that holds: the reset vector while it is unprogrammed, and the programmed address `A` after the vector is written and locked (`sep_cpu_ctrl.adoc`, `SEP_NMI_VEC`). Control leg (step 4): with the vector at its reset value, the first retired PC after the loop is 0xC000_0100 and the marker `M0` appears, so the detection can see the reset-vector path. Programmed leg (steps 15 to 17): before the bark, `SEP_NMI_VEC` and `SEP_NMI_VEC_LOCK` read their RDL reset values after the cold reset, then `A` and 1 after the writes; the first retired PC after the loop equals `A`, the marker `Mk` appears and `M0` does not. A DUT that ignores the programmed vector shows 0xC000_0100 and `M0`. A DUT that keeps the lock across the cold reset shows the vector at its reset value before the write, which fails the precondition and not the jump. Anchor: the retired PC on `cpu_trace_addr_i` and the firmware console markers, both read by the host. Evidence: `CHK-BARK-VEC PASS leg=reset_vector retired_pc=0xC0000100 marker=M0` and `CHK-BARK-VEC PASS leg=programmed programmed=0xH retired_pc=0xH marker=Mk reset_marker_seen=0 control_pc=0xC0000100`.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope limit*: The reset vector default, the vector write-back, the sticky lock, the order vector then lock then bark enable and the handler at the programmed trampoline stay with `sep_nmi_sanity_test`. The reserved bit 0 stays with `sep_reg_bit_bash_rand_test`, and the write shape of the RW1S lock stays with `sep_cpu_ctrl_reg_shape_test` (Phase 3). The bite and its reset request stay with `sep_reset_wdt_sanity_test`. This test does not claim the order of the NMI against a takeable PIC interrupt, a second NMI, an NMI during an external handler, the DCCM fast-interrupt NMI source, or the response to an uncorrectable ICCM error at the reset vector. The bite threshold stays above the count, so no bite fires. The vector written without the lock is not driven. An uncorrectable ICCM error at 0xC000_0100 is not driven, because the spec states two different responses for it.

'''''

[[sep-vplan-area-4]]
==== 4. SPI and DMA

[[sep_dma_hash_test]]
===== 4.1 `sep_dma_hash_test`

*Phase*: 1

*Area*: SPI and DMA

*Run mode*: `cpu`, `+skip_fuse_sense`

*Source Module*: `sep_dma_hash_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip, CPU FW, `tb/sep_outbound_mbx.sv` (console + verdict mailbox; OKAY / zero read data for any address)

*Objective*: Drives the secure DMA engine from real firmware to copy a block from SRAM into the CPU's data tightly-coupled memory with the inline hash engine enabled, then proves two things independently: the copied data is identical to the source, and the hardware digest is correct. Completion is delivered as an interrupt to a registered service routine, so the interrupt path is proven as well as the datapath. The digest comparison is the strong part: copy correctness alone would not show the inline hash engine consumed the same bytes that were copied. Two digest lengths are walked. SHA-256 runs over build-varying data (the firmware never seeds `rand()`, so the byte vector is fixed within one build and changes when the firmware is rebuilt) against a software SHA-256 computed in firmware over the same bytes. SHA-384 has no 64-bit SHA-2 core in this firmware, so it runs over a fixed message against the published FIPS 180-4 digest for that message; `OpcSha384` is a supported DMA opcode alongside `OpcSha256`.

*Test Coverage*: Firmware DMA SRAM to DCCM with inline SHA-256 and SHA-384, digest compare, copy, and IRQ.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Initialise the fabric filter; register the DMA done and error service routines.
. Program the enabled memory range and confirm the configuration lock is open.
. Fill the SRAM source region with random data.
. Program source, destination, size, transfer width and increment modes.
. Start the transfer with the SHA-256 opcode and digest-swap set.
. Wait on interrupt; the service routine clears status.
. Read the hardware digest; compute the software digest; compare. Compare source against destination word for word.
. Then stage the fixed FIPS 180-4 56-byte test message in the same SRAM region, reprogram only the length and the opcode, and start a second transfer with the SHA-384 opcode.
. Wait on the interrupt again; read the twelve digest words; render them as hex and compare against the published vector. Compare the copied message against the source bytes.
. Disable the DMA interrupt enables, then carry the same 56-byte message as two 28-byte chunks, pacing the chunks on `STATUS.chunk_done` and counting them. Compare the digest against the published SHA-256 vector for the whole message.
. Finally run the same single-chunk SHA-256 twice, once with `DIGEST_SWAP` set and once clear, and compare the two digest word arrays against each other.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-CFG
|The DMA configuration lock is open before programming. A wrong value is counted as an error: the firmware emits `ERROR: CFG_REGWEN not unlocked`, increments its error count, and that count gates the mailbox PASS magic.
|CHK-COMPLETE
|The transfer completes and the interrupt reaches the service routine.
|CHK-DIGEST
|The hardware digest equals an independent software SHA-256 over the same data. The eight hardware digest words are read through the array-indexed accessor `SHA2_DIGEST_0_BASE_ADDR(i)`, so a wrong array stride or a wrong register symbol shifts the assembled digest and the `memcmp` below fails.
|CHK-COPY
|Destination matches source word for word.
|CHK-NONVAC
|For the SHA-256 pass: the software digest is recomputed from the actual SRAM contents on every run and no SHA-256 digest literal exists anywhere in the firmware or the testbench, so the comparison cannot be satisfied by a constant. `rand()` is never seeded, so the byte vector is the same for every seed within one firmware build -- the seed randomises only the clock period -- but it is not stable across builds.
|CHK-SHA384
|The twelve hardware digest words, rendered big-endian as hex, equal the FIPS 180-4 digest for the 56-byte message the firmware staged. Unlike the SHA-256 pass this compares against a literal, so its non-vacuity argument is different and is stated rather than inherited: the message is the published input and the vector is the published output, neither is read back from the engine, and a DUT that returned a constant, a zero digest, or the SHA-256 of the same message fails. The 56-byte message is used in place of the one-block "abc" vector because the DMA transfers whole 4-byte words. `OPCODE_ERROR` on this transfer is reported as a failure, not skipped, so a build that does not implement `OpcSha384` fails here rather than passing quietly.
|CHK-SHA384-COPY
|The same SHA-384 transfer also copied the message to the destination, checked byte for byte. A digest engine fed correctly while the copy path is broken fails here.
|CHK-MULTICHUNK
|The same 56-byte message carried as two 28-byte chunks produces the published FIPS 180-4 SHA-256 digest for the whole message. A hash that restarted per chunk, or that dropped the tail, produces a different digest and fails. The observed chunk count is required to be at least two before the digest is compared, so a transfer that silently completed in one chunk fails rather than passing a single-chunk digest under a multi-chunk name. A chunk counts only when its pacing poll ends on `STATUS.chunk_done` or `STATUS.done`; a poll that runs out of budget fails the pass and is never counted. Interrupts are disabled for this pass because the service routine clears `STATUS.chunk_done`, which the pacing loop has to read.
|CHK-DIGEST-SWAP
|Every digest word produced with `DIGEST_SWAP` clear is the byte-reverse of the corresponding word produced with it set, over the same message. Every other pass in this entry sets the bit, so none of them can tell a working `DIGEST_SWAP` from a DMA that ignores it; this is the only entry that grades the bit. All-words-identical is failed explicitly, since a palindromic digest is the one way a byte-reverse comparison could be satisfied while the bit does nothing.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Evidence*: CHK-NONVAC is a property of the sources rather than a run record -- no SHA-256 digest literal exists in the firmware or the testbench, so the comparison cannot be satisfied by a constant. Every other row is logged by the test: CHK-DIGEST compares the two digests the console carries, and CHK-CFG, CHK-COMPLETE, CHK-COPY, CHK-SHA384-COPY, CHK-SHA384, CHK-MULTICHUNK and CHK-DIGEST-SWAP each gate on the firmware line that scores them.

'''''

[[sep_spi_ot_dma_rx_test]]
===== 4.2 `sep_spi_ot_dma_rx_test`

*Phase*: 1

*Area*: SPI and DMA

*Run mode*: `cpu`, `+skip_fuse_sense`

*Source Module*: `sep_spi_ot_dma_rx_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip, ocah_spi_vip, CPU FW, `tb/sep_outbound_mbx.sv` (console + verdict mailbox; OKAY / zero read data for any address)

*Objective*: Proves the hardware handshake between the SPI host and the secure DMA engine.

*Test Coverage*: SPI-FIFO to DMA to SRAM handshake with a known RX pattern.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Initialise the fabric filter; preload the flash model with a known byte pattern.
. Configure the SPI host: receive watermark, clock divider, enable, watermark event.
. Issue a flash read command and address, then request the payload.
. Program the DMA: source is the receive register in wrapping mode, destination is SRAM incrementing, hardware handshake enabled; start.
. Poll to completion, read the status again and require done still set, then write-one-to-clear the status bits.
. Check every DMA-written SRAM word against the pattern.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-DATAPATH
|Every word the DMA wrote to SRAM carries the preloaded pattern, proving the chain from flash model through receive queue and trigger to SRAM. The compare is exclusive: all-ones is rejected, since that is what a mis-wired MISO, a garbled address phase and an unrecognised opcode all produce.
|CHK-RW1C
|The DMA done status bit still reads set on a second read after the poll, so a read does not clear it and it does not drop by itself; it then clears on write-one-to-clear and reads back clear. Both status values are logged. `ERROR` and `CHUNK_DONE` are never set in hardware-handshake mode, so their clear is not exercised.
|CHK-NOERR
|The DMA reports no error and the SPI controller reaches idle with clean error status.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

'''''

[[sep_dma_cpu_contention_test]]
===== 4.3 `sep_dma_cpu_contention_test`

*Phase*: 1

*Area*: SPI and DMA

*Run mode*: `cpu`, `+skip_fuse_sense`

*Source Module*: `sep_dma_cpu_contention_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip, CPU FW, `tb/sep_outbound_mbx.sv` (console + verdict mailbox; OKAY / zero read data for any address)

*Objective*: Prove CPU and DMA SRAM traffic is correct under real local-crossbar contention. A TB monitor counts cycles where both masters present an SRAM request on the same AXI address channel; DMA BUSY is the independent proof that the job spans the CPU store loop.

*Test Coverage*: CPU and DMA as concurrent SRAM masters.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Inherit the global side-effect region marking from startup code; this test performs no per-test region write of its own.
. Seed the source pattern; clear the destination and the CPU's own region.
. Start the DMA copy and do not wait.
. Immediately run the CPU store loop.
. Sample DMA status at store-loop exit, then poll to completion. After firmware completion, require the TB's same-channel CPU/DMA SRAM-request overlap count to be nonzero.
. Check both regions; read the status again and require done still set, then clear the status bits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-IN-FLIGHT
|A status sample at store-loop exit shows the DMA busy and not done, proving the DMA job spans the CPU store loop.
|CHK-OVERLAP
|The CPU-LSU and DMA masters simultaneously present SRAM requests on the same local-crossbar AW or AR channel for at least one cycle. The monitor filters both addresses to the generated SRAM aperture, so a concurrent DMA-CSR status read cannot satisfy this checker.
|CHK-NOERR
|The DMA completes with no error.
|CHK-RW1C
|The done status bit still reads set on a second read after the poll, so a read does not clear it and it does not drop by itself; it then clears on write-one-to-clear. Both status values are logged. Chunk-done is never raised in this single-chunk configuration, so its clear is not exercised.
|CHK-DMA-DATA
|The DMA destination matches its source.
|CHK-CPU-DATA
|The CPU's own region holds exactly what the CPU wrote — its traffic was not corrupted by the competing master.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

'''''

[[sep_spi_ot_dma_tx_test]]
===== 4.4 `sep_spi_ot_dma_tx_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: SPI and DMA

*Run mode*: `cpu`, `+skip_fuse_sense`, firmware `spi_ot_dma_tx_test`

*Source Module*: `sep_spi_ot_dma_tx_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip, ocah_spi_vip, CPU FW, `tb/sep_outbound_mbx.sv` (console + verdict mailbox; OKAY / zero read data for any address), observation-only probes `spi_tx_qd_probe_o`, `spi_lsio_trigger_probe_o` and `dma_busy_probe_o`

*Objective*: Drives SRAM through the secure DMA into the OpenTitan SPI host transmit FIFO and on to the flash BFM, then reads the flash back and compares against the cocotb-seeded random source data. After the walk, a TXDATA write past `STATUS.TXFULL` must latch exclusive `ERROR_STATUS.OVERFLOW` and the host must run again after recovery.

*Test Coverage*: DMA SRAM to SPI TX to flash, readback compare, and TX overflow recovery.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Walk the seeded length and trigger cells: DMA SRAM into the OpenTitan SPI TX FIFO, page-program the flash BFM, read the flash back and compare to the SRAM source; read the DMA status again and require done still set, then W1C-clear DMA done. While DMA `STATUS.busy` is set, cocotb samples the DMA trigger input and the transmit FIFO depth on each clock.
. Write TXDATA past `STATUS.TXFULL`; expect exclusive `ERROR_STATUS.OVERFLOW`; `CONTROL.SW_RST` plus write-one-to-clear; a flash status read must complete.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-TRIGGER
|The transmit watermark tracks FIFO occupancy across the threshold, with the exact polarity asserted and the observed values logged. `EVENT_ENABLE.TXWM` is programmed.
|CHK-DMA-TX
|The flash content equals the SRAM source, compared against cocotb-seeded random data.
|CHK-DMA-DONE
|The DMA done bit still reads set on a second read after the poll, so a read does not clear it and it does not drop by itself; it then clears on write-one-to-clear and reads back clear. Both status values are logged. Handshake mode does not raise `STATUS.chunk_done` (RTL: chunk_done is the inverse of cfg_handshake_en); that status is `sep_dma_basic_test`.
|CHK-SPI-IDLE
|The SPI host returns to idle with a clean error status.
|CHK-NONVAC
|The flash readback holds content that is not the erased 0xFF pattern, so the content compare above is not erased-against-erased. Scanned on the value the flash returned, not on the staged source, which the config forces non-erased and could never fail.
|CHK-RAND-REP
|The cocotb golden walked the deterministic length and trigger cells, requiring a literal floor of write-enable and page-program transactions on the bus and a per-case address and data match.
|CHK-MULTICHUNK
|The transmit watermark paces every DMA transfer. Per case, during DMA `STATUS.busy`, the DMA trigger input shows at least as many separate assertions as the transfer has 16-byte chunks, with a literal floor of 2, and the transmit FIFO depth never goes above `TX_WATERMARK` - 1 + one chunk (7 words). A trigger held high, or a DMA that refills without waiting for the watermark, fills the FIFO past that bound in one burst. Graded on DUT probes, not on the bus byte count.
|CHK-ERR-OVERFLOW
|A TXDATA write past `STATUS.TXFULL` latches exactly `ERROR_STATUS.OVERFLOW`; `CONTROL.SW_RST` plus write-one-to-clear then lets a flash status read complete.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

'''''

[[sep_spi_ot_flash_cmd_rand_test]]
===== 4.5 `sep_spi_ot_flash_cmd_rand_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: SPI and DMA

*Run mode*: `cpu`, `+skip_fuse_sense`, firmware `spi_ot_flash_cmd_test`, 3 seeds

*Source Module*: `sep_spi_ot_flash_cmd_rand_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip, ocah_spi_vip, CPU FW, `tb/sep_outbound_mbx.sv` (console + verdict mailbox; OKAY / zero read data for any address)

*Objective*: JEDEC, WREN/RDSR, WRDI, page program, FAST_READ, and sector erase against the flash BFM, with a neighbour-sector intact check, write-protect and status-register breadth, and the three host `ERROR_STATUS` classes with recovery.

*Test Coverage*: JEDEC, program, read, erase, write-protect, and host error-status recovery.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. READ ID, then prove WEL set by WREN and cleared by WRDI.
. Program, FAST_READ, and sector-erase with neighbour intact.
. After the erase: prove WEL consumed; the controller delivers a page program with WEL clear (the device model refuses it); opcode `0x35` returns the seeded status-register-2 value.
. `ERROR_STATUS` is zero after that sequence. Then inject underflow, reserved `COMMAND.SPEED`, and an out-of-range chip-select, each exclusive and recovered; READ ID works again.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-PROGRAM / CHK-READ
|A page program followed by a read returns the exact random pattern at the exact random address.
|CHK-ERASE
|A sector erase leaves the programmed region reading all-ones and leaves the adjacent 4 KiB neighbour sector intact. The region is proven non-erased earlier in the walk, by the page program and read-back pair that `CHK-PROGRAM`/`CHK-READ` covers, so the all-ones result is a change of state rather than a region that was never written.
|CHK-NO-ERROR
|The SPI host error status is zero after the sequence.
|CHK-JEDEC
|READ ID returns the BFM JEDEC identity.
|CHK-RDSR
|RDSR sees WEL set after WREN. A controller timeout is a distinct failure, not a status byte that looks like WEL.
|CHK-WRDI
|WRDI runs on a WEL that RDSR just proved set, then RDSR sees WEL clear.
|CHK-FAST-READ
|FAST_READ returns the programmed pattern.
|CHK-WEL-AUTOCLR
|The erase consumes the write-enable latch. The latch is state of the SPI flash device model, not of SEP: what this grades is that the controller drove a well-formed erase the device accepted and retired, and it fails if the controller leaves the device armed. It is not RTL coverage of a SEP register, and takes no feature credit as such.
|CHK-WP-PP
|The controller delivers a page program issued with the write-enable latch clear: the firmware command completes, and the golden requires a third page-program transaction at the device with the full address phase at the random address. It fails if the controller drops, truncates or mis-addresses the command. The refusal itself is device-model behaviour, not SEP: the latch is state of the SPI flash device model, which drops any page program while the latch is clear, whatever the controller drives. The firmware all-ones read-back, the empty payload record and the direct read of the model's stored array are therefore model self-checks and take no feature credit, the same as `CHK-WEL-AUTOCLR`.
|CHK-RDSR2
|Opcode `0x35` returns the seeded non-zero status-register-2 value. A decode that folds `0x35` onto `0x05` returns the write-enable SR1 encoding (`0x02`) and fails. A receive path that returns all-zero also fails. The firmware does not re-read SR1 on this step; the fail cases are the two wrong bytes, not a live SR1 compare.
|CHK-ERR-UNDERFLOW
|Reading `RXDATA` with the receive FIFO empty latches exactly `ERROR_STATUS.UNDERFLOW`, then write-one-to-clear releases it.
|CHK-ERR-CMDINVAL
|A command with the reserved speed encoding latches exactly `ERROR_STATUS.CMDINVAL`, then write-one-to-clear releases it.
|CHK-ERR-CSIDINVAL
|A segment whose chip-select is outside `NumCS` — driven at the top of the 32-bit `CSID` field, so the stimulus assumes no particular `NumCS` — latches exactly `ERROR_STATUS.CSIDINVAL`, then write-one-to-clear releases it.
|CHK-ERR-RECOVER
|READ ID completes with the BFM JEDEC identity after the three injections, so the host was released rather than left disabled.
|CHK-RAND-REP
|The seed varies the programmed address, word count and payload. The opcode sequence is fixed, and the BFM golden requires that exact observed order.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope*: the transaction-order golden requires the BFM-visible opcode sequence
(JEDEC, WREN, RDSR, WRDI, program/read, FAST_READ, neighbour program/read, erase,
primary and neighbour read, post-erase status, the ignored write-protect program,
RDSR2, and the recovery READ ID). The three `ERROR_STATUS` injections put nothing
on the bus: the host disables its core the cycle the error latches. Dual and quad
modes are not exercised: the flash BFM does not support them.

'''''

[[sep_dma_basic_test]]
===== 4.6 `sep_dma_basic_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: SPI and DMA

*Run mode*: `cpu`, `+skip_fuse_sense`, firmware `dma_basic_test`, 3 seeds

*Source Module*: `sep_dma_basic_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip, CPU FW, `tb/sep_outbound_mbx.sv` (console + verdict mailbox; OKAY / zero read data for any address)

*Objective*: Secure-DMA control and copy breadth over the CPU LSU: documented reset values, the configuration lock reading locked while the engine is observed busy, the range-valid gate and its rw0c lock each with a positive control, FIXED/INCR/WRAP against a per-mode golden, 1/2/4-byte widths, `STATUS.done` RW1C, one invalid-opcode error with recovery, the address, address-space-id and transfer-width refusals, the inverted-range refusal, a copy that leaves SRAM for the instruction memory and back, a DMA-issued host-path command-integrity inject, and a fabric DECERR dest that raises `host_path_err` with the pin low. The mode and width walk is directed.

*Test Coverage*: Secure-DMA locks, address modes, widths, errors, and host-path integrity.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Read DMA config registers at documented reset, then prove CFG_REGWEN lock while BUSY.
. While the range registers are still writable: `RANGE_VALID=0` raises `range_valid_error`, and an enabled range whose limit sits below its base raises exclusive `base_limit_error` with `STATUS.done` clear. Then lock `RANGE_REGWEN`.
. Walk INCR / FIXED / WRAP × 1B/2B/4B; consume the seed-patched SCENARIO line.
. Provoke one invalid opcode, then four exclusive address-alignment refusals; a clean copy after each error class proves the engine recovers.
. With `dma_host_intg_inject_i` high, one legal SRAM copy raises exclusive `host_path_err` and aggregator bit 41. `DMA_BUS_ERR_CLEAR` returns STATUS and bit 41 to 0. A legal copy with the pin low then matches the source snapshot.
. With the pin low, one copy whose destination is the first word past the DMA CSR window raises exclusive `host_path_err` from the fabric DECERR. CLEAR and a legal recovery copy follow.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-RESET
|The DMA configuration registers read their documented reset values.
|CHK-CFG-REGWEN
|The model check in this entry: the configuration lock reads locked while the engine is busy — with busy actually observed, failing loudly if the copy finished too fast — and the *same* write is rejected while locked and lands while unlocked.
|CHK-RANGE-REGWEN
|The range-valid gate produces the documented error, an enabled range whose limit sits below its base raises `base_limit_error` *exclusively* and sets no `STATUS.done`, and the range base register rejects a write once locked. A positive control precedes the lock — a non-reset value is written and proven to land first — so "unchanged after the lock" cannot pass identically for a read-only register or a missing decode.
|CHK-COPY-MODE
|Increment, fixed-source, fixed-destination and wrap addressing each produce their expected image against an independent local snapshot of the source fill, with a sentinel neighbour check per iteration.
|CHK-WIDTH
|Each transfer-width encoding is written *and read back*, and the copy is byte-exact. Without the read-back the three iterations are indistinguishable — 16 bytes is a whole multiple of 1, 2 and 4, so a register stuck at its reset produces identical output.
|CHK-DONE-RW1C
|The done bit is observed set and then cleared to zero.
|CHK-ERR-OPCODE
|An invalid opcode raises exactly the opcode error — asserted *exclusively*, so no other error bit may be set — with the done bit required clear, then cleared by write-one-to-clear. The recovery copy after the error matches the independent source snapshot.
|CHK-ERR-ADDR
|The address validation the engine applies before it moves a byte. Four refused descriptors, each asserting its `ERROR_CODE` bit *exclusively*: a 4-byte transfer whose source is not 4-byte aligned raises `src_addr_error`, the same on the destination raises `dst_addr_error`, a 2-byte transfer on an odd source raises `src_addr_error`, and a 2-byte transfer on an odd destination raises `dst_addr_error`. None may set `STATUS.done`, and a clean copy after the four proves the engine recovers. The inverted-range leg sits in `CHK-RANGE-REGWEN`, which must run before the one-way range lock closes.
|CHK-ERR-ASID
|An address-space id outside the three encodings the IP register specification enumerates (`OT_ADDR` 0x7, `SYS_ADDR` 0x9, `SOC_ADDR` 0xa) is refused. Walked on the source field and on the destination field separately, each asserting `asid_error` *exclusively* with `STATUS.done` clear, then cleared by write-one-to-clear, then a clean copy at the legal id. The legal set is a DV-owned table in `fw/drivers/sep_dma.h`, since the register description carries only the reset value.
|CHK-ERR-SIZE
|A transfer width outside the 1/2/4-byte encodings raises `size_error` *exclusively* with `STATUS.done` clear, then clears, then a clean copy at a legal width. Distinct from `CHK-ERR-ADDR`, where the width is legal and the address is not: this is the width decode itself refusing.
|CHK-ICCM
|A copy that leaves SRAM. Every other transfer in this entry is SRAM to SRAM, so an engine that cannot reach the instruction memory passes all of them. The data goes SRAM to ICCM and back to a second SRAM region, and the returned words are compared against the source over a sentinel pre-fill, with the count of words that changed required to be non-zero so a transfer that moved nothing fails. The round trip is used because the core takes a store access fault on a direct write to ICCM, so the processor cannot pre-fill or read back that memory; only the DMA touches it, which is what the checker is about.
|CHK-HOSTINTG
|A DMA-issued host command under `dma_host_intg_inject_i` raises exactly `DMA_BUS_ERR_STATUS.host_path_err`. Aggregator bit 41 is 1 and bit 40 stays 0. `DMA_BUS_ERR_CLEAR` returns STATUS and bit 41 to 0. A legal copy with the pin low then matches the independent source snapshot. Each leg also requires the transfer to terminate, so a wedged engine cannot pass on a latch raised from its first command.
|CHK-HOSTFABRIC
|A DMA transfer whose destination is the first word past the DMA CSR window, with the inject pin low, raises exactly `host_path_err`. `DMA_BUS_ERR_CLEAR` returns STATUS to 0. The CLEAR register is a write-only single-pulse field that always reads 0, so its read value is not graded. A legal copy then matches the independent source snapshot.
|CHK-RAND-REP
|Mode and width cells walk every seed; src/dst/length/fill come from the run seed.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Evidence*: `CHK-HOSTINTG-ARM`, `CHK-HOSTINTG-RELEASE` and `CHK-HOSTFABRIC-ARM` are firmware handshake markers: the host drives `dma_host_intg_inject_i` high from the first to the second and requires it low at the third. `CHK-HOSTINTG-PIC` (aggregator bit 41 set, bit 40 clear) and `CHK-HOSTINTG-CLR` (bit 41 back to 0 after the clear) are the host-side records of CHK-HOSTINTG.

*Not claimed*: lockstep punch-through. The register path (`reg_path_err`) is not
exercised by this leaf at all; the unmapped-window term is proven by
<<sep_irq_ip_to_aggregator_test>>. Persistence across a CPU-only reset, and
the rule that a fault arriving in the clear cycle still latches — both stated in
the register description — are unproven here.

'''''

[[sep-vplan-phase3-spi-dma]]
==== 4. SPI and DMA, Phase 3

This section holds the Phase 3 entries of the SPI and DMA area. Entry 4.10
extends an open test. Every entry names the open test it builds on and states
only the cells that the open test does not grade. The contracts that the
specification leaves open are in <<sep-vplan-phase3-blocked,Blocked features>>.
A check that needs a value that the specification does not state is blocked and is marked `Blocked: <value>`
(<<sep-vplan-credit-rules>>). A blocked check does not run and is not counted as reached.
Every contract below comes from the specification and the register description.
No contract comes from the RTL.

*Sources*. Short names used in this section:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Short name |Path
|`spi.adoc`, `dma.adoc`, `cpu.adoc`, `fabric.adoc`, `interrupts.adoc`, `reset_controller.adoc`, `rom.adoc`, `lifecycle_controller.adoc`, `clk_rst.adoc`, `port_table.adoc`
|`hw/sys/sep/doc/<name>`
|`memory_map.adoc`
|`hw/sys/sep/regs/gen/adoc/memory_map.adoc`
|`sep_cpu_ctrl.adoc`
|`hw/sys/sep/regs/gen/adoc/blocks/sep_cpu_ctrl.adoc`
|`spi_controller.adoc`
|`vendor/lowRISC/opentitan/overlay/regs/spi_controller/regs/gen/adoc/spi_controller.adoc`
|`secure_dma.adoc`
|`vendor/lowRISC/opentitan/overlay/regs/secure_dma/regs/gen/adoc/secure_dma.adoc`
|`secure_dma.rdl`
|`vendor/lowRISC/opentitan/overlay/regs/secure_dma/regs/secure_dma.rdl`
|`dma.hjson`

|`spi_host.hjson`
|`vendor/lowRISC/opentitan/upstream/hw/ip/spi_host/data/spi_host.hjson`
|`spi_controller.rdl`
|`vendor/lowRISC/opentitan/overlay/regs/spi_controller/regs/spi_controller.rdl`

|`doc/programmer/src/sep-programming.adoc`
|`SEP_TB_ARCH.adoc`
|`hw/sys/sep/dv/docs/SEP_TB_ARCH.adoc`
|===

A citation names the file and the section or register of that file.

*Rules for every entry in this section*. An entry states only what differs.

* Seed. Every random value, and every per-seed choice of a leg, an order or an
enable value, is a pure function of the seed. No stimulus depends on a seed
index. `--stage sim --seed N` replays the leaf. The generator is not a CSPRNG.
All drawn data is test data. No document quotes a per-seed value as evidence.
* Log shape. Each check logs `CHK-<NAME> PASS|FAIL seed=<n> <values>`. The leaf
ends with `RESULT <test> seed=<n> PASS checks=<k>`, where k counts the checks
that run. PASS needs positive evidence in `results.xml`. A clean simulator exit
is not evidence. A leg whose control shows no cause logs `CTRL-MISSING` and
fails. An `OBS-` line records a value and grades nothing. A check marked
Blocked does not run, does not count in k and is not a reached check.
* Probes and injects. Each entry names the probes it reads. A probe is
"approved" when `SEP_TB_ARCH.adoc` lists it or `tb_top.sv` has it. A probe
outside the closed set of `docs/SEP_TB_ARCH.adoc` is an observation tap the test adds to the SEP_TB_ARCH observation-probe list. No entry adds an error inject
or a top-port drive. A check is blocked only when it needs a PROPOSED item or a
value that the specification does not state (<<sep-vplan-credit-rules>>).

[cols="3,2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Probe |Status |What it observes
|Register frontdoor over `s_axi` (CPU-LSU splice)
|approved (`SEP_TB_ARCH.adoc`, CPU-LSU AXI)
|Every SPI and DMA register read and write with the response code, and the content of SEP SRAM at `0x1000_0000`.
|SPI pad ports `spi_sck_o`, `spi_cs_n_o`, `spi_mosi_o` and the responder input `spi_miso_i`
|approved (`SEP_TB_ARCH.adoc`, SPI host pads; `tb_top.sv`)
|The sck edges, the chip select and `sd[0]`. The pad bridge shows no other data line. The responder is `OcahSpiFlash`. With no responder the input stays at its testbench default.
|`sep_internal_interrupts_probe_o`
|approved (`SEP_TB_ARCH.adoc`, IRQ aggregate; `tb_top.sv`)
|PIC source n at index n-1: sources 9, 10 and 11 (DMA) and 14 (SPI).
|`spi_tx_qd_probe_o`, `spi_lsio_trigger_probe_o`, `dma_busy_probe_o`
|approved (`SEP_TB_ARCH.adoc`, SPI-to-DMA pacing probes)
|The TX queue depth, the SPI trigger at the DMA input and `STATUS.BUSY` of the DMA, on each clock.
|`dbg_sep_reset_n_o`
|approved (`SEP_TB_ARCH.adoc`, SEP reset probes)
|The release of `sep_reset_n` after `rst_ni`.
|`dma_axi_req_probe_o`
|observation tap the test adds to the SEP_TB_ARCH observation-probe list
|The DMA master AR, AW, W and B channel fields after the alias remap: address, AxLEN, write strobes and handshakes. Read-only.
|`dma_status_probe_o`
|observation tap the test adds to the SEP_TB_ARCH observation-probe list
|The level of `STATUS.DONE`, `CHUNK_DONE`, `ERROR`, `ABORTED` and `SHA2_DIGEST_VALID` of the DMA, on each clock. Read-only.
|===

The specification does not list the members of the SPI pad structs (see
<<sep-vplan-phase3-blocked,Blocked features>>). No check claims a signal
polarity or reads a pad struct member other than through an approved port.

* Control window. Each "never" check names a window in which a healthy design
drives the signal, and the leaf logs the value of that window.
* Reset release. After every `rst_ni` pulse the leaf waits, with a bound, for the
`sep_reset_n` release on `dbg_sep_reset_n_o` (`reset_controller.adoc`, SEP Reset
Controller) before the first register access.
* One fault per injection, from a clean state. SPI clean state: write-one-to-clear
on ERROR_STATUS and INTR_STATE.ERROR, CSID=0, then SW_RST with both FIFOs empty
before release. DMA clean state: write one to STATUS.ERROR, STATUS.ABORTED,
STATUS.DONE and STATUS.CHUNK_DONE. A write of one to STATUS.ERROR clears
ERROR_CODE (`dma.hjson`, ERROR_CODE). INTR_STATE is read-only
(`secure_dma.adoc`, INTR_STATE) and the specification states no write that
releases it (see <<sep-vplan-phase3-blocked,Blocked features>>), so a trial that
grades INTR_STATE or an interrupt line starts from a cold reset.
* DMA codes. OPCODE 0 is COPY, and 1, 2 and 3 select SHA-256, SHA-384 and
