It does not grade the exit of secure test mode other than the cold reset between the epochs, the status value of a blocked program, or the response code of a blocked write. It does not grade masking of fields other than the four named secret fields. The JTAG cells run in TEST_DEV only. The open tests `sep_efuse_secure_tm_write_lock_test` and `sep_efuse_lcc_lc_state_stitch_test` keep the cells that they grade, and the Key Manager use of the masked fields belongs to the Key Manager tests.

'''''
[[sep_efuse_jtag_access_rand_test]]
===== 6.28 `sep_efuse_jtag_access_rand_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: eFuse, lifecycle, SEC_DIS, locked-field

*Run mode*: `no_cpu` (`lsu_stub_all_live`), real fuse sense, 4 seeds; one testlist entry; the seed draws the state of the t=0 image (the preload hook stages it from the seed); tool: both (Verilator and VCS); testlist groups `all` and `cpu_stub`, file `testlists/efuse_lcc.toml`

*Source Module*: `sep_efuse_jtag_access_rand_test`

*BFM / Model*: JTAG master on `axil_sep_otp_jtag_req_i` and `axil_sep_otp_jtag_resp_o` (approved). Frontdoor master, the CPU-side bench master of `lsu_stub_all_live`, with the response code of every access (approved). OTP image preload (approved), and the direct OTP word read through the frontdoor read interface (the read interface is not the unit under test; approved). `lcc_feat_ctrl_probe_o`, `sep_fuse_sense_done_o` and `secure_tm_o` (approved). A SHA-256 model that builds the golden match code from the array content at each go. The fixed vectors `TOKEN_T1`, `TOKEN_T2` and `TOKEN_OTHER`. The post-guard command tap `efuse_shim_command_req_o` (the command statement of CHK-JTAG) is an observation tap the test adds to the SEP_TB_ARCH observation-probe list. No inject.

*Randomization*: `SepSeededRng` from the run seed (RANDCFG). The seed draws the state, PROD or RMA_SIP with equal weight. The access list of every leaf holds each of the eight (class, operation) cells at least once: shadow word read and write, interface-control register read and write, token word read and write, `TOKEN_EOP` write and match register read; the seed draws the order of these eight accesses and the other N - 8 accesses. Dimensions: access count N (15 to 20; the eight cells need at least 15 accesses, because the `TOKEN_EOP` write follows the eight word writes of its array, the token word read follows one of those writes, and the match read and the four denied cells take one access each), per drawn access the operation, the class, the in-class address and the written pattern, the two free spare bits, the `SYS_DIS` and `SIP_DIS` function-group bits, and the vector (`TOKEN_T1`, `TOKEN_T2` or `TOKEN_OTHER`) that each token-word write takes its word from. A draw never makes a token value. Trap filters: no `TOKEN_MATCH_FAULT` access; no concurrent frontdoor and JTAG traffic; no token word read before the leaf writes that word; a `TOKEN_EOP` write carries one go bit, on the SIP or the chiplet channel, and follows the write of all eight words of that array; no word write between a go and its result; a go gives a golden result that differs from the previous result of that channel (Match after Mismatch, Mismatch after Match), so a stale read cannot equal it, and the word writes between two goes on a channel rebuild the array so that the SHA-256 model gives the other result (the draw is checked against the model and a sequence that fails is redrawn); the token-block accesses run in the drawn order, interleaved by kind; the SEC_DIS array holds `TOKEN_OTHER` only and gets no go; a match register is only read and `TOKEN_EOP` is only written; a shadow-word write draws only `LOCKS`, `LOCKS_SPARE`, `SIP_DIS`, `SYS_DIS`, `REQUIRED_SIGNERS` or `REQUIRED_ALGS` (the shadow registers with writable bits in `hw/sys/sep/regs/gen/adoc/blocks/sep_efuse_map.adoc`), only a register that has a writable bit at 0 in the staged image, and a pattern that sets such a bit, while every other shadow word is drawn as a read only; the drawn `SIP_DIS` and `SYS_DIS` function-group bits leave at least one writable bit at 0 in each. `reseed = 4` gives four access sequences per regression. The state is a seed-dependent cell: a regression runs both states with a probability of about 0.88 (1 - 2 x (1/2)^4), and a merge of regressions closes the 14 graded state-class-operation cells (the PROD token word read and write are logged, see Test Coverage).

*Objective*: In PROD and in RMA_SIP the JTAG port reaches only the token block (three token arrays, `TOKEN_EOP`, three match registers). Every other JTAG read or write completes with an error response and changes nothing. No feature-control bit gates the port. Sources: `hw/sys/sep/doc/otp_fuse_controller.adoc` (section Shadow Register and JTAG Access Control); `hw/ip/efuse/doc/architecture.adoc` (section Lifecycle State (LC_STATE) Effects); `hw/sys/sep/doc/lifecycle_controller.adoc` (sections Debug and Test Port Path Gating, row SEP OTP JTAG2AXIL path; Per-LC-state Feature Control Profile); `hw/ip/efuse/regs/gen/adoc/efuse_mmr.adoc` (section eFuse Token Registers Address Map); `hw/ip/efuse/regs/gen/adoc/efuse_interface_ctrl.adoc`. The specification does not state the JTAG policy in the other states or before sense, whether `TOKEN_MATCH_FAULT` belongs to the token block, the response code of a denied access, or the arbitration of concurrent AXI and JTAG requests. The test draws only PROD and RMA_SIP, serializes the two ports and grades a response that is not OKAY. The integrity-error state is a leg of `sep_lcc_state_codeword_rand_test`, which is blocked: it needs its injection point.

*Test Coverage*: Two states (PROD, RMA_SIP) by five target classes: shadow word (read and write), interface-control register (read and write), token word (read and write), `TOKEN_EOP` (write only) and match register (read only), which gives 16 state-class-operation cells, of which this test grades 14. The token match through the JTAG port with every DBG_1 and DBG_2 feature bit closed, in both states. The target readback after each denied access and the OTP bit p at the end of the leaf. The open test `sep_efuse_jtag_axil_el2_cpu_mux_test` grades the response of the PROD read of the shadow map, of `EFUSE_PROGRAM_CTRL` and of the token-block sample (`SEC_DISABLE_TOKEN_I[0]`, `SEC_DISABLE_TOKEN_MATCH`), and the PROD token word write and readback (OKAY, and the word last written). The open test `sep_efuse_jtag_window_allow_test` grades the shadow map and `EFUSE_PROGRAM_CTRL` in TEST_DEV. They keep those cells, and this test logs the response of those PROD accesses (and the data of a PROD token word read) and does not grade it. Only the new cells are graded here: the write of every class other than the token word in PROD, the write of every class in RMA_SIP, the read of every class in RMA_SIP, the token word readback in RMA_SIP and the match golden of the channels with a go, the unchanged target after each denied access and the unburned bit p at the end of the leaf, in both states (including the PROD denied reads), and the token match with every debug bit closed in both states. Functional coverage: `sep_efuse_jtag_policy_cg` (`cp_state` for PROD and RMA_SIP, `cp_class`, `cp_resp`, `x_state_class_op`, `cp_gate_independent_of_feat`; `cp_state`, `x_state_class_op` and `cp_gate_independent_of_feat` are seed-dependent, because one leaf draws one state).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Draw from the seed the state, N, the order of the eight required (class, operation) accesses among the N, and for each access the operation, class, in-class address and pattern. Print `SEED seed=<n> state=<name>` and one `DRAW` line per drawn value. Draw the control bit c and the probe bit p: two different spare bits that read 0 in the image and whose field is unlocked. Every wait in the steps below is a bounded wait; a timeout fails the check that the step feeds.
. Stage the OTP image through the preload: the `LC_STATE` encoding of the drawn state; `SIP_DIS` with every DBG_1 and DBG_2 bit set (an exception to the vector filter: the test grades no demotion, owner veto or RMA bypass); `SYS_DIS` with a drawn non-zero value that has at least one 0 bit; `RMA_SIP_TOKEN_DIGEST` as the digest of `TOKEN_T1` and `RMA_CHIPLET_TOKEN_DIGEST` as the digest of `TOKEN_T2`, staged by the digest rule of this bucket; `TRANSIENT_RMA_EN` at 0, so that no SIP or chiplet Match moves the state shadow and `FEAT_CTRL` stays at the profile of the drawn state; every lock bit 0; the other fields by the image rules.
. Hold `secure_tm_req_i` at 0. Cold reset and wait for `sep_fuse_sense_done_o`. Measure the sense time; the window W is a multiple of it (the multiple is a test parameter). Read `secure_tm_o`; it reads 0, so the shadow protection of secure test mode cannot hide an accepted write.
. Read `FEAT_CTRL` through the frontdoor and at `lcc_feat_ctrl_probe_o`. Both read the same value, and bits 47:0 (DBG_1 and DBG_2) read 0. If a debug bit reads 1, the leaf fails with `CHK-JTAG-TOKEN FAIL`.
. Set a status flag that a denied write could clear. Through the frontdoor, write `EFUSE_READ_CTRL` with `read_enable` = 1, `efuse_addr` = 8192 (the first bit address past the 256 words of 32 bits) and `efuse_read_go` = 1. Wait the full window W with no early exit; `read_done` is not graded, because the register description does not state that an out-of-range read sets it. Read `EFUSE_INTERFACE_CTRL_STATUS`; `efuse_read_addr_error` reads 1, else the leaf fails with `CHK-HOOK FAIL`. Write `EFUSE_READ_CTRL` with `read_enable` = 0.
. Control program. Through the frontdoor, write `EFUSE_PROGRAM_CTRL` with `program_enable` = 1, `efuse_data` = 1, `efuse_addr` = the bit address of c and `efuse_program_go` = 1. Wait the full window W with no early exit. Read `EFUSE_PROGRAM_CTRL`; `program_done` reads 1. Write `EFUSE_PROGRAM_CTRL` with all fields 0. Read the word of c through the direct read; bit c reads 1, and bit p reads 0 in the word of p.
. For each drawn access of a denied class (shadow word or interface-control register), in the drawn order: read the target through the frontdoor; issue the JTAG read or write; record the response code; read the target through the frontdoor again. A shadow-word write pattern sets a writable bit that reads 0 in the staged image, so an accepted write changes the readback. A write to `EFUSE_INTERFACE_CTRL_STATUS` sets bit 10 (`efuse_read_addr_error_clear`). A write to `EFUSE_PROGRAM_CTRL` sets `program_enable`, `efuse_data` and `efuse_program_go` with `efuse_addr` = the bit address of p, so an accepted write burns p. A write to `EFUSE_READ_CTRL` sets `read_enable` and `efuse_read_go` with a drawn `efuse_addr` below 8192. A read pattern is the address alone. Error injection: the point is the JTAG master; the kind is a read or write outside the token block; the expected response is a response that is not OKAY and no change. The read data is not graded. After the last denied access of the leaf wait the window W, then read the word of p through the direct read. Bit p reads 0.
. Run the drawn token-block accesses in the drawn order, one at a time, each as the action of its kind in the four steps that follow. The kinds are interleaved as drawn and do not run as separate passes.
. Token-word write: issue the JTAG write of the drawn vector word to the drawn array and word index (index 0 holds `token[31:0]`); record the response; in RMA_SIP it is OKAY, and in PROD it is logged and not graded.
. Token-word read: issue the JTAG read of a word that the leaf has written; record the response and the data; in RMA_SIP the response is OKAY and the data is the word last written, and in PROD both are logged and not graded.
. `TOKEN_EOP` write: issue the JTAG write with one go bit (bit 0 for the SIP array, bit 8 for the chiplet array) after the eight words of that array are written; record the response; it is OKAY. The array content at the go gives a golden that differs from the previous result of that channel. Poll the JTAG read of that channel's match register until it reads the SHA-256 golden of the array content at the go: Match is 0x15, Mismatch is 0x2a. An Idle (0x00) read keeps the poll running.
. Match-register read: issue the JTAG read; record the response. For a channel with a go in the leaf, compare the data with the golden of its last go. For a channel with no go since power-on, log the data in `OBS-JTAG-MATCH-NOGO` and do not grade it.
. Token match under closed debug bits. If the last SIP result is Match, first write the eight words of `TOKEN_OTHER` and go bit 0 and poll `RMA_SIP_TOKEN_MATCH` through the JTAG master until it reads 0x2a, so the result that follows cannot be a stale read. Write the eight words of `TOKEN_T1` through the JTAG master to `RMA_SIP_TOKEN_I[0]` to `RMA_SIP_TOKEN_I[7]`, each answered OKAY. Write 0x1 to `TOKEN_EOP` through the JTAG master. Poll `RMA_SIP_TOKEN_MATCH` through the JTAG master until it reads 0x15 (6'b010101). Read `RMA_SIP_TOKEN_MATCH` through the frontdoor; it reads 0x15.
. Read `FEAT_CTRL` through the frontdoor and at `lcc_feat_ctrl_probe_o`. Bits 47:0 read 0 in both.
. End the match. Write the eight words of `TOKEN_OTHER` to the SIP array through the JTAG master and write 0x1 to `TOKEN_EOP`. Poll `RMA_SIP_TOKEN_MATCH` through the frontdoor until it reads 0x2a. If the chiplet channel holds a Match, do the same on that channel with `TOKEN_OTHER`, go bit 8 and `RMA_CHIPLET_TOKEN_MATCH`. The next leaf starts with no held match.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-JTAG
|Each access answers as its class requires. For the allowed classes the response is OKAY, except the PROD token word read and write and the PROD read of `SEC_DISABLE_TOKEN_MATCH`, whose response (and for a token word read, the data) is logged and graded by `sep_efuse_jtag_axil_el2_cpu_mux_test`: in RMA_SIP a token word read returns the word last written, and a match read of a channel with a go in the leaf returns the SHA-256 golden result of the last go (`hw/sys/sep/doc/token_processing.adoc`, sections Token Matching Mechanism and Token Submission). A match read of a channel with no go since power-on answers OKAY and logs its value without grading it, because the retained digest and its valid bit have no reset value. For the denied classes (`hw/sys/sep/doc/otp_fuse_controller.adoc`, section Shadow Register and JTAG Access Control) the response is not OKAY (except the PROD read of a shadow word or of `EFUSE_PROGRAM_CTRL`, whose response is logged and graded by `sep_efuse_jtag_axil_el2_cpu_mux_test`), the target reads the same at the frontdoor before and after, and the bit p reads 0 at the direct read at the end of the leaf. A shadow-word write changes a writable bit that reads 0, so an accepted write shows in the readback. A DUT that lets a write reach a shadow word or an interface-control register, answers OKAY for a denied access, burns the bit p, or blocks the token block fails. Anchor: the JTAG response code, the frontdoor readback of the target (a real readback) and the direct read of the word of p. Control: the control program of step 6 sets bit c at the same direct read, so a burn can show; the status flag of step 5 reads 1 before the denied write to the status register, so a taken clear shows; the allowed accesses answer OKAY in each state. No program command reaches the post-guard port `efuse_shim_command_req_o` after a denied write; its control is one program command at the tap for the program of step 6, and a leaf in which that command does not show fails with `CHK-HOOK FAIL`. Evidence: one line per access, `CHK-JTAG PASS seed=<n> state=<PROD\|RMA_SIP> op=<rd\|wr> tgt=<class> addr=0x<a> exp=<allow\|deny> resp=<code> resp_graded=<1\|0> data_ok=<1\|na> target_unchanged=<1\|na>`. For a denied access `target_unchanged` is 1. For an allowed access it is `na`. A logged PROD access prints `resp_graded=0 data_ok=na`, and a logged PROD token word read adds `data=0x<d> last_wr=0x<w>`. One line at the end of the leaf, `CHK-JTAG PASS seed=<n> state=<PROD\|RMA_SIP> tgt=otp_word_p p_bit_read=0 ctl_bit_read=1 ctl_cmd=1`, reports the direct reads.
|CHK-JTAG-TOKEN
|A JTAG write of `TOKEN_T1` into the SIP array and a go at `TOKEN_EOP` bit 0 give the SIP match 0x15 at a frontdoor read, while `FEAT_CTRL` has every DBG_1 and DBG_2 bit at 0 before and after the go (`hw/sys/sep/doc/lifecycle_controller.adoc`, row SEP OTP JTAG2AXIL path: no feature-control bit gates the path; `hw/sys/sep/doc/token_processing.adoc`, section Token Matching Mechanism). A DUT that gates the token path on a feature-control bit shows a response that is not OKAY or a match value other than 0x15, and fails. The leaf fails if `FEAT_CTRL` has an open debug bit, because the check could then not tell a gated port from an open one. Anchor: the frontdoor readback of `RMA_SIP_TOKEN_MATCH` and of `FEAT_CTRL`, and `lcc_feat_ctrl_probe_o`. Control: in the same leaf the allowed accesses of CHK-JTAG answer OKAY while the debug bits are closed. Evidence: `CHK-JTAG-TOKEN PASS seed=<n> state=<PROD\|RMA_SIP> feat=0x<64b> dbg_open=0x0 sip_match=0x15`.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope limit*: The JTAG policy in TEST_DEV, PROD_END, RMA_CHIPLET, INVALID and before sense, the access to `TOKEN_MATCH_FAULT`, the arbitration of concurrent AXI and JTAG requests, the read data of a denied read and the code of a denied response are not claimed (see <<sep-vplan-phase3-blocked,Blocked features>>). No SEC_DIS go is made, so the leaf needs no SEC_DIS digest. The integrity-error state is graded in `sep_lcc_state_codeword_rand_test`. The open test `sep_efuse_jtag_axil_el2_cpu_mux_test` keeps the grade of the response of the PROD read of the shadow map, of `EFUSE_PROGRAM_CTRL` and of the token-block sample, and of the PROD token word write and readback, and the open test `sep_efuse_jtag_window_allow_test` keeps the TEST_DEV cells; this entry logs those responses and grades only the new cells listed in Test Coverage.

'''''

[[sep_sec_dis_timing_rand_test]]
===== 6.29 `sep_sec_dis_timing_rand_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: eFuse, lifecycle, SEC_DIS, locked-field

*Run mode*: `no_cpu` (`lsu_stub_all_live`), real fuse sense, `+sep_edn_jtag_reset_waive`, 3 seeds; every leaf runs one class, B or C, which the seed draws with equal weight; tool: VCS only, because the reset behaviour and the unreset shadow values need X; testlist groups `all` and `cpu_stub`, file `testlists/efuse_lcc.toml`

*Source Module*: `sep_sec_dis_timing_rand_test`

*BFM / Model*: Frontdoor master, the CPU-side bench master of `lsu_stub_all_live` (approved). OTP image preload (approved). `sep_fuse_sense_done_o`, `security_disable_o`, `secure_tm_req_i` and `secure_tm_o` (approved boundary ports). `efuse_shadow_probe_o`, `lcc_feat_ctrl_probe_o` and the SEP reset net (approved read-only probes). IC_RESET TDR driver on the SEP slice of the override (approved). The fixed vectors `TOKEN_ZERO` and `TOKEN_OTHER`. The post-guard command tap `efuse_shim_command_req_o` (the class C statement of CHK-SDIS-HOLD) is an observation tap the test adds to the SEP_TB_ARCH observation-probe list. No inject.

*Randomization*: `SepSeededRng` from the run seed (RAND-REP). Dimensions: the class, B or C with equal weight, the match offset k after reset release (class B, between the bounds k_lo and k_hi that the control sense and the match latency L of step 3 give), the staged image (which fields hold non-zero distinct words, at least four, with at least one below byte offset 0x200 and at least one at or above it, so that the staged loads span the sense), the disable-vector pair from the vector filter. Trap filters: one match per simulation segment; every class ends with a mismatch and a cold reset; `secure_tm_req_i` held at 0. `reseed = 3` gives three classes per regression. The class is a seed-dependent cell: a regression runs both classes with a probability of 0.75 (1 - 2 x (1/2)^3), and the cells that only one class fills (the before-sense and during-sense bins of `cp_match_phase` and the two phase bins of `cp_stops_sense`) close over a merge of regressions.

*Objective*: A SEC_DIS match made before sense keeps sense done low and every sensed shadow word at its reset value. A match made during sense keeps sense done low and the sensed shadow words unchanged. A cold reset under the match leaves every shadow word at its reset value with sensing off. After a mismatch hash and a cold reset, a full sense loads the staged image; the sense and the feature control of that recovery are logged controls. The sense stop, the OKAY map read, the feature override and the drop after a mismatch hash are logged controls here, because `sep_sec_dis_override_test` grades them. Sources: `hw/sys/sep/doc/security_disable.adoc` (sections Token Activation, Fuse Sensing and the Shadow Map, Reset Persistence); `hw/sys/sep/doc/otp_fuse_controller.adoc` (section Fuse Sensing and Boot Sequencing, the SLVERR of the map window until sense completes); `hw/sys/sep/doc/token_processing.adoc` (sections Token Matching Mechanism and Attack Countermeasures, Token Submission); `hw/ip/efuse/doc/architecture.adoc` (section Security Disable Bypass Mechanism); `hw/sys/sep/doc/reset_controller.adoc` (section Isolation and Reset Sequencing); `hw/sys/sep/regs/gen/adoc/blocks/sep_efuse_map.adoc` (reset values). `test_mode.adoc` and `security_disable.adoc` word the strap sample edge at the early capture point differently, so the strap is held low (see <<sep-vplan-phase3-blocked,Blocked features>>). The shadow reset value of `LC_STATE` and the upper nibble of `lc_state_o` before sense are not graded (see <<sep-vplan-phase3-blocked,Blocked features>>).

*Test Coverage*: Class B, a `TOKEN_ZERO` match that lands during sense while a staged non-zero shadow word still holds its reset value, then a release of the SEP reset through the IC_RESET TDR. Class C, a match held over a cold reset with the token arrays retained, so the match is present from reset release and before sense. In both classes: the sensed shadow words held over the window, a cold reset under the match, the reset value of every shadow field after it, and the recovery by a mismatch hash, a cold reset and a full sense, which is a logged control. Logged controls: sense done low and `security_disable_o` at 1 over the window, an OKAY shadow-map read, the sense-done time, the shadow words and the `FEAT_CTRL` value of the recovery sense, a control sense that measures the sense time, the SLVERR of a map read before sense done in that sense, and the staged non-zero fields reading non-zero there. `sep_sec_dis_override_test` grades the match override of `FEAT_CTRL`, the drop after a mismatch, the stop of sensing, the OKAY read of the map while sensing is open, the full sense after a mismatch and a reset together with the `FEAT_CTRL` golden of the staged vector pair after it, and the match after sense. `sep_sec_dis_reset_reach_test` grades the reset override. The open owners keep those cells. Only the new cells are graded here: the class C shadow words at their reset values over the window, the class B unchanged sensed shadow words, and the reset value of every shadow word after a cold reset under the match. Functional coverage: Phase 1 group `sep_sec_dis_boot_cg` (`cp_hold`, `cp_release`, `cp_rehold`, `cp_map_resp`), `sep_sec_dis_activation_cg` (`cp_match_phase` before-sense and during-sense bins, seed-dependent) and `sep_sec_dis_robustness_cg` (`cp_stops_sense`, seed-dependent, `cp_reset_values_hold`). The logged controls (the retained match after the cold reset, the OKAY map read, the recovery) credit no bin.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Draw the class, the staged image and the disable-vector pair. Print `SEED seed=<n> class=<B/C>` and one `DRAW` line per drawn value. Run the class sequence once: steps 4 to 9 for class B or steps 10 to 12 for class C, then steps 13 and 14. Stage a TEST_DEV image through the preload with non-zero distinct words in the drawn fields (`LC_STATE` excepted) and the drawn vector pair. Hold `secure_tm_req_i` at 0 for the whole leaf. Count the staged non-zero fields as m. Every wait in the steps below is a bounded wait; a timeout fails the check that the step feeds.
. Control sense. Cold reset. From reset release, sample `sep_fuse_sense_done_o` and `efuse_shadow_probe_o` on every clock until sense done rises. While sense done is low, issue one frontdoor read of a shadow-map word; the response is SLVERR. If sense done is already high at the response, the leaf fails with `CHK-HOOK FAIL`.
. At sense done, record t_sense, the clocks from reset release to the rise of sense done. Record t_first and tl, the clocks of the first and the last change of a staged non-zero shadow word in the probe trace. Read every shadow register through the frontdoor; each staged non-zero field reads non-zero and equals its staged value. Set the window W to 3 times t_sense (the multiple 3 is a test parameter). Match latency. Write the eight words of `TOKEN_ZERO` to `SEC_DISABLE_TOKEN_I[0]` to `SEC_DISABLE_TOKEN_I[7]` through the frontdoor and write 0x10000 to `TOKEN_EOP`. Record L, the clocks from the issue of the first token-word write to the rise of `security_disable_o`; if it does not rise, the leaf fails with `CHK-HOOK FAIL`. Write the eight words of `TOKEN_OTHER` and write 0x10000 to `TOKEN_EOP`. Poll `SEC_DISABLE_TOKEN_MATCH` until it reads 0x2a and check that `security_disable_o` is 0. Cold reset and wait for sense done.
. Class B only. Draw k from k_lo = max(1, t_first - L + 1) to k_hi = tl - L - 1 clocks, so that the match lands after the first and before the last load of a staged non-zero word, or take the k that step 6 sets. If k_lo is greater than k_hi, no try can land inside sense, and the leaf fails with `CHK-HOOK FAIL reason=window`. Cold reset. Release it. After k clocks, write the eight words of `TOKEN_ZERO` to `SEC_DISABLE_TOKEN_I[0]` to `SEC_DISABLE_TOKEN_I[7]` through the frontdoor, then write 0x10000 (go bit 16) to `TOKEN_EOP`.
. Class B only. Wait for the rise of `security_disable_o`. If it does not rise, the leaf fails with `CHK-HOOK FAIL`. At the rise, read `sep_fuse_sense_done_o` and the probe. The try is accepted when sense done is low, at least one staged non-zero shadow word reads its staged value and at least one staged non-zero shadow word still reads its reset value. At an accepted try, save the probe sample S and the count n_loaded of staged non-zero words that read their staged value.
. Class B only. A try that is not accepted is retried. Set k to the midpoint of k_lo and k when sense done is high or no staged non-zero word reads its reset value; set k to the midpoint of k and k_hi when no staged non-zero word reads its staged value. Write the eight words of `TOKEN_OTHER` to `SEC_DISABLE_TOKEN_I[0]` to `SEC_DISABLE_TOKEN_I[7]` and write 0x10000 to `TOKEN_EOP`. Poll `SEC_DISABLE_TOKEN_MATCH` until it reads 0x2a and check that `security_disable_o` is 0. Cold reset and wait for sense done. Repeat steps 4 and 5, up to three tries in all; after the third try that is not accepted, the leaf fails with `CHK-HOOK FAIL`.
. Class B only. For W clocks from the rise, sample on every clock: sense done is low, `security_disable_o` is 1 and the probe equals S. Within the window, issue one frontdoor read of a shadow-map word; the response is OKAY.
. Class B only. Through the IC_RESET TDR driver, override `sep_reset_n` to release the SEP reset. Read the SEP reset net; it reads released. For W clocks, sample on every clock: sense done is low, `security_disable_o` is 1 and the probe equals S. Then return the TDR slice to the value of the harness reset state.
. Class B only. Cold reset with the token arrays and the match retained. Release it. Go to step 13.
. Class C only. After the control sense, write the eight words of `TOKEN_ZERO` to the SEC_DIS array through the frontdoor and write 0x10000 to `TOKEN_EOP`. Poll `SEC_DISABLE_TOKEN_MATCH` through the frontdoor until it reads 0x15 (6'b010101). Wait for the rise of `security_disable_o`; if it does not rise, the leaf fails with `CHK-HOOK FAIL`.
. Class C only. Cold reset with the token arrays retained. Release it.
. Class C only. For W clocks from reset release, sample on every clock: sense done is low, `security_disable_o` is 1 and every probe word except the `LC_STATE` word equals 0. Within the window, issue one frontdoor read of a shadow-map word; the response is OKAY.
. Reset values under the match. While sense done is low, read every register of the eFuse map through the frontdoor. Each response is OKAY. Each field except `LC_STATE` reads its reset value 0x0, and each of the m staged non-zero fields reads 0. Sample `sep_fuse_sense_done_o` at each response; it is low.
. Recovery. Write the eight words of `TOKEN_OTHER` to the SEC_DIS array through the frontdoor and write 0x10000 to `TOKEN_EOP`. Poll `SEC_DISABLE_TOKEN_MATCH` through the frontdoor until it reads 0x2a (6'b101010); `security_disable_o` is 0. Cold reset. Wait for sense done within 2 times t_sense (the multiple 2 is a test parameter). Read every shadow register and `FEAT_CTRL` through the frontdoor and at `lcc_feat_ctrl_probe_o`. The shadow words equal the staged image, with `LC_STATE` as `{~raw[3:0], raw[3:0]}`. Log `OBS-SDIS-RECOVER LOG seed=<n> feat=0x<64b> ctl_mismatch=0x2a ctl_sense_done_cycles=<c> ctl_shadows_eq_staged=<0\|1>` and grade nothing: `sep_sec_dis_override_test` grades the recovery.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-SDIS-HOLD
|Under the match, the sensed shadow words do not change over the window. Sense done low, `security_disable_o` at 1 and the OKAY frontdoor shadow-map read are logged controls inside the `PASS` line; `sep_sec_dis_override_test` grades them (`hw/sys/sep/doc/security_disable.adoc`, section Fuse Sensing and the Shadow Map). In class B the sensed shadow words at `efuse_shadow_probe_o` equal their values at the rise of `security_disable_o` over the window and again after the TDR release, and sense done stays low after the TDR release. In class C the sensed shadow words equal their reset values from reset release over the window (`LC_STATE` word excepted; `hw/sys/sep/doc/security_disable.adoc`, section Reset Persistence). A DUT that senses under the match, loads a word after the match, or restarts sensing at the SEP reset release fails. The class B try is accepted only when at least one staged non-zero word is loaded and at least one is still at reset at the rise (step 5), so the probe holds a loaded word and an unloaded word that a DUT could change. Anchor: `sep_fuse_sense_done_o`, `security_disable_o` and `efuse_shadow_probe_o` on every clock, and the frontdoor response code. Controls: the control sense shows sense done and the staged non-zero shadow words inside the measured sense time (`ctl_sense_done_cycle`); the probe of the control sense at clock k differs from its probe at sense done, so the same words do change after the class B offset (`ctl_probe_changed=1`); a map read before sense done in the control sense answers SLVERR (`ctl_map_resp`); and in class B the SEP reset net reads released after the TDR step (`sep_rst_released=1`), so the window after it tests a released reset. In class C no read command reaches the bank port `efuse_shim_command_req_o` from reset release over the window; its controls are the read commands that the control sense and the recovery sense show at the tap, and a leaf whose control sense shows no read command at `efuse_shim_command_req_o` fails with `CHK-HOOK FAIL`. Evidence: `CHK-SDIS-HOLD PASS seed=<n> class=<B\|C> t_sense=<c> window=<w> probe_unchanged=<1\|na> shadow_reset_over_window=<1\|na> ctl_sense_done_cycle=<c> ctl_probe_changed=1 ctl_map_resp=SLVERR sep_rst_released=<1\|na> match_lat=<c> k=<c\|na> n_loaded=<n\|na> ctl_sense_done=0 ctl_sdis_o=1 ctl_map_resp=OKAY ctl_sense_cmds=<n\|na>`.
|CHK-SDIS-RESET-VALUES
|After a cold reset under the match, every shadow field reads its described reset value 0x0 through the frontdoor, `LC_STATE` excepted, and each response is OKAY. Sense done low at each response is a logged control that `sep_sec_dis_override_test` grades (`hw/sys/sep/doc/security_disable.adoc`, section Reset Persistence; `hw/sys/sep/regs/gen/adoc/blocks/sep_efuse_map.adoc`, reset values). The staged non-zero fields read 0. In class B the cold reset follows an interrupted sense in which at least one staged non-zero word is loaded and at least one is not loaded (step 5, `n_loaded` in the evidence line), so a DUT that keeps the partial words has a loaded word to keep and fails. In class C the cold reset follows a full sense, so a DUT that keeps the sensed words fails. Anchor: the frontdoor readback of every register of the map. Control: the same fields read non-zero in the control sense of the leaf (step 3), so a zero reading is a cleared word and not an unwritten one. Evidence: `CHK-SDIS-RESET-VALUES PASS seed=<n> class=<B\|C> fields=<n> staged_nonzero=<m> n_loaded=<n\|na> all_reset_value=1 ctl_sense_done=0`.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope limit*: The strap sample edge at the early capture point, the shadow reset value of `LC_STATE`, the upper nibble of `lc_state_o` before sense and the secure scan chain are not claimed (see <<sep-vplan-phase3-blocked,Blocked features>>). The revision enable of SEC_DIS keeps its A0 value; the test does not set it. A token match with `secure_tm_req_i` at 1 is not made. The sense stop, the OKAY map read, the feature override, the drop after a mismatch, the sense-done time of the recovery sense, its shadow words and its `FEAT_CTRL` are logged controls here, and `sep_sec_dis_override_test` keeps their grade. The TOKEN_ZERO bind to the SEC_DIS digest is graded in `sep_sec_dis_override_test`; this test shows it only through the rise of `security_disable_o` and the 0x15 readback. The reset override is graded in `sep_sec_dis_reset_reach_test`. The match after sense is graded in `sep_sec_dis_override_test`. The SMC fuse controller is not driven.

'''''

[[sep_efuse_shim_response_fault_test]]
===== 6.30 `sep_efuse_shim_response_fault_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: eFuse, lifecycle, SEC_DIS, locked-field

*Run mode*: `no_cpu` (`lsu_stub_all_live`), real fuse sense with the injected shim response, 3 seeds; every leaf runs the injected sense of leg A at one word class that the seed draws, with one cold reset; tool: both (Verilator and VCS); testlist groups `all` and `cpu_stub`, file `testlists/efuse_lcc.toml`

*Source Module*: `sep_efuse_shim_response_fault_test`

*BFM / Model*: Frontdoor master, the CPU-side bench master of `lsu_stub_all_live`, with the response code of every access (approved). OTP image preload and the direct OTP word read through the frontdoor read interface (approved). `efuse_shadow_probe_o`, `sep_fuse_sense_done_o` and the program interface outputs (busy, done, error) (approved). Added hooks, error injects that the test adds to the inject exceptions of `docs/SEP_TB_ARCH.adoc`: the bank-model sense status inject, `efuse_sense_status_inject_i` with `efuse_sense_status_word_i`, which sets the status bit on the sense response of one word; and the shim response hold `efuse_shim_resp_hold_i`, which withholds the shim response of a program request on the `sep` input `efuse_shim_command_resp_i` while it is high.

*Randomization*: `SepSeededRng` from the run seed (RAND-REP). Dimensions: the word class of w, one per leaf, with weight 2 for each edge class (the first allowed word 10, the last allowed word 254) and weight 1 for each other class (the word of the 32-bit field `CHIPLET_PUBK_REVOKE` at offset 0x88, and a word drawn from 11 to 253 inside a 256-bit field), the drawn word of the last class, the three spare bits, the program timeout cycles T and the hold multiple m. Trap filters: w in 10 to 254; the staged value of each w and of its w + 1 is non-zero; each spare bit reads 0 in the image and its field is unlocked, and the three bits are different; the timeout cell draws T so that m times T clocks fit the run budget, with m at least 2. `reseed = 3` samples other word classes, drawn words, spare bits, timeout cycles and hold multiples. The word class is seed-dependent: the four classes are graded over a merge of regressions, about 4 regressions, because each of the two lighter classes takes 1 in 6 of the leaves and a regression has 3 leaves.

*Objective*: A shim response whose status bit is set during sensing still advances the sensing word counter and leaves that shadow word unwritten, so it reads its reset value, and sense done still rises. Every other word loads its staged value. A program request that waits for its shim response shows `program_busy` and not `program_done` while it waits with the program timeout disabled, and shows `program_done` with `program_status` 0 and no busy after the response. Sources: `hw/sys/sep/doc/otp_fuse_controller.adoc` (section Fuse Sensing and Boot Sequencing, the paragraph on the sensing sequence: a strobe with its status bit set advances the counter and leaves that word unwritten); `hw/sys/sep/regs/gen/adoc/blocks/sep_efuse_map.adoc` (the reset value 0x0 of every field except `LC_STATE`); `hw/ip/efuse/regs/gen/adoc/efuse_interface_ctrl.adoc` (registers `EFUSE_INTERFACE_CTRL_STATUS`, `EFUSE_PROGRAM_CTRL`, `EFUSE_PROGRAM_REQ_TIMEOUT`); `hw/ip/efuse/doc/interface.adoc` (section Fuse Command Protocol, the response status bit). The specification does not state what a program request reports when its timeout fires, what a sense response status does to the lock words or the `LC_STATE` word, or what the last word (255) does with a status (see <<sep-vplan-phase3-blocked,Blocked features>>). The timeout cell is logged and not graded, and words 0 to 9 and 255 are not drawn.

*Test Coverage*: Leg A, a sense response with its status bit set at one word w of 10 to 254, one drawn word class per leaf: the first allowed word, the last allowed word, a word of a 32-bit field or a word inside a 256-bit field; the word w reads its reset value, its neighbour w + 1 and every other word read the staged value, and sense done rises. Leg B, the program lifecycle with the program timeout disabled: a program with a normal response ends with done, status 0 and no busy; a program with a withheld response shows busy and not done, and shows done, status 0 and no busy after the release. A timeout cell with the timeout enabled and the response withheld, logged and not graded. `sep_efuse_sense_test` and `sep_efuse_image_test` sense an image with every response normal, `sep_efuse_program_read_back_select_test` drops a program write through the bank-model plusargs, and `sep_efuse_illegal_state_fail_closed_test` grades the read timeout. The open owners keep those cells. Only the new cells are graded here: the sense response with the status bit set and the busy and done lifecycle of a program request whose shim response is late. Functional coverage: `sep_efuse_if_status_cg` (`cp_sense_status_word`, `x_prog_lifecycle`; both fill on every seed).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Draw from the seed the word class, the word of the drawn class, the three spare bits a, b and c, T and m. The class gives one word w and its neighbour w + 1. Print `SEED seed=<n>` and one `DRAW` line per drawn value. Every wait in the steps below is a bounded wait; a timeout fails the check that the step feeds.
. Stage a TEST_DEV image through the preload with non-zero distinct words in every field of shadow words 10 to 254, every lock bit 0 and the other fields by the image rules. Each of a, b and c sits at a 0 bit of its staged spare word. Hold `secure_tm_req_i` at 0.
. Leg A control sense. With both injects low, cold reset. From reset release, count the clocks until `sep_fuse_sense_done_o` rises; the count is t_sense. Read the probe `efuse_shadow_probe_o`; every word equals its staged value, with `LC_STATE` as `{~raw[3:0], raw[3:0]}`. Read words w and w + 1 through the frontdoor; both read their staged value, which is non-zero.
. Leg A injected sense, at the drawn word class. Drive `efuse_sense_status_word_i` = w and `efuse_sense_status_inject_i` = 1. Cold reset. Wait for `sep_fuse_sense_done_o` within a multiple of t_sense (the multiple is a test parameter); a timeout fails CHK-SENSE-STATUS.
. After sense done, read `efuse_shadow_probe_o` for all 256 words. Read words w and w + 1 through the frontdoor. Read `EFUSE_INTERFACE_CTRL_STATUS` through the frontdoor. Drive `efuse_sense_status_inject_i` = 0.
. Leg B control program. With both injects low, cold reset and wait for sense done. Write `EFUSE_PROGRAM_REQ_TIMEOUT` with `program_req_timeout_enable` = 0. Write `EFUSE_PROGRAM_CTRL` with `program_enable` = 1, `efuse_data` = 1, `efuse_addr` = the bit address of a, `efuse_program_read_back` = 0 and `efuse_program_go` = 1. Poll `program_done` until it reads 1. Read `EFUSE_PROGRAM_CTRL`. Read the word of a through the direct read; bit a reads 1.
. Leg B held program. Cold reset and wait for sense done; the program interface registers read their reset values. Write `EFUSE_PROGRAM_REQ_TIMEOUT` with `program_req_timeout_enable` = 0. Drive `efuse_shim_resp_hold_i` = 1. Write `EFUSE_PROGRAM_CTRL` with `program_enable` = 1, `efuse_data` = 1, `efuse_addr` = the bit address of b and `efuse_program_go` = 1.
. Poll `efuse_program_busy_o` and `program_busy` until both read 1. Then, for a window of a multiple of t_sense (a test parameter), sample the program interface outputs on every clock and read `EFUSE_PROGRAM_CTRL` through the frontdoor at least 4 times (a test parameter): `program_busy` is 1 and `program_done` is 0 at every sample and every read.
. Drive `efuse_shim_resp_hold_i` = 0. Poll `program_done` until it reads 1. Read `EFUSE_PROGRAM_CTRL` and the program interface outputs. Read the word of b through the direct read; bit b reads 1.
. Timeout cell. Cold reset and wait for sense done. Write `EFUSE_PROGRAM_REQ_TIMEOUT` with `program_req_timeout_enable` = 1 and `program_req_timeout_cycles` = T. Drive `efuse_shim_resp_hold_i` = 1. Write `EFUSE_PROGRAM_CTRL` with `program_enable` = 1, `efuse_data` = 1, `efuse_addr` = the bit address of c and `efuse_program_go` = 1. After m times T clocks, read `EFUSE_PROGRAM_CTRL` and log `program_busy`, `program_done` and `program_status`. Drive `efuse_shim_resp_hold_i` = 0.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-SENSE-STATUS
|In the injected sense, sense done rises within the bound, the sensed-shadow output `efuse_shadow_probe_o` and the frontdoor read of word w equal the reset value 0x0, every other word at the probe equals its staged value, and `EFUSE_INTERFACE_CTRL_STATUS.efuse_sense_done` reads 1 (`hw/sys/sep/doc/otp_fuse_controller.adoc`, section Fuse Sensing and Boot Sequencing; `hw/sys/sep/regs/gen/adoc/blocks/sep_efuse_map.adoc`, reset values; `hw/ip/efuse/regs/gen/adoc/efuse_interface_ctrl.adoc`). A DUT that stops the counter, stores the data of a status word, shifts the following words by one or hangs fails. Anchor: `efuse_shadow_probe_o`, `sep_fuse_sense_done_o` and the frontdoor readback. Control: the control sense of the same leaf loads word w with its staged value, which is non-zero, so a zero reading comes from the status bit and not from an unwritten word. Evidence: `CHK-SENSE-STATUS PASS seed=<n> word=<w> got_probe=0x0 got_read=0x0 staged=0x<v> others_equal=1 sense_done=1 status_sense_done=1 ctl_word=0x<v>`.
|CHK-PROG-LIFE
|With the program timeout disabled, `program_busy` reads 1 and `program_done` reads 0 over the window; after the release `program_done` reads 1, `program_status` reads 0, `program_busy` reads 0 and the direct read of the word of the programmed bit reads it set (`hw/ip/efuse/regs/gen/adoc/efuse_interface_ctrl.adoc`, `EFUSE_PROGRAM_CTRL`, `EFUSE_PROGRAM_REQ_TIMEOUT`; `hw/ip/efuse/doc/interface.adoc`, section Fuse Command Protocol). A DUT that completes without a response, loses the request or reports an error after a late response fails. Anchor: the program interface outputs on every clock, the frontdoor readback of `EFUSE_PROGRAM_CTRL` and the direct read of the programmed word. Control: the same program without a withheld response, in the same leaf from a cold reset, ends with done 1, status 0 and busy 0 and sets its bit at the direct read, so the done bit can read 1 and the direct read can show a burn. Evidence: `CHK-PROG-LIFE PASS seed=<n> bit_addr=<a> held_busy=1 held_done=0 rel_done=1 rel_status=0 rel_busy=0 bit_read=1 ctl_done=1 ctl_bit_read=1`.
|CHK-PROG-TIMEOUT
|A logged cell, not a graded check. The bits `program_busy`, `program_done` and `program_status` after the timeout window are logged as `INFO` and are not graded, because the specification does not state what a program request reports when its timeout fires. Evidence: `CHK-PROG-TIMEOUT INFO seed=<n> cycles=<c> held=<k>x busy=<0\|1> done=<0\|1> status=<0\|1>`.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: CHK-SENSE-STATUS and CHK-PROG-LIFE PASS. UVM_ERROR == 0. CHK-PROG-TIMEOUT logs one `INFO` line, is not counted in `checks=<k>`, and a leaf without that line fails.

*Scope limit*: The test does not claim the report of a program request whose timeout fires, the effect of a sense status on the lock words (words 0 to 2), the `LC_STATE` word (word 3), words 4 to 9 or the last word (word 255), the program with read back, or the response of a read request (see <<sep-vplan-phase3-blocked,Blocked features>>). Only the new cells are graded: the open owners `sep_efuse_sense_test`, `sep_efuse_image_test`, `sep_efuse_program_read_back_select_test` and `sep_efuse_illegal_state_fail_closed_test` keep the normal-response sense, the dropped program write and the read timeout.

'''''

[[sep-vplan-area-7]]
==== 7. Key Manager vault

[[sep_km_otbn_sideload_kat_test]]
===== 7.1 `sep_km_otbn_sideload_kat_test`

*Phase*: 1

*Area*: Key Manager vault

*Run mode*: `no_cpu`, real fuse sense, `+esrc_noise_force`

*Source Module*: `sep_km_otbn_sideload_kat_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip, KM path / golden

*Objective*: Proves the full key-distribution chain from the real entropy datapath to a real cryptographic consumer: the OpenTitan entropy stack seeds the Key Manager, the Key Manager's firmware accepts a known 384-bit key over its mailbox and sideloads it to OTBN over the dedicated key bus, and an OTBN program running on the real core reconstructs the key from its two shares and writes it to data memory, where the host reads it back and compares against the known value. Nothing on the key's own proof path is forced or read through a backdoor, so an exact data-memory match shows that the key physically traversed the sideload bus and was consumed. Key-bus isolation is proven by construction — only the Key Manager and OTBN are released from reset, with AES, HMAC and KMAC held parked for the whole transfer.

*Test Coverage*: Known-key Key Manager to OTBN sideload; DMEM reconstruct equals the key.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Stage a valid production eFuse image and run real fuse sense.
. Park OTBN, AES, HMAC and KMAC; bring up the entropy stack with strict golden checking.
. Release the Key Manager and wait for its firmware to report ready over the mailbox.
. Load a known 384-bit key with `CMD_KEY_LOAD`; require a non-zero handle.
. Release OTBN and wait for its post-reset secure wipe to reach idle.
. Issue `CMD_KEY_TRANSFER` for that handle with OTBN as destination.
. Load the key-dump program into instruction memory, execute it, poll to idle.
. Read the result and share dump out of data memory and compare.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-A
|`CMD_KEY_LOAD` accepts the known key and returns a non-zero handle.
|CHK-B
|`CMD_KEY_TRANSFER` succeeds with OTBN as destination.
|CHK-ISO
|Only the Key Manager and OTBN are out of reset during the transfer. AES, HMAC and KMAC are parked. The check is a mask over those bits, not an equality on the whole register. Adams Bridge stays released: the Key Manager firmware does not reach ready with that domain held, and the Adams Bridge sideload leaf is the isolation claim for that engine.
|CHK-C
|The OTBN program loads, executes to idle, and reports no error bits.
|CHK-F
|The two raw shares are non-trivial and distinct, neither equals the key, and their exclusive-or reconstructs it — so the masking is real, not degenerate.
|CHK0
|Key Manager firmware boots and reports ready over the mailbox.
|CHK-D/E
|Data memory holds the exact known 384-bit key, and the high result word padding is zero — the known-answer test itself.
|CHK1..CHK3
|The entropy stack matches its golden model bit-exactly at the decorrelator, compress and seed stages, with zero mismatches.
|CHK4
|Generated entropy blocks match the golden model. Generate segmentation is `sep_drbg_gen_segmentation_test`, not this `glen=32` budget.
|CHK5
|The Key Manager and OTBN both take real entropy beats from the shared bus. Alive-mode beat count; bit-exact per-sink compare is the small KM ROM tests (`sep_esrc_e2e_smoke_test`, `sep_drbg_gen_segmentation_test`), not `rom_main`.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

'''''

[[sep_km_aes_sideload_kat_test]]
===== 7.2 `sep_km_aes_sideload_kat_test`

*Phase*: 1

*Area*: Key Manager vault

*Run mode*: `no_cpu`, real fuse sense

*Source Module*: `sep_km_aes_sideload_kat_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip, KM path / golden

*Objective*: Proves that a known key loaded over the Key Manager mailbox and sideloaded to AES encrypts to the independent golden and decrypts back to the plaintext, and that the software-key path reaches the same golden.

*Test Coverage*: Known-key Key Manager to AES sideload known-answer.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Real-sense a production fuse image; park OTBN, KMAC and HMAC; leave AES released. The isolation check is a mask over those bits, not an equality on the whole register. Adams Bridge stays released so the Key Manager firmware can reach ready.
. Bring up real entropy; release the Key Manager and wait for firmware ready.
. Load the known 256-bit key for AES; require a non-zero handle.
. Encrypt the plaintext with a decoy software key; check against golden.
. Transfer the key to AES; read back the reset register for the isolation record.
. Read the public key registers and require zero, with a readable register in the same window as a positive control.
. Encrypt in sideload mode; decrypt the result in sideload mode.
. Load the known key through software and encrypt again, proving the engine reaches the same golden independently of the sideload route.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-A
|The key is staged and a non-zero handle returned.
|CHK-B
|The transfer to AES succeeds.
|CHK-ISO
|Only the Key Manager and AES are released during the transfer. OTBN, HMAC and KMAC are parked. The check is a mask over those bits, not an equality on the whole register. Adams Bridge stays released: the Key Manager firmware does not reach ready with that domain held, and the Adams Bridge sideload leaf is the isolation claim for that engine.
|CHK-NEG
|The decoy-key ciphertext matches its own golden, so the comparison baseline is sound.
|CHK-F
|The sideload ciphertext equals the independent golden for the known key.
|CHK-H
|The software-key path reaches the same golden ciphertext, so the engine is correct independently of the sideload route. `CHK-F` proves the delivered key bit-exactly. Guards that only relate two results already pinned to the same golden are not claimed here — they hold with the simulator off.
|CHK-RT
|Decrypting the sideload ciphertext recovers the original plaintext.
|CHK0
|Key Manager firmware boots on real entropy and reports ready over the mailbox.
|CHK1..CHK3
|The entropy stack matches its golden bit-exactly at the decorrelator, compress and seed stages.
|CHK5
|Both the Key Manager and AES draw real entropy beats. Alive-mode beat count; bit-exact per-sink compare is the small KM ROM tests, not `rom_main`.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Observation*: `PUB-OBSERVATION`. The test asserts that the public key registers read zero, but `aes.hjson` declares `KEY_SHARE0`/`KEY_SHARE1` `swaccess = wo`, so a frontdoor read returns zero whether a key was sideloaded, mirrored elsewhere, or never delivered, and that half cannot fail. It also asserts that a STATUS read over the same frontdoor is non-zero, which fails if the read path is dead. Software-unreadability here is a property of the register description, not a runtime behaviour this leaf can demonstrate. The key-protection evidence that *can* fail is CHK-F: the sideload key encrypts to the golden ciphertext.

'''''

[[sep_km_hmac_sideload_kat_test]]
===== 7.3 `sep_km_hmac_sideload_kat_test`

*Phase*: 1

*Area*: Key Manager vault

*Run mode*: `no_cpu`, real fuse sense

*Source Module*: `sep_km_hmac_sideload_kat_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip, KM path / golden

*Objective*: Proves that a known key loaded over the Key Manager mailbox and sideloaded to HMAC produces the independent HMAC-SHA256 golden, and that the digest differs from the golden of the decoy software key.

*Test Coverage*: Known-key Key Manager to HMAC sideload known-answer.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Bring up real entropy; boot the Key Manager; load the known key for HMAC.
. Transfer the key; read back the reset register for the isolation record.
. Read the public key registers and require zero.
. Write a seeded software decoy key to the public key registers. Each decoy word differs from the Key Manager key word at the same index.
. Configure keyed SHA-256; start; feed the message; process; read the digest.
. Require the digest to differ from the decoy golden, then to equal the golden of the Key Manager key under the pinned convention.
. Clear the done event and confirm it reads back clear.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-A
|The key is staged with a non-zero handle.
|CHK-B
|The transfer to HMAC succeeds.
|CHK-ISO
|Only the Key Manager and HMAC are released during the transfer. AES, KMAC and OTBN are parked. The check is a mask over those bits, not an equality on the whole register. Adams Bridge stays released: the Key Manager firmware does not reach ready with that domain held, and the Adams Bridge sideload leaf is the isolation claim for that engine.
|CHK-DECOY
|The digest differs from the independent HMAC-SHA256 golden of the software decoy key, under both the software-key and the sideload key byte conventions. The decoy is in the public key registers while the sideloaded key is valid, so the check fails if the engine uses the register key in place of the sideloaded key.
|CHK-MAC
|The digest equals the independent HMAC-SHA256 golden for the known key.
|CHK-RW1C
|The done event clears on write-one-to-clear.
|CHK0
|Key Manager firmware boots on real entropy and reports ready over the mailbox.
|CHK1..CHK3
|The entropy stack matches its golden bit-exactly at the decorrelator, compress and seed stages.
|CHK5
|The Key Manager draws real entropy beats from the shared bus while the key is staged: the `CHK5_km` beat count after the `CMD_KEY_TRANSFER` response is higher than the count taken just before `CMD_KEY_LOAD`. Alive-mode beat count; bit-exact per-sink compare is the small KM ROM tests, not `rom_main`.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Observation*: `PUB-OBSERVATION`. The test asserts that the public key registers read zero, but `hmac.hjson` declares `KEY` `swaccess = wo`, so a frontdoor read returns zero whether a key was sideloaded, mirrored elsewhere, or never delivered, and that half cannot fail. It also asserts that a STATUS read over the same frontdoor is non-zero, which fails if the read path is dead. Software-unreadability here is a property of the register description, not a runtime behaviour this leaf can demonstrate. The key-protection evidence that *can* fail is CHK-MAC: the sideload key produces the golden digest.

'''''

[[sep_km_kmac_sideload_kat_test]]
===== 7.4 `sep_km_kmac_sideload_kat_test`

*Phase*: 1

*Area*: Key Manager vault

*Run mode*: `no_cpu`, real fuse sense

*Source Module*: `sep_km_kmac_sideload_kat_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip, KM path / golden

*Objective*: Proves that a known key loaded over the Key Manager mailbox and sideloaded to KMAC produces the software-key digest, that this digest equals the independent KMAC256 golden, and that it differs from the decoy-key digest.

*Test Coverage*: Known-key Key Manager to KMAC sideload known-answer.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Real-sense a production image; park the engines; bring up real entropy.
. Boot the Key Manager; load the known key for KMAC.
. Release KMAC and run a decoy-key operation for the reference digest.
. Read back the reset register; transfer the key.
. Read the public key registers and require zero.
. Run the operation in sideload mode, then again with the known key in software.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-A
|The key is staged with a non-zero handle.
|CHK-B
|The transfer to KMAC succeeds.
|CHK-NEG
|The decoy-key digest is not all zero, so it is a real observation and CHK-SIDE does not compare against garbage. No KMAC golden is applied to this digest; it is an alive check, not a value check.
|CHK-ISO
|Only the Key Manager and KMAC are released during the transfer. AES, HMAC and OTBN are parked. The check is a mask over those bits, not an equality on the whole register. Adams Bridge stays released: the Key Manager firmware does not reach ready with that domain held, and the Adams Bridge sideload leaf is the isolation claim for that engine.
|CHK-SIDE
|The sideload digest differs from the decoy-key digest.
|CHK-MAC
|The sideload digest equals the software-key digest for the same known key.
|CHK-MAC-GOLDEN
|The software-key digest equals KMAC256(K, X, L=256, S="") from `env/sep_kmac_golden.py` (NIST SP 800-185). The sequence programs `PREFIX` as `encode_string("KMAC") \|\| encode_string("")` and ends the message with the 3-byte `right_encode(256)`, so a wrong encoding fails here and not only in a comparison of the engine with itself.
|CHK-ENT
|The engine draws real masking entropy. Alive-mode beat count. Bit-exact per-sink compare is the small KM ROM tests, not `rom_main`. The scoreboard reports it as `CHK5_km` / `CHK5_kmac`.
|CHK0
|Key Manager firmware boots on real entropy and reports ready over the mailbox.
|CHK1..CHK3
|The entropy stack matches its golden bit-exactly at the decorrelator, compress and seed stages.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Observation*: `PUB-OBSERVATION`. The test asserts that the public key registers read zero, but `kmac.hjson` declares `KEY_SHARE0`/`KEY_SHARE1` `swaccess = wo`, so a frontdoor read returns zero whether a key was sideloaded, mirrored elsewhere, or never delivered, and that half cannot fail. It also asserts that a STATUS read over the same frontdoor is non-zero, which fails if the read path is dead. Software-unreadability here is a property of the register description, not a runtime behaviour this leaf can demonstrate. The key-protection evidence that *can* fail is CHK-SIDE and CHK-MAC.

*Not claimed*: fail-closed `CFG.sideload=1` START with no valid Key Manager key
(`ErrKeyNotValid`), and a later software-key digest after `CMD.err_processed`
recovery. <<sep-vplan-scope>> lists them.

'''''

[[sep_km_isolate_termination_test]]
===== 7.5 `sep_km_isolate_termination_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: Key Manager vault

*Run mode*: `no_cpu`, `+skip_fuse_sense`, `+km_rom_hex=km_rom_iso.parhex`

*Source Module*: `sep_km_isolate_termination_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip, KM CPU image

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE — one directed path, three directed legs.

*Objective*: What a Key Manager master transaction receives when its own AXI-Lite path to a destination is isolated. The KM CPU reaches the `km_*` paths; the SEP host port reaches only the `host_*` paths. The KM CPU image stores to the same HMAC wrapper key address three times: clean while the path is open, an AXI error while `km_hmac` is isolated, clean again after release.

*Test Coverage*: `km_hmac` isolate termination, and that isolation does not wedge the KM path.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Dedicated `km_rom_iso` on the KM CPU bus, not `rom_main`. The image publishes a phase marker in KM SRAM word0 and blocks on an inbound mailbox word between legs, so the host controls when each leg runs.
. Each leg W1Cs `IRQ_STATUS` AXI_SLVERR and AXI_DECERR and requires them to read back clear before its store. The bits are sticky, so without that precondition a leg would also be satisfied by an earlier fault anywhere on the KM CPU bus.
. Leg A with HMAC released: the store completes with neither bit set.
. The host parks HMAC by read-modify-write of `SW_RESET_N`, preserving the Key Manager's own release bit, then waits for the `km_hmac` isolate-completion bit before releasing the image into leg B. A leg B that raced the coordinator would store into a still-open path.
. Leg B: the same store raises AXI_SLVERR or AXI_DECERR.
. The host releases HMAC; leg C repeats the store and requires it clean.

[NOTE]
====
Legs A and C cannot fail on their own — "no error" is also what a dead poll loop
reports — and are not offered as evidence by themselves. They are the controls
that make `CHK-KM-ISO-TERM` discriminating: the same instruction at the same
address in the same image, differing only in whether the host holds HMAC in
reset. Without them the error leg would be satisfied by an address that always
errors.
====

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |What it proves
|CHK-KM-ISO-PRECOND
|Every leg began with both AXI error bits clear, so the bit a leg reports belongs to that leg's store.
|CHK-KM-PATH-LIVE
|With HMAC released, the KM store to the HMAC key aperture completes with no AXI error — the path is open.
|CHK-KM-ISO-TERM
|With `km_hmac` isolated, the same store raises AXI_SLVERR or AXI_DECERR. It neither completes nor hangs.
|CHK-KM-ISO-REOPEN
|After release the same store is clean again, so isolation did not leave the KM path wedged.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Functional Coverage*: `sep_crypto_isolate_cg` in <<sep-fcov-isolate,SEP_FCOV>>. This leaf fills all three bins: it isolates a KM path, presents a KM master transaction to it, and reopens it. The bins are edges rather than states, because both isolate bits hold high for the whole reset window and a state bin would fill even on a run whose reset preceded the drain.

*Not claimed*: the other five KM destination paths (`km_otbn`, `km_aes`,
`km_kmac`, `km_abr`, `km_efuse`). They share the mechanism; only `km_hmac` is
demonstrated. The response code is graded as "an AXI error", not pinned to
SLVERR specifically, because the KM CSR status bit the image polls reports the
two codes as one field.

'''''

[[sep_km_ic_reset_release_test]]
===== 7.6 `sep_km_ic_reset_release_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: Key Manager vault

*Run mode*: `no_cpu`, `+skip_fuse_sense`, `+km_rom_hex=km_rom.parhex`. VCS only (`tools = ["vcs"]` in `testlists/km.toml`).

*Source Module*: `sep_km_ic_reset_release_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip, IC_RESET TDR (`jtag_ic_reset_reg` in `tb_top`), KM CPU image

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE -- one directed walk.

*Objective*: The Key Manager ROM request stays known across an IC_RESET override of the Key Manager. `hw/top/sep_ip_integration.sv` connects that request to the `prim_rom` chip select, and `prim_rom` asserts `noXOnCsI` on it on every clock (`vendor/lowRISC/opentitan/upstream/hw/ip/prim_generic/rtl/prim_rom.sv`). The port is `km_jtag_rst_n`, the TDO-end port of the SEP slice (`doc/integrator/src/smu.adoc`, SEP slice). The walk follows the IC_RESET field table in `hw/ip/jtag/jtag_ptap/doc/architecture.adoc`: stage `reset_control=0` with `reset_enable=1`, apply `reset_enable=0`, then release control and disable the override in separate Update-DR operations.

*Test Coverage*: stage, apply and release of the `km_jtag_rst_n` override while the KM fetches from its ROM; the request through a window that starts at the first fetch after the release.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Bring-up with the KM held in software reset. TRST the TDR, select it, and require the shifted-out word to be the TDR reset value.
. Release the KM through `SW_RESET_N`. The smoke image stores its SRAM marker and spins, so every loop turn is a ROM fetch.
. Stage and apply the override, one Update-DR each. Release `reset_control` while the override remains enabled, then disable the override in a second Update-DR. The host samples the KM ROM request counter after each operation.
. After the release, count the cycles to the first ROM request, then run a 4000-cycle fetch window.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |What it proves
|CHK-TDR-SELECT
|After TRST the TDR shifts out its reset value (every `reset_enable` and `reset_control` at 1). That the TDR word reaches the Key Manager reset is shown by CHK-TDR-APPLY.
|CHK-KM-LIVE
|The KM left software reset: the ROM request count rises and KM SRAM word0 holds the smoke marker.
|CHK-TDR-STAGE
|`reset_control=0` with `reset_enable=1` does not stop the KM: the count still rises.
|CHK-TDR-APPLY
|`reset_enable=0`, `reset_control=0` holds the KM: the count does not move over 64 cycles.
|CHK-TDR-RELEASE
|Releasing `reset_control` while the override remains enabled restarts the KM: a ROM request comes within 64 cycles of that Update-DR. Returning `reset_enable` to 1 in a separate Update-DR does not stop the requests. The log gives the latency and both counter values.
|CHK-KM-ROM-WINDOW
|At least 64 ROM requests in the 4000-cycle window after the release. `noXOnCsI` grades the request on every cycle of it; a firing prints `Error:` and the run fails.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes, and the VCS log has no `noXOnCsI` failure.

*Anti-vacuity*: `noXOnCsI` is compiled into the VCS `lsu_stub_all_live` model: `prim_assert.sv` defines `OCAH_OT_INC_ASSERT` for a flow that defines neither `VERILATOR` nor `SYNTHESIS`, and the SEP VCS build defines neither. The cocotb checkers cannot see X; they only prove the override reached the KM and that the KM fetches through the graded window.

*Not claimed*: any four-state property on Verilator, which is two-state and compiles no RTL assertions (see Known Limitations, "RTL assertions are backend-dependent"). The other seven SEP-slice ports. The KM ROM image is always loaded on this bench; a request that is X because the ROM array holds X is a bench condition and is not graded here.

'''''

[[sep_km_key_policy_vault_test]]
===== 7.7 `sep_km_key_policy_vault_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: Key Manager vault

*Run mode*: `no_cpu`, `+skip_fuse_sense`, `+km_rom_hex=km_rom_vault.parhex`

*Source Module*: `sep_km_key_policy_vault_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip, KM path / golden

*Randomization*: RANDCFG — slot, SRAM lock region (1..31) and the seal/free slot pair from the run seed, logged on the `km vault:` line; extent endpoints 0 and 63 and the lock/W1C sequence are directed.

*Objective*: The key/policy vault refuses what it should: a store to a locked SRAM region is dropped with the readback unchanged, the matching `SRAM_WRITE_LOCK_VIOLATION` bit sets, a store past the KPV register map raises `IRQ_STATUS` AXI_SLVERR only, and the status bit clears W1C. The seal walk is here too: the same erase must retire a sealed slot and free an unsealed one.

*Test Coverage*: Vault lock, seal, retire, erase, and SRAM write-lock on the KM CPU bus.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Bring up in `no_cpu`, release the KM CPU on the dedicated `km_rom_vault` image, and post the seeded config word (slot, SRAM region, seal slot, free slot) through the mailbox.
. The ROM stores key data to the seed slot before any lock and requires AXI SLVERR to stay clear. It sets `CTRL.lock_write` on slot 0, the seed slot and slot 63 (CHK-SLOT).
. The ROM repeats the same key-data store to the write-locked seed slot and requires AXI SLVERR (CHK-LOCKWR).
. The ROM reads the seed slot while it holds only `lock_write` and requires the stored word with AXI SLVERR clear. It sets `lock_use`, requires the same read to raise AXI SLVERR and return zero, and stores that data in KM SRAM word 1 (CHK-LOCKUSE).
. The ROM stores to `0x13108` and requires AXI SLVERR with AXI DECERR clear (CHK-EXTENT).
. The ROM write-locks the seeded SRAM region and stores to it. It requires the write dropped and `SRAM_WRITE_LOCK_VIOLATION` plus `IRQ_STATUS.SRAM_WRITE_LOCK_ERR` set, then W1C-clears both to 0 (CHK-DROP, CHK-VIOL, CHK-IRQ, CHK-W1C).
. The ROM seals the seal slot with one `CTRL` write, then erases it twice and requires the slot retired after each erase (CHK-SEAL, CHK-RETIRE, CHK-RETSTICK).
. The ROM preloads two key words in the free slot, marks it with `lock_write`, and erases it. It requires `CTRL` all clear and both words changed and different from each other (CHK-FREE, CHK-ERASEDATA).
. The ROM sets `IRQ_SET.DRBG_ERR_SET`, requires `IRQ_STATUS.DRBG_ERR`, then W1C-clears it (CHK-IRQSET).
. The host polls KM SRAM word 0 for the result magic and decodes each flag. It requires the echoed config fold to match (CHK-RANDCFG) and KM SRAM word 1 to read 0 through `km_sram_probe_o` (CHK-LOCKUSE).

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-SLOT
|`CTRL.lock_write` sticks on slots 0, the seed slot, and 63.
|CHK-LOCKWR
|A key-data write to a write-locked slot raises AXI SLVERR. This is the LOCK path, not the decode path CHK-EXTENT grades: a legal key-entry address on a locked slot. The sticky error bits are cleared and confirmed clean first, so an earlier fault cannot satisfy it. A control store comes first, to the same address before `lock_write` is set: with AXI_SLVERR cleared and confirmed clean, the store must land and AXI_SLVERR must stay clear for the same poll bound. Without the control, a design that answered SLVERR on every key-entry store would pass.
|CHK-LOCKUSE
|A key-data read of a `lock_use` slot raises SLVERR and returns zero data. Both halves are required: the refusal alone would not show the data path is also forced. The zero is graded twice so that X data cannot pass: the ROM takes its pass branch only on a known zero (the 4-state PicoRV32 does not take a branch on an X condition), and the ROM stores the read data in KM SRAM word 1, which the host reads through `km_sram_probe_o` with no unknown bits allowed and requires to be 0. A control read comes first, on the same slot while `CTRL` holds only `lock_write`: it must return the stored `0xA11CE000` with AXI_SLVERR clear. `lock_write` is write-1-set, so it stays set under the `lock_use` read, and without the control a design that refused reads on `lock_write` would pass. The control value also shows the refused CHK-LOCKWR write did not land.
|CHK-EXTENT
|Store to `0x13108` sets `IRQ_STATUS` AXI_SLVERR and leaves AXI_DECERR clear. `hw/ip/key_manager/regs/key_manager.rdl` (memory-map summary): an unmapped offset inside a window answers SLVERR.
|CHK-DROP
|Write to the locked SRAM region is dropped (readback unchanged).
|CHK-VIOL
|`SRAM_WRITE_LOCK_VIOLATION` reads EXACTLY the locked region's bit. Compared whole rather than masked, so a decoder that set every region's bit fails.
|CHK-IRQ
|`IRQ_STATUS.SRAM_WRITE_LOCK_ERR` is set and no ROM/SRAM parity or ROM-write error is raised alongside it.
|CHK-W1C
|Violation and IRQ bits read back 0 after W1C.
|CHK-SEAL
|One `CTRL` write on the seed's seal slot sets `seal` and raises `lock_write` with it, and `lock_use` and `erase` read 0. So the `lock_use` that CHK-RETIRE requires is set by the erase, not by the seal.
|CHK-RETIRE
|Erasing that sealed slot leaves it retired: `lock_write` held and `lock_use` gained.
|CHK-RETSTICK
|A SECOND erase of the retired slot leaves it retired. Retirement is stated to hold until warm reset, so it is graded as a sticky property rather than a one-shot transition.
|CHK-FREE
|An unsealed slot is marked with `lock_write`, and the erase clears `CTRL` entirely, so the slot is reusable. The mark matters: the reset value is already clear, so without it a no-op erase would pass. The contrast is the point: the same erase, one sealed and one not.
|CHK-ERASEDATA
|The erase overwrites the stored key words, not just the CTRL bookkeeping. Two words are preloaded before the slot is marked; after the erase both differ from the preload AND from each other, so a fill that never ran or that is stuck at one value fails.
|CHK-IRQSET
|`IRQ_SET.DRBG_ERR_SET` raises `IRQ_STATUS.DRBG_ERR`, and W1C clears it. This grades the software-inject path and the status plumbing ONLY -- it is not coverage of the DRBG fault source, and must not be recorded as such.
|CHK-RANDCFG
|The ROM echoes an eight-bit fold of the WHOLE config word, so all four seeded operands are proven received. Echoing only the slot would let a ROM that ignored the region or either seal-walk slot produce an identical result word.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope*: The test runs a dedicated `km_rom_vault` image on the KM CPU bus, not `rom_main`. The seal walk lives here rather than on the command set because no mailbox command seals a slot: over that surface an erase always frees, so the retire path has no vehicle there. PicoRV32 is RV32E (`x0`–`x15` only). The store at `0x13108` is past `KM_KPV_SIZE` and still inside the 8 KB KPV window. `km_csr.rdl` `SRAM_LOCK` defines 32 regions. The seeded region is never region 0, which holds the result words: `SRAM_LOCK` is write-1-set until warm reset, so a lock there would drop the final result store.

*Precondition*: the vault image must publish its result magic in KM SRAM word 0 within the cycle budget, and the graded word is re-read with no unknown bits. Every checker decodes that word, so a KM CPU that never ran stops the test with `CHK-LIVE FAIL` before any checker is graded. There is no `CHK-LIVE` PASS record.

*Aperture*: the vault is on the KM CPU bus, so the ROM evaluates these
contracts and the host reads one summary word from KM SRAM. The host observes a
result word, not the individual registers. What keeps it from being a firmware
self-report is the seeded configuration -- the slot, region and slot pair are
chosen by the host, and the result word carries a fold of the whole config word
the ROM received, so a firmware that reported success unconditionally would
still have to have consumed every one of the host's operands. Every pass/fail
decision in the ROM reaches its flag only through a taken branch on a known
compare result; the fall-through goes to the fail label. The 4-state PicoRV32
does not take a branch on an X condition, so an X register readback or an X
status bit leaves its flag clear and the named checker FAILs.

'''''

[[sep_km_command_set_rand_test]]
===== 7.8 `sep_km_command_set_rand_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: Key Manager vault

*Run mode*: `no_cpu`, real fuse-sense, `+esrc_noise_force`,
`+km_rom_hex=rom_main.rom.parhex`

*Source Module*: `sep_km_command_set_rand_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip, KM path / golden

*Randomization*: RANDCFG. Generate / transfer / revoke-or-shred /
illegal-to-error walk every seed, with both generated key sizes (8 and 12
words). The extra transfer dest (one of HMAC / KMAC / AES / OTBN), the
out-of-policy destination (outside `AES | xfer_dest`), and the undefined
command IDs come from the run seed. The
undefined IDs always include the five IDs immediately outside the defined
runs. One seed writes one classic dest cell plus the directed ABR cell; the
entry does not claim all four classic dests in one invocation.

*Objective*: the KM mailbox command set is this vehicle's surface — generate,
transfer, revoke-or-shred, illegal-to-error, version queries, OTP cold lock,
recoverable-fault ACK, and a directed ABR seed transfer. The sideload KATs prove
only that a consumer can consume a key; none of them exercises the command
interface that produces, moves and destroys one.

*Test Coverage*: Generate, transfer, revoke-or-shred, version, OTP lock, recoverable ACK, ABR dest, and illegal-to-error on the KM mailbox.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Stage a valid PROD OTP image and sense it for real: the KM firmware reads OTP
at boot. Park OTBN, KMAC and HMAC, leave AES released as the consume witness, so
a transferred key can only land where the test says it lands.
. Bring entropy up strict, then release the KM and wait for `RESP_KM_READY`.
. Query `CMD_HW_VER`, `CMD_ROM_VER` and `CMD_SRAM_VER`.
. Generate an 8-word key and a 12-word key for AES; check the handles and the
echoed argument fields.
. Load a known key with `DEST_VALID = AES | xfer_dest`, transfer it to AES, and
encrypt: the ciphertext is compared against an independent AES-256-ECB golden.
. Transfer the same handle to the seed-selected dest (`xfer_dest`) in a
dedicated mailbox beat. When that dest is not AES, release that engine for
the key-bus write (OTBN waits idle after release), then park it again.
Consume of HMAC / KMAC / OTBN stays on the sideload KATs.
. Load an 8-word seed and transfer it to dest ABR ML-DSA seed
(`0x10`). Every seed walks this cell. Consume of that seed is
`sep_km_abr_seed_sideload_test`.
. Transfer the same handle to an engine outside its permitted set.
. Shred the AES key, then load and transfer a second, distinct known key and
encrypt again.
. Transfer the generated handle to AES, revoke it, then transfer on it again.
. Revoke the reserved null handle; walk seeded undefined command IDs; send a
defined command with the wrong payload length. Probe with `CMD_STAT` after each
refusal, and once after the undefined-ID walk.
. Lock one identity OTP bit with `CMD_OTP_READ_LOCK_COLD`; refuse a reserved bit
and a zero-length payload.
. Pulse SEP mailbox `CTRL.FLUSH`, receive `RESP_RECOVERABLE_FAULT`, ACK it, and
prove `CMD_STAT` clears the latched bit. The following transfer and shred are
the key commands that must be accepted after the ACK.
. Transfer the second known key to AES again and encrypt one block, then shred
the AES key and start the same block: the engine must produce no output.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK0
|`rom_main` boots on real entropy and announces `RESP_KM_READY`. This is the bench build with the boot and unrecoverable-fault SRAM wipes compiled out; see Known Limitations, "KM application ROM wipe paths".
|CHK-HW-VER
|`CMD_HW_VER` returns success and `RETURN_ARG` equals the KMCSR VERSION word 1.0.0.
|CHK-ROM-VER
|`CMD_ROM_VER` returns success and the packed ROM 1.1.0 word: patch `[7:0]`, minor `[15:8]`, major `[23:16]`, `[31:24]` zero, per the return-argument layout in `hw/ip/key_manager/doc/firmware.adoc` (`km-cmd-rom-ver`). The KM firmware spec does not state a release number, so 1.1.0 is the DV-owned expected value. The test holds it as a constant and does not read it from the KM firmware headers, because the ROM builds its reply from those headers.
|CHK-SRAM-VER
|`CMD_SRAM_VER` returns the failure code: this image is ROM-only.
|CHK-GEN
|`CMD_KEY_GENERATE` returns success and a non-null handle, and its return argument echoes the requested size and destination mask.
|CHK-SAMPLER
|`CMD_KEY_GENERATE` raises the observed EDN->KM beat count on the DRBG scoreboard `CHK5_km` stream. The KMCSR sampler counters are not SEP-reachable.
|CHK-UNIQ
|A second generate, of the other key size, returns a different handle and echoes its size.
|CHK-XFER
|`CMD_KEY_TRANSFER` of a known loaded key succeeds and the AES ciphertext equals the independent golden.
|CHK-XFER-DEST
