Argument faults of CMD_KEY_GENERATE, CMD_KEY_LOAD and CMD_ABR_SK_TRANSFER, with a positive twin of each command and a DEST_VALID walk over the ABR bits 4 to 7. A wrap pass of more than 256 frames. The three transport causes on every seed, in drawn order (an overflowing partial frame, a SEP flush, a warm reset), with CMD_RECOV_ACK and no extra boot between them, each with the old counter value refused. The recovery handshake after `rx_buff_oflow` and after a SEP flush. The gate matrix (five admitted commands, ten gated commands) after each of the two fault sources, the validation order under the gate, the clear by CMD_RECOV_ACK and by a warm reset, and the gate-clear twin of each gated command. The 257-word frame with the separator on the last word. The mailbox transport: order under a full outbound FIFO, separator reads, `SEP_IRQ_ENABLE` subsets with a response waiting and after the drain, and a SEP flush with two unread responses. Error cases: the malformed frames and arguments, the 257 words with no separator, the wrong sequence number after a reset cause and the SEP flush are error injection (see the procedure). The test extends the open tests. `sep_km_command_set_rand_test` grades each single-fault code (header CRC, sequence, command ID, length, payload CRC), CMD_STAT after every rejection, and the SEP flush with its fault frame, the latched recov_fault, aggregator bit 31 and CMD_RECOV_ACK. `sep_km_wipe_reset_test` and `sep_km_handover_test` grade the restart at sequence 0 after a `SW_RESET_N` park. `sep_km_abr_mlkem_sideload_test` grades the refusal of CMD_ABR_SK_TRANSFER with no shared key pending. `sep_km_mailbox_protocol_rand_test` grades the inbound flush, the inbound_write_space_avail level and aggregator bit 14 with an enable, with the KM held. The frame receive check of every open KM host test grades the response sequence +1 and the per-word separator pattern. The Phase 3 test `sep_km_key_vault_alloc_rand_test` grades the echoed size field and DEST_VALID of every key command and the first handle of a boot, and the Phase 3 test `sep_km_mailbox_km_side_rand_test` grades the empty outbound FIFO after a SEP flush. Those cells run here as controls, only the new cells are graded, and each owner keeps the rest. The new cells are the fault-pair order, the forced values, the kind (d) code and its sequence update, the argument rejections, the wrap of both counters, the `rx_buff_oflow` leg, the refusal of the old counter value, the gate matrix, the validation order, the persistence of the output, the end-to-end recovery handshake, the outbound separator hold, the inbound separator, the order under a full FIFO, the outbound level source and the fault frame after an outbound flush with pending responses. Functional coverage: `sep_km_frame_validation_cg` (`cp_fv_first_fail`, `cp_fv_pair_order`, `cp_fv_seq`, `cp_km_seq_wrap`, `cp_fv_counter_reset`, `cp_fv_invalid_id_gap`, `cp_fv_plen`, `cp_fv_arg_kind`, `cp_fv_rx_buffer`, `cp_fv_reserved_bits`), `sep_km_cmd_reject_cg` (`cp_gate`, `cp_gate_cmd`, `cp_load_arg_order`), `sep_km_command_cg` (`cp_cmd_x_outcome`, `cp_ret_code`, `cp_resp_shape`, `cp_stat_recov`), `sep_km_mailbox_fault_cg` (`cp_mbf_flush`, `cp_mbf_raw_transport`), `sep_km_mailbox_transport_cg` (`cp_mbt_access`, `cp_mbt_occupancy`, `cp_mbt_separator`, `cp_mbt_irq_src_x_en`, `cp_mbt_irq_aggregate`, `cp_mbt_backpressure`), `sep_km_kmcsr_status_cg` (`cp_csr_recov_err`), `sep_km_fault_report_cg` (`cp_fr_code_encoding`, `cp_fr_rec_code`, `cp_fr_resp_pairing`, `cp_fr_recovery_handshake`) and `sep_km_secret_nonexposure_cg` (`cp_nx_permitted_channel`). The test also hits the Phase 1 groups `sep_km_host_cmd_cg` (`cp_cmd`), `sep_km_generate_cg` (`cp_generate`) and `sep_mailbox_pic_cg` (`cp_km_raise`, `cp_km_clear`), and adds no bin to them.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Stage and sense a PROD fuse image for real. Bring the entropy source up with noise forced. Leave every engine out of reset (the reset value of `SW_RESET_N` bits 6:1 is 1), because a key write that meets an engine held in reset ends in an AXI error (`hw/sys/sep/doc/reset_controller.adoc`, section "Isolation and Reset Sequencing"). Before the release, read `SEP_STATUS` and record `inbound_separator` (CHK-SEP-IN): the KM has read no inbound word since the cold reset, so the bit holds its reset value 0 (`km_mailbox_sep.adoc`, `SEP_STATUS`). Release the KM (`SW_RESET_N` bit 0) and wait for `RESP_KM_READY`. Every wait in this procedure is a bounded wait, and a timeout fails the leaf. Print `SEED seed=<S>` and a `DRAW` line for every drawn value.
. Set the models: r = 1 (the RESP_KM_READY frame carries response sequence 0) and e = 0. Every warm reset in this procedure sets both models again after its RESP_KM_READY.
. Define the host routines. The frame writer builds {HEADER_CRC8, PAYLOAD_LEN, COMMAND_ID, CMD_SEQ_NUM}, the payload words and, when PAYLOAD_LEN is above 0, PAYLOAD_CRC32. It writes `SEP_WRITE_SEPARATOR.set` = 1 before the last word and writes a word only while `SEP_STATUS.inbound_full` reads 0. The response reader pops the header, then PAYLOAD_LEN payload words and the CRC, each after a bounded wait on `SEP_IRQ_STATUS.outbound_read_data_avail`. The response check compares the header CRC-8, RESPONSE_ID 0x00, the echoed CMD_SEQ_NUM and COMMAND_ID, the return code in bits [7:0] with bits [31:8] equal to 0, the argument and the response sequence with r, and then increments r. A frame fault of every kind below first asserts that the wrong value differs from the right value.
. Frame-fault leg, kinds (a), (b) and (c). Error injection, point: the header of the command frame on `SEP_WRITE_DATA`; kind: (a) wrong HEADER_CRC8, (b) wrong CMD_SEQ_NUM, (c) COMMAND_ID outside the valid IDs; expected response: RESP_CMD -2 with the CRC-8/ROHC of the header as sent, -3 with the next expected sequence number, -4 with no argument. Send, with a drawn carrier from CMD_HW_VER, CMD_ROM_VER and CMD_RECOV_ACK, (a) a wrong HEADER_CRC8, with the forced values right XOR 0x01, right XOR 0x80 and 0x00 or 0xFF (whichever differs), (b) a wrong CMD_SEQ_NUM, with the forced values e+1, e-1 and 255 (whichever differs from e), and (c) a COMMAND_ID outside the 15 valid IDs, with the forced edges of each ID gap 0x05, 0x0F, 0x13, 0x21, 0x29 and 0xFF. Add drawn values of each kind. Check the code and argument of each response and update e: unchanged after (a) and (b), plus one after (c).
. Frame-fault leg, kind (d). Error injection, point: PAYLOAD_LEN of the command frame; kind: PAYLOAD_LEN contradicts the number of words on the wire; expected response: RESP_CMD -5. Send frames whose PAYLOAD_LEN differs from the number of words on the wire (the header CRC is right for the header as sent, the separator is on the last word), with a drawn wire length L in [1, 257] words (separator on the last word, non-zero payload words), a drawn PAYLOAD_LEN in [0, 255] with 1 + PAYLOAD_LEN + (1 if PAYLOAD_LEN is above 0, else 0) not equal to L, and a carrier from CMD_HW_VER, CMD_ROM_VER and CMD_RECOV_ACK (valid command IDs, so that the command ID check passes). Check the code -5. Log the argument. Update e: plus one.
. Frame-fault leg, kind (e). Error injection, point: PAYLOAD_LEN of a self-consistent frame; kind: PAYLOAD_LEN differs from the length that the command requires, the 257-word frame included; expected response: RESP_CMD -5 with the received payload length. Send self-consistent frames (right header CRC, right payload CRC-32C, non-zero payload words) whose PAYLOAD_LEN differs from the length that the command requires, with carriers CMD_HW_VER, CMD_ROM_VER and CMD_RECOV_ACK (required length 0). Use the forced PAYLOAD_LEN values 1, 2, 3, 254 and 255 and drawn values in [1, 255]. Check the code -5 and the argument (the received length). Update e: plus one. The frame with PAYLOAD_LEN 255 has 257 words with the separator on the last word.
. Frame-fault leg, kind (f). Error injection, point: PAYLOAD_CRC32 of the command frame; kind: one flipped bit in a byte lane; expected response: RESP_CMD -6 with the CRC-32C of the received payload. Send CMD_ENGINE_SHRED with mask 0x80 and a wrong PAYLOAD_CRC32: the forced values are the right CRC with one bit flipped in each of the four byte lanes, and drawn values. Check the code -6 and the argument (the CRC-32C of the received payload). Update e: plus one.
. Send the twin of each kind with every field right: CMD_HW_VER, CMD_ROM_VER and CMD_RECOV_ACK each return success, and CMD_ENGINE_SHRED with mask 0x80 returns success with argument 0x80. Update e.
. Pair leg. Error injection, point: two fields of one command frame; kind: two frame faults; expected response: RESP_CMD with the code and argument of the earlier check. For each of the 13 ordered pairs of kinds (a), (b), (c), (d), (f), (e), in this order of checks (the pairs (c, e) and (d, e) have no valid frame and are not drawn), send one frame with both faults. Use CMD_ENGINE_SHRED with mask 0x80 as the carrier of every pair that contains kind (f), with PAYLOAD_LEN other than 1 for the pair (f, e), and CMD_HW_VER otherwise. Check that the response is the code and argument of the earlier check. Update e by the rule of the earlier kind. Send the twin with only the later fault, check the later code and update e by the rule of the later kind.
. Send CMD_STAT and check that it succeeds with bit 0 of the status word equal to 0 and bits [31:1] equal to 0. Sample `KM-KPV` and `KM-VALID` after every rejection of the frame-fault leg, the pair leg and the argument leg below, and require every KPV CTRL bit and every key_valid bit to read 0.
. Argument leg, CMD_KEY_GENERATE. Error injection, point: REQ_SIZE or DEST_VALID of CMD_KEY_GENERATE; kind: reserved bit set or zero mask; expected response: RESP_CMD -7 with argument 0 for REQ_SIZE and argument 1 for DEST_VALID. Send frames with a self-consistent payload and one bad word: REQ_SIZE with bit 7 set, with bit 8 set, with bit 31 set and with a drawn value of 128 or more (legal DEST_VALID), and DEST_VALID equal to 0, equal to 0x100, equal to 0x8000_0001 and a drawn value with reserved bits set (legal REQ_SIZE). Check -7 with argument 0 for REQ_SIZE and argument 1 for DEST_VALID. Send one frame with both words bad and log the code and argument without grading them.
. Argument leg, CMD_KEY_LOAD. Error injection, point: PAYLOAD_LEN, KEY_SIZE and DEST_VALID of CMD_KEY_LOAD; kind: a fault of one validation check; expected response: RESP_CMD -7 with the word index of the first failing check. Send self-consistent frames, one first failure each, in the order of the validation table (`firmware.adoc`, section "0x26 - CMD_KEY_LOAD"): (1) PAYLOAD_LEN 0, 1 or 2, (2) a KEY_SIZE word with a reserved bit set, (3) a legal KEY_SIZE with PAYLOAD_LEN other than KEY_SIZE+3, (4) a DEST_VALID word with a reserved bit set, (5) DEST_VALID equal to 0. Check -7 with argument 0 for the checks 1 to 3 and argument 1 for the checks 4 and 5. Then send pairs of one fault of the checks 1 to 3 and one fault of the checks 4 and 5 in one frame (PAYLOAD_LEN 2 carries both words for the check 1). Check argument 0, and send the twin with only the later fault and check argument 1.
. Argument leg, CMD_ABR_SK_TRANSFER. Error injection, point: DEST_VALID and PAYLOAD_LEN of CMD_ABR_SK_TRANSFER; kind: zero or reserved-bit mask, wrong payload length; expected response: RESP_CMD -7 with argument 0 and -5 with the received payload length. With no shared key pending, send DEST_VALID equal to 0 and a drawn DEST_VALID with a reserved bit set. Check -7 with argument 0. Send frames with 0 and with 2 payload words and a right payload CRC. Check -5 with the received payload length.
. Positive twins. Send CMD_KEY_GENERATE with 5 words (REQ_SIZE field 4) and DEST_VALID 0x04, then CMD_KEY_LOAD with 4 words (KEY_SIZE field 3, non-zero words) and DEST_VALID 0xF0. Check success and that the first handle of the boot equals 1. After the CMD_KEY_GENERATE, sample `KM-KPV` (the control of CHK-NOCHG-VAULT). The echoed size field and mask are logged with `control=1`, because `sep_km_key_vault_alloc_rand_test` grades them. Send CMD_ABR_SK_TRANSFER with a legal DEST_VALID and no shared key pending: check -1 with no argument.
. DEST_VALID walk. Send 12 CMD_KEY_LOAD frames with 4 words each, with the masks 0x10, 0x20, 0x40, 0x80, 0xF0, 0xFF and six drawn masks in [1, 255] that each contain at least one of the bits 4 to 7. Check success. Each echoed mask is compared with the sent mask and logged with `control=1`, because `sep_km_key_vault_alloc_rand_test` grades the echo. Send CMD_STAT and check that it succeeds with bit 0 equal to 0.
. Wrap and transport-cause leg. Warm reset the KM through `SW_RESET_N` (bit 0 low, then high, the other bits 1) and wait for RESP_KM_READY. Send CMD_STAT with e = 0, then send CMD_STAT with sequence 0 at e = 1 and check -3 with argument 1 (control of the wrap check).
. Wrap pass: send 260 frames with carriers drawn from CMD_HW_VER, CMD_STAT and CMD_SRAM_VER, one response read for each frame, with no fault and no reset. The frame at e = 255 is followed by a frame with sequence 0. Check that the frame with sequence 0 succeeds and that the response after the response with sequence 255 has sequence 0.
. Transport-cause loop. This step and the next three run once for each of the three transport causes (`rx_buff_oflow`, SEP flush, warm reset), in drawn order. Before a cause that follows `rx_buff_oflow` or a SEP flush, send CMD_RECOV_ACK and check success, so that the gate of the previous cause is clear. The loop has no warm reset other than the warm-reset cause. Send p further frames, p drawn in [10, 40] for each cause, so that both counters hold a non-zero value. Record the command sequence number e_old that the next frame would carry.
. Apply the transport cause of the pass. Error injection, point: the KM mailbox FIFO, `SEP_CTRL` or `SW_RESET_N`; kind: an overflowing partial frame, a SEP flush or a warm reset; expected response: for the first two one RESP_RECOVERABLE_FAULT (-2 for `rx_buff_oflow`, -5 for the SEP flush) with sequence 0 and no paired RESP_CMD, for the warm reset RESP_KM_READY with sequence 0. For `rx_buff_oflow`: write 257 words with no separator (non-zero words, host writes only while `inbound_full` reads 0) and stop. For the SEP flush: read every response word, then write `SEP_CTRL.flush` = 1 with the KM idle (every command is answered) and read `SEP_CTRL` until the bit self-clears. For the warm reset: write `SW_RESET_N` bit 0 low and then high.
. For `rx_buff_oflow` and the SEP flush, read the fault frame (a bounded wait). For the warm reset, read RESP_KM_READY. The frame has response sequence 0. Set r = 1 and e = 0.
. Error injection, point: CMD_SEQ_NUM of the frame after the cause; kind: the old, non-zero counter value; expected response: RESP_CMD -3 with argument 0. Send CMD_STAT carrying the old sequence number e_old. Check -3 with argument 0, and that this response is the first frame after the fault frame or RESP_KM_READY. Then send CMD_STAT with sequence 0 and check success. On the `rx_buff_oflow` and flush causes the status word has bit 0 equal to 1.
. Gate-matrix leg. This step and the next seven run once for each of the two fault sources, in drawn order. Warm reset the KM, wait for RESP_KM_READY and set the models.
. Pre-fault window with the gate clear. Send CMD_KEY_GENERATE (DEST_VALID with bit 2), CMD_KEY_LOAD (DEST_VALID with bit 2), CMD_KEY_REVOKE of the generated key, CMD_KEY_TRANSFER of the loaded key to AES (bit 2), CMD_ENGINE_SHRED with mask 0x80 and CMD_OTP_READ_LOCK_COLD with mask 0x001. Check that each returns its success. After the CMD_KEY_TRANSFER to AES, sample `KM-VALID` (the control of CHK-NOCHG-VAULT). Then load one more key (8 words, DEST_VALID with bit 2) and keep its handle h. No command of the window uses h.
. Apply the fault source of the boot with the procedure of the transport-cause step (`rx_buff_oflow` or SEP flush), and read the fault frame. Check the code (-2 after `rx_buff_oflow`, -5 after the SEP flush, bits [31:8] all ones), response sequence 0 and the probe bit 31 equal to 1.
. Error injection, point: CMD_SEQ_NUM of the frame after the fault frame; kind: the old, non-zero counter value; expected response: RESP_CMD -3 with argument 0. Send CMD_STAT carrying the old sequence number e_old of the window. Check -3 with argument 0 and that this response is the first frame after the fault frame (no paired RESP_CMD). Send CMD_STAT with sequence 0: check success, bit 0 of the status word equal to 1, bits [31:1] equal to 0 and probe bit 31 equal to 1.
. Gate matrix. In drawn order, send CMD_HW_VER, CMD_ROM_VER, CMD_SRAM_VER, CMD_STAT and the ten gated commands with legal arguments: CMD_KEY_GENERATE, CMD_KEY_LOAD, CMD_KEY_REVOKE of h, CMD_KEY_TRANSFER of h to AES, CMD_ENGINE_SHRED with mask 0x80, CMD_OTP_READ_LOCK_COLD with mask 0x001, CMD_ABR_SK_TRANSFER, CMD_EXEC_ROM, CMD_SRAM_LOAD_EXEC with FW_WORDS 0 and CMD_SRAM_EXEC. Check -1 with no argument for each gated command, and the admitted results of the four admitted commands. Sample probe bit 31 after each admitted command.
. Validation first. Send CMD_KEY_TRANSFER of h to AES with a wrong header CRC and then with a wrong payload CRC, with the gate set. Check -2 and -6. Send the same frame with right CRCs and check -1.
. Wait the drawn host delay, then send CMD_RECOV_ACK. Check success with no argument. Send CMD_STAT and check bit 0 equal to 0 and probe bit 31 equal to 0.
. Gate-clear twins. Send each of the seven gated commands that can reach a handler again with the same arguments: CMD_KEY_GENERATE, CMD_KEY_LOAD, CMD_KEY_TRANSFER of h to AES, CMD_KEY_REVOKE of h (after the transfer, because the revoke destroys the handle), CMD_ENGINE_SHRED with mask 0x80, CMD_OTP_READ_LOCK_COLD with mask 0x001, and CMD_ABR_SK_TRANSFER. Check the success of the six and -1 with no argument for CMD_ABR_SK_TRANSFER (no shared key is pending).
. Handover-twin leg. This step and the next two run once for each of CMD_EXEC_ROM, CMD_SRAM_LOAD_EXEC and CMD_SRAM_EXEC, each in its own boot. Warm reset the KM, wait for RESP_KM_READY, apply a drawn fault source and read the fault frame. Send the command as the first frame (sequence 0) with the gate set: CMD_SRAM_LOAD_EXEC carries FW_WORDS 0. Check -1 with no argument.
. Warm reset the KM and wait for RESP_KM_READY. Send CMD_STAT and check bit 0 equal to 0 and probe bit 31 equal to 0.
. Send the same command as the first handover command of the epoch. Check success for CMD_EXEC_ROM, -7 with argument 0 for CMD_SRAM_LOAD_EXEC (FW_WORDS 0) and -7 with no argument for CMD_SRAM_EXEC (no stored image).
. Transport leg. Warm reset the KM and wait for RESP_KM_READY. Write `SEP_IRQ_ENABLE` with the first subset of the drawn order of the three non-empty subsets of bits [1:0]. Every write to `SEP_CTRL` in the leg keeps bit 2 clear.
. Pacing and stall, one pass with Q = 2 and one pass with a drawn Q in [3, 24]. Draw the carriers from CMD_STAT, CMD_HW_VER and invalid_len carriers (CMD_HW_VER with a drawn PAYLOAD_LEN in [1, 6], non-zero payload words, right CRCs). Every response has six words. The host writes the Q frames in order, starts a frame only when `SEP_STATUS.inbound_depth` plus the frame length is at most 16, writes with the drawn word gap, and reads no response. If the inbound limit stops it, it writes the frames that remain during the drain of the next step. In the pass with Q = 2, once both frames are written, it waits until `SEP_STATUS.outbound_depth` reads 12 (a bounded wait; a timeout fails the leaf). In a pass with a Q of 3 or more it waits until `SEP_STATUS.outbound_full` reads 1 (a bounded wait; a timeout fails the leaf), because three responses of six words exceed the 16-word FIFO. Then it waits the drawn read delay, reads `SEP_STATUS` and records `outbound_full`.
. Drain every response with the response reader, and write the frames that remain unsent with the same inbound limit and word gap between the response reads. After each word read `SEP_STATUS` and record `outbound_separator`. After the last word of each response read `SEP_STATUS` twice more. After the first word of the next response read it again. Check that the count of responses equals Q and that the echoed CMD_SEQ_NUM values are in command order.
. Inbound separator. The frame writer of the two steps above reads `SEP_WRITE_SEPARATOR` after the arm and again after the last word write of every frame. After the response of the last frame of the leg is read, wait until `SEP_STATUS.inbound_depth` reads 0 (a bounded wait), so that no inbound word is pending and the KM is idle, and then read `SEP_STATUS.inbound_separator` once. The other frames of the leg are not sampled, because the KM can be in the middle of a later frame.
. Level sources. For each of the three non-empty subsets of bits [1:0] (0x1, 0x2 and 0x3), in the drawn order, write `SEP_IRQ_ENABLE` with the subset and run this sequence: send one CMD_STAT and wait until `outbound_read_data_avail` reads 1. Read `SEP_IRQ_STATUS` and sample probe bit 14. Read the response. Read `SEP_IRQ_STATUS` and sample probe bit 14 again. Wait until `SEP_STATUS.inbound_depth` reads 0 and read `SEP_STATUS.inbound_separator` (the single-frame sample; taken in the first subset only). After the three subsets write `SEP_IRQ_ENABLE` = 0 and repeat the sequence with one more CMD_STAT (control: probe bit 14 reads 0 in both samples).
. Flush with traffic pending. Error injection, point: `SEP_CTRL.flush` with two responses waiting; kind: SEP flush; expected response: one RESP_RECOVERABLE_FAULT -5 with sequence 0. Send two CMD_STAT frames and read no response. Wait until `SEP_STATUS.outbound_depth` reads 12 (two responses of six words). Write `SEP_CTRL.flush` = 1 with the KM idle and read `SEP_CTRL` until the bit self-clears. Wait for the fault frame. Read the first word and check that its RESPONSE_ID is 0xFE, then read the outbound FIFO word by word until `SEP_STATUS.outbound_depth` reads 0. Check the code -5 and the response sequence 0 of the frame.
. Send CMD_STAT with sequence 0 and check bit 0 of the status word equal to 1. Send CMD_RECOV_ACK, then CMD_STAT, and check bit 0 equal to 0.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-FRAME
|For the forced values of kinds (a), (b) and (f) and for kind (e) the response is the RESP_CMD of the failing check with its argument: -2 with the CRC-8/ROHC of the header as sent, -3 with the next expected sequence number, -6 with the CRC-32C of the payload as sent, -5 with the received payload length (`hw/ip/key_manager/doc/firmware.adoc`, sections "0x00 - RESP_CMD" and "Incoming Message Handler"). For kind (d) only the code -5 is graded and the argument is logged (<<sep-vplan-phase3-blocked,Blocked features>>). The expected sequence number follows the sequence model: unchanged after -2 and -3, plus one after every other rejection, kind (d) included. A DUT that returns another code or argument, or that advances e after -2 or -3, or does not advance it after -4, -5 or -6, fails the next frame of the leg. An altered payload word turns the -5 of kind (e) into -6, so the code also shows that the payload words arrive unaltered. The CRC goldens follow the parameter tables of the specification and not the KM. Anchor: RESP_CMD readback and the sequence model. Control: each kind has a twin with every field right; its non-validation result is logged as `twin_code`. A random single fault of kinds (a), (b), (c), (e) and (f) logs `control=1` and cannot fail on its code. Evidence: `CHK-FRAME PASS seed=<n> kind=hdr_crc draw=forced code=-2 arg=0x<crc> golden=0x<crc> e=<e> e_after=<e> twin_code=0`, `CHK-FRAME PASS kind=len_self plen=254 code=-5 arg=254 e=<e> e_after=<e+1>` and `CHK-FRAME PASS kind=len_wire code=-5 arg_logged=<n> e=<e> e_after=<e+1>`.
|CHK-PAIR
|For each of the 13 ordered pairs the frame with two faults returns the code and argument of the earlier check in the order header CRC, sequence, command ID, frame length, payload CRC, dispatch length, and the twin with only the later fault returns the later code (`firmware.adoc`, section "Incoming Message Handler"). A DUT that answers the later check first fails the pair, and a DUT that returns the earlier code for the twin fails the twin. The model sets e after the pair frame and after the twin by the rule of CHK-FRAME. Anchor: RESP_CMD readback. Control: the twin. Evidence: `CHK-PAIR PASS seed=<n> first=seq second=len_self code=-3 arg=<e> twin_code=-5 pairs=13`.
|CHK-ARG
|A frame with one bad argument field returns invalid_arg (-7) with the payload word index that the specification states: 0 for REQ_SIZE and KEY_SIZE, 1 for DEST_VALID, 0 for the sole word of CMD_ABR_SK_TRANSFER. A CMD_ABR_SK_TRANSFER frame with 0 or 2 payload words returns invalid_len (-5) with the received length, because its length is fixed (`firmware.adoc`, sections "0x22 - CMD_KEY_GENERATE", "0x26 - CMD_KEY_LOAD", "0x27 - CMD_ABR_SK_TRANSFER", "Incoming Message Handler"). A DUT that returns another code or index fails. A CMD_ABR_SK_TRANSFER frame with a legal DEST_VALID and no shared key pending returns failure (-1) with no argument, so the -7 of the same command with a bad DEST_VALID comes from the argument check and not from the missing key (`firmware.adoc`, section "0x27 - CMD_ABR_SK_TRANSFER": the payload is validated first, then the pending key is looked up). A frame with both words of CMD_KEY_GENERATE bad logs its argument and is not graded, because the specification states no order for two bad words (<<sep-vplan-phase3-blocked,Blocked features>>). Anchor: RESP_CMD readback. Control: the positive twin, which differs from the rejected frame only in the bad field (CHK-TWIN). Evidence: `CHK-ARG PASS seed=<n> cmd=0x22 field=dest_valid val=0x100 code=-7 arg=1` and `CHK-ARG PASS cmd=0x27 legal_dest=0x04 no_key_code=-1 arg=none bad_dest_code=-7 bad_dest_arg=0`.
|CHK-ARG-PAIR
|A CMD_KEY_LOAD frame with one fault of the validation checks 1 to 3 and one fault of the checks 4 and 5 returns -7 with argument 0 (the earlier check), and the twin with only the later fault returns argument 1 (`firmware.adoc`, section "0x26 - CMD_KEY_LOAD", validation table). A DUT whose later check answers first returns argument 1 for the pair. Pairs within the checks 1 to 3 return argument 0 for every check, so they cannot show the order and are not drawn. Anchor: RESP_CMD readback. Control: the twin. Evidence: `CHK-ARG-PAIR PASS cmd=0x26 first=key_size second=dest_valid code=-7 arg=0 twin_arg=1`.
|CHK-NOCHG-HANDLE
|A rejected frame does not consume a handle: the first positive twin of the boot returns handle 1 (the first handle of a boot after a warm reset is graded in `sep_km_key_vault_alloc_rand_test`, and this cell grades that the rejections of this test consume none) (`firmware.adoc`, sections "Key Registry" and "Key Management": handles start at 1 and a handle is registered only after the arguments pass). A DUT that registers a handle before it validates returns a later number. No successful key command comes before the first positive twin in the boot. Anchor: RESP_CMD KEY_HANDLE. Control: the twin succeeds. Evidence: `CHK-NOCHG-HANDLE PASS rejected=<n> first_twin_handle=1`.
|CHK-NOCHG-VAULT
|A rejected frame sets no KPV CTRL bit and no key_valid bit (`hw/ip/key_manager/doc/architecture.adoc`, section "Host Coordination": a failed check leaves the KPV and the key registry unchanged). A DUT that writes the vault before it validates shows a CTRL bit or a key_valid bit. Anchor: `KM-KPV` and `KM-VALID`. Control on the same taps: after the CMD_KEY_GENERATE of the positive twins `KM-KPV` shows `lock_write` set in at least one CTRL entry (a load or a generate write-locks every slot of its span, `firmware.adoc`, section "Key Management"), and after the CMD_KEY_TRANSFER to AES of the pre-fault window of the gate-matrix leg `KM-VALID` shows the AES key_valid bit (bit 2) at 1. A missing bit fails CHK-NOCHG-VAULT. Evidence: `CHK-NOCHG-VAULT PASS seed=<n> rejected=<n> ctrl_nonzero=0 key_valid=0x00 control_ctrl_lock_write=1 control_aes_key_valid=1`.
|CHK-TWIN
|Control. Each positive twin and each frame of the DEST_VALID walk succeeds (`firmware.adoc`, sections "0x22 - CMD_KEY_GENERATE" and "0x26 - CMD_KEY_LOAD"), so every rejection above differs from a legal frame only in its fault. The echoed DEST_VALID, encoded size (words minus 1) and handle are logged and not graded: `sep_km_key_vault_alloc_rand_test` grades the echo of every key command. Anchor: RESP_CMD readback. Evidence: `CHK-TWIN PASS control=1 cmd=0x26 code=0 echo_size=3 echo_dest=0xF0 handle=2`.
|CHK-WRAP
|The command counter rolls over from 255 to 0: the frame with sequence 0 after the frame with sequence 255 is accepted. The response counter rolls over: the response after the response with sequence 255 has sequence 0 (`firmware.adoc`, section "Command Message Reference": both counters are 8-bit and wrap after 255). A DUT that stops at 255, or rejects the wrapped frame, fails. Anchor: the response header sequence and the acceptance of the frame with sequence 0. Evidence: `CHK-WRAP PASS cmd_e=255 sent=255 next=0 resp_prev=255 resp_next=0`.
|CHK-WRAP-CTRL
|Control. A frame with sequence 0 at e = 1 returns cmd_noseq (-3) with argument 1, so the acceptance of sequence 0 in CHK-WRAP comes from the wrap and not from a DUT that accepts any sequence number. Evidence: `CHK-WRAP-CTRL PASS control=1 e=1 sent=0 code=-3 arg=1`.
|CHK-CNT-RESET
|After `rx_buff_oflow`, a SEP flush and a warm reset both counters are 0 (`firmware.adoc`, section "Error Recovery": the first response after the reset has sequence zero and commands resume at sequence zero). The first response after the cause has sequence 0. The frame that carries the old, non-zero counter value is refused with -3 and argument 0, and the frame with sequence 0 is accepted. A DUT that keeps counting accepts the old value or returns a non-zero argument. The old-counter frame follows the fault frame and precedes CMD_RECOV_ACK on the `rx_buff_oflow` and flush causes. Anchor: the response header and RESP_CMD readback. Control: the counters hold a non-zero value before the cause. Evidence: `CHK-CNT-RESET PASS cause=rx_oflow first_resp_seq=0 old_seq_code=-3 arg=0 first_cmd_seq=0` and `CHK-CNT-RESET PASS cause=flush old_seq_code=-3 arg=0 first_resp_seq=0`, and the same line with `cause=warm_reset`.
|CHK-RECOVER
|After `rx_buff_oflow` and after a SEP flush exactly one RESP_RECOVERABLE_FAULT arrives with the code of its cause (-2 `rx_buff_oflow`, -5 `flushed_by_sep`, `firmware.adoc`, section "0xFE - RESP_RECOVERABLE_FAULT") and no paired RESP_CMD (the next frame answers the next command), the first response has sequence 0, CMD_STAT reports recov_fault 1, a gated command returns -1 with no argument, CMD_RECOV_ACK returns success with no argument, CMD_STAT then reports recov_fault 0, the gated command then succeeds, and probe bit 31 (`km_recoverable_err_o`) follows recov_fault: 1 after the fault, 0 after the acknowledge (`firmware.adoc`, section "Error Recovery"; `km_csr.adoc`, `RECOVERABLE_ERR`). A DUT that reports the code of the other cause, pairs a RESP_CMD with the fault, keeps the gate after the acknowledge, or leaves the output at the wrong level, fails. For the cause `rx_buff_oflow` every field is graded. For the cause SEP flush the CMD_STAT value, the CMD_RECOV_ACK result and probe bit 31 are logged with `control=1`, because `sep_km_command_set_rand_test` grades them, and the check grades the first sequence number, the absence of a paired RESP_CMD, the gated -1 and the gate-clear success. Anchor: response frames, CMD_STAT and probe bit 31. Control: the gate-clear success of the same command before the fault. Evidence: `CHK-RECOVER PASS cause=rx_oflow frames=1 code=-2 first_seq=0 stat=0x1 gated=-1 ack=0 stat_after=0x0 gated_after=0 pic31=1,0`.
|CHK-GATE
|Each of the gated commands CMD_EXEC_ROM, CMD_SRAM_LOAD_EXEC, CMD_SRAM_EXEC, CMD_KEY_GENERATE, CMD_KEY_REVOKE, CMD_KEY_TRANSFER, CMD_ENGINE_SHRED, CMD_KEY_LOAD and CMD_OTP_READ_LOCK_COLD returns failure (-1) with no argument while RECOVERABLE_ERR is set, and its handler does not act (`firmware.adoc`, section "Error Recovery"). A DUT that runs a handler returns the handler result. Controls: the gate-clear window before the fault gives each of the six key and OTP commands its success, the gate-clear twin after the acknowledge gives each its handler result, and each handover command returns its handler result as the first handover command of a boot (CMD_EXEC_ROM success, CMD_SRAM_LOAD_EXEC with FW_WORDS 0 -7 with argument 0, CMD_SRAM_EXEC with no stored image -7 with no argument). CMD_ABR_SK_TRANSFER with no pending key and CMD_SRAM_VER return -1 with no argument in both states, so they are logged as `witness=0` and are not gate witnesses. Anchor: RESP_CMD readback. Evidence: `CHK-GATE PASS seed=<n> source=rx_oflow cmd=0x22 code=-1 arg=none pre_fault_code=0 clear_code=0`.
|CHK-ADMIT
|While RECOVERABLE_ERR is set the four admitted commands other than CMD_RECOV_ACK return their normal result: CMD_HW_VER succeeds with the VERSION word 0x0001_0000 (`km_csr.adoc`, `VERSION` reset value), CMD_ROM_VER succeeds with bits [31:24] of the version word equal to 0, CMD_STAT succeeds with bit 0 equal to 1 and bits [31:1] equal to 0, and CMD_SRAM_VER returns failure with no argument (the ROM always returns failure, so it is logged as `witness=0`). A DUT that refuses an admitted command returns -1 for the first three. CMD_RECOV_ACK is the clear step (CHK-RECOVER). Anchor: RESP_CMD readback. Evidence: `CHK-ADMIT PASS cmd=0x03 code=0 stat=0x1` and `CHK-ADMIT PASS cmd=0x00 code=0 ver=0x00010000`.
|CHK-VALID-FIRST
|With the gate set a CMD_KEY_TRANSFER frame with a wrong header CRC returns -2 and one with a wrong payload CRC returns -6, and the same frame with right CRCs returns -1 (`firmware.adoc`, section "Error Recovery": normal frame validation still runs first). A DUT whose gate answers before the validation returns -1 for the faulty frames. Anchor: RESP_CMD readback. Control: the right frame returns -1. Evidence: `CHK-VALID-FIRST PASS cmd=0x24 hdr_crc_code=-2 payload_crc_code=-6 right_frame_code=-1`.
|CHK-PERSIST
|Probe bit 31 stays 1 after every admitted query between the fault and CMD_RECOV_ACK, whatever the host delay (`km_csr.adoc`, `RECOVERABLE_ERR`; `firmware.adoc`, section "Error Recovery": the gate holds until the acknowledge). A DUT whose output drops before the acknowledge fails. Anchor: probe bit 31 sampled after each admitted query. Control: the probe reads 1 after the fault frame and 0 after the acknowledge (CHK-RECOVER). Evidence: `CHK-PERSIST PASS samples=5 err_o=1 delay_clk=<d>`.
|CHK-RESET-CLR
|A warm reset clears RECOVERABLE_ERR: after the boot CMD_STAT reports bit 0 equal to 0 and probe bit 31 reads 0 (`hw/ip/key_manager/doc/architecture.adoc`, section "Reset Conditioning": `RECOVERABLE_ERR` is in the warm reset domain). A DUT that keeps the bit or the output fails. Anchor: CMD_STAT after the boot and probe bit 31. Control: both read 1 before the reset (CHK-RECOVER). Evidence: `CHK-RESET-CLR PASS stat=0x0 err_o=0`.
|CHK-257
|A frame of 257 words with the separator on the last word raises no transport fault and is answered as a command: CMD_HW_VER with PAYLOAD_LEN 255 returns invalid_len (-5) with argument 255 (`firmware.adoc`, section "Message Buffers": the receive buffer holds 257 words and `rx_buff_oflow` means a full buffer without a separator). The 257 words without a separator raise RESP_RECOVERABLE_FAULT -2 in the `rx_buff_oflow` boot of the gate-matrix leg. A DUT that raises the fault for the separated frame, or does not raise it for the unseparated one, fails. Anchor: the response frame. Control: the unseparated frame of the same leaf. Evidence: `CHK-257 PASS sep=1 fault=0 code=-5 arg=255 nosep_fault=-2`, printed after both frames ran.
|CHK-ORDER
|Every response arrives, once and in command order, when the host is slow and the outbound FIFO fills: the count equals the number of frames sent and the echoed CMD_SEQ_NUM values rise in command order (`hw/ip/key_manager/doc/architecture.adoc`, section "Mailbox Transport": the mailbox is an ordered FIFO; `hw/ip/key_manager/doc/firmware.adoc`, sections "Mailbox" and "Outgoing Message Handler": the TX path copies at most the free FIFO space and spin-waits, so a full outbound FIFO stalls the KM and no response is dropped). A DUT that drops, repeats or reorders a response fails. Anchor: `SEP_READ_DATA` and `SEP_STATUS.outbound_full`. Control: the pass with Q = 2 delivers every response with no `outbound_full`, and the pass with a Q of 3 or more waits until `outbound_full` reads 1 (a timeout fails the leaf) and records `outbound_full` = 1 before the drain, so the stall is real. The frames that the inbound limit holds back are written during the drain, and the count of responses equals Q. Evidence: `CHK-ORDER PASS q=12 gap=5 delay=2000 stalled=1 received=12 in_order=1`.
|CHK-SEP-OUT
|`SEP_STATUS.outbound_separator` is 1 after the last word of a response and 0 after every other word, and it does not clear on a status read: two further reads after the last word both read 1, and the read after the first word of the next response reads 0 (`km_mailbox_sep.adoc`, `SEP_STATUS`: 1 if the last word read had the separator, read-only, not sticky). A DUT that clears the bit on a read, or sets it on a body word, fails. Anchor: `SEP_STATUS`. Control: the 0 on the body words of the same responses (logged `control=1`). Evidence: `CHK-SEP-OUT PASS frames=12 last_reads=1,1 control_body_flag=0`.
|CHK-SEP-IN
|`SEP_STATUS.inbound_separator` reads 1 when the last word that the KM read from the inbound FIFO carried the separator (`km_mailbox_sep.adoc`, `SEP_STATUS`). The check samples it only with no inbound word pending and the KM idle: after the response of the last frame of the transport leg with `inbound_depth` 0, and after the response of the single CMD_STAT of the level step with `inbound_depth` 0. At those points the last word read is the last word of a frame, so a healthy DUT reads 1. Before the first KM release the bit reads its reset value 0, because the KM has read no inbound word, so the 1 at the sample points is a change. A DUT that never sets the bit, or holds it at 1, fails. Anchor: `SEP_STATUS`. Control: `SEP_WRITE_SEPARATOR.set` reads 1 after the arm and 0 after the write of the last word (the self-clear, logged `control=1`). Evidence: `CHK-SEP-IN PASS before_release=0 inbound_sep=1 single_frame_sep=1 inbound_depth=0 control_arm=1,0`.
|CHK-LEVEL
|`SEP_IRQ_STATUS.outbound_read_data_avail` is 1 while a response waits and 0 after the drain, and probe bit 14 equals (enable 0 AND outbound_read_data_avail) OR (enable 1 AND inbound_write_space_avail), with both levels read from `SEP_IRQ_STATUS` (`km_mailbox_sep.adoc`, `SEP_IRQ_STATUS` and `SEP_IRQ_ENABLE`; `hw/sys/sep/doc/interrupts.adoc`, source 15 on vector bit 14). With enable 1 set the bit stays 1 after the drain, because the inbound FIFO has space. A DUT whose source selection ignores an enable, or whose level does not follow the FIFO, fails. Anchor: `SEP_IRQ_STATUS` and probe bit 14. Control: with `SEP_IRQ_ENABLE` = 0 probe bit 14 reads 0 in both samples, and the inbound_write_space_avail level and the aggregator with an enable are logged `control=1`. Evidence: `CHK-LEVEL PASS en=0x1 data_avail=1 probe14=1 after_drain=0 model_after_drain=0`.
|CHK-FLUSH-PEND
|After a SEP flush with two unread responses (12 words) and the KM idle, the first frame that the host reads is RESP_RECOVERABLE_FAULT (RESPONSE_ID 0xFE) with code -5 and response sequence 0 (`firmware.adoc`, section "Error Recovery"). A DUT that sends the fault frame with another code or sequence number fails. The count of waiting words, the empty outbound FIFO after the flush (`outbound_depth` 0) and the absence of a stale word are logged with `control=1`, because `sep_km_mailbox_km_side_rand_test` grades the outbound FIFO after a SEP flush. Anchor: `SEP_READ_DATA`. Control: `outbound_depth` reads 12 before the flush. Evidence: `CHK-FLUSH-PEND PASS first_frame=0xFE code=-5 resp_seq=0 waiting_words=12 control_stale_words=0`.
|CHK-RESPSEQ
|Control. The response sequence number rises by one on every response frame, wrapping after 255, except where a reset cause restarts it at 0. Evidence: `CHK-RESPSEQ PASS control=1 n=<n> monotonic=1`.
|CHK-ALIVE
|Control. CMD_STAT succeeds with bit 0 of the status word equal to 0 after the rejections of a leg, so a rejection does not set RECOVERABLE_ERR. Evidence: `CHK-ALIVE PASS control=1 stat=0x00000000`.
|CHK-CARRIER
|Control. Each self-consistent frame whose PAYLOAD_LEN differs from the required length returns -5 with the received payload length, so the carriers of the transport leg and kind (e) are real invalid_len frames. Evidence: `CHK-CARRIER PASS control=1 carriers=<n> code=-5 len_match=<n>`.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope limit*: The reserved bits of CMD_KEY_REVOKE, CMD_KEY_TRANSFER and CMD_ENGINE_SHRED, and the argument of CMD_KEY_GENERATE with both words invalid, are not stated and are not graded (<<sep-vplan-phase3-blocked,Blocked features>>). Only the `rx_buff_oflow` and `flushed_by_sep` legs of the mailbox ISR are host reachable. The `mbox_overflow` (-3) and `mbox_underflow` (-4) faults and the ISR order of the three mailbox errors need an injected KM mailbox error and are in <<sep-vplan-phase3-noobs,Features with no observation point>>. A SEP flush while the KM is blocked in the middle of a response, and `SEP_IRQ_STATUS.flushed_by_km` after the boot flush, are not stated. The test grades only the cells listed under Test Coverage as new. The open tests named there keep the cells that they grade. CHK-NOCHG-VAULT grades the unchanged vault through `KM-KPV` and `KM-VALID`, and CHK-NOCHG-HANDLE grades it through the handle.

'''''

[[sep_km_key_vault_alloc_rand_test]]
===== 7.23 `sep_km_key_vault_alloc_rand_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: Key Manager vault

*Run mode*: `no_cpu` (`lsu_stub_all_live`), vehicle HOST (Key Manager image `rom_main`, real fuse sense, `+esrc_noise_force`, `+km_rom_hex=rom_main.rom.parhex`), 3 seeds, Verilator and VCS. Testlist: groups `all` and `cpu_stub`, `hw/sys/sep/dv/testlists/km.toml`.

*Source Module*: `sep_km_key_vault_alloc_rand_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (the CPU-LSU master is the SEP host) on the `km_mailbox_sep` window; a host frame builder and response decoder; an allocator model written from the specification: 64 slots of 16 words, ceil(words/16) consecutive slots for a key, handles 1 to 255 in order, with the live keys and their words taken from the host's own load and revoke list. The model never predicts a start slot, because the start slot is DRBG-selected. Probes and injects. Approved: `HOST-MBX` and `KM-ENTROPY` (`km_entropy_tvalid_o`, `km_entropy_tdata_o`, `km_entropy_tready_o`). `KM-KPV` (CHK-SPAN, CHK-REVOKE, CHK-FRAG) is an observation tap the test adds to the SEP_TB_ARCH observation-probe list. Injects: none.

*Randomization*: `SepSeededRng` from the run seed (RAND-REP). The draws are: the key sizes (the forced corners 1, 15, 16, 17, 31, 32, 33, 64, 127 and 128 words on every seed, plus 6 uniform sizes in [1, 128]), the command (every forced size runs with both CMD_KEY_LOAD and CMD_KEY_GENERATE), DEST_VALID in [1, 255] (forced to 0xFF on the first CMD_KEY_LOAD and the first CMD_KEY_GENERATE of the leaf, so that every destination bit runs with both commands on every seed), the key words (non-zero, the first 8 words pairwise different), the order of the sizes, the keys to revoke, and the load order of the capacity leg. The handle-space leg is directed because its threshold is the fixed handle width. The seed draws only the key word and DEST_VALID of each load in that leg. `reseed = 3` samples different sizes, words, masks and revoke orders.

*Objective*: A key of 1 to 128 words takes ceil(words/16) consecutive free slots inside the vault. A load write-locks every slot of the span. A revoke erases every slot of the span and frees it. Handles are allocated in order from 1 to 255, are never reused in a boot and never wrap, and a boot restores the handle space. With no free run or with no handle left a load returns failure with no argument and changes nothing. The allocator requires every slot of a run to be unassigned, so the slots of a live key never serve a second key. It starts at a DRBG-selected slot, wraps its search once and does not let a run cross the vault end. A generated key draws its words from the DRBG. Every response carries only a handle, a size and a mask. Sources: `hw/ip/key_manager/doc/firmware.adoc` (sections "0x22 - CMD_KEY_GENERATE", "0x23 - CMD_KEY_REVOKE", "0x26 - CMD_KEY_LOAD", "Key Registry", "Key Management"); `hw/ip/key_manager/doc/architecture.adoc` (sections "Key and Policy Vault (KPV)" and "DRBG Sampler": the sampler takes one 32-bit word for each full-strobe beat).

*Test Coverage*: Key sizes at the slot corners 1, 15, 16, 17, 31, 32, 33, 64, 127 and 128 words and drawn sizes, each by CMD_KEY_LOAD and by CMD_KEY_GENERATE (spans of 1, 2 and 8 slots). Revoke churn on live keys and a load after a revoke. Capacity: 64 loads of 16-word keys, a 65th load, one revoke followed by a 17-word load (two slots) and a 16-word load, and two revokes followed by a 2-slot request that is logged. Fragmentation: free slots that are never adjacent, a 2-slot request before and after an adjacent revoke. The handle space: 255 load-and-revoke cycles of a 1-word key, the 256th load, a CMD_KEY_GENERATE after it, a warm reset and one more load. Error cases: the full vault and the used-up handle space are legal resource conditions graded as failure with no argument. No error injection. The test extends `sep_km_command_set_rand_test`, which grades a generated key with a non-null handle and its echo, a second handle that differs from the first, CMD_KEY_REVOKE, and the refusal of the null handle. Those cells run here as controls. Only the new cells are graded, and the open owner keeps the rest. The new cells are the slot span of every key size, the capacity of the vault, the handle space to its end, the restore of the handle space, the DRBG draw of a generated key and the response contents. Functional coverage: `sep_km_cmd_reject_cg` (`cp_key_extent`, `cp_capacity`), `sep_km_kpv_slot_cg` (`cp_kpv_extent`), `sep_km_key_registry_cg` (`cp_reg_handle_value`, `cp_reg_handle_lifecycle`, `cp_reg_run_start`, `cp_reg_span`, `cp_reg_eligibility`, `cp_reg_revoke`, `cp_reg_gen_size`), `sep_km_secret_nonexposure_cg` (`cp_nx_resp_payload`) and `sep_km_sideload_delivery_cg` (`cp_sd_dest_x_cmd`). The test also hits the Phase 1 group `sep_km_generate_cg` (`cp_generate`) and adds no bin to it.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Stage and sense a PROD fuse image for real. Bring the entropy source up with noise forced. Release the KM (`SW_RESET_N` bit 0) and wait for `RESP_KM_READY`. Every wait in this procedure is a bounded wait, and a timeout fails the leaf. Print `SEED seed=<S>` and a `DRAW` line for every drawn value. Set the models: r = 1, e = 0, next handle 1, no live key. A frame writer and a response reader as in `sep_km_command_protocol_rand_test` build every frame and check every response frame.
. With `KM-KPV`, read the 64 KPV CTRL words and require every one to read 0.
. Define the entropy counter. It counts the clocks in which `km_entropy_tvalid_o` and `km_entropy_tready_o` are both high, from the write of the last word of a command to the read of its response.
. Size leg. Build the size list: the 10 forced sizes and 6 drawn sizes in [1, 128], in drawn order. For each size s run the next five steps.
. Revoke the oldest live generated keys until at most 7 slots are live. With at most 7 live slots and a request of at most 8 slots a free run always exists, because 64 slots minus at most 7 live slots leave at least 57 free slots in at most 8 gaps.
. Send CMD_KEY_LOAD of s words (non-zero words, drawn DEST_VALID). Read delta_load from the entropy counter. Check success, the echoed DEST_VALID, the echoed size field s-1 and the handle equal to the next handle. With `KM-KPV`, read the CTRL words and require that exactly ceil(s/16) CTRL entries gained `lock_write`, that they are consecutive slot indices, that no run crosses slot 63 and that no other CTRL bit is set. Record the run.
. Send CMD_KEY_REVOKE of that handle. Check success and the echoed handle. With `KM-KPV`, require that the CTRL of every slot of the run reads 0 and that the CTRL of every other live key is unchanged, and log the number of stored words of the whole KPV that change across the revoke.
. Send CMD_KEY_GENERATE of s words with the same DEST_VALID. Read delta_gen from the entropy counter. Check success, the echoed DEST_VALID, the echoed size field s-1 and the handle equal to the next handle. With `KM-KPV`, read the CTRL words and apply the same span check as for the load. The generated key stays live.
. Compare every response frame of the size leg, word for word, with the RESP_CMD frame that the model predicts (CHK-NOEXPOSE).
. Revoke churn. Send CMD_KEY_REVOKE for up to two drawn live generated keys. Check success and the echoed handle of each. With `KM-KPV`, apply the revoke check of step 7 to each. Then send CMD_KEY_REVOKE for the oldest live generated keys, one at a time, until at most 7 slots are live (the model counts the live slots), and apply the same checks to each. With at most 7 live slots a free run of 8 slots always exists, as in step 5. Send CMD_KEY_LOAD of a drawn size and check success and that its handle is the next unused number and not the handle of a revoked key.
. Capacity leg. Warm reset the KM through `SW_RESET_N` (bit 0 low, then high, the other bits 1) and wait for `RESP_KM_READY`. Set the models again.
. Send 64 CMD_KEY_LOAD frames of 16 words each (non-zero words, drawn DEST_VALID). Check success for each and the handles 1 to 64. The vault is full.
. Send a 65th CMD_KEY_LOAD of 16 words. Check -1 with no argument.
. Send CMD_KEY_REVOKE for one drawn live key and check success. Send CMD_KEY_LOAD of 17 words (two slots) and check -1 with no argument. Send CMD_KEY_LOAD of 16 words and check success with a handle above the last returned handle.
. Send CMD_KEY_REVOKE for two further drawn live keys. Send CMD_KEY_LOAD of 17 words. Log the response and the number of free slots of the model. Do not grade it, because the leaf does not know whether the two freed slots are adjacent.
. Fragmentation leg. Warm reset the KM, wait for `RESP_KM_READY` and send 64 CMD_KEY_LOAD frames of 16 words each. Record the slot of every handle from the CTRL change at its load (CHK-SPAN). Revoke two live keys whose slots are not adjacent, so that the longest free run is 1 slot. Send CMD_KEY_LOAD of 17 words and check -1 with no argument and CTRL unchanged. Revoke a live key whose slot is next to a free slot, so that a run of 2 free slots exists. Send CMD_KEY_LOAD of 17 words and check success.
. Handle-space leg. Warm reset the KM, wait for `RESP_KM_READY` and set the models. Repeat 255 times: send CMD_KEY_LOAD of a 1-word key (non-zero word, drawn DEST_VALID in [1, 255]) and check success and a handle equal to the loop index. Then send CMD_KEY_REVOKE of that handle and check success. The revoke keeps the vault free, so only the handle space is consumed.
. Send a 256th CMD_KEY_LOAD of 1 word and check -1 with no argument. Send CMD_KEY_GENERATE of 1 word and check -1. Log the argument of the CMD_KEY_GENERATE response and do not grade it.
. Warm reset the KM, wait for `RESP_KM_READY` and send CMD_KEY_LOAD of 1 word. Check success and the handle 1.
. For every size of the size leg compare delta_gen and delta_load: delta_gen minus delta_load must be at least s.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-HANDLE
|Handles are allocated in order from 1: every handle of a boot is above the previous one, none repeats, and none wraps. The 255 loads of the handle-space leg return the handles 1 to 255, each equal to its loop index. Every response echoes the sent size field and DEST_VALID (`hw/ip/key_manager/doc/firmware.adoc`, section "Key Registry": handles are 8-bit, allocated monotonically from 1 through 255, destroyed handles are not reused within a boot). A DUT that returns an out-of-order or repeated handle, wraps, or echoes another size or mask fails. Anchor: RESP_CMD KEY_HANDLE, size and mask. Control: every load before the first capacity failure succeeds. Evidence: `CHK-HANDLE PASS n=255 distinct=255 first=1 last=255 monotonic=1`, and `CHK-HANDLE PASS leg=size monotonic=1` for the other legs.
|CHK-CAP
|With 64 live 16-word keys the 65th load returns -1 with no argument. After one revoke a 17-word key (two slots) returns -1 with no argument, because only one slot is free, and a 16-word key succeeds (`firmware.adoc`, sections "0x26 - CMD_KEY_LOAD" and "Key Management": a key needs ceil(words/16) consecutive free slots; exhaustion returns failure with no argument before the vault changes). A DUT that loads the 65th key, loads the 17-word key into one slot or returns an argument fails. Anchor: RESP_CMD readback; the capacity of 64 slots and the slot count from the specification. Control: the 64 loads and the 16-word load after the revoke succeed. Evidence: `CHK-CAP PASS live=64 load65=-1 arg=none after_revoke_17w=-1 after_revoke_16w=0`.
|CHK-HANDLE-END
|After handle 255 the 256th CMD_KEY_LOAD returns -1 with no argument and a CMD_KEY_GENERATE returns failure, and after a warm reset the first handle is 1 (`firmware.adoc`, section "Key Registry": allocation fails instead of wrapping; boot initialization restores the handle space). The argument of the CMD_KEY_GENERATE failure is logged and not graded, because the specification states "no argument" for CMD_KEY_LOAD only. A DUT that wraps to a used handle, succeeds, or restarts at a handle other than 1 fails. Anchor: RESP_CMD. Control: the load with handle 255 succeeds and the next load fails in the same leaf, and the load after the warm reset succeeds. Evidence: `CHK-HANDLE-END PASS load_code=-1 load_arg=none gen_code=-1 gen_arg_logged=<a> first_after_boot=1`.
|CHK-ENT
|A generated key draws at least `s` more DRBG words than the equal-size load of the same leaf: delta_gen minus delta_load is at least s, where s is the word count (`firmware.adoc`, section "Key Management", Generate: the KM obtains `encoded_size + 1` words from the DRBG; the sampler takes one word for each full-strobe beat). A DUT that takes key words from the firmware PRNG shows a smaller difference. Anchor: the entropy handshake counters on `km_entropy_tvalid_o` and `km_entropy_tready_o`. Control: the load of the same size gives the baseline delta_load. Evidence: `CHK-ENT PASS words=33 delta_gen=41 delta_load=8 diff=33`.
|CHK-NOEXPOSE
|Every response frame of the size leg equals, in length and word for word, the RESP_CMD frame that the model predicts from the specification: the header word (HEADER_CRC8 from the CRC-8/ROHC golden, PAYLOAD_LEN 4, COMMAND_ID 0x00 and the response sequence number r), the four payload words (the source sequence number, the source command ID, return code 0, and the return argument: KEY_HANDLE, REQ_SIZE and DEST_VALID for CMD_KEY_LOAD and CMD_KEY_GENERATE, KEY_HANDLE for CMD_KEY_REVOKE, with every reserved bit 0) and PAYLOAD_CRC32 from the CRC-32C golden (`firmware.adoc`, sections "Command Message Reference", "0x00 - RESP_CMD", "0x22 - CMD_KEY_GENERATE", "0x23 - CMD_KEY_REVOKE", "0x26 - CMD_KEY_LOAD", "Outgoing Message Handler": the response carries only these fields). Every expected word comes from the stimulus and the handle model, so the expected frame holds no key word. A DUT that adds a word, puts a key word in place of a stated field, or sets a reserved bit fails. Anchor: `SEP_READ_DATA`, the response frames. Evidence: `CHK-NOEXPOSE PASS responses=<n> plen=4 frames_equal=<n>`.
|CHK-SPAN
|A key of s words takes exactly ceil(s/16) slots that gain `lock_write` and no other CTRL bit, the slots are consecutive and do not cross slot 63, and the slot count is 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 4, 8 and 8 for 1, 15, 16, 17, 31, 32, 33, 64, 127 and 128 words (`firmware.adoc`, section "Key Management"; `hw/ip/key_manager/doc/architecture.adoc`, section "Key and Policy Vault (KPV)"). A DUT that takes another slot count, a gap, or a run past slot 63 fails. CHK-SPAN also grades the 64 loads of the fragmentation leg: each load sets `lock_write` on exactly one slot and no other CTRL bit changes, and the 64 slots are pairwise different, so in every leaf one run starts at slot 0 and one run ends at slot 63. Anchor: `KM-KPV` CTRL and the RESP_CMD fields. Control: the keys already live keep their CTRL. Evidence: `CHK-SPAN PASS words=33 slots=3 run=21-23 ctrl_lock_write=3 other_ctrl=0 handle=4`, and `CHK-SPAN PASS leg=frag loads=64 one_slot_each=64 slots_distinct=64`.
|CHK-REVOKE
|A revoke clears the CTRL of every slot of the span and changes the CTRL of no other live key: the CTRL of every other live key keeps the value that it had before the revoke (`firmware.adoc`, section "Key Management", Revoke; `km_kpv.adoc`, `CTRL[64]`, `erase`). The CTRL bits are write-one-to-set, and with no reset or wipe in the step only an erase that completes on an unsealed slot clears them, so CTRL 0 on each slot of the span, which held `lock_write` after the load, shows that an erase of that slot completed. The stored words of the KPV are not graded, and this part is blocked: the specification does not state the physical KPV word position under the scrambler. The ROM enables and locks the KPV scrambler at boot (`firmware.adoc`, section "Boot Sequence"), so a logical key word sits at a keyed physical index that the scrambler text does not state, and the erase fill is not stated either (<<sep-vplan-phase3-blocked,Blocked features>>). The leaf logs the number of stored words of the whole KPV that change across the revoke (`OBS-REVOKE-FILL LOG`). That the revoked key is not used after the revoke is graded by `sep_km_key_transfer_rand_test` (CHK-XFER-REVOKED: a transfer of the revoked handle gives no key to the HMAC witness). A DUT that leaves a CTRL bit of the span set, or changes the CTRL of another live key, fails. Anchor: `KM-KPV` CTRL. Control: every slot of the span shows `lock_write` on the same tap after the load (CHK-SPAN), so CTRL 0 after the revoke is a change; a span slot with CTRL 0 before the revoke fails the check. Evidence: `CHK-REVOKE PASS handle=4 words=33 run=21-23 ctrl_before=lock_write ctrl_after=0 other_ctrl_same=1`, and `OBS-REVOKE-FILL LOG handle=4 kpv_words_changed=<n>`.
|CHK-FRAG
|With no two adjacent free slots a 2-slot load returns -1 with no argument and changes no CTRL bit, and after an adjacent revoke the 2-slot load succeeds (`firmware.adoc`, section "Key Management": a run needs consecutive eligible slots). A DUT that splits a key over two separate slots, or refuses after a free pair exists, fails. Anchor: RESP_CMD and `KM-KPV` CTRL. Control: the load after the adjacent revoke succeeds. Evidence: `CHK-FRAG PASS longest_free_run=1 fail=1 after_adjacent_revoke=ok`.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope limit*: Trailing words in the last slot of a short key are graded by `sep_km_kpv_rand_test`. A sealed, a retired or a read-locked slot never reaches the allocator, because no ROM flow and no host command sets seal or lock_use before an allocation (<<sep-vplan-phase3-noobs,Features with no observation point>>). A slot-write error during a load, which destroys the registration and keeps the earlier writes, needs an injected slot-write failure (<<sep-vplan-phase3-noobs,Features with no observation point>>). The DRBG-selected start slot has no net and is not graded. The two-revoke 2-slot request is logged only. The open test `sep_km_command_set_rand_test` keeps the cells listed under Test Coverage.

'''''

[[sep_km_key_transfer_rand_test]]
===== 7.24 `sep_km_key_transfer_rand_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: Key Manager vault

*Run mode*: `no_cpu` (`lsu_stub_all_live`), vehicle HOST (Key Manager image `rom_main`, real fuse sense, `+esrc_noise_force`, `+km_rom_hex=rom_main.rom.parhex`), every engine out of reset, 3 seeds, Verilator and VCS. Testlist: groups `all` and `cpu_stub`, `hw/sys/sep/dv/testlists/km.toml`.

*Source Module*: `sep_km_key_transfer_rand_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (the CPU-LSU master is the SEP host) on the `km_mailbox_sep` window and on the AES and HMAC register windows; a host frame builder and response decoder; the independent goldens `env/sep_aes_golden.py` and `env/sep_hmac_golden.py`. Probes and injects. Approved: `HOST-MBX`, `ENGINE-OUT` (the AES and HMAC witnesses) and `KM-ENTROPY` (`km_entropy_tvalid_o`, `km_entropy_tdata_o`, `km_entropy_tready_o`). `KM-BUS` (CHK-DELIV, CHK-ORDER, CHK-SHRED-ORDER) and `KM-VALID` (CHK-BANKS) are observation taps the test adds to the SEP_TB_ARCH observation-probe list. Injects: none. A witness engine is an engine whose output is checked against its independent golden. The HMAC witness shows a key (the digest equals the golden of the delivered key) or no key (the digest equals the golden of its software key, which the HMAC text states). The AES witness grades only a key (the output equals the golden of the delivered key): the output of an AES without a key is not stated, so no AES result grades the absence of a key. KMAC, OTBN and the ABR seeds have no witness.

*Randomization*: Two classes. RANDCFG for the delivery leg: `SepSeededRng` from the run seed draws the round order, one size class (below, equal to or above the width, equally likely) for each of KMAC, OTBN and the ABR ML-DSA seed, the size inside that class, and the key words (non-zero, the first 12 words pairwise different). AES and HMAC run every forced size on every seed, so their six (engine, size class) cells fill in each run. The nine cells of KMAC, OTBN and the ABR seed are drawn, one for each engine in a leaf, and fill on a merge of regressions: one regression of three seeds misses a given class of an engine with a probability of about 30 %. Legal ranges: size 1 to 128 words, engine bits 0 to 4. RAND-REP for the policy leg: the seed draws the policy P1, the policy P2, the permitted mask M, the mixed mask X, the outside mask Z, the second mask M2, the shred subset S and the order of the revoke and shred legs. Legal range: policy and masks 1 to 255, with P1 not equal to 0xFF, with bit 0 (the HMAC witness) set in P1, in M, in X and in S, with bit 2 (the AES witness) clear in S, and with the ABR bits 5 to 7 set in V and in S, so that the CMD_ENGINE_SHRED cells of the ABR seed and message banks run on every seed. `reseed = 3` samples different round orders, size classes, sizes, words, policies and masks. The forced sizes and the all-bank pass run on every seed.

*Objective*: A transfer writes one full-width share pair to each selected bank (8 words per share, 12 for OTBN), and the XOR of the shares is the key. A key longer than the share width delivers its leading words and is not rejected. A shorter key is padded with DRBG words. Every share word is written once, in a shuffled order interleaved across the two shares, and key_valid is written last and only for the selected banks. A shred writes key_valid 0 first. A transfer succeeds only when every requested destination is in the stored policy. Any disallowed destination refuses the whole request with no engine write. A multi-engine transfer writes every selected bank. A revoke leaves the engine copies. CMD_ENGINE_SHRED of a subset purges exactly that subset. Sources: `hw/sys/sep/doc/crypto.adoc` (section "Key Manager Key Delivery"); `hw/sys/sep/doc/hmac.adoc` and `hw/sys/sep/doc/aes.adoc` (the delivered-key rules); `hw/ip/key_manager/doc/architecture.adoc` (sections "Key Delivery", "Host Coordination"); `hw/ip/key_manager/doc/firmware.adoc` (sections "0x23 - CMD_KEY_REVOKE", "0x24 - CMD_KEY_TRANSFER", "0x25 - CMD_ENGINE_SHRED", "Firmware PRNG", "Register Access Shuffling", "Crypto Engine Drivers (HMAC / KMAC / AES / OTBN / Adams Bridge)", "Key Management"); `hw/ip/key_manager/regs/gen/adoc/abr_wrapper_key.adoc` (section "Adams Bridge Key Sideload Registers").

*Test Coverage*: The five engine classes (AES, HMAC, KMAC, OTBN, the ABR ML-DSA seed) at key sizes below, equal to and above the share width: the forced sizes 1, width-1, width, width+1, 16, 17 and 128 on the two witness engines on every seed, and one drawn size class for each of the other three engines. Repeated transfers of one key to one engine for the write order. A policy P1 of at least 3 bits and a policy P2, a permitted multi-engine mask inside P1, a mixed mask (some bits inside P1, some outside) and a mask fully outside P1. A revoke of the key, a transfer of the revoked handle and a transfer of a second key. A shred of one engine after the transfer, a proper-subset shred of the loaded banks that holds the ABR bits 5 to 7 on every seed, and an all-bank pass with the ABR bits 5 to 7 (its all-bank shred runs as a control). Error cases: a key length above the engine width (success with the leading `width` words, no rejection) and a mixed mask with bits outside the stored policy (failure with no argument, no engine write), both graded as error injection (see the procedure). The mask fully outside P1 is the cell that `sep_km_command_set_rand_test` grades, so it runs as a control. The test extends the open tests. `sep_km_sideload_share_walk_test` grades both shares, the four ABR seed blocks and the word order for key sizes equal to the share width on all eight destinations. `sep_km_command_set_rand_test` grades one transfer outside the stored policy, the refusal of a transfer of a revoked handle and a shred that reaches the key. Those cells run here as controls. Only the new cells are graded, and each open owner keeps the rest. The new cells are the size above the width, the DRBG word count of the padding below the width, the share write count, key_valid written last, the mixed-mask refusal, the multi-engine transfer, the copies kept after a revoke, the absence of a key for a revoked handle and the subset shred. Functional coverage: `sep_km_cmd_reject_cg` (`cp_transfer_policy`), `sep_km_secret_nonexposure_cg` (`cp_nx_resp_payload`) and `sep_km_sideload_delivery_cg` (`cp_sd_mask_shape`, `cp_sd_dest_x_cmd`, `cp_km_size_vs_width`, `cp_sd_write_order`, `cp_sd_shred_order`). The test also hits the Phase 1 group `sep_km_command_sideload_cg` (`cp_dest`) and adds no bin to it.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Stage and sense a PROD fuse image for real. Bring the entropy source up with noise forced. Leave every engine out of reset (the reset value of `SW_RESET_N` bits 6:1 is 1), because a key write that meets an engine held in reset ends in an AXI error (`hw/sys/sep/doc/reset_controller.adoc`, section "Isolation and Reset Sequencing"). Release the KM (`SW_RESET_N` bit 0) and wait for `RESP_KM_READY`. Every wait in this procedure is a bounded wait, and a timeout fails the leaf. Print `SEED seed=<S>` and a `DRAW` line for every drawn value. Set the models: r = 1 and e = 0. A frame writer and a response reader as in `sep_km_command_protocol_rand_test` build every frame and check every response frame.
. Define the AES witness. Program `CTRL_SHADOWED` with `sideload` = 1 and the 256-bit key length encoding, encrypt one fixed block in ECB mode, and wait for the output. The output equals the AES-256 golden of the delivered key words 0 to 7 (state `key`, graded). An output that differs from that golden, or no output within the bound W, is state `other`. The output of an AES that holds no key is not stated (see <<sep-vplan-phase3-blocked,Blocked features>>), so the leaf logs an `other` result as `OBS-AES-NOKEY` and never counts it as the pass of a refusal, a shred or a revoke: a wrong ciphertext is also `other`. Where a step expects no key, an AES result `key` fails the check of the step (a leaked key). After an `other` result write `SW_RESET_N` bit 2 low and then high and program the AES again, because an AES that waits for a key stays waiting. W is 8 times the duration of the first AES output of the leaf (8 is a test parameter; the duration is a control measured in the same leaf), so the positive result lies inside the window. The leaf prints `aes_first_clk` and `w_clk` with every `other` result. The first AES read of the leaf must produce an output; W does not apply to it, and a timeout of its bounded wait fails the leaf.
. Define the HMAC witness. Program the software key registers with a fixed 256-bit value that differs from every delivered key and set `CFG.key_length` to the 256-bit encoding. Hash one fixed message and wait for the digest (a bounded wait). The digest equals the HMAC golden of the delivered key words 0 to 7 as the engine takes them (the key is most-significant-bit justified in the 1024-bit field, `hw/sys/sep/doc/hmac.adoc`) (state `key`), or it equals the golden of the software key (state `nokey`, because the delivered key is used only while `KEY_CTRL.KEY_VALID` is set). Any other digest fails.
. Delivery leg. Build the round list: for AES and HMAC one round for each forced size (width 8: 1, 7, 8, 9, 16, 17, 128), and for each of KMAC, OTBN and the ABR ML-DSA seed one round in its drawn class (below, equal to or above the width; width 8, 12 for OTBN) with a drawn size in the class. Error injection, point: the key length of CMD_KEY_LOAD; kind: a key longer than the share width of the engine; expected response: success with the leading `width` words delivered and no rejection. Run the rounds in drawn order. Each round runs the next seven steps, the last of which ends with the revoke of the round's key.
. Send CMD_ENGINE_SHRED with mask 0xFF and check success with the echoed mask 0xFF. Reset and program the AES witness if it is waiting. With `KM-VALID`, require that every key_valid bit reads 0.
. Send CMD_KEY_LOAD of s words (non-zero words, the first `width` words pairwise different, trailing words above the width different from the leading words) with DEST_VALID equal to the bit of the engine E. Check success.
. Send CMD_KEY_TRANSFER of the handle to E. Read the entropy counter delta over the command. Check success and the echoed handle and mask. Record the writes of the five key-path ports with `KM-BUS`, and the key_valid bits with `KM-VALID`.
. For a witness engine read its witness. At or above the width the result is `key` and the output equals the golden of the leading `width` words. Below the width no golden exists, so the AES result and the HMAC digest are logged (`OBS-PAD-OUT`). With `KM-BUS`, require exactly 2 x width share-word writes to the window of E, each (share, word) address once, no write to another bank, and the last write equal to `KEY_CTRL.key_valid` = 1. With `KM-VALID`, require that the key_valid bit of E is the only bit set.
. Below the width only, for a witness engine: send CMD_ENGINE_SHRED for E (success, echoed mask), reset the AES if it is waiting, send CMD_KEY_TRANSFER of the same handle to E again, and read the witness. Log the two outputs, whether they are equal, and the DRBG words that `KM-ENTROPY` shows over each short transfer (`OBS-PAD-OUT`). Run the equal-width round of the same engine in the same leaf as the twin: two transfers of one equal-width key give equal outputs. Read delta_short from the short transfer and delta_equal from the equal-width transfer.
. At the width, for AES and for HMAC, repeat CMD_ENGINE_SHRED and CMD_KEY_TRANSFER of the same handle four times and read the witness after each transfer: the four outputs are equal. With `KM-BUS`, log the share-write address sequences of the four transfers (`OBS-ORDER`).
. Send CMD_ENGINE_SHRED for E and check success with the echoed mask. With `KM-BUS`, require that the first write is `KEY_CTRL.key_valid` = 0, followed by writes that cover every (share, word) address at least once, and that `KM-VALID` shows the bit of E clear. The number of passes is not graded. Then send CMD_KEY_REVOKE of the loaded handle and check success and the echoed handle (the engine copies stay, `firmware.adoc`, section "Key Management", Revoke). A round that ends this way leaves no live key, so the vault holds at most the key of the current round and a free run of 8 slots exists for every load of the leg.
. Policy leg. Warm reset the KM through `SW_RESET_N` (bit 0 low, then high, the other bits 1) and wait for `RESP_KM_READY`. Set the models. Draw P1 (at least 3 bits, not 0xFF, bit 0 set), P2, M (a subset of P1 with bit 0 and at least one more bit), X (bit 0, the HMAC witness, which P1 holds, and at least one bit outside P1), Z (a non-empty subset of the bits outside P1) and M2 (a subset of P2).
. Send CMD_ENGINE_SHRED with mask 0xFF and check success, and reset the AES if it is waiting. Send CMD_KEY_LOAD of K1 (8 words, DEST_VALID P1) and CMD_KEY_LOAD of K2 (8 words, DEST_VALID P2). Check success.
. Permitted transfer. Send CMD_KEY_TRANSFER of K1 to M. Check success and the echoed handle and mask M. Read the witnesses: each witness in M reads `key` with the golden of K1. Read the AES last if it is outside M, because an AES without a key can stay waiting. The HMAC witness is always in M. An AES witness outside M must not read `key` (a leaked key fails CHK-POLICY); its `other` result is logged as `OBS-AES-NOKEY` and is not part of the pass. With `KM-VALID`, require key_valid equal to M exactly.
. Whole-request refusal. Send CMD_ENGINE_SHRED with mask 0xFF and reset the AES. Error injection, point: the DEST_VALID mask of CMD_KEY_TRANSFER; kind: a mask with a bit outside the stored policy; expected response: RESP_CMD -1 with no argument and no engine write. Send CMD_KEY_TRANSFER of K1 with the mixed mask X and check -1 with no argument. Send CMD_KEY_TRANSFER of K1 with the mask Z and check -1 with no argument. Read the witnesses: the HMAC witness, which X always holds, reads `nokey` (graded). An AES witness in X or in Z must not read `key`, and its `other` result is logged as `OBS-AES-NOKEY`. With `KM-VALID`, require key_valid equal to 0x00.
. Revoke leg and shred leg, in drawn order. Revoke leg: send CMD_ENGINE_SHRED with mask 0xFF and reset the AES, then send CMD_KEY_TRANSFER of K1 to M and read the witnesses (`key`). Send CMD_KEY_REVOKE of K1 and check success and the echoed handle. Read the witnesses again and check that each witness in M still reads `key`. Send CMD_ENGINE_SHRED with mask 0xFF, reset the AES, and send CMD_KEY_TRANSFER of the revoked handle K1 to bit 0 and a drawn subset of the other bits of P1, so that the HMAC witness is in the mask. Log the response code. Read the witnesses: the HMAC witness reads `nokey`, and the AES result is logged with `control=1`. Send CMD_KEY_TRANSFER of K2 to M2 and check success, the echoed mask and the witnesses of M2 (`key` with the golden of K2).
. Shred leg. Send CMD_KEY_LOAD of K3 (8 words, DEST_VALID 0xFF). Send CMD_ENGINE_SHRED with mask 0xFF and reset the AES. Send CMD_KEY_TRANSFER of K3 to V, a mask that holds both witness bits 0 and 2, the ABR bits 5 to 7 and a drawn subset of the bits 1, 3 and 4. Check success and the echoed mask V, and read the HMAC witness: `key` with the golden of K3 (the pre-state of the shred; any other result fails CHK-SHRED-SUBSET). Draw S as a proper subset of V that holds the HMAC witness bit 0 and the ABR bits 5 to 7, not the AES witness bit 2, and a drawn subset of the other bits of V. Send CMD_ENGINE_SHRED with mask S and check success with the echoed mask S. Read the witnesses: the HMAC witness (in S) reads `nokey` and the AES witness (outside S) reads `key`. With `KM-VALID`, require key_valid equal to V with the bits of S cleared.
. All-bank pass. Send CMD_ENGINE_SHRED with mask 0xFF and reset the AES. Send CMD_KEY_TRANSFER of K3 to the mask 0xFF and check success and the echoed mask 0xFF. Read the witnesses (`key`). Send CMD_ENGINE_SHRED with mask 0xFF, check the echoed mask 0xFF and read the witnesses (the HMAC witness reads `nokey`; the AES result is logged). The all-bank echo and the witness reads of this step are logged with `control=1`, because `sep_km_command_set_rand_test` and `sep_km_sideload_share_walk_test` grade the all-bank shred. With `KM-VALID`, require key_valid equal to 0xFF after the transfer and 0x00 after the shred.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-GOLD
|At and above the share width a witness engine that holds the delivered key produces the output of its independent golden over the leading `width` words: the AES block equals the AES-256 golden and the HMAC digest equals the HMAC golden (`hw/sys/sep/doc/crypto.adoc`, section "Key Manager Key Delivery": word index N carries value bits [32N+31:32N] and the XOR of the shares is the value; `hw/ip/key_manager/doc/firmware.adoc`, section "Crypto Engine Drivers (HMAC / KMAC / AES / OTBN / Adams Bridge)": a longer key delivers its leading words and is not rejected). The trailing words above the width differ from the leading words, so a DUT that uses another word set fails. A DUT that rejects the longer key, or delivers the wrong words, fails. Anchor: `ENGINE-OUT`. Control: the equal-width round gives the same golden and is graded by the open sideload tests. Evidence: `CHK-GOLD PASS eng=hmac size=12 leading=8 digest_match=1`.
|CHK-PAD
|Below the width the key is padded with DRBG words (`firmware.adoc`, section "Crypto Engine Drivers (HMAC / KMAC / AES / OTBN / Adams Bridge)": short keys are padded with DRBG words). The short transfer draws at least `width - size` more DRBG words than the equal-width transfer of the same engine, and two transfers of an equal-width key give equal outputs. The specification does not state which key-word positions the pad words fill, or where they lie in the DRBG stream relative to the mask words (<<sep-vplan-phase3-blocked,Blocked features>>), so no golden exists for a padded output: the leaf logs the two outputs of the short key, whether they are equal, and the DRBG words that `KM-ENTROPY` shows over each short transfer (`OBS-PAD-OUT LOG`), and grades no output below the width. A DUT that pads from the firmware PRNG draws fewer DRBG words and fails. A DUT that draws the DRBG words and then pads with zero or with a fixed pattern is not claimed. Anchor: the handshake counters on `km_entropy_tvalid_o` and `km_entropy_tready_o`; `ENGINE-OUT` for the twin. Control: the equal-width twin (`twin_equal`); the PASS line is printed after the equal-width round of the same engine ran. Evidence: `CHK-PAD PASS eng=aes size=1 pad_words=7 twin_equal=1 delta_short=18 delta_equal=11 diff=7 min=7`, where `min` is `width - size`, and `OBS-PAD-OUT LOG eng=aes size=1 out_equal=<0/1>`.
|CHK-POLICY
|A permitted transfer returns success with the requested handle and mask in the response, and every witness in the mask holds the key of the transferred handle (`firmware.adoc`, section "0x24 - CMD_KEY_TRANSFER": the response carries the key handle and the engines to which the key is transferred). The delivery leg grades the same echo for every engine, KMAC, OTBN and the ABR seeds included. An AES witness outside the mask that reads `key` fails; its `other` result is logged as `OBS-AES-NOKEY` and is not part of the pass. A DUT that returns another mask, or leaves a witness in the mask without the key, fails. Anchor: RESP_CMD echo and `ENGINE-OUT`. Control: every witness is shredded before the transfer, so a `key` result comes from this transfer. Evidence: `CHK-POLICY PASS p1=0x5D m=0x15 echo=0x15 witness_aes=golden witness_hmac=golden`.
|CHK-REFUSE
