*Randomization*: `SepSeededRng` from the run seed: the keys kA and kB (non-zero, every byte of kA differs from the same byte of kB), 8 word addresses in [0x8400, 0xFFFC] (one adjacent pair, one pair at the same offset in two 1 KiB regions), 8 plaintexts (non-zero, one pair of equal plaintexts at two of the addresses, the pair stored first), 64 further distinct word addresses in the same range (disjoint from the 8) with 64 distinct non-zero words, and, for the lock-without-enable leg, 2 word addresses in the same range (disjoint from the others) with 2 non-zero words. `reseed = 3` samples different keys, addresses and words. The plan shape (the key sequence, the 8-word and 64-word sets and the boot sequence) is the same on every seed. The stream is not a CSPRNG, and no drawn key is used outside the simulation.

*Objective*: With the SRAM scrambler enabled, the stored form of a word depends on the key and on the address. The same plaintext at the same address stores a different word under another key, and the old key reads its data back after a key change. Two distinct logical addresses do not share a physical row, because the read path scrambles the address and does not descramble it. Once the lock is set with the enable at 1, a write of the key and a write of the enable are ignored, a write of 0 to the lock leaves it set, SCRAMBLER_KEY reads 0, and the scrambler stays on. A lock set with the enable at 0 forces the scrambler into the enabled state. The key, the enable, the lock and the SRAM contents survive a warm reset. A cold reset clears the enable and the lock, and a key write after it lands. The outbound mailbox FIFO holds 16 words and drops a word that is written to a full FIFO, so the image reports in groups that the host drains. Spec: `hw/ip/scrambler/doc/architecture.adoc`, sections "Address Tweaking", "Address Scrambling", "Integration in the Key Manager"; `hw/ip/key_manager/doc/architecture.adoc`, sections "Parameters", "Reset Conditioning", "Key Manager Control and Status Registers (KMCSR)", "ROM and SRAM Error Detection", "ROM Warm-Persistent SRAM Region", "Mailbox Transport"; `hw/ip/key_manager/regs/gen/adoc/km_csr.adoc`, sections "SCRAMBLER_KEY", "SCRAMBLER_CTRL"; `hw/ip/key_manager/regs/gen/adoc/km_mailbox_km.adoc`, section "KM_STATUS".

*Test Coverage*: This test extends the open test `sep_km_mem_smoke_test`. That test grades the round trip under one key and the stored form that differs from the plaintext, including the array word at each kept row. Those cells run here as controls. Only the new cells are graded here, and the open owner keeps the rest. This test owns the SRAM scrambler lock.

* Key dependence: one plaintext stored at one address under kA and under kB; 8 words stored under kA, read under kA (control), under kB (logged), and under kA again.
* Address dependence: two addresses with the same plaintext store different words.
* One-to-one address map: 64 distinct words at 64 distinct logical addresses read back under kA, and 64 physical rows change.
* The lock: set with the enable at 1 in one write; then a key write, an enable write and a write of 0 to the lock; SCRAMBLER_KEY reads 0 while locked and reads the written value before the lock (control).
* The lock set with the enable at 0: in a later cold boot a store with the lock clear and the enable 0 is not a scrambled write (control), and the same kind of store after the lock is written with the enable 0 counts as a scrambled write.
* The reset domains: a warm reset with the lock set (enable, lock and the stored words kept) and, in a later boot, a cold reset (enable and lock cleared, a key write lands).

Error cases: the writes after the lock are legal accesses that the register description defines as ignored. The test has no error injection.

Functional coverage: `sep_km_memory_boot_cg` (`cp_mem_iface_req`, `cp_mem_scr_key_access`, `cp_mem_scr_ctrl`, `cp_km_scr_key`).

*Test Procedure*:

The image reports every value through the KM mailbox write register. It performs no SRAM store other than the drawn stores, because a scrambled store can reach any row of the array and a result store at a logical row could overwrite a stored word that is still in use. The image writes one message per group, with at most 16 words in a group, and the separator on the last word. After a group, the image waits with a bounded poll of KM_STATUS.outbound_depth until the depth is 0, so the outbound FIFO never holds more than one group. A timeout of the poll stops the image. The host reads each group through `HOST-MBX` when it appears, with a bounded wait; a timeout of the wait fails the checker that needs the group.

[arabic]
. Draw the configuration from the seed. The prestage step writes it into the parameter block of IMG-SCR (`HK-IMG-PARAM`), and the image load preloads the image at t=0.
. Release the KM. The host posts the phase word of boot 1 through the KM inbound mailbox (`SEP_WRITE_DATA` with the separator), and the image reads it with a bounded poll of the KM-side inbound status (a timeout stops the image). Every later boot reads its phase word the same way. Boot 1: the image writes kA to SCRAMBLER_KEY and sets SCRAMBLER_CTRL to enable 1 with the lock clear.
. The image stores the equal-plaintext pair P at its two addresses a1 and a2, writes kB to SCRAMBLER_KEY, stores P at a1 again, writes kA to SCRAMBLER_KEY, and then stores the 8 plaintexts to the 8 addresses in the drawn order, the pair among them, so that every row that a later kA read uses holds its kA store. The image performs no other SRAM write while the enable is 1, so the first four scrambled writes are the pair, the kB store and the first of the 8 stores. The host reads the four kept writes through `KM-SRAM-MON`.
. The image reads the 8 words under kA with consecutive loads and reports them (group of 8). The host drains the group.
. The image writes kB to SCRAMBLER_KEY, reads the 8 words and reports them (group of 8). The SRAM parity status that a read under kB sets is not graded. The image leaves IRQ_ENABLE at its reset value. The host drains the group.
. The image writes kA to SCRAMBLER_KEY, reads the 8 words and reports them (group of 8). The host drains the group.
. With the key at kA, the image clears the enable, reads SCRAMBLER_CTRL and the 8 words, reports them (group of 9), and sets the enable again. This is the control for the enable write after the lock. The host drains the group.
. The image reports a ready message of one word and waits until the host has read it. Before the host reads the ready message, it takes the first snapshot of the `KM-SRAM` tap and reads `KM-COUNT`.
. The image stores the 64 words to the 64 addresses with the enable at 1 and the key at kA. The image performs no other SRAM write. It then reports a done message of one word and waits until the host has read it. When the done message appears, and before the host reads it, the host takes the second snapshot of the `KM-SRAM` tap and reads `KM-COUNT` again.
. The image reads the 64 words under kA in 4 groups of 16 and reports each group. The host drains each group before the image writes the next one.
. Lock leg. The image writes kA to SCRAMBLER_KEY, reads SCRAMBLER_KEY back and reports the value (group of 1, control for the locked read), then writes SCRAMBLER_CTRL with enable 1 and lock 1 in one value. In boot 1 the image sets the lock with the enable at 1 only; boot 4 sets it with the enable at 0. The host drains the group.
. The image reads SCRAMBLER_CTRL and SCRAMBLER_KEY and reports both (group of 2). The host drains the group.
. The image writes kB to SCRAMBLER_KEY, reads the 8 words and reports them (group of 8). The host drains the group.
. The image writes SCRAMBLER_CTRL with enable 0 and lock 1, reads SCRAMBLER_CTRL, reads the 8 words and reports the SCRAMBLER_CTRL value and the 8 words (group of 9). The host drains the group.
. The image writes SCRAMBLER_CTRL with enable 1 and lock 0, reads SCRAMBLER_CTRL, reads the 8 words and reports the SCRAMBLER_CTRL value and the 8 words (group of 9). The host drains the group.
. The host confirms that it has read every group of boot 1. The mailbox is empty before the reset.
. Warm reset leg. With the lock set, the host writes `SW_RESET_N` bit 0 low (the other bits at 1). Then the host writes `SW_RESET_N` bit 0 high to release the KM and posts the phase word of boot 2. The image reads SCRAMBLER_CTRL, reads the 8 words under kA without any key write, and reports the SCRAMBLER_CTRL value and the 8 words (group of 9).
. The host reads the group of boot 2 from the mailbox.
. Cold reset leg. The host applies the SEP system cold reset (a pulse of `rst_ni`) and waits for the `sep_reset_n` release on `dbg_sep_reset_n_o` (a bounded wait; a timeout fails the leaf). `SW_RESET_N` is back at its reset value 0x7E, so the KM stays held (`sep_reset_ctrl.adoc`, "SW_RESET_N"). The host writes `SW_RESET_N` = 0x7F to release the KM and posts the phase word of boot 3. The image reads SCRAMBLER_CTRL, writes kB to SCRAMBLER_KEY, reads SCRAMBLER_KEY back, and reports the SCRAMBLER_CTRL value and the key value (group of 2).
. The host reads the group of boot 3 from the mailbox.
. Lock-without-enable leg. The host applies the SEP system cold reset and waits for the `sep_reset_n` release as in step 19. The host writes `SW_RESET_N` = 0x7F to release the KM and posts the phase word of boot 4. The image reports a ready message of one word and waits until the host has read it. Before the host reads it, the host reads `km_sram_scr_wr_count_o` (`KM-SRAM-MON`) as c0. The image writes kA to SCRAMBLER_KEY, stores the first drawn word with the scrambler off and the lock clear (the control), reports a message of one word and waits until the host has read it. Before the host reads it, the host reads the count as c1. The image writes SCRAMBLER_CTRL with enable 0 and lock 1 in one value, reads SCRAMBLER_CTRL, stores the second drawn word, and reports the SCRAMBLER_CTRL value and a done message (group of 2). Before the host reads the group, the host reads the count as c2.
. The host reads the group of boot 4 from the mailbox. The bench compares every reported value with the expected value and logs the checker lines.

*Checkers*:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Contract
|CHK-SSCR-KEY
|With the scrambler on, the key tweaks the data (`hw/ip/scrambler/doc/architecture.adoc`, "Data Scrambling Algorithm", "Address Tweaking", "Byte-Wise Scrambling Mode": the stored word is a fixed permutation of the S-box output of the data XOR the key XOR the expanded address, and each stage is one-to-one). The kept write of P at a1 under kB carries a different data word than the kept write of P at a1 under kA, because kA differs from kB and the same address gives the same expanded address; this holds for every key pair and every plaintext. The 8 words read under kA again, after the key returns to kA, equal the plaintexts. A scrambler that ignores the key stores the same word twice and fails the pair. A key write that damages the stored data, or a key register that does not return to kA, fails the second kA count. The 8 words read under kB are logged (`OBS-SSCR-KB LOG`) and not graded: a read under kB reaches the row that the kB address scramble selects, and neither perm13 nor the content of that row is stated. Control: the first kA reads. The open test `sep_km_mem_smoke_test` owns that cell, and a failed control means the read path itself is broken. The anchor is the DUT writes at the SRAM macro port (`KM-SRAM-MON`) and the frames of boot 1 read through `HOST-MBX`, compared with the plaintexts that the bench drew. Evidence: `CHK-SSCR-KEY PASS ka_ok=8(control) key_pair_ne=1 ka_again_ok=8`, and `OBS-SSCR-KB LOG kb_eq=<n>`. The lines carry counts and no per-seed value.
|CHK-SSCR-STORED
|The address tweaks the key, so the same data at different addresses has a different scrambled value (`hw/ip/scrambler/doc/architecture.adoc`, "Address Tweaking"). The first four scrambled writes are kept by `KM-SRAM-MON`, in the order that the image stores them. The two kept writes that carry the same plaintext at two different addresses carry different data. A scrambler without the address tweak stores the same word twice and fails the pair count. This pair count is the new cell. Control, owned by `sep_km_mem_smoke_test`: the array word at each kept row equals the kept data. Whether each kept data word differs from its plaintext is logged, because a one-round cipher can map a word to itself. The pair lies inside the first four stores because the monitor keeps no later write. The anchor is the DUT writes at the SRAM macro port and the array word. Evidence: `CHK-SSCR-STORED PASS array_eq=4(control) same_p_pair_ne=1`, and `OBS-SSCR-STORED LOG stored_ne=<n>`.
|CHK-SSCR-ALIAS
|The read path scrambles the address and does not descramble it (`hw/ip/scrambler/doc/architecture.adoc`, "Address Scrambling"), so a word returns only if its logical address reaches the row that the store used. Each of the 64 words, at a distinct logical address, reads back equal to the word that the image stored there under kA. Two logical addresses that share a physical row make the later store overwrite the earlier word, and the earlier address reads a different word. The words are distinct and non-zero, so an overwrite is visible. The image performs no other SRAM write, so no result store can overwrite a stored word. The anchor is the 4 groups of boot 1 read through `HOST-MBX`. Evidence: `CHK-SSCR-ALIAS PASS logical=64 readback_ok=64`.
|CHK-SSCR-LOCK
|Once the lock is set, the key register reads as zero, writes to it are ignored, and the scrambler is forced into the enabled state (`hw/ip/scrambler/doc/architecture.adoc`, "Integration in the Key Manager"). SCRAMBLER_CTRL.lock is write-once, and key and enable cannot be modified until reset (`hw/ip/key_manager/regs/gen/adoc/km_csr.adoc`, "SCRAMBLER_KEY", "SCRAMBLER_CTRL"). After the lock is set with the enable at 1, SCRAMBLER_KEY reads 0; the 8 words read after the write of kB equal the plaintexts under kA, so the key write is ignored; SCRAMBLER_CTRL reads 0x3 after the write of enable 0 and after the write of 0 to the lock, and the 8 words read after each of the two writes equal the plaintexts, so the scrambler stays on and the enable write is ignored. A key that lands shows another value in the reads. An enable that clears shows CTRL bit 0 at 0. A lock that clears shows CTRL below 0x3. Controls: SCRAMBLER_KEY read before the lock returns kA, so a read can show a non-zero key; the kB write before the lock changes the stored word (CHK-SSCR-KEY); SCRAMBLER_CTRL reads 0x0 after the enable is cleared before the lock, so the enable write has an effect before the lock, and the 8 reads with the enable clear are logged. The anchor is the KM mailbox readback of the registers and of the stored words under kA, read through `HOST-MBX`. Evidence: `CHK-SSCR-LOCK PASS key_rd_unlocked_ok=1(control) en0_ctrl=0x0(control) key_rd_locked=0 key_write_ignored=1 enable_write_ignored=1 lock_write0_kept=1 ctrl_rd=0x3 reads_ok=16`, where `ctrl_rd` is the value of every SCRAMBLER_CTRL read after the lock and `reads_ok` is the count of the 16 reads after the two writes that equal the plaintexts.
|CHK-SSCR-RST
|The SRAM scrambler key, enable and lock are cold-domain state and survive a warm reset, and SRAM contents survive a warm reset (`hw/ip/key_manager/doc/architecture.adoc`, "Key Manager Control and Status Registers (KMCSR)", "ROM Warm-Persistent SRAM Region"). A cold reset clears both domains, and the SCRAMBLER_CTRL fields have reset value 0 (`hw/ip/key_manager/regs/gen/adoc/km_csr.adoc`, "SCRAMBLER_CTRL"). After the warm reset with the lock set, SCRAMBLER_CTRL reads 0x3 and the 8 words read under kA, with no key write, equal the plaintexts. After the cold reset, SCRAMBLER_CTRL reads 0x0, and a write of kB to SCRAMBLER_KEY reads back as kB. A warm reset that clears the enable or the lock shows CTRL below 0x3. A warm reset that drops the key or the data fails the reads. A cold reset that keeps the lock ignores the key write and reads 0, and a cold reset that keeps the enable shows CTRL bit 0. Controls: the SCRAMBLER_CTRL value 0x3 before the reset is the non-zero record that CHK-SSCR-LOCK logs, and kB is non-zero, so a locked read of 0 differs from the written value. SCRAMBLER_KEY has no reset value, so the test reads it only after a write. The anchor is the groups of boot 2 and boot 3 read through `HOST-MBX`. Evidence: `CHK-SSCR-RST PASS warm_ctrl=0x3 warm_reads_ok=8 cold_ctrl=0x0 cold_key_write_lands=1`.
|CHK-SSCR-LOCK0
|A lock set with the enable at 0 forces the scrambler into the enabled state (`hw/ip/scrambler/doc/architecture.adoc`, "Integration in the Key Manager": once locked, the scrambler is forced into the enabled state). After the write of enable 0 and lock 1 the second store counts as one scrambled write: `km_sram_scr_wr_count_o` rises by 1 from c1 to c2. The store with the lock clear and the enable 0 does not count: c1 equals c0. A DUT that leaves the scrambler off after the lock fails the count. The value that SCRAMBLER_CTRL.enable reads after the write is logged and not graded, because the register text says that key and enable cannot be modified after the lock and no sentence says which value the enable bit reads (<<sep-vplan-phase3-blocked,Blocked features>>). Anchor: `km_sram_scr_wr_count_o` (`KM-SRAM-MON`, approved). Control: the store before the lock does not count, so the count follows the enabled state. Evidence: `CHK-SSCR-LOCK0 PASS c1_minus_c0=0(control) c2_minus_c1=1 ctrl_rd_logged=0x<v>`.
|CHK-SSCR-ROWS
|The 64 stores at 64 distinct logical addresses touch no row other than their own (`hw/ip/scrambler/doc/architecture.adoc`, "Address Scrambling": the scrambled address selects the row). The first snapshot is taken before the ready message is read, and the second when the done message appears, so the 64 stores lie between them and no store marker is used. `KM-COUNT` shows that the count of accepted SRAM writes between the snapshots is 64, and at most 64 rows change, counted over the whole array. A scrambler that writes a second row for one store changes more rows. The number of changed rows is logged and is not required to be 64: a row whose new stored word and parity equal its old content does not change, and the old content is the power-up content, which is not stated. Two addresses that share a row are graded by CHK-SSCR-ALIAS. The anchor is the `KM-SRAM` tap in stored form and the `KM-COUNT` write count. Evidence: `CHK-SSCR-ROWS PASS logical=64 changed_rows_max=64 sram_writes=64`, and `OBS-SSCR-ROWS LOG changed_rows=<n>`.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every named checker PASSes. UVM_ERROR == 0.

*Scope limit*: The test extends `sep_km_mem_smoke_test`. Only the new cells are graded here: the open owner keeps the round trip under one key, the stored form that differs from the plaintext and the array word at each kept row, and those cells are controls. The byte permutation `perm8` of the KM SRAM and the address permutation `perm13` are not tabulated in the scrambler document, so the stored word and the physical row have no cipher golden (<<sep-vplan-phase3-blocked,Blocked features>>). The cipher golden is graded on the KPV path in `sep_km_kpv_rand_test`. The test grades a lock set with the enable at 0 by the scrambled-write count only: the value that SCRAMBLER_CTRL.enable reads after such a lock is not stated (<<sep-vplan-phase3-blocked,Blocked features>>). The SRAM parity status that a read under another key sets, the SRAM array contents after a cold reset and the SCRAMBLER_KEY value after a cold reset are not stated and are not graded. The number of SCRAMBLER_KEY writes in a boot, and the key provisioning order of the boot ROM, belong to `sep_km_boot_reset_rand_test`. The KPV scrambler belongs to `sep_km_kpv_rand_test`. The SCRAMBLER_KEY write and read with the lock clear belong to `sep_km_kmcsr_reset_rand_test`.

'''''

[[sep-vplan-phase3]]
=== Phase 3 Tests

Phase 3 tests prove the residual contracts of each area (<<sep-vplan-phase3-overview>>).
Each area has its Phase 3 summary rows in its table of the
Scenario-Expanded Test Summary, and its Phase 3 entries at the end of its
section of Test Procedures, after the entries of Phase 1 and Phase 2. The rows
are for human readers and the entries are for tools and audits. The two name
the same tests. An entry follows the field rules of Test Procedures and adds the fields
that its area section states. A Phase 3 test never overlaps a Phase 1 or
Phase 2 test. An entry that extends an open test names that test and the cell
that the entry adds. The Phase 3 contracts that no test can grade are in
<<sep-vplan-phase3-lists>>. The randomization class of every test is in
<<sep-vplan-phase3-random>>. Each Phase 3 leaf opens the coverage window of its
own entry only around its graded stimulus (<<sep-fcov-graded-window,SEP_FCOV>>).
The window gate is a testbench variable that only the coverage sampler reads; it
drives nothing and touches no DUT net. The sampler `u_sep_fcov` exists only on
VCS, so a Verilator leaf skips the gate write and runs the same checks.
Its bring-up, its control legs and a reset sequence between legs run with the
window closed, so they fill no Phase 3 bin, and neither does the traffic of
another test.

[[sep-vplan-phase3-overview]]
==== Phase 3 Overview

[cols="3,2,8",options="header"]
|===
|Area |Test numbers |Scope
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|1.25 to 1.53
|Crypto interrupt lines and cross-engine concurrency (two extension legs of open tests), HMAC, AES, KMAC, OTBN, ABR, delivered-key select, crypto alerts, ESRC health, FIFO integrity, autotune and conditioning, DRBG faults and sinks, TRNG stream handshake and external entropy to the Key Manager.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-fabric-remap,Fabric and remap>>
|2.25 to 2.33
|Inbound and outbound filter match with granule, default deny and source ID, global-to-local rebase, outbound route and output remap, alias remap, SMC route, extension port window, row responses with burst refusal, and DMA endpoint reach.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-mailbox-irq-pic,Mailbox, IRQ, PIC>>
|3.13 to 3.24
|Mailbox lines, FIFOs, errors, filter types and reset; PIC registers, priority, gateway cells, source map and external inputs; bridge fault latches and the fault-versus-clear race; timeout registers; NMI vector; timer and software interrupt tie-offs.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-spi-dma,SPI and DMA>>
|4.7 to 4.15
|SPI pad, FIFO, interrupt, error, strobe and reset contracts (one entry extends an open SPI test); DMA address modes, geometry, interrupt gate, abort, inline hash and SPI handshake. The DMA range-lock checks are blocked legs: they need a value that the specification does not state (<<sep-vplan-phase3-blocked-legs,Blocked legs>>).
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-mem-boot-reset,Memory, boot, reset, WDT, clock>>
|5.13 to 5.29
|Reset release, cold and CPU-only reset, software reset and isolation, JTAG and scan overrides, reset vector and run request, `SECURE_TM`, scratch and CPU control registers, watchdog, wakeup timer and reference counter, memory apertures and ECC, CPU demux, debug master, ISA and PMP.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-efuse-lifecycle,eFuse, lifecycle, SEC_DIS, locked-field>>
|6.18 to 6.30
|eFuse windows and fields, lifecycle code words, feature control, demotion and DFT gate ports, transient RMA, token channels, faults and latch freeze, interface status, lock slots, secure test mode, JTAG access, SEC_DIS timing, sense response and program interface faults.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-key-manager,Key Manager vault>>
|7.22 to 7.37
|Command framing, recovery and arguments; key slots, handles and allocator capacity; engine delivery and transfer policy; ABR shared key; boot and cold domain; SRAM load and handover; fault reports and SRAM latency; KMCSR, SRAM lock and reset domains; KPV; CPU trap and execute protection; crossbar and eFuse window; KM-side mailbox; DRBG sampler; OTP interface; engine key registers; SRAM scrambler.
|===

[[sep-vplan-phase3-parked]]
==== Phase 3 Parked Tests

A parked test has no graded check that runs without a PROPOSED item or an
unstated value (<<sep-vplan-credit-rules>>). Its entry carries the field
`*Needs*:`, its summary row reads "3, parked", it takes no credit, it is not in
an executable total, and its bins are blocked bins of `SEP_FCOV.adoc`
(<<sep-fcov-parked,Phase 2 Planned Groups>>).

No Phase 3 entry carries a `*Needs*:` field, so every Phase 3 test is
executable: at least one of its graded checks is not blocked. An entry names
the PROPOSED item or the unstated value of each of its blocked checks and legs.


[[sep-vplan-phase3-random]]
==== Phase 3 Randomization

Every Phase 3 stimulus that has a legal matrix is a pure function of the run
seed, and `--stage sim --seed N` replays the leaf. The stream is not a CSPRNG
and no drawn value is a key, a token or a nonce. No document quotes a per-seed
value as evidence. The class of a test is one of:

* `RAND-REP`: the seed draws points from a legal matrix, and every point has a stated outcome.
* `RANDCFG`: the seed draws a configuration, the test runs one scenario under it, and the expected outcome is a function of the configuration.
* `RAND-NONE`: the stimulus is directed, for the reason the entry states.

[[sep-vplan-phase3-drawn]]
*Drawn cells.* Regression seeds are random per leaf, and a leaf does not know
its run index, so no seed and no testlist entry pins a cell. A leaf draws its
cells from its seed (`SepSeededRng`, weighted toward the corners where the entry
says so, with the constraint filters of the entry). A leaf walks a cell set in
every run only when the set is cheap and contract-critical: a legal minimum or
maximum, one representative of each leg, or the error-injection case itself,
with no extra boot, no extra cold reset and no extra transfer of real size per
cell. The coverage bins of such cells fill in one `all --cov` regression. The
coverage bins of drawn cells are seed-dependent and close over a merge of
regressions, never in one regression (<<sep-fcov-rand-phase2,SEP_FCOV>>). For N
equally likely cells and d draws per leaf the expected closure is about
N * ln(N) / (d * reseed) regressions. The seed count of an entry stays small
(3 or 4) and is not raised to fill cells; an entry that runs more seeds states
the reason.

*Testlist entries.* A Phase 3 test has one testlist entry. One entry on
`lsu_stub_all_live` gives a Verilator leaf on that build and a VCS leaf on
`--target default`, so a test that grades some checks on one simulator only
splits them inside its one entry, and the leaf selects them from the simulator.
A second entry exists only when the run mode differs in a way that one entry
cannot carry: a time-0 bench plusarg that the prestage hook cannot set, or a
different run mode (`cpu` and `no_cpu`). No entry exists to pin a cell (no
per-cell variant, no cell or field plusarg). The tests with a second entry are
5.13 `sep_boot_release_terms_test`, whose entry
`sep_boot_release_terms_test_smc_hold` adds the bench plusarg
`+sep_smc_fuse_sense_hold`; 5.28 `sep_debug_master_target_matrix_test`, which
has one `cpu` entry and one `no_cpu` entry of the one module; and 7.28
`sep_km_fault_inject_rand_test`, which has one entry for each of its two
preloaded `rom_main` builds (HOST and HOST-UNREC, set by the t=0 plusarg
`+km_rom_hex`). An extension leg runs in the testlist entry of its
open test and adds no entry. Where the leg needs more seeds than that entry
runs, the entry takes the seed count of the leg (1.25 and 1.26).

[[sep-vplan-phase3-edn-waiver]]
*JTAG reset override waiver.* The JTAG `sep_reset_n` override and the per-IP
JTAG reset holds reset the crypto engines without the isolation sequence, so an
engine can drop an ungranted EDN request with no endpoint cancel, and the
`tb_top` crypto EDN request-hold assertions fire on a compliant DUT. Every
testlist entry whose leaf drives the `sep_reset_n` override (on the bench pins
`jtag_sep_reset_n_ovrd_i` / `jtag_sep_reset_n_val_i` or through the IC_RESET
TDR) or a per-IP hold `jtag_<ip>_rst_hold_i` adds `+sep_edn_jtag_reset_waive`.
The plusarg turns off only the crypto EDN arbiter and adapter request-hold
assertions (`tb/tb_top.sv`), and `tb_top` logs that it is set. The Phase 3
entries that add it are 5.17, 5.20, 5.22 and 6.29.

A test with two classes uses two of the three classes on different legs: a
drawn configuration for one leg and a matrix point for another, or a directed
leg next to a drawn leg. The entry names the dimensions of each class, and the
table below gives both classes of such a test. A row marked "extension" or
"extension leg" names an open test. Its class is the class of the cells that
the entry adds. A row marked "parked" names a parked test
(<<sep-vplan-phase3-parked>>).

[[sep-vplan-phase3-lists]]
==== Phase 3 Blocked Features, Observation Gaps and Scope

Each item is listed once. The area column names every area that the item
concerns. No Phase 3 test grades a blocked feature, and no random draw uses
one. A feature with no observation point has no check that can fail on it. An
out of scope feature is graded by an open Phase 1 or Phase 2 test, or has no
stated pass or fail value, or belongs to another area. A PROPOSED internal
drive, an added hook and an observation tap that a test adds are listed in
<<sep-vplan-phase3-proposed>>. A check that needs a PROPOSED item is blocked
(<<sep-vplan-credit-rules>>). A check that needs only observation taps and added
hooks is not blocked.

[[sep-vplan-phase3-blocked]]
===== Blocked features

A blocked feature has no check in Phase 3, because the specification or the
register description does not state the value that a check needs. The
question names what the specification must state before a check can fail on
the feature. Where a test uses part of a blocked feature, the note says what
the test does.

|Secure test mode program request status
|Does the secure test block of a program request show as `program_done`, `program_status` or `efuse_req_error`? The text states that all fuse commands are blocked, that default all-zero responses are returned and that secure test mode contributes to the write lock status (`hw/ip/efuse/doc/architecture.adoc`, Secure Test Mode (`secure_tm_i`)). `efuse_interface_ctrl.adoc` defines `efuse_req_error` as a block by a read or program lock, and no sentence says whether secure test mode sets it. (`hw/ip/efuse/regs/gen/adoc/efuse_interface_ctrl.adoc`, `efuse_req_error`.)
|`sep_km_crossbar_efuse_window_rand_test` grades the zero read word, equal KM and host results and an unchanged fuse bit, and logs the tuple
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-key-manager,Key Manager>>
|SRAM scrambler lock with the enable clear
|What does `SCRAMBLER_CTRL.enable` read after the lock is set while enable is 0? The register text says key and enable cannot be modified after the lock and does not say which value the enable bit reads; the scrambler text says the scrambler is forced into the enabled state. (`hw/ip/key_manager/regs/gen/adoc/km_csr.adoc`, `SCRAMBLER_CTRL`; `hw/ip/scrambler/doc/architecture.adoc`, Integration in the Key Manager.)
|`sep_km_sram_scrambler_key_rand_test` grades the forced scrambling by the scrambled-write count and logs the read value
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-key-manager,Key Manager>>
|Extent of each SRAM shred pass of the fatal handler
|`hw/ip/key_manager/doc/firmware.adoc`, Error Recovery, states one Weyl pass and two xoshiro128++ passes of the SRAM and does not state the extent of each pass. The full 0x8000 to 0xFFFF extent is stated only for the handover scramble.
|`sep_km_fault_inject_rand_test` grades at least 8192 SRAM writes and logs the count and the 24576 value of three full passes
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-key-manager,Key Manager>>
|`invalid_len` (-5) argument when `PAYLOAD_LEN` contradicts the frame length
|How is the received payload length of the `invalid_len` (-5) argument counted when `PAYLOAD_LEN` contradicts the frame length on the wire? (hw/ip/key_manager/doc/firmware.adoc, section "0x00 - RESP_CMD".)
|`sep_km_command_protocol_rand_test` grades the -5 code and logs the argument
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-key-manager,Key Manager>>
|`OTP_DEMOTION_STATE` group encoding
|What are the bit order and polarity of the two `OTP_DEMOTION_STATE` groups {demote_2[1:0], demote_1[1:0]}, that is, which code means "not demoted"? (hw/ip/key_manager/doc/architecture.adoc, section "OTP Inputs and Readout".)
|`sep_km_otp_interface_rand_test` grades complementary groups and a change from the recorded value
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-key-manager,Key Manager>>
|Level bits of the Key Manager mailbox interrupt status after reset
|Which value does a read after reset return for `KM_IRQ_STATUS.outbound_write_space_avail`, `KM_IRQ_STATUS.inbound_read_data_avail` and the level bits of `SEP_IRQ_STATUS`? The register description gives the reset value 0x0, and the field text says level 1 means space available, with both FIFOs empty at reset. (hw/ip/key_manager/regs/gen/adoc/km_mailbox_km.adoc, `KM_IRQ_STATUS`; hw/ip/key_manager/regs/gen/adoc/km_mailbox_sep.adoc, `SEP_IRQ_STATUS`.)
|`sep_km_mailbox_km_side_rand_test` logs the level bits at reset and grades them after the first FIFO event
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-key-manager,Key Manager>>
|A shredded or revoked engine holds no key (`key_valid` 0). The output of an AES in that state is not stated.
|What does an engine output after its `key_valid` is cleared (no output, an error, or an output under a zero key)? Source: `hw/sys/sep/doc/aes.adoc` (`CTRL_SHADOWED.sideload` states the selection only); `hw/ip/key_manager/doc/firmware.adoc` ("Key Transfer and Sideload Purge").
|`sep_km_key_transfer_rand_test`, `sep_km_boot_reset_rand_test` and `sep_km_fault_inject_rand_test` grade the absence of a key on the HMAC witness only: its no-key result is the digest of its software key, which the HMAC text states. An AES output that differs from the golden of the delivered key, or no output, is logged as `OBS-AES-NOKEY` and is never counted as a pass of a refusal, a shred or a revoke; an AES output that equals the golden where no key is expected fails. They do not claim that the AES gives no output.
|===

A tested feature can have one blocked leg. The test grades the rest of the
feature, and the note says how the test treats the blocked leg.

[[sep-vplan-phase3-unstated]]
====== Unstated cells that block no feature

<<sep-vplan-phase3-mailbox-irq-pic,Mailbox, IRQ, PIC>>:

* The response of a write of 0 to a W 1P clear register is not stated beyond "write 1 to clear". `sep_cpu_bridge_fault_matrix_rand_test` grades that 0 leaves the latch set and does not grade the response code.

<<sep-vplan-phase3-fabric-remap,Fabric and remap>>:

* The response of a Reserved, Past Extent or Hole in Extent cell as seen by the CPU LSU or the DMA. `hw/sys/sep/doc/memory_map.adoc` states the cells for a 32-bit access as seen at the inbound AXI port, and says what the SEP CPU sees only for the boot ROM, reset control, ICCM, DCCM, PIC and AP/STEE rows. The fabric leaves grade the reset-control gaps, tails and past-extent cells from the LSU against the table, because the specification states the CPU view for those rows. For every other row, the fabric leaves grade the cells through the System Interface and log the LSU value. The response of the fabric to a DMA-master access at a reserved window is not stated either, so no address can stand in for the non-OKAY response control of the outbound responder. The non-OKAY leg of the DMA host-path latch in `sep_cpu_bridge_fault_matrix_rand_test` uses that control, an error inject that the test adds (see <<sep-vplan-phase3-added-hooks,Hooks that the tests add>>).
* The response and read data of a 1-, 2- or 8-byte access to a Reserved, Past Extent or Hole in Extent cell. The table states the cells only for a 32-bit access. The row leaf grades AxSIZE 2 in both halves of the bus and logs AxSIZE 3.

<<sep-vplan-phase3-mem-boot-reset,Memory, boot, reset>>:

* The assertion timing of `sep_intermediate_reset_n`, and so of `sep_reset_n`, after the `rst_ni` fall. `hw/sys/sep/doc/reset_controller.adoc` (SEP Reset Controller) states that the eFuse wrapper synchronizes the AND of the boot terms into `sep_intermediate_reset_n` and that `u_sep_reset_sync` asserts its input asynchronously, and gives no assertion behaviour for the first synchronizer. `sep_cold_reset_phase_test` logs the delay as `OBS-RST-ASSERT` and grades the release only.

<<sep-vplan-phase3-key-manager,Key Manager vault>>:

* The reserved bits of CMD_KEY_REVOKE, CMD_KEY_TRANSFER and CMD_ENGINE_SHRED, the transfer mask 0 and the shred mask 0. (hw/ip/key_manager/doc/firmware.adoc, sections "0x22 - CMD_KEY_GENERATE", "0x25 - CMD_ENGINE_SHRED".) The tests keep the reserved bits clear and never draw them.
* The return code of CMD_KEY_REVOKE for an unavailable handle, and the return code of any command for a null or never-issued handle. (hw/ip/key_manager/doc/firmware.adoc, section "0x23 - CMD_KEY_REVOKE".) A CMD_KEY_TRANSFER of a revoked handle is a failure (section "Key Transfer and Sideload Purge") and `sep_km_key_transfer_rand_test` grades it.
* The return argument of CMD_KEY_GENERATE when both REQ_SIZE and DEST_VALID are invalid. (hw/ip/key_manager/doc/firmware.adoc, section "0x22 - CMD_KEY_GENERATE".) `sep_km_command_protocol_rand_test` logs it and does not grade it.
* The read response of a write-only register (KM_WRITE_DATA and the key-share registers). `sep_km_crossbar_efuse_window_rand_test` logs it and does not grade it.
* The TIMEOUT_ERR and COUNT_BAD results when a stream error and a timeout expiry fall in one cycle (STREAM_ERR set is stated). (hw/ip/key_manager/doc/architecture.adoc, section "Errors and reset".) `sep_km_drbg_sampler_rand_test` logs them and does not grade them.
* The precedence of the handover-disabled and zero-size conditions of CMD_SRAM_EXEC. (hw/ip/key_manager/doc/firmware.adoc, section "0x12 - CMD_SRAM_EXEC".)
* The CMD_SRAM_LOAD_EXEC image ceiling value. `sep_km_handover_rand_test` grades sizes at or above the SRAM size and logs the rest.
* The read value of a locked KPV_SCRAMBLER_KEY. (hw/ip/key_manager/regs/gen/adoc/km_kpv.adoc, sections "CTRL[64]", "KPV_SCRAMBLER_KEY".)
* The value of OTP_EFUSE_REMAP_BASE. (hw/ip/key_manager/doc/architecture.adoc.) `sep_km_crossbar_efuse_window_rand_test` grades that the base is constant.
* The OTP readout value before the sense completes, and the length of the OTP change suppression window. (hw/sys/sep/doc/otp_fuse_controller.adoc, section "Fuse Sensing and Boot Sequencing"; hw/ip/key_manager/doc/architecture.adoc, section "OTP Inputs and Readout".)
* Whether SEP_IRQ_STATUS.flushed_by_km sets at the boot flush of the ROM. (hw/ip/key_manager/regs/gen/adoc/km_mailbox_sep.adoc, section "SEP_IRQ_STATUS".) `sep_km_command_protocol_rand_test` logs it.
* The byte-wise permutation (perm8) of the KM SRAM scrambler and the address permutations (perm10, perm13) are not tabulated in hw/ip/scrambler/doc/architecture.adoc. No cipher golden exists for the KM SRAM stored word. `sep_km_sram_scrambler_key_rand_test` grades the KM SRAM by key, address and bijection, and `sep_km_kpv_rand_test` grades the cipher on the KPV path (whole-word permutation) and logs the KPV cells read after a cold reset, because the stored words then lie at the indices that perm10 selects.

[[sep-vplan-phase3-noobs]]
===== Features with no observation point

A disposition says what is done about the missing observation. `ADD-PORT`: a
testbench port, drive or hook that the bench lacks would give the observation,
and the DUT does not change. `ACCEPT-PROBE`: a read-only probe or hierarchical
reference, or a firmware CSR read, is the observation. A probe or reference that
`hw/sys/sep/dv/docs/SEP_TB_ARCH.adoc` does not list is an observation tap the
test adds to the SEP_TB_ARCH observation-probe list, and a check on it is
executable. `PERMANENT-HOLE`: no observation exists at SEP level, so no check can
fail on the contract.

A read-only probe, tap or reference is an observation tap and is not PROPOSED.
A port, drive, inject or hook that exists in `hw/sys/sep/dv/tb/tb_top.sv` or that
`SEP_TB_ARCH.adoc` lists is not PROPOSED, and the row says so. An error inject
and a drive of a port of the `sep` module are added hooks and are not PROPOSED
(<<sep-vplan-credit-rules>>). A drive, force or deposit of a net inside `sep`
for a purpose other than error injection is PROPOSED.
<<sep-vplan-phase3-proposed>> lists each observation tap, each added hook and
each PROPOSED item with the tests that use it. A check that needs a PROPOSED
item is blocked (<<sep-vplan-credit-rules>>).

[cols="3,4,4,2,8",options="header"]
|===
|Area |Feature |Missing observation |Disposition |Reason
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|Secret keys travel only on the private Key Manager AXI4-Lite key buses. Host data and CSR traffic uses the separate AXI4 bus from the SEP fabric.

|The key buses have no SEP port and no register view. The delivered-key outcome is graded end to end by the open Key Manager tests.

The alert receiver probe (`crypto_alert_pulse`, read-only, 11 bits; named `crypto_alert_pulse_probe_o` at the boundary) is an observation tap the test adds to the SEP_TB_ARCH observation-probe list. It serves `sep_pic_pending_map_walk_rand_test` (CHK-ALERT-IDX). The aggregate leg is a register and vector check.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>

The integration module, public bus infrastructure and combinational entropy muxes are not roots.

|Isolation of the AES, OTBN and eFuse paths
|The isolation request and acknowledge of the AES, OTBN and eFuse paths, the drain of accepted transactions and the order against the warm reset
|ADD-PORT
|Only three isolation probes exist (HMAC, KMAC, ABR). `sep_km_kmcsr_reset_rand_test` grades those three. The reset controller tests own the sequencer.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-key-manager,Key Manager>>
|KM SRAM scratch locations of key material
|KM SRAM scratch locations of key material
|PERMANENT-HOLE
|The scratch lives in the scrambled SRAM at addresses the specification does not state. A test cannot search the array for plaintext.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-key-manager,Key Manager>>
|The allocator never uses a read-locked, sealed or retired slot.
|A stimulus that sets seal or lock_use on a slot before an allocation
|PERMANENT-HOLE
|No ROM flow and no host command sets seal or lock_use before an allocation. The allocator capacity oracle (CHK-CAP of `sep_km_key_vault_alloc_rand_test`) covers the live-key and revoked-slot cases only.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-key-manager,Key Manager>>
|A slot-write error during CMD_KEY_LOAD destroys the handle registration, keeps the earlier vault writes and does not reuse the handle.
|A failure of one KPV slot write
|ADD-PORT
|The slot-write failure needs an injected KPV write failure. No inject of `tb_top.sv` and no added hook of a Phase 3 entry provides it, and no entry grades the contract.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-key-manager,Key Manager>>
|CMD_KEY_TRANSFER stops at the first driver failure and keeps the earlier engine writes.
|A failure of one engine key write
|ADD-PORT
|The failure needs an injected engine-write failure. No inject of `tb_top.sv` and no added hook of a Phase 3 entry provides it, and no entry grades the contract.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-key-manager,Key Manager>>
|The OTP change interrupt flow of the ROM.
|The source is not enabled at boot, so the flow is dormant in the ROM.
|PERMANENT-HOLE
|No stimulus reaches a dormant flow without a firmware change.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-key-manager,Key Manager>>
|The allocator starts at a DRBG-selected slot.
|The start slot of an allocation
|PERMANENT-HOLE
|No net shows the DRBG-selected start slot. The capacity oracle does not depend on it.
|===

[[sep-vplan-phase3-proposed]]
===== Observation taps, added hooks and proposed drives

This section has three lists. <<sep-vplan-phase3-obs-taps>> lists the read-only
observations that Phase 3 tests use and that `hw/sys/sep/dv/docs/SEP_TB_ARCH.adoc`
does not list: each is an observation tap the test adds to the SEP_TB_ARCH
observation-probe list. <<sep-vplan-phase3-added-hooks>> lists the error injects
and the top-port drives that Phase 3 tests use and that `SEP_TB_ARCH.adoc` does
not list: each is an added hook that the test adds to the inject exceptions or
to the HDL Top port table of `SEP_TB_ARCH.adoc`. It also lists the existing
bench hooks of `hw/sys/sep/dv/tb/tb_top.sv` that Phase 3 tests use and that
`SEP_TB_ARCH.adoc` does not list. An observation tap, an added hook and an
existing bench hook are not PROPOSED, so a check or bin that needs only these is
executable (<<sep-vplan-credit-rules>>). <<sep-vplan-phase3-proposed-drives>> lists the
PROPOSED items: each drives, forces or deposits into a net inside the `sep`
module for a purpose other than error injection, and it is not in
`SEP_TB_ARCH.adoc` and not in `hw/sys/sep/dv/tb/tb_top.sv`. No item changes DUT
RTL. A check that needs a PROPOSED item is blocked: it is not a pass and takes no
credit. An item with two uses is one row in each list that applies. A preload
(<<sep-vplan-credit-rules>>) is part of the approved t=0 image load and is in
none of the three lists; <<sep-vplan-km-proposed>> names the preloads of the Key
Manager tests.

Notes on these lists:

* `sep_cpu_ctrl_err_pulse_probe_o` (Mailbox, IRQ, PIC) and `dma_bus_err_latch_probe_o` (SPI and DMA) give the same observation of the DMA host-path latch.
* The Key Manager contracts of a partial `CMD_KEY_LOAD` failure, a partial `CMD_KEY_TRANSFER` failure, a Key Manager mailbox overflow or underflow, and a Key Manager CPU interrupt line need four injects: a KPV slot-write failure, an engine key-write failure, a Key Manager mailbox error and a CPU interrupt line. No Phase 3 entry uses them, so they are not in this list (<<sep-vplan-phase3-noobs>>).

[[sep-vplan-phase3-added-hooks]]
====== Hooks that the tests add

Each item is an added hook (<<sep-vplan-credit-rules>>): an error inject, which
the test adds to the inject exceptions of `hw/sys/sep/dv/docs/SEP_TB_ARCH.adoc`,
or a top-port drive, which the test adds to the port table of the HDL Top
section of `SEP_TB_ARCH.adoc`. An item of the kind "Existing bench hook" exists
in `hw/sys/sep/dv/tb/tb_top.sv` and `SEP_TB_ARCH.adoc` does not list it: it is
approved, and the test that uses it adds its row to `SEP_TB_ARCH.adoc`
(<<sep-vplan-credit-rules>>). An item of the kind "Existing bench hook, listed"
exists in `tb_top.sv` and in the inject exceptions of `SEP_TB_ARCH.adoc`; the
list names it for its users only, and the test adds no row. An added hook and an
existing bench hook are not PROPOSED and block no check, leg or bin. The column "Port or inject point" names the `sep` port of a top-port
drive (`hw/sys/sep/rtl/sep.sv`) and the point of an error inject. The memory
macros, the eFuse integration and the external TRNG source are in
`hw/top/sep_ip_integration.sv`, outside the `sep` module. The column "Tests that
use it" names the entries whose checks need the hook.

[[sep-vplan-phase3-proposed-drives]]
====== PROPOSED internal drives

Each item drives, forces or deposits into a net inside the `sep` module for a
purpose other than error injection, and it is not in `SEP_TB_ARCH.adoc` and not
in `hw/sys/sep/dv/tb/tb_top.sv`. A check that needs one is blocked. The column
"Tests that need it" names the entries that carry the blocked check.

[cols="2,3,2,6,6",options="header"]
|===
|Area |Name |Kind |What it drives |Tests that need it
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-key-manager,Key Manager>>
|`HK-STRM-PAT`
|Drive
|`TVALID`, `TDATA` and `TSTRB` of the DRBG sampler stream at the KM sink, with legal beat patterns, in place of the live stream for one read: every non-zero `TSTRB` value, drawn byte values and drawn `TVALID` delays; a partial beat (`TSTRB` 0x1) followed by a stall; one-cycle `TVALID` pulses with `TREADY` high; a complete beat followed by a `TVALID` drop after the handshake.
|`sep_km_drbg_sampler_rand_test` (CHK-SMP-PACK, CHK-SMP-TO-ASM, CHK-SMP-STRM-CTRL)
|===


[[sep-vplan-phase3-oos]]
===== Out of scope

No Phase 3 test grades these features. The reason says which open test grades
a feature, or why no pass or fail value exists.

[cols="3,5,8",options="header"]
|===
|Area |Feature |Reason
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|The effect of the `HT_WATERMARK_NUM` selector codes.
|The RDL states the `WATERMARK_TEST` codes REPCNT_HI 0, APT_HI 1, APT_LO 2, MARKOV_HI 3 and MARKOV_LO 4 and the effect that `HT_WATERMARK` shows: a `CTRL.MODULE_ENABLE` rising edge arms a high code to 0 and a low code to 0xFFFF (`entropy_source.rdl`, `HT_WATERMARK`). The open Phase 2 test `sep_esrc_ht_watermark_arming_test` grades this effect for every supported code, the resolution of an unsupported code to REPCNT_HI, and the fall of both low codes. `sep_esrc_csr_rw_walk_rand_test` stores a value of the selector inside its stated range and reads it back.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|Each wrapper terminates the key bus in a key CSR block: HMAC, AES and KMAC take 8 words per share, OTBN takes 12, and ABR takes 8 per seed block (four blocks).
|Words per share are graded end to end: a wrong count breaks the delivered-key results of the open sideload tests for HMAC, AES, KMAC, OTBN and the ABR seeds.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|Each OpenTitan wrapper path is 64-bit AXI, narrowed to 32-bit AXI, converted to AXI4-Lite, isolated, then bridged to TL-UL.
|The bridge chain is graded by use of every accelerator register in `sep_reg_bit_bash_rand_test` and `sep_hmac_kmac_cpu_crypto_smoke_test`.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|HMAC masks its host address to a 13-bit (8 KB) window that holds the register space and the message FIFO window at offset 0x1000.
|The HMAC window width and the FIFO offset are graded by use: a digest needs the FIFO window.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|KMAC masks its host address to a 12-bit (4 KB) window before the AXI-to-AXI-Lite stage.
|The KMAC window width is graded by use.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|Without SEP_ABR_EN, both the ABR crossbar port and the KM ABR key bus end in error responders that return DECERR.
|`sep_abr_absent_decerr_test`.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|The crypto EDN adapter forwards the per-beat FIPS tag to OTBN RND. OTBN RND checks the tag and can set ERR_BITS.rnd_fips_chk_fail. The integration ties the CSRNG seed tag and the external mux tag high, so a high tag only prevents the check from failing.
|`sep_crypto_edn_round_robin_grant_test` and `sep_otbn_compute_rand_test` grade RND consumption and ERR_BITS. The tag is 1 on every path, so a tag of 0 cannot be driven and rnd_fips_chk_fail has no control window.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|The OTBN IMEM and DMEM SRAM interfaces leave SEP as four ports: sep_crypto_pka_{imem,dmem}_sram_{req_o,rsp_i}.
|`sep_otbn_mem_smoke_test` and `sep_axi_strobe_window_test`.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|OTBN has a 256-bit datapath with a 32-entry register file, a 32-bit control path with a 32-entry register file, flow control, dual flags, modular arithmetic and a TRNG noise stream.
|Descriptive statement of the core datapath. The executed behaviour is graded by `sep_otbn_compute_rand_test`. The register files and flags have no register view.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|The OTBN driver library supports ECDSA/ECDH P256 and P384, Ed25519, X25519, RSA 2k/3k/4k and SHA-256/512; microcode loads into SRAM.
|A library statement. The spec gives no vectors and no program images, so no SEP-level pass or fail value exists. The OpenTitan IP-level DV owns the library.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|AES supports 128, 192 and 256-bit keys; KEY_LEN is one-hot (AES_128 = 001, AES_192 = 010, AES_256 = 100, reset AES_128).
|`sep_aes_mode_keysize_rand_test` grades the three key sizes in ECB, CBC and CTR.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|The AES key CSR block carries 8 words per share. AES passes the two shares into the cipher as a masked pair and does not combine them on the delivery path.
|The sideload tests grade the delivered key through the engine.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|KMAC kstrength selects L128, L224, L256, L384 or L512 (reset 0; the codes come from the upstream register description named in the Conventions).
|`sep_kmac_mode_strength_rand_test` grades every legal strength cell.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|KMAC CFG_SHADOWED.kmac_en = 1 makes KMAC mode active and prepends the secret key to the incoming message.
|`sep_kmac_mode_strength_rand_test` grades the keyed KMAC digests.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|KEY_LEN.len selects Key128, Key192, Key256, Key384 or Key512 (codes from the upstream register description named in the Conventions); key registers hold up to 512 bits per share.
|`sep_kmac_mode_strength_rand_test` grades the five key lengths.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|Eleven RW PREFIX registers hold the encoded function-name and customization strings for cSHAKE.
|`sep_kmac_mode_strength_rand_test` grades the PREFIX words through the digest.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|KMAC CFG_SHADOWED.sideload (reset 1) selects the delivered 256-bit key (8 words per share). The engine applies the key length itself and ignores the key-length register. A keyed operation with KEY_CTRL.KEY_VALID = 0 raises an error.
|`sep_km_kmac_sideload_kat_test` and `sep_km_sideload_share_walk_test`.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|The Key Manager key bus ends in abr_wrapper_key_reg. sep_abr_kv_shim presents the dual-share secrets to abr_top over kv_read/kv_write. Four seed blocks (MLDSA_SEED, MLKEM_SEED_D, MLKEM_SEED_Z, MLKEM_MSG) each have 8 words per share and their own KEY_VALID.
|`sep_km_sideload_share_walk_test` and the Key Manager ABR tests.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|ABR reports faults only by interrupt: PIC source 35 (error) and 36 (notification).
|The ABR error and notification interrupts reach sources 35 and 36.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|ML-DSA is the post-quantum signature path intended for secure boot. REQUIRED_SIGNERS selects owners and REQUIRED_ALGS selects algorithms per owner. SEP ROM does not use it and verifies one RSA-3072 signature.
|A secure-boot flow statement. REQUIRED_SIGNERS and REQUIRED_ALGS belong to the life-cycle chapter and its bucket.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|Source requirements are described by NIST SP 800-90B. Source characterization and health-test thresholds belong to entropy-source qualification, and conditioning does not by itself establish entropy.
|A requirement statement with no stated pass or fail value.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|The internal chain is ESRC (ring oscillators, extraction, health checks, SHA-256 conditioning), CSRNG (AES-CTR DRBG) and EDN. The gating health test sees the extracted 32-bit stream before SHA-256.
|A decomposition statement. Each element is covered by its own entry, except the position of the gating test before SHA-256 (<<sep-vplan-phase3-blocked,Blocked features>>).
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|The health tests are repetition-count, adaptive-proportion and Markov. No bucket test is named.
|States that no bucket test exists. A statement of absence has no observation.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|The DRBG is AES-CTR-DRBG (NIST SP 800-90A), built from CSRNG and EDN.
|A construction statement. The CSRNG output is graded against an AES-256 CTR_DRBG golden by CHK3 and CHK4 of the open entropy tests.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|The internal path is ESRC to CSRNG to EDN to the three sinks. External data can replace a sink stream after EDN, which bypasses the internal chain.
|The chain from ESRC to the sinks is graded stage by stage.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|SW_RESET_N.trng_sw_rst_n resets ESRC, CSRNG, EDN and the DRBG endpoint queues; post-mux adapters and the pool clear while it is active.
|`sep_crypto_per_ip_reset_isolation_test` and `sep_trng_reset_recovery_test`.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|Reset and isolation are released together.
|`sep_trng_reset_recovery_test` CHK-TRNG-CLEAR-SYNC and CHK-TRNG-JTAG.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|The external TRNG CSR path is outside the internal TRNG reset and isolation boundary.
|`sep_trng_reset_recovery_test` CHK-TRNG-EXTERNAL.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|The TRNG reset is not an atomic restart of all entropy consumers.
|The spec states that the TRNG reset is not an atomic restart and states no outcome. A test cannot assert a non-contract.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|The seed adapter packs 32-bit words (twelve per 384-bit seed) and attaches the provisional FIPS constant 1. The constant does not measure source quality. Qualification must justify the source separately.
|The seed words and the FIPS constant are graded by CHK3 of the open entropy tests.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|CSRNG pulls seeds through the entropy_src_hw_if handshake (es_req, es_ack, es_bits, es_fips); it must not take a partly packed seed.
|CHK3 of the open entropy tests grades the 384-bit seed against the 12-word golden.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|The CSRNG and EDN 64-bit AXI4-Lite lane adapter forwards only aligned single-lane accesses with strobe 0x0F or 0xF0 and answers others SLVERR. It holds one downstream slot: a read is taken only when no write half is pending, and a same-cycle read and write give the read first.
|`sep_drbg_axil_adapter_refusal_test`, `sep_drbg_axil_adapter_port_arbitration_test` and the two concurrent AW-then-AR tests.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|The pool is filled over DRBG stream 2 through the pool post-mux adapter, which converts to the native EDN fill port of u_entropy_fifo. The DRBG itself has no native endpoint.
|The pool fill path is graded by `sep_entropy_pool_aperture_test` and the CHK5_pool rows.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|The BIW stage (Barak-Impagliazzo-Wigderson) combines the 12 byte streams with four GF(2^8) multiply-add units (polynomial 0x1B) into one 32-bit word.
|CHK2 of the open entropy tests grades the compressed words.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|DEBUG_CTRL routes one of 256 signals to signal_monitor_o. Both DEBUG_CTRL fields are locked by FIPS_LOCK. SEP leaves signal_monitor_o unconnected and false-paths it.
|`sep_esrc_fips_lock_test` grades the DEBUG_CTRL lock.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|The ESRC follows NIST SP 800-90B guidelines and is intended for FIPS 140-2 and 140-3. It includes a configurable SHA-256 whitener that software can bypass. AIS31 is a design intent.
|A statement of intent. The whitener bypass is graded in `sep_esrc_conditioning_matrix_rand_test`.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|The Key Manager delivers a value as two 32-bit-word shares whose XOR is the value. Word N carries bits [32N+31:32N]. Both shares are always used, an unwritten share reads as zero, and KEY_CTRL.KEY_VALID qualifies the value.
|`sep_km_sideload_share_walk_test` grades that both shares are used.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|ABR takes four independently qualified seed blocks (MLDSA_SEED, MLKEM_SEED_D, MLKEM_SEED_Z, MLKEM_MSG), each 8 words per share with its own KEY_VALID. The ML-KEM seed is D then Z in 512 bits and completes only when both are valid. A seed is used only when its seed read is enabled.
|`sep_km_sideload_share_walk_test` grades the four seed blocks and the D plus Z rule.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|Word i of a delivered ABR seed or message is software register index i, with byte 0 of the FIPS byte string in bits [7:0]. MLKEM_SHARED_KEY.KEY[i] holds shared-key bytes 4i to 4i+3 in the same order.
|`sep_km_sideload_share_walk_test` and `sep_km_abr_mldsa_kat_test` grade the word order with a non-palindromic seed.
|<<sep-vplan-phase3-crypto-entropy,Crypto and entropy>>
|An OTBN, AES or KMAC software reset cancels that engine's endpoints in the shared crypto EDN adapter from the cycle its paths report isolated until reset releases. A word committed to the engine but not acknowledged is dropped and not given to another client. Other clients are unaffected.
|`sep_crypto_per_ip_reset_isolation_test` CHK-EDN-*.
